mv-k03-v318.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v318.question: Why does figurative usage fail to establish real agency in the self?
premises: Figurative usage does not attain the real nature of a thing.
A merely figurative designation may be devoid of real substance.
A designation lacking real substance cannot establish actual agency.
mv-k03-v318.inference: Therefore, attributing agency to the self by figurative usage does not prove that the self is truly an agent.

mv-k03-v319.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v319.question: What follows if agency is attributed to the self only by figurative designation?
premises: A merely figurative designation does not make something what it is called.
Even if a person were figuratively called fire, he would not remove cold caused by snow, hail, showers, and wind.
Real causal power requires more than a figurative name.
mv-k03-v319.inference: Therefore, figuratively calling the self an agent does not give it real causal efficacy.

mv-k03-v320.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v320.question: If the self is not truly an agent, who could bear agency even figuratively?
premises: Prakṛti is not declared to be the seer of the seeing self.
No other candidate exists to take over agency from the self.
Figurative agency still requires some locus to which it can be attributed.
mv-k03-v320.inference: Therefore, there is no suitable bearer for even a figurative attribution of agency.

mv-k03-v321.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v321.question: What practical purpose does a merely figurative attribution of agency serve?
premises: A figurative usage of agency has no clear explanatory purpose.
A mere designation, even if unreal, can still be changed or replaced.
What can be altered without loss of reality does not establish real agency.
mv-k03-v321.inference: Therefore, the figurative attribution of agency is explanatorily dispensable.

mv-k03-v322.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v322.question: What challenge is posed to those who accept the self as an agent?
premises: Some doctrinal thinkers accept the self as an agent.
Accepting agency requires explaining what kind of agency is meant.
The author poses a prior question to test that explanation.
mv-k03-v322.inference: Therefore, those who affirm the self's agency must first answer what kind of agency they attribute to it.

mv-k03-v323.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v323.question: Can ordinary action-based agency apply to an all-pervading self without vibration?
premises: Ordinary agency is established through connection with action.
Such ordinary agency involves vibration or movement.
The all-pervading self is described as devoid of vibration.
mv-k03-v323.inference: Therefore, ordinary action-based agency does not fit an all-pervading, vibrationless self.

mv-k03-v324.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v324.question: How do opponents define agency in the self without invoking vibration?
premises: Opponents propose knowledge, desire to act, and effort as a triad.
This triad is said to belong to the self.
They identify the possession of this triad as agency.
mv-k03-v324.inference: The opponent's position is that agency consists in the self's possession of knowledge, desire to act, and effort.

mv-k03-v325.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v325.question: How does the author evaluate the opponent's definition of agency?
premises: The proposed definition is presented as misleading.
It could deceive only those with childish understanding.
Even children are not entirely devoid of awareness.
mv-k03-v325.inference: Therefore, the opponent's definition of agency is too weak to withstand scrutiny.

mv-k03-v326.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v326.question: Why does the triad of knowledge, desire, and effort fail to define agency?
premises: Knowledge by itself is not agency because it is present everywhere.
Desire and effort are also generally present in many cases.
What is widely present without producing action cannot be the defining mark of agency.
mv-k03-v326.inference: Therefore, the mere presence of knowledge, desire, and effort does not constitute agency.

mv-k03-v327.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v327.question: Can knowledge, desire, and effort by themselves produce an action?
premises: A potter may know, desire, and make effort to have a house.
Despite possessing these three, he may still fail to make a house for himself.
Agency requires more than the mere presence of the triad.
mv-k03-v327.inference: Therefore, knowledge, desire, and effort are insufficient to constitute real agency.

mv-k03-v328.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v328.question: Does lack of know-how explain why the potter cannot build the house?
premises: An opponent may claim the potter does not know how to do it.
From that lack of know-how, desire and effort would also be absent.
If the relevant know-how is absent, the action cannot occur.
mv-k03-v328.inference: The objection tries to preserve the triad theory by saying the potter lacks the specific knowledge of doing.

mv-k03-v329.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v329.question: What does the qualifier 'to do' add to knowledge, desire, and effort?
premises: The opponent qualifies knowledge, desire, and effort with the phrase 'to do'.
This qualifier must have a determinate meaning.
One possible meaning is that it implies vibration or dynamic activity.
mv-k03-v329.inference: The debate turns on whether 'to do' adds a real dynamic factor beyond the triad.

mv-k03-v330.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v330.question: If 'to do' means vibration, where is that vibration located in an all-pervading self?
premises: If agency means vibration, the self would know and desire to vibrate.
Any such vibration would have to be located in the self.
An all-pervading self, by its nature, does not admit such produced vibration.
mv-k03-v330.inference: Therefore, interpreting 'to do' as vibration does not rescue agency for an all-pervading self.

mv-k03-v331.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v331.question: Can knowledge without vibration explain agency even in the highest subject?
premises: Knowledge entirely without vibration is not admissible, even for Śiva.
The opponent treats the triad as an instrument of agency.
An instrumental account still does not show the self as the true agent.
mv-k03-v331.inference: Therefore, redefining agency through a vibrationless triad fails to establish real agency.
uncertainties: The reading śarvasyāpi follows the transmitted text; some editions may normalize the name differently.

mv-k03-v332.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v332.question: What does the phrase 'of the self, to do' amount to when analyzed?
premises: The phrase 'to do' must be analyzed in terms of the self's acts.
Analysis yields knowing, desiring, and striving.
These can be further specified as knowing to know, striving to strive, and desiring to desire.
mv-k03-v332.inference: The analysis reduces 'to do' to internal cognitive-volitional acts rather than external agency.

mv-k03-v333.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v333.question: Does analyzing 'to do' into separate mental acts yield real agency?
premises: Taken individually, the analysis yields knowing to do and desiring to do.
Being a desirer to act is not the same as being an agent.
A verbal analysis of 'to do' does not by itself produce agency.
mv-k03-v333.inference: Therefore, the proposed analysis yields only desire or cognition, not genuine agency.

mv-k03-v334.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v334.question: If agency is only mental, how can bodily and verbal actions belong to the agent?
premises: If agency is defined only by mental factors, speech and bodily actions become equivalent to mental ones in the wrong way.
Alternatively, it becomes unclear how speech and bodily actions could belong to the same agent.
A theory of agency must account for mental, verbal, and bodily action together.
mv-k03-v334.inference: Therefore, defining agency by the mental triad alone fails to explain agency in speech and bodily action.

mv-k03-v335.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v335.question: How can even mental actions be attributed to the self on the triad theory?
premises: The opponent appeals to the presence of the triad of qualities.
Actions arise from mind, speech, and body.
The mere presence of the triad does not explain how these actions belong to the self.
mv-k03-v335.inference: Therefore, the triad theory does not adequately explain the self's ownership of any class of actions.

mv-k03-v336.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v336.question: Can accumulated karma make the self a real agent rather than a figurative one?
premises: An opponent may say the self is the sharer of accumulated actions.
Calling the self a sharer of action can still be only figurative.
A figurative attribution does not establish real agency.
mv-k03-v336.inference: Therefore, appeal to accumulated karma does not overcome the charge of figurative agency.

mv-k03-v337.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v337.question: Does mere proximity to qualities of the self make it the locus of agency?
premises: Qualities such as motion, greatness, and others may be present in relation to the self.
Mere presence or proximity of qualities does not by itself constitute agency.
A locus of agency must be more than a passive substrate near qualities.
mv-k03-v337.inference: Therefore, the self does not become an agent merely because certain qualities are present with it.
uncertainties: The compound ātmagamahattvādi is compressed; the exact list of qualities intended is not fully explicit in this verse.

mv-k03-v338.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v338.question: What unwanted consequence follows if proximity to qualities makes one an agent?
premises: If proximity to qualities were enough, agency could arise even in liberation.
The same rule would apply when qualities of another self are nearby.
A theory that yields agency in liberation or by another's qualities is unacceptable.
mv-k03-v338.inference: Therefore, proximity to qualities cannot be the basis of agency.

mv-k03-v339.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v339.question: What further doctrinal faults follow from mislocating agency in selves?
premises: If agency is wrongly assigned among selves, karmic accounting breaks down.
This would produce loss of what has been done and arrival of what has not been done.
The discussion then turns to whether the Lord is needed as cause in intelligent arrangements.
mv-k03-v339.inference: Therefore, misplacing agency leads to karmic disorder and raises the question of the Lord's causal role.

mv-k03-v340.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v340.question: If material and accessory causes are complete, what room remains for an intelligent agent?
premises: An opponent may assign efficient causality to the Lord in effects with complex arrangement.
Such effects may already be fully supplied by inherent and other causal factors.
If all causal factors are complete, an extra efficient agent seems unnecessary.
mv-k03-v340.inference: The opponent challenges the need for the Lord's efficient causality when material conditions are sufficient.

mv-k03-v341.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v341.question: Can the Lord's causality be modeled on the partial causality of agents like a potter?
premises: Ordinary agents like potters contribute only a partial causal factor.
The all-doer cannot be limited to contributing a mere part.
There is no trace of such partial contribution in the all-doer.
mv-k03-v341.inference: Therefore, the Lord's causality cannot be understood on the model of ordinary finite agents.

mv-k03-v342.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v342.question: Why can no being other than the Lord possess true agency?
premises: True agency consists only in knowledge, will, and effort.
No other factor constitutes agency beyond knowledge, will, and effort.
Therefore agency cannot belong to any other being at any time.
mv-k03-v342.inference: Since agency is nothing but knowledge, will, and effort, no one other than the supreme agent can ever be a true doer.

mv-k03-v343.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v343.question: How is the Lord's autonomy related to the agency of individual selves?
premises: The wise know that the Lord's autonomy is agency.
Even the Lord's own agency is understood as autonomy.
This holds even when supreme lords or individual selves appear in difference.
mv-k03-v343.inference: Agency is ultimately the Lord's autonomy, even when it appears distributed among distinct selves.
uncertainties: The phrase 'parameśānāṃ bhede bhede 'pi vātmanām' is compact; it may refer to apparent plurality among supreme lords and/or individual selves.

mv-k03-v344.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v344.question: Do actions bind beings by their own intrinsic nature?
premises: Actions do not arise for bondage by their own nature.
Good and bad results do not come from action by itself.
Therefore bondage and its results must be traced to another source.
mv-k03-v344.inference: Since actions do not bind by their own nature, their good or bad fruits depend on a higher determining agency.

mv-k03-v345.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v345.question: To whom does the sovereignty that determines karmic results belong?
premises: The sovereignty that determines results belongs to the supreme Lord alone.
This point has been conclusively established.
The author has elaborated it elsewhere.
mv-k03-v345.inference: The power governing karmic outcomes is the exclusive sovereignty of the supreme Lord, as established in detail elsewhere.

mv-k03-v346.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v346.question: Why is the Lord's supreme power of action called Aghorā?
premises: The discussion returns to the main topic of the supreme power of action.
This supreme power belongs to the Lord.
It is proclaimed Aghorā because of its non-terrifying nature.
mv-k03-v346.inference: The Lord's supreme power of action is designated Aghorā precisely because it is not terrifying.

mv-k03-v347.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v347.question: What shows the benevolent character of this supreme power of action?
premises: This power is benevolent toward beings in their resort to Śiva.
Through it the path becomes direct and immediate.
The action it performs is not confined to a limited self.
mv-k03-v347.inference: The supreme power of action is benevolent because it leads beings directly to Śiva through an action not restricted to the finite self.
uncertainties: The sense of 'sātmikā' here is read as 'self-centered/limited to the self'; context supports a contrast with universal grace.

mv-k03-v348.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v348.question: How should one answer the objection that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents?
premises: An objection claims that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents.
The objection is conceded as true in a limited sense.
The instructed student should ascertain the matter in the proper way.
mv-k03-v348.inference: Although no finite beings are independently established in Śiva-hood, the teaching must be understood in a way that preserves the Lord's agency.

mv-k03-v349.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v349.question: What is the nature of the Lord and his power beyond limiting constructions?
premises: The Lord of gods is free from constructions of place, time, action, and form.
His power is likewise characterized.
That power is of universal form.
mv-k03-v349.inference: Both the Lord and his power transcend limiting categories while the power manifests as the universe.

mv-k03-v350.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v350.question: How can the universe be described if it abides in non-difference from Bhairava?
premises: The universe is also that same reality.
It is free from the stain-marks of time and other limiting factors.
It abides in non-difference from Bhairava.
mv-k03-v350.inference: The universe, in its highest truth, is not limited by time and remains non-different from Bhairava.
uncertainties: The token '\hspace{3cm}' is editorial spacing, not a Sanskrit word; glossed minimally as spacer.

mv-k03-v351.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v351.question: How does the universe remain autonomous and never outside Śiva-awareness?
premises: By the Lord's autonomy, the universe is autonomous.
It abides surging forth within itself.
Because it shines forth, it is never excluded from immersion in Śiva.
mv-k03-v351.inference: The universe's manifestation is an autonomous expression within Śiva and never falls outside Śiva-awareness.
uncertainties: The compound 'astaśivāveśabahiṣkṛtam' is read as 'excluded from the loss of Śiva-immersion'; the negational layering is compact.

mv-k03-v352.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v352.question: Why is the supreme power described as both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā?
premises: The supreme power is therefore both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā in form.
Scripture will state that such powers grant the fruit of Śiva's abode.
This applies within the circle of beings.
mv-k03-v352.inference: The supreme power's dual Dakṣiṇā-Aghorā nature is justified because it bestows the liberating fruit of Śiva's abode on beings.

mv-k03-v353.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v353.question: How is Śiva's power of action described at the supreme and bound levels?
premises: Knowers of the doctrine declare the supreme Śiva-powers to be Aghorā.
Elsewhere the same power of action of Śiva operates in the bound soul.
The power of action thus functions at different levels.
mv-k03-v353.inference: Śiva's power of action is supreme and Aghorā, yet it also operates within the condition of the bound soul.

mv-k03-v354.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v354.question: How does the power of action function as both binding and liberating?
premises: The power of action binds when it abides in its own path.
When known, the same power brings about accomplishment.
This power is proclaimed as the expansion from A to Ha.
mv-k03-v354.inference: The same phonemic expansion of the power of action binds in ignorance and grants accomplishment when known.

mv-k03-v355.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v355.question: How does the power of action unfold as the entire garland of letters?
premises: The same phonemic expansion proceeds from the abode of bindu.
It takes on the state of non-vowel manifestation.
This unfolding is the entire garland of letters.
mv-k03-v355.inference: The whole alphabet is the unfolding of the power of action as it emanates from bindu into articulated phonemic form.
uncertainties: The phrase 'asvaratvam upāśritaḥ' is read in relation to consonantal manifestation from bindu; the exact technical nuance depends on the surrounding phonematic doctrine.

mv-k03-v356.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v356.question: What arises when the garland of letters is embraced by reflective I-awareness?
premises: The phonemic unfolding is embraced in the awareness 'I'.
This awareness has the nature of reflective self-consciousness.
From that arises the vivid flash of full supreme I-consciousness.
mv-k03-v356.inference: When the power of action is gathered into reflective I-awareness, it manifests as the full supreme I-consciousness.

mv-k03-v357.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v357.question: How does the supreme I-consciousness relate to all beings and the universe?
premises: The supreme I-consciousness devours the mass of bound souls from Ananta to Brahmā.
It brings the moving and unmoving world into the cave of its own belly.
Thus all beings and worlds are contained within it.
mv-k03-v357.inference: The supreme I-consciousness encompasses and reabsorbs the entire range of beings and the whole universe within itself.

mv-k03-v358.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v358.question: Under what condition does the power of action manifest in this reabsorptive form?
premises: The supreme consciousness has swallowed the aggregate of individuals within its own reflective awareness.
It flashes forth dynamically.
As long as it flashes forth, it does so by the nature of the power of action.
mv-k03-v358.inference: The dynamic flashing forth of reabsorptive consciousness is itself the operation of the power of action.

mv-k03-v359.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v359.question: What kinds of differentiated states characterize this manifestation of the power of action?
premises: The manifestation includes countless varieties lacking full consciousness.
It also takes forms divided into gentle and fierce modes.
These modes include peace and endless activity among others.
mv-k03-v359.inference: The power of action manifests as a vast spectrum of states, ranging from unconscious multiplicity to gentle and fierce divine modalities.
uncertainties: The compound analysis is dense; 'anantakāryaśānti' is read as 'endless activity and peace' as representative modalities.

mv-k03-v360.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v360.question: Why do manifold forms arise from the splendor of Bhairava?
premises: Bhairava's splendor has a firm state revealed by the glory of its own reabsorption.
By appropriateness, manifold forms arise from it.
These varied forms do not contradict its stable nature.
mv-k03-v360.inference: The manifold forms of manifestation arise appropriately from Bhairava's splendor, whose stability is grounded in its power of self-reabsorption.

mv-k03-v361.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v361.question: What characterizes the powers that arise from Bhairava's splendor?
premises: These powers are variegated by the recurrence of empty, full, and mixed states.
They are solely intent on reabsorbing their own portion called the universe.
Their reabsorption is into the nature of Śakti.
mv-k03-v361.inference: The powers manifest in alternating modes yet are fundamentally oriented toward reabsorbing the universe into Śakti's nature.

mv-k03-v362.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v362.question: How do the powers act to uproot long-entrenched worldly states?
premises: The powers are conditioned to uproot states long rooted in world and time.
From their own expansion they emit radiance.
Each power emits its own mass of rays.
mv-k03-v362.inference: The powers uproot entrenched worldly conditions by radiating their own distinct expansions.

mv-k03-v363.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v363.question: On what basis do the powers spread forth their fitting manifestations?
premises: The powers spread forth their own fitting manifestations.
They do so by relying on the true state of will.
Their operation is excluded from worldly left-hand practice.
mv-k03-v363.inference: Grounded in efficacious will, the powers manifest what is fitting to them in a mode beyond ordinary worldly left-hand practice.
uncertainties: The compound 'lokotthavāmācārabahiṣkṛteḥ' is read as indicating exclusion from worldly left-hand practice; the doctrinal nuance may be more specific in context.

mv-k03-v364.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v364.question: How do the powers produce scriptures that reach fullness?
premises: The powers bring about scriptures.
These scriptures attain fullness.
Their model is the first-arisen teaching in the sphere of transcending the world.
mv-k03-v364.inference: The powers fashion scriptures to fullness in accordance with the primordial teaching that transcends the world.

mv-k03-v365.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v365.question: What is the nature of the practice and creation established here?
premises: The same transcendent practice appears here with the state of difference swallowed.
This is the full great creation of the supreme Lord.
That creation is established here.
mv-k03-v365.inference: The practice established here is nondual, and it is identical with the supreme Lord's full great creation.

mv-k03-v366.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v366.question: Why can this creation not properly be called the first creation?
premises: In this creation all portions of dissolution and creation abide in the middle.
A first creation would not contain dissolution and creation as intermediate portions within it.
Therefore it is not fitting to call this creation the first.
mv-k03-v366.inference: Because dissolution and creation are both present within it as middle phases, this creation cannot rightly be designated as the primordial first creation.

mv-k03-v367.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v367.question: How can a first arising occur in a principle beyond place and time?
premises: The ultimate principle is beyond place and time.
A first arising presupposes temporal sequence.
This waking state is the primary state that partakes of unfolding.
mv-k03-v367.inference: Since the principle transcends place and time, no literal first arising occurs there; rather, the waking state is the primary mode of unfolding.

mv-k03-v368.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v368.question: From what highest form down to what lowest form do these powers unfold?
premises: Brahma is seated on the lotus of awakening of a portion of his own power.
The powers unfold beginning from the auspicious Śiva form.
They extend down to the form of Brahma.
mv-k03-v368.inference: The powers of consciousness unfold in a graded descent from the supreme Śiva form to the Brahma form.

mv-k03-v369.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v369.question: Can the Lord of consciousness be limited to a definite measurable extent?
premises: The powers of the Lord of consciousness unfold by assuming form.
One might try to say that the god is only this much.
Such a statement is considered as a possible attempt.
mv-k03-v369.inference: Although the powers manifest in definite forms, the attempt to delimit the Lord to a fixed extent is only a provisional claim.

mv-k03-v370.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v370.question: Why cannot the great Lord of consciousness be described as limited in extent?
premises: The great Lord's nature is consciousness.
Consciousness is immeasurable.
This point was stated clearly in the Prabodhapañcadaśikā.
mv-k03-v370.inference: Because the great Lord is of the nature of immeasurable consciousness, he cannot truly be said to be limited.

mv-k03-v371.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v371.question: What distinguishes awareness from inert matter in terms of measurability?
premises: Limited manifestation is the characteristic of the inert.
Awareness is distinct from the inert.
Awareness is not measured.
mv-k03-v371.inference: Because awareness cannot be measured, it is fundamentally different from inert matter, whose defining mark is limited manifestation.

mv-k03-v372.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v372.question: How does the immeasurable Lord appear as the measurable universe?
premises: The Lord is by nature free from measure.
He acts by the exercise of his own freedom.
By that freedom he makes himself into the moving and unmoving universe.
mv-k03-v372.inference: Though immeasurable in essence, the Lord freely manifests himself as the measurable world of moving and unmoving beings.

mv-k03-v373.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v373.question: Through what combinations of principles do the divisions of Śiva arise?
premises: The principles Īśa, Tatpuruṣa, and Aja are involved.
They function as arisen and about to arise.
They combine as singles, six, one, a triad, and three dyads.
mv-k03-v373.inference: The manifold divisions of Śiva arise through specific combinatory arrangements of these principles in their arisen and emerging modes.
uncertainties: The precise mapping of each numerical grouping to specific Śiva divisions is compressed in this verse.

mv-k03-v374.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v374.question: Why do the ten divisions of Śiva appear in manifold forms?
premises: The ten divisions of Śiva arise in a manifold state.
Consciousnesses are varied.
Their mixture produces further variation.
mv-k03-v374.inference: The manifold condition of the ten Śiva divisions results from the mixture of varied forms of consciousness.

mv-k03-v375.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v375.question: How do differentiated knowledges arise even within what is called Śiva?
premises: Even in the state called Śiva, knowledges of difference appear.
These varied knowledges are extended or unfolded.
They arise when the left and right of the three faces come into union.
mv-k03-v375.inference: Differentiated knowledges emerge within Śiva through the conjunction of the left and right aspects of the three faces.

mv-k03-v376.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v376.question: How does the Rudra division become eighteenfold?
premises: Each becomes a distinct power in relation to future, present, and arisen modes.
Six such powers are arranged in a triad.
This arrangement establishes the Rudra division eighteenfold.
mv-k03-v376.inference: The Rudra division becomes eighteenfold through the triadic distribution of six powers across future, present, and arisen modes.

mv-k03-v377.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v377.question: Why do the divisions of Śiva become innumerable?
premises: Each unit is declared to be five-faced.
The system is already divided into ten and eighteen.
Further subdivision by faces multiplies the divisions.
mv-k03-v377.inference: Because each division is itself five-faced, the ten-and-eighteenfold scheme expands into innumerable divisions.

mv-k03-v378.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v378.question: Why is the detailed enumeration of divisions not mere repetition?
premises: The divisions are variegated by each one's own knowledge and action as previously described.
These distinctions are determined within those divisions.
Distinct knowledge and action prevent sameness.
mv-k03-v378.inference: Because each division is distinguished by its own knowledge and action, the account is not repetitive.

mv-k03-v379.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v379.question: How can diverse practices and actions all lead to the abode of Śiva?
premises: Awareness, practice, and the sequence of action differ in each case.
These differences are declared in their respective contexts.
Yet all of them go to the abode of Śiva.
mv-k03-v379.inference: Although knowledge and practice vary by context, all valid forms ultimately converge in the abode of Śiva.

mv-k03-v380.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v380.question: What analogy explains how all knowledges and actions converge in the great Lord?
premises: All drops of water come to rest in the great ocean.
All knowledges and actions are diverse in form.
The great Lord is the ocean of consciousness.
mv-k03-v380.inference: Just as all water drops rest in the ocean, all knowledges and actions ultimately rest in the great Lord, the ocean of consciousness.

mv-k03-v381.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v381.question: How do all forms of knowledge and action ultimately return to Śiva?
premises: Even limited water on earth is drawn up by the sun and returns to the great ocean through rain.
All knowledge and action in the world arise in various ways.
Some arise by themselves and some through transmission by others.
mv-k03-v381.inference: By analogy with the water cycle, all knowledge and action, whether direct or transmitted, ultimately merge in the ocean of Śiva.

mv-k03-v382.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v382.question: What is the nature of the supreme heart-mark described at the right end?
premises: At the right end there is a heart-mark regarded as supreme.
That mark is identified with the heart.
It contains within itself all created beings in fullness.
mv-k03-v382.inference: The supreme heart-mark is not empty but inwardly contains the fullness of all created beings.

mv-k03-v383.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v383.question: Why is that supreme heart-mark described as dark and bearing the form of darkness?
premises: It devours the rays of māyā that produce difference.
By doing so it functions as the dissolver of all.
Dissolution of all differentiated light is represented as darkness.
mv-k03-v383.inference: Because it absorbs all differentiating māyā and dissolves all, the supreme heart-mark appears dark, bearing the form of darkness.

mv-k03-v384.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v384.question: What scriptural teaching supports the identification of the Lord's darkness with dissolution?
premises: The Vijñānaśāstra contains a teaching by the great Lord.
That teaching states that all space is dissolved in the head.
This supports the description of the Lord's darkness.
mv-k03-v384.inference: The scriptural statement that all space dissolves in the head confirms the Lord's darkness as the state of universal dissolution.

mv-k03-v385.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v385.question: When and how should the Bhairava form of darkness be contemplated?
premises: The Bhairava form is associated with darkness and dissolution.
A dark night at the arrival of the dark fortnight corresponds to that form.
Contemplators should meditate on that hard-to-name form for a long time.
mv-k03-v385.inference: The Bhairava form of darkness should be contemplated for a long time on a dark night at the coming of the dark fortnight.

mv-k03-v386.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v386.question: What characterizes the nondual state where ignorance and karma do not bind?
premises: In that state light, suffering, and darkness are covered by nonduality.
There is no connection with ignorance and karma.
Dependence and similar limiting conditions are not seen there.
mv-k03-v386.inference: The nondual state transcends the oppositions of light, suffering, and darkness, and therefore excludes bondage by ignorance, karma, and dependence.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of svar duḥkhaṃ tamo in the source line is compact; the sense follows the nondual covering indicated by advayasaṃvṛte.

mv-k03-v387.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v387.question: How do the four faces appear within the dark Bhairava body?
premises: The Bhairava body is of the form of darkness.
The four faces are present within it.
They shine by being inwardly dissolved.
mv-k03-v387.inference: Within the dark Bhairava body, the four faces shine in a latent, inwardly dissolved manner.

mv-k03-v388.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v388.question: How does the fourfold structure become sixteenfold in the Bhairava body?
premises: Each aspect can be about to emerge, emerged, about to withdraw, or withdrawn.
These states apply simultaneously.
The division yields a sixteenfold structure.
mv-k03-v388.inference: By the simultaneous application of emergence and withdrawal states, the structure becomes sixteenfold.

mv-k03-v389.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v389.question: How does the Bhairava scripture become an eight-times-eight system within Śiva?
premises: The teaching enters the right, emissive, heart, and autonomous aspects in Śiva.
The sixteenfold structure is further articulated.
The scripture named Bhairava becomes eight-times-eight simultaneously.
mv-k03-v389.inference: By entering the autonomous Śiva through its right, emissive, and heart aspects, the Bhairava scripture unfolds simultaneously as an eight-times-eight system.
uncertainties: The technical mapping of dakṣa, vaisargika, hārda, and svatantra to the full eight-times-eight structure is compressed in this verse.

mv-k03-v390.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v390.question: How is the scripture divided and how does the being of knowledge unfold?
premises: The scripture named Rudra, Shiva, and Bhairava is established threefold.
This division holds in reality, not merely conventionally.
The being of knowledge itself unfolds in a threefold way.
mv-k03-v390.inference: The threefold division of the scripture corresponds to a real threefold unfolding of the being of knowledge.

mv-k03-v391.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v391.question: What are the three modes by which knowledge unfolds and which powers correspond to them?
premises: Knowledge unfolds by difference, by difference-and-nondifference, and by the full junction of nondifference.
There are three principal powers belonging to Shambhu.
These powers begin with will and correspond to the three modes.
mv-k03-v391.inference: The three principal Shambhu powers of will and so on correspond to the three modes of difference, mixed difference-nondifference, and full nondifference.

mv-k03-v392.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v392.question: How does the elaboration of the five powers relate to the supreme triad?
premises: In that same context there is an elaboration involving the five powers and so on.
In the middle that triad appears divided.
Even so, that triad is indeed supreme.
mv-k03-v392.inference: The elaboration into five powers occurs within the triad, yet the triad remains the supreme reality.

mv-k03-v393.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v393.question: How is this scripture established in the teacher's lineage and why is it near the left and right streams?
premises: The scripture is established in our teacher's house through the sequence of transmission.
Its position follows from nearness to the left and right scriptures.
This nearness explains its particular placement in the tradition.
mv-k03-v393.inference: The scripture's transmission in the teacher's lineage is grounded in its proximity to the left and right scriptural streams.

mv-k03-v394.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v394.question: Where does the Kaula stream unfold and what state arises from it?
premises: The Kaula stream fully unfolds at the edge of the edge-stream.
From that unfolding arises a state beyond limiting conditions.
In that state all limitations of beings are withdrawn and fullness remains.
mv-k03-v394.inference: The Kaula stream unfolds at the outermost edge and leads to a fullness in which all limiting conditions of beings are withdrawn.

mv-k03-v395.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v395.question: How does Bhairava abide in relation to the three powers across the channels?
premises: Bhairava's activity is expanded by the rising fluid of supreme reality.
In the Ishana, left, and right channels the triad of powers appears in sequence.
Bhairava embraces that triad from Apara up to Para and abides.
mv-k03-v395.inference: Bhairava abides as the encompassing reality that holds the full triad of powers across the three channels from Apara to Para.

mv-k03-v396.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v396.question: How is the supreme lord described in relation to division and reabsorption?
premises: That principle manifests the division of difference and makes it clear.
The same supreme lord is infinite and about to reabsorb that division.
In reality the tradition declares that supreme form to be three-headed.
mv-k03-v396.inference: The supreme lord both manifests differentiated division and reabsorbs it, and is therefore declared in reality to be three-headed.

mv-k03-v397.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v397.question: Why are the upper, left, and other tantras and kulas established in that stream?
premises: The upper, left, and other tantras and kulas are established in that stream.
Their establishment serves a specific purpose.
That purpose is the removal of the contraction caused by difference.
mv-k03-v397.inference: The various tantras and kulas are grounded in that stream in order to remove the contraction produced by difference.

mv-k03-v398.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v398.question: How is the triad-meaning established in supreme light?
premises: triad-meaning is established threefold
supreme lord utters it as knowledge-moon
mv-k03-v398.inference: The verse identifies the triad-meaning as established by supreme lord under the name knowledge-moon.
uncertainties: exact sandhi of jñānacandrākhyayoditaḥ not expanded

mv-k03-v399.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v399.question: What is the nature of all scripture-meaning?
premises: all scripture-meaning is supported by supreme speech course
it lacks unfolded meaning-word distinctions
mv-k03-v399.inference: Scripture-meaning is supreme speech supported and undivided at the level of meaning and word.

mv-k03-v400.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v400.question: What follows after the supreme speech level?
premises: afterward knowledge-power part dominates in self
action-power is very subtle in sadākhya lordship
mv-k03-v400.inference: The descent moves from supreme speech to a subtler action-power within sadākhya lordship.

mv-k03-v401.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v401.question: How does it exist in paśyantī and madhyamā?
premises: in paśyantī and madhyamā abodes through stirring mention
it exists in word and sentence form in letter form
mv-k03-v401.inference: At these speech stations it appears as word and sentence in letter form.

mv-k03-v402.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v402.question: What did sadāśiva do in svacchanda scripture?
premises: in svacchanda scripture thus said
sadāśiva himself joined tantra with prior and later words and sentences
mv-k03-v402.inference: Sadāśiva composed the tantra by joining prior and later words and sentences.

mv-k03-v403.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v403.question: What is said about sadāśiva in that covering?
premises: thus there too said in that sushiva covering on path
sushiva covering first there sadāśiva to be known
mv-k03-v403.inference: In that covering on the path, Sadāśiva is first to be known.
uncertainties: leading apostrophe in 'dhvani retained as token

mv-k03-v404.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v404.question: Where does authority and desire to grasp belong?
premises: joined with ten śiva and endowed with eighteen rudra
authority indeed in īśa principle
desire to grasp that in sauśiva
mv-k03-v404.inference: Authority belongs to īśa principle, while the desire to grasp it belongs to sauśiva.

mv-k03-v405.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v405.question: What triad arises in the power principle?
premises: in covering from bindu in enjoyment-abode
from abundance of lord
of called-bhairava knowledge in power-principle supreme triad
mv-k03-v405.inference: In the power principle there is a supreme triad of Bhairava knowledge arising from the lord's abundance.

mv-k03-v406.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v406.question: Where is the position said to be?
premises: position therefore above īśvara
from sadāśiva station below
said by sushiva covering in glorious svacchanda scripture
mv-k03-v406.inference: The position is above Īśvara and below Sadāśiva station, as said in the Svacchanda scripture.

mv-k03-v407.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v407.question: What is said after those distinctions?
premises: after that in these śiva-rudra distinctions enough
on māyīya path established by śivas said named śiva
mv-k03-v407.inference: After those distinctions, on the māyīya path, the one named Śiva is said by the Śivas.

mv-k03-v408.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v408.question: How does difference reach variety?
premises: difference by rudras and called-rudra thus reached variety
then from flourishing essence of rising action gradually clearly
mv-k03-v408.inference: The difference reaches variety through Rudras, then gradually becomes clear from the flourishing essence of rising action.

mv-k03-v409.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v409.question: What is the nature of scriptural meanings that are accessible to the world?
premises: Scriptural meanings rest on Maya-born Vaikhari speech heard by all.
They take the form of letters, sentences, and words.
Such meanings fall within the range of ordinary worldly cognition.
mv-k03-v409.inference: The scriptural meanings accessible to the world are those expressed through Maya-born Vaikhari speech in the form of letters, sentences, and words.

mv-k03-v410.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v410.question: Through what level of speech do scriptural meanings proceed to the transmitters of the tantras?
premises: Scriptural meanings proceed by resorting to the various transmitters of the tantras.
This transmission occurs first at the level of Maya-born Vaikhari.
Vaikhari is described as a cavity or channel through which the meaning comes down.
mv-k03-v410.inference: The descent of scriptural meaning to the transmitters of the tantras first passes through the Maya-born level of Vaikhari speech.

mv-k03-v411.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v411.question: Does scriptural meaning bound by Maya-born letters reach the inner supreme speech?
premises: Scriptural meaning can be bound by Maya-born letters.
The inner level consists of supreme speech letters of essential awakening.
Meaning in that outer form does not arrive at that inner level.
mv-k03-v411.inference: Scriptural meaning confined to Maya-born letters does not reach the inner essence of supreme speech.

mv-k03-v412.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v412.question: Where does the scriptural meaning refined by supreme immersion ultimately abide?
premises: Scriptural meaning can be refined by the root impression of uncontrived supreme immersion.
Such meaning extends even to the worldly level.
Its true locus is the supreme lord, the thirty-seventh principle.
mv-k03-v412.inference: The scriptural meaning rooted in uncontrived supreme immersion, though reaching the worldly level, abides in the supreme thirty-seventh lord.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'thirty-seventh' follows the Śaiva tattva scheme but is not glossed in the verse itself.

mv-k03-v413.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v413.question: Can unreal beings possess reality or can respect arise in a nature overcome by disrespect?
premises: Unreal beings have no reality anywhere at all.
A nature overcome by disrespect is opposed to respect.
Respect cannot arise where its opposing condition dominates.
mv-k03-v413.inference: Just as unreal beings lack reality, respect cannot arise in a nature overcome by disrespect.

mv-k03-v414.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v414.question: What is the ultimate status of all scriptural meaning and of the Vedas and other teachings?
premises: The entire meaning of scripture is established as the nature of the supreme principle.
The Vedas and other teachings appear as distinct scriptural portions.
Those portions belong to the Maya-born level of expression.
mv-k03-v414.inference: All scriptural meaning is grounded in the supreme principle, while the Vedas and other teachings are Maya-born portions of that teaching.

mv-k03-v415.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v415.question: From what source do the teachings shine forth and can there be any other cause?
premises: The teachings shine forth from the power of the Bhairava-sun alone.
No other source accounts for their manifestation.
Apart from the reflective awareness of consciousness there can be no other cause anywhere.
mv-k03-v415.inference: The teachings manifest solely from the reflective awareness of consciousness, symbolized as the power of the Bhairava-sun.

mv-k03-v416.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v416.question: Why can consciousness be spoken of as both cause and effect?
premises: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness is nothing other than consciousness itself.
The terms effect and cause are applied to it.
This application is figurative rather than a real division.
mv-k03-v416.inference: Because consciousness remains only consciousness, the distinction between cause and effect is applied to it only figuratively.

mv-k03-v417.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v417.question: What appears as the true form of a being through sequential transformation?
premises: A being undergoes transformation in sequence and displays extended properties.
Such transformation has a beginning and an end.
At both beginning and end, consciousness alone appears as its form.
mv-k03-v417.inference: Throughout the sequential transformation of a being, consciousness alone is what appears as its true form at beginning and end.

mv-k03-v418.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v418.question: What absurd consequence follows if consciousness were subject to division by time?
premises: The verse considers the hypothesis that consciousness endures division by time.
If that were so, an impossible consequence would follow.
The consequence is as absurd as enjoying gravel bits of sky cut by a sharpened sword.
mv-k03-v418.inference: Consciousness cannot be subject to division by time, because that hypothesis leads to an absurd impossibility.

mv-k03-v419.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v419.question: Why are all the scriptures self-luminous in reality?
premises: All the scriptures do not fall away from the form of consciousness.
Consciousness is self-luminous.
What does not fall away from self-luminous consciousness shares that luminosity.
mv-k03-v419.inference: Because all scriptures remain within the form of self-luminous consciousness, they are in reality self-luminous.

mv-k03-v420.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v420.question: Can the expressed meaning ever stand apart from the expressing word?
premises: One might object that the expressed stands apart from the expresser.
By its autonomy the expresser alone appears as what will be expressed.
Therefore the expressed does not exist as a separate independent entity.
mv-k03-v420.inference: The expressed meaning never stands apart from the expresser, because the autonomous expresser itself appears as the future expressed.

mv-k03-v421.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k03-v421.question: In what different ways can the expressing aspect of a word appear?
premises: The expressing aspect of a word does not appear in only one fixed mode.

mv-k04-v510.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v510.question: How does clear perception arise once eye-rays are settled?

mv-k04-v511.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

mv-k04-v512.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v512.question: How can mind know when lamp and eye cover it?

mv-k04-v513.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v513.question: Why is blindness and its treatment not a fit support fault?

mv-k04-v515.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v515.question: Why is one-taste cognition impossible when bile abounds?

mv-k04-v516.question: Why is bitterness not tongue-gone if bile-gone?

mv-k04-v517.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v517.question: How can simultaneous bitter-sweet cognition occur?

uncertainties: jñaptis may be cognition of taste.

mv-k04-v518.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v518.question: Why does water-nature not imply hardness for nose?
premises: If from nature, what is this water-ness grasp?

Why is its hardness not seen?
mv-k04-v518.inference: Sense organs are not reducible to their element's qualities.

mv-k04-v519.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v519.question: Why does smell not shine if quality-excessive?
premises: If smell-quality-excessive, why does smell not shine?

mv-k04-v520.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v520.question: How can mind grasp smell if smell-less and non-earth?

mv-k04-v521.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v521.question: Why does elemental sense-aggregate not fit?
premises: Therefore elemental sense-aggregate does not fit.
But in egoity there is pervasion.
There is non-distinctness.
mv-k04-v521.inference: Sense organs are better explained by egoity than by elements.

mv-k04-v522.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v522.question: Why must speech and five action-senses be distinguished?

mv-k04-v523.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

mv-k04-v525.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v525.question: Why are you not speaker when I utter sound?

mv-k04-v526.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v526.question: If the vocal organ stays the same, how do distinct and indistinct sounds arise?

mv-k04-v527.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v527.question: Whence is sound-difference in whisper and memory if effort too originates?

mv-k04-v528.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

mv-k04-v530.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

mv-k04-v530.inference: Acceptance defined, with the self-as-root premise opening the next move.

mv-k04-v552.inference: Not-that-form entry fails, and stated reasoning voids variety everywhere.

mv-k04-v553.question: How is our Caitra such, being as it were variegated?

Thus this Caitra of ours, being as it were variegated, is such.
mv-k04-v553.inference: Variety-shining births the variegated state instanced in ordinary Caitra.

mv-k04-v554.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v554.question: Who is established in samadhi, seeing by seeing?
premises: Enough of Mitra view of that.
Seen, me the seer of beings, seeing he sees.

mv-k04-v555.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v555.question: Who will be freed, having enjoyed through crores of births?

mv-k04-v556.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v556.question: Who shares freedom in the long-undivided light?
premises: This one too, another, is a freedom-sharer, thus of unended rise.

mv-k04-v556.inference: Another shares freedom in the ever-undivided one light.

mv-k04-v557.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v557.question: What difference could split the nondual Great Lord?
premises: Therefore indeed there is no difference.
Which could split the nondual Great Lord, beautiful with light-bliss.
mv-k04-v557.inference: No difference splits Maheshvaras light-bliss beauty.

mv-k04-v558.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v558.question: If place-time-form shine as difference-makers, what is that shining?
premises: Beginning with place, time, form, knowledge, property, and other adjuncts — agreed.
If they shine as difference-makers, that shining is just so.
mv-k04-v558.inference: Agreed difference-makers shine as just-that shining.

mv-k04-v559.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v559.question: What if shining is just such — what of the word difference?
premises: But if that shining is just such, then this nondualism is clear.
The mere word difference is devoid of shine.
mv-k04-v559.inference: Such-like shining clears nondualism while difference stays an unlustrous mere word.

mv-k04-v560.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v560.question: What happens even granting difference-reckoning?
premises: Let there be difference-reckoning growing in shining.
But by the stated reasoning it will be well-established right there.
mv-k04-v560.inference: Conceded difference-reckoning is absorbed on the spot by stated reasoning.

mv-k04-v561.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v561.question: How do pot and cloth differ, from each other, others, and me?

And those two differ even from me.
mv-k04-v561.inference: Pot and cloth exemplify threefold difference: mutual, inter-knower, and from-me.

mv-k04-v562.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v562.question: Is the one-light view not partisan — how is nondualism yours?
premises: Thus this one light, of the nature of such relishing.

mv-k04-v562.inference: The one-light relishing-nature draws the partisanship charge against nondualism.

mv-k04-v563.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v563.question: What is arguing difference with the deaf?

This is delighting deaf assemblies with song and music.
mv-k04-v563.inference: Difference granted then struck, dispute with the deaf is song-and-music delight.

mv-k04-v564.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v564.question: Why not state nondualism by excluding dualism?
premises: For nondualism is not stated by us through exclusion of dualism entry.
That would be reaching your side, for that dualism is blatant.
mv-k04-v564.inference: Exclusionary nondualism concedes the opponent ground while dualism stays blatant.

mv-k04-v565.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v565.question: What is called nondual where all shines the same?

That is called nondual.
mv-k04-v565.inference: Equipollent shining of the alternatives is itself called nondual.

mv-k04-v566.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v566.question: Why quibble over difference if nothing is to accept or reject?
premises: Well then, so be it, even difference; we are no lovers of mere words.
Let it be, for us there is nothing to reject or accept, as with you here.
mv-k04-v566.inference: Difference conceded without word-fondness, with nothing to take or leave on either side.

mv-k04-v567.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v567.question: What refuge for one who would cling to the all-favoring position?

mv-k04-v567.inference: The all-favoring position resolves into the supreme-nondual refuge.

mv-k04-v568.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k04-v568.question: What will come in the eighteenth chapter?

mv-k05-v607.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v607.question: What objection arises if an object's luminosity is treated as its own power or property?

mv-k05-v608.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v608.question: Can luminosity be coherently located as some separate entity among object, subject, and cognition?

mv-k05-v608.inference: Luminosity cannot be explained as a separate entity situated within the object-subject-cognition triad.

mv-k05-v609.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v609.question: What dilemma follows if beings are intrinsically unmanifest yet somehow become illuminated?

mv-k05-v609.inference: Treating beings as intrinsically unmanifest makes either universal non-manifestation or loss of nature unavoidable.

mv-k05-v610.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v610.question: Does the arising of knowledge preserve or destroy the nature of a being that remains in its own form?

The opponent must explain manifestation without altering the being's nature.
mv-k05-v610.inference: Manifestation cannot be explained as a change in the object's nature while it remains what it is.

mv-k05-v611.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v611.question: Why would manifestation not occur universally if beings remain undifferentiated in their own nature?

mv-k05-v611.inference: The manifestation of the universe is grounded in the delimiting principle, not in undifferentiated objective being.

mv-k05-v612.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)

mv-k05-v613.inference: To avoid infinite regress, the ultimate delimiting principle must itself be unlimited.

mv-k05-v614.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v614.question: Why is the unlimited limiter not within the domain of time according to the scriptures?

mv-k05-v616.inference: To avoid regress, the knowing subject must ultimately be free from time's delimitation.

mv-k05-v649.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v649.question: Why is the opponent's appeal to conceptual construction refuted in the case of taking food?
premises: Hungry people take food and so on in order to eat.
They do so without the mediation of pervasion and other inferential steps.
The opponent claims such cognition is mere conceptual construction.
mv-k05-v649.inference: Because the act occurs without inferential mediation, the opponent's claim that it is conceptual construction is thereby refuted.

mv-k05-v650.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v650.question: In well-practiced cases, what need is there for cognition pervaded by conceptual construction?
premises: In well-practiced cases there is awareness of pervasion whose nature is invariable concomitance.
The opponent proposes cognition pervaded by conceptual construction to explain such cases.
The author rejects that proposed mechanism.
mv-k05-v650.inference: Since the awareness is already established through practice, there is no need to posit cognition pervaded by conceptual construction.

mv-k05-v651.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v651.question: Does the swift arising of the cognition justify inferring hidden conceptual construction?
premises: The cognition arises so swiftly that it is not clearly noticed.
The opponent infers from this lack of noticing that conceptual construction is present.
The author presents this inference as the opponent's position.
mv-k05-v651.inference: The opponent concludes that the unnoticed swift cognition is itself conceptual construction, but this rests only on its not being noticed.

mv-k05-v652.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v652.question: What fault does the author find in the logicians who defend this position?
premises: The opponents are blinded by attachment to their own side.
They repeatedly forget even what they themselves have accepted.
They pride themselves on being logicians.
mv-k05-v652.inference: Their attachment to their own position makes them inconsistent with their own admitted doctrines.

mv-k05-v653.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v653.question: What do the opponents themselves hold about how cognition manifests its object?
premises: According to the opponent, every cognition ends in a single moment.
According to the opponent, cognition manifests its object by the mere fact of arising.
This doctrine is admitted by the opponents themselves.
mv-k05-v653.inference: On the opponent's own view, a cognition reveals its object at the very moment of its arising, without needing further duration.

mv-k05-v654.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v654.question: If cognition lasts only a moment, what follows about swift manifestation?
premises: Swift manifesting capacity is not anything beyond a single moment.
Every cognition, on the opponent's view, operates within that momentary arising.
No extra duration is available to distinguish swift from non-swift manifestation.
mv-k05-v654.inference: Therefore, in truth, every cognition would have to be counted as swiftly manifesting.

mv-k05-v655.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v655.question: What problematic consequence follows if momentariness makes all cognition unnoticed or extended?
premises: If momentariness alone explains non-noticing, that consequence would apply everywhere among things.
Alternatively, one might appeal to unbroken seeing over a longer time.
The opponent must account for cognition that ranges over a longer duration.
mv-k05-v655.inference: The opponent's momentary model either makes non-noticing universal or fails to explain cognition that spans a longer time.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic break between the two halves is compressed; the contrast is read from atha and the genitive plural.

mv-k05-v656.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v656.question: If an object is manifested by mere arising, how can arising alone explain its clarity?
premises: The opponent holds that an object is manifested by the mere birth of cognition.
The opponent also holds that cognition becomes clear in its object because of arising alone.
Both claims rely on the same momentary arising.
mv-k05-v656.inference: If mere arising is sufficient for manifestation and clarity, the opponent must explain how differences in clarity or timing arise.

mv-k05-v657.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v657.question: How can a swifter experience create difference if cognition is already self-luminous?
premises: The opponent treats a swifter experience as what makes a difference.
The opponent also says cognition is self-luminous, though possibly related to grasping.
A self-luminous cognition does not obviously need speed to differentiate it.
mv-k05-v657.inference: If cognition is self-luminous, the appeal to a swifter experience cannot by itself explain the relevant difference.
uncertainties: grahāpekṣaṃ is read as 'dependent on grasping' in the opponent's framework; the exact polemical target is compressed.

mv-k05-v658.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v658.question: Can temporal duration, like lightning or a lamp, explain cognitive difference?
premises: A cognition might serve as a means elsewhere, like lightning or a lamp.
Lightning and lamps differ by lasting briefly or longer.
The opponent may use that temporal difference to explain cognitive difference.
mv-k05-v658.inference: Even if temporal duration appears to make a difference in such analogies, that does not yet show how momentary cognitions yield the required unified awareness.

mv-k05-v659.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v659.question: Why does repeated clarity not support the opponent's account of inference?
premises: In inferences, the grasping of pervasion and related factors does not recur as a newly noticed event each time.
If it became clear again and again, that repeated clarification would be noticed.
Such repeated noticing is not what actually occurs in ordinary inference.
mv-k05-v659.inference: Because inferential grasping does not become repeatedly clear in a noticeable way, the opponent cannot explain inference by repeated momentary clarifications.

mv-k05-v660.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v660.question: How can a series of successive cognitions produce the manifestation of a single object?
premises: Inferential cognition may involve a series of successive cognitions, such as smoke and so on.
Each member of that series may arise clearly.
Inference requires the manifestation of one unified object or conclusion.
mv-k05-v660.inference: A merely successive series of clear cognitions cannot by itself account for the manifestation of one unified object.

mv-k05-v661.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v661.question: Can a final connecting cognition unify earlier cognitions if it is itself distinct?
premises: The opponent may propose a final connecting cognition to unify the series.
That final cognition is, on the same theory, distinct like the earlier cognitions.
A distinct momentary cognition faces the same problem of separation.
mv-k05-v661.inference: A final connecting cognition cannot unify the series if it is just another distinct momentary cognition.

mv-k05-v662.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v662.question: How can a final cognition connect earlier cognitions if they no longer exist?
premises: The opponent claims the final cognition connects the earlier series of cognitions.
On momentarism, earlier cognitions are no longer existent when the final cognition arises.
Connection requires something available to be connected.
mv-k05-v662.inference: If the earlier cognitions have perished and are non-existent, their connection by a later cognition is not possible.

mv-k05-v663.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v663.question: Can memory connect cognitions if there is no underlying experience to ground it?
premises: The opponent may propose memory as the connection between cognitions.
Memory requires some prior experience.
On the opponent's momentary model, the needed experience is not available as a unifying ground.
mv-k05-v663.inference: Memory cannot supply the required connection if there is no genuine experience available to ground it.

mv-k05-v664.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v664.question: Why cannot awareness experience cognitions on the opponent's own momentary view?
premises: The opponent holds that two cognitions do not exist simultaneously.
Experience of a cognition by awareness would require a relation not available within that restriction.
The opponent's own doctrine blocks simultaneous pairing of cognitions.
mv-k05-v664.inference: Given the opponent's denial of simultaneous cognitions, an experience of cognitions by awareness does not fit their system.

mv-k05-v665.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v665.question: Under what condition is the cognition-known relation observed, and when is it impossible?
premises: The relation of cognition and known is observed when two factors abide simultaneously.
Successive factors arise in prior and later form and are opposed in that way.
The opponent's model relies on such successive arising.
mv-k05-v665.inference: The cognition-known relation cannot be established between successively arising, mutually opposed factors.

mv-k05-v666.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v666.question: What kind of knowing is present even in cognition that follows pervasion?
premises: Some cognition appears to be preceded by manifestation following pervasion.
The preceding argument has undermined a merely sequential account of such cognition.
The author offers a positive characterization of that cognition.
mv-k05-v666.inference: Even cognition that follows pervasion is, at its core, a non-sequential knowing akin to direct perception.

mv-k05-v667.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v667.question: What analogy illustrates immediate perceptual knowing after waking from deep sleep?
premises: A person awakened suddenly from deep sleep has eyes just beginning to open.
That person acts to remove the dimness affecting the appearance of things.
The analogy is used to clarify immediate knowing.
mv-k05-v667.inference: The waking person’s situation illustrates a direct apprehension that is not constructed through sequential inference.

mv-k05-v668.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v668.question: What does the waking analogy show about ordinary inferential self-awareness?
premises: The person awakened from sleep rubs the eyes and does similar actions.
That person does not think, 'I am inferring these things.'
The same point applies to the disputed case of inference.
mv-k05-v668.inference: Immediate practical cognition does not present itself as an inferential process, so the disputed cognition should be understood similarly.

mv-k05-v669.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v669.question: What does the momentary confusion after deep sleep illustrate about awareness?
premises: One who rises from the delusion of deep sleep may momentarily forget himself.
In that same moment he may also forget where he is.
This forgetting is temporary and occurs at the threshold of waking.
mv-k05-v669.inference: The analogy shows that awareness can be temporarily veiled without ceasing to be the underlying ground of recognition.

mv-k05-v670.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v670.question: What restores self-recognition after the momentary confusion of waking?
premises: After initial confusion, effort gathers and clear seeing awakens.
The person then recognizes, 'I am that one.'
This recognition is grounded in awareness itself.
mv-k05-v670.inference: Self-recognition arises from awareness in the ultimate sense, not from a merely sequential construction.

mv-k05-v671.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v671.question: Who is the ultimate agent behind the concealment and revelation of awareness?
premises: The processes of forgetting and recognition occur within awareness.
The Lord Bhairava is consciousness in nature.
By his freedom he conceals and reveals his own form.
mv-k05-v671.inference: The alternation of concealment and revelation in cognition is ultimately the free activity of Bhairava, whose nature is consciousness.

mv-k05-v672.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v672.question: How do ignorance and knowledge arise from the Lord's concealment and revelation?
premises: Bhairava freely conceals and reveals his own form.
Concealment corresponds to ignorance and revelation corresponds to knowledge.
The knowledge that arises appears with clarity.
mv-k05-v672.inference: Ignorance and knowledge arise according to the Lord's concealment and revelation, and the resulting knowledge is clear and directly evident to all.

mv-k05-v673.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v673.question: What happens in cognition when the word for pot is heard?
premises: When the word for pot is heard, a cognition of broad base, belly, and so on arises.
In that cognition, convention, memory, and similar factors are present.
These factors are of the same kind as in other acts of recognition.
mv-k05-v673.inference: Hearing a word produces a complex cognition involving remembered conventions and associated features.

mv-k05-v674.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v674.question: How does clear awareness arise in the examination of a gem?
premises: In the examination of a gem, one awakens one's own awareness.
This awakening occurs through assemblages of other cognitions.
The resulting awareness stands forth as clear in nature.
mv-k05-v674.inference: Clear awareness of an object is brought about through the support of other cognitions.

mv-k05-v675.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v675.question: What role do other cognitions play once the gem's reality shines forth?
premises: The reality of the gem shines forth from the connection with the final awakened clear awareness.
At that point, other cognitions have no further use.
The decisive illumination comes from that final awareness itself.
mv-k05-v675.inference: Once the final clear awareness arises, auxiliary cognitions are no longer operative.

mv-k05-v676.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v676.question: Why do auxiliary cognitions lose their usefulness at the moment of manifestation?
premises: Those other cognitions served only as causes for awakening that final awareness.
In the very connection of that awareness's manifestation, they have no usefulness.
Their role is preparatory rather than constitutive of the final illumination.
mv-k05-v676.inference: Auxiliary cognitions are instrumental causes but not operative in the final manifestation itself.

mv-k05-v677.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v677.question: Does verbal cognition also involve a single clear illumination like the gem example?
premises: The example of a child and a gem-cutter's knowledge shows a single clear cognition.
This example applies by itself to verbal cognition as well.
In verbal cognition too, one clear illumination-cognition arises.
mv-k05-v677.inference: Verbal cognition, like perceptual expertise, culminates in a single clear illuminating awareness.
uncertainties: vaikaṭika is read as gem-cutter or lapidary; context supports that sense.

mv-k05-v678.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v678.question: What is the nature of the cognition that arises immediately after hearing a word?
premises: When such a word is heard, a cognition arises immediately after.
That cognition occurs in the manifestation of meaning.
It is a determinate cognition of a specific extent and character.
mv-k05-v678.inference: The immediate post-hearing cognition is a determinate manifestation of meaning.

mv-k05-v679.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v679.question: Can the unity of a pot serve as an analogy for the relation between word and meaning?
premises: The meaning stands there with that extent, like the prior and posterior parts of a pot.
An objector suggests the pot may be one whole composed of parts.
This raises the question whether word and meaning share a similar unity.
mv-k05-v679.inference: The analogy of a unified whole is introduced to probe the relation between word and meaning.

mv-k05-v680.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v680.question: Why is the analogy between a pot's unity and word-meaning unity rejected?
premises: The objector claims there is no unity between word and meaning.
Therefore the objector questions how such sameness could hold.
This objection arises from eyes clouded by the habit of grasping difference.
mv-k05-v680.inference: The denial of word-meaning unity is attributed to a habitual perception of difference.

mv-k05-v681.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v681.question: What does the undivided Bhairava assume within himself despite the objector's clouded vision?
premises: Even with the application of the collyrium of true reasoning, the objector has not attained clear vision.
The undivided Lord Bhairava assumes the state of both enjoyed and enjoyer.
This assumption occurs within Bhairava himself.
mv-k05-v681.inference: The ultimate nondual reality encompasses both subject and object within itself.

mv-k05-v682.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v682.question: What happens to the earlier objection once Bhairava's nondual fullness is established?
premises: Bhairava, always full-bodied, unifies everything within himself.
This nondual fullness has been established previously.
Given that establishment, the earlier question loses its basis.
mv-k05-v682.inference: Once nondual fullness is established, the objection about word-meaning separation cannot arise.

mv-k05-v683.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v683.question: Does the primacy of perceptual awareness extend beyond ordinary perception to other means of knowing?
premises: The argument extends to comparison and other means of knowing.
In all these cases, what appears is clearly of the form of awareness-perception.
This perceptual form of awareness shines forth everywhere.
mv-k05-v683.inference: All valid means of knowing ultimately manifest as forms of perceptual awareness.

mv-k05-v684.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v684.question: How does a blind person experience clear cognition without visual perception?
premises: Even a blind person perceives each respective form through touch, sound, and other senses.
That person cognizes a clarity of such a kind.
The clarity is genuine even without visual input.
mv-k05-v684.inference: Clear perceptual awareness does not depend exclusively on vision but arises through available modes of cognition.

mv-k05-v685.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v685.question: Do those congenitally deaf also attain clear cognition of things?
premises: Those congenitally deaf apprehend aspects of things through form, touch, and other senses.
They apprehend these aspects clearly.
For them, cognition is never entirely unknown in any respect.
mv-k05-v685.inference: Clear cognition of objects is available through non-auditory senses as well.
uncertainties: jātijaḍā is read as congenitally deaf or congenitally dull; the sensory examples favor deaf.

mv-k05-v686.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v686.question: Can a congenitally blind person form a vivid appreciative cognition of beauty?
premises: A congenitally blind person touches a woman's limbs.
From that touch he forms an appreciative cognition expressed as a lake of beauty and a shoot of the garden of youth.
He is pleased by that cognition.
mv-k05-v686.inference: Vivid and affectively charged cognition can arise through non-visual sensory experience.

mv-k05-v687.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v687.question: How can a deaf person appreciate a song as ornamented?
premises: A deaf person sees the singer's face.
From that visual perception alone, he concludes that the singing is ornamented.
He is satisfied by that cognition.
mv-k05-v687.inference: Aesthetic appreciation can arise from cross-modal cues even when the primary sense is absent.

mv-k05-v688.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k05-v688.question: What follows from establishing perception as the sole unrivaled means of knowing?
premises: Perception alone expands without rival.
This has been shown through the preceding examples.
