mv-k06-v841.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v841.question: Why is the manifold emanation rightly grounded in will?
premises: The universal emanation is indeed of will.
That emanation is established in many ways.
Therefore its having its own place is fitting.
mv-k06-v841.inference: Because universal emanation proceeds from will, its manifold placement is coherent and justified.

mv-k06-v842.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v842.question: What is the womb-like resting state of the living being identified with?
premises: The living being has a womb-like resting state.
That same state is the power of the supreme god.
This identification is explained here.
mv-k06-v842.inference: The womb-like resting state of the individual is the supreme god's own power.

mv-k06-v843.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v843.question: How are the inner principles mapped onto the phonetic classes?
premises: The inner principles are located there by the sequence of speech levels.
In the a-class is the śiva principle.
In the group from ka to ha is the range extending up to śiva.
mv-k06-v843.inference: The phonetic classes encode a graded deployment of principles from śiva through the full consonantal range.
uncertainties: The exact scope of śivāntakam in this mapping is compressed.

mv-k06-v844.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v844.question: What follows if the goddess-consciousness is clearly full and unlimited?
premises: The meaning of the thirty has been explained as an enclosing union.
The goddess-consciousness may be understood as full and unlimited.
This understanding is presented as a clear condition.
mv-k06-v844.inference: If goddess-consciousness is clearly full and unlimited, the enclosing structure of the thirty is fully intelligible.
uncertainties: The referent of triṃśaka is not specified in this verse.

mv-k06-v845.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v845.question: What vision corresponds to the full and unlimited goddess-consciousness?
premises: If consciousness is full and unlimited, all would be in her and she would be everywhere.
One who sees the divine everywhere sees all in the divine.
This reciprocal vision expresses non-separation.
mv-k06-v845.inference: Full goddess-consciousness entails a reciprocal vision in which all is in her and she is in all.

mv-k06-v846.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v846.question: What assurance is given to one who sees the divine in all?
premises: One who sees the divine everywhere and all in the divine is established in non-separation.
To such a one the divine declares non-loss and mutual belonging.
This teaching is cited by the sage through the words of teacher Arjuna in various places.
mv-k06-v846.inference: The reciprocal vision of non-separation guarantees mutual non-loss between the divine and the seer.
uncertainties: The exact source context of the cited words of teacher Arjuna is not specified here.

mv-k06-v847.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v847.question: What would happen if consciousness were cut off from all things?
premises: Consciousness is by nature awareness itself
If consciousness were cut off from all things it would become a mere object
A mere object would be like a pot defined only by its own mark
mv-k06-v847.inference: Consciousness cannot be cut off from all things without ceasing to be consciousness.

mv-k06-v848.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v848.question: What follows if consciousness is sought to be cut off?
premises: Cutting consciousness off from things means loss of its nature as consciousness
If consciousness loses its nature as consciousness it perishes
Consciousness flees away if one tries to divide it
mv-k06-v848.inference: Any attempt to cut consciousness off destroys consciousness itself.

mv-k06-v849.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v849.question: Why does the ordinary person not see all things in the divine?
premises: All things are declared to exist in the divine
The ordinary person does not see all things in the divine
This is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head
mv-k06-v849.inference: The ordinary person fails to see all in the divine because it is inseparably close, like one's own shadow.

mv-k06-v850.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v850.question: Why is the ordinary person established in the divine yet unaware of it?
premises: The ordinary person abides in the midst of all and is established in the divine
He is not grounded in the light of awareness
He treats the divine presence as if it were unreal
mv-k06-v850.inference: Being established in the divine does not guarantee recognition when one lacks grounding in light.

mv-k06-v851.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v851.question: What did the sage declare by following both paths?
premises: The sage declared destruction by both paths of reasoning
This is the order of reality described so far
This order is called the enclosure or mutual containment
mv-k06-v851.inference: The sage's twofold teaching establishes the principle of mutual enclosure as the order of reality.

mv-k06-v852.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v852.question: How does consciousness relate to the seat containing all paths?
premises: From that very enclosure arises the seat containing all paths
Consciousness attains the state of being supported in that abode
Consciousness again attains the state of being the support
mv-k06-v852.inference: Consciousness alternately appears as supported and as support within the seat of all paths.

mv-k06-v853.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v853.question: Why does the sage speak again of the seat in this context?
premises: The seat was already spoken of in the supreme worship
Here the sage speaks again for those wishing to enter
He does so according to the order of cognition
mv-k06-v853.inference: The sage restates the teaching of the seat to guide aspirants according to their cognitive progression.
uncertainties: The spacing marker \hspace{3cm} is editorial and not a lexical token.

mv-k06-v854.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v854.question: Why does the Lord declare the universe to be nothing other than himself?
premises: The Lord has spoken that the universe is not otherwise than himself
The freedom of undivided consciousness shines forth on the path of difference
What appears as difference is the expression of that same freedom
mv-k06-v854.inference: The universe is identical with the Lord because undivided consciousness freely appears as difference.

mv-k06-v855.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v855.question: How is the distinction between teacher and taught established?
premises: The arrangement of taught and teacher is extended on the path of difference
One's own self is regarded as the teacher
That same self is regarded as the supreme god
mv-k06-v855.inference: The roles of teacher and taught are projections of the one self appearing as distinct.

mv-k06-v856.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v856.question: How does the self misrecognize its own expressions in the state of difference?
premises: One considers self-uttered statements as spoken by another
The thing to be taught and the means by which it is taught appear distinct
These distinctions arise within the same self
mv-k06-v856.inference: In the differentiated state, the self attributes its own expressions and teachings to an other.

mv-k06-v857.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v857.question: How is the differentiated teaching comparable to a dream?
premises: All of this is in reality of the nature of the self
Yet one regards it only through difference
This is like experiencing a lineage of instruction in a dream state
mv-k06-v857.inference: Differentiated teaching is a self-created appearance, analogous to instruction occurring within a dream.

mv-k06-v858.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v858.question: How is waking experience similar to a dream experience?
premises: In a dream a dull creature hears and takes what is self-produced as spoken by another
The entire waking world of ordinary activity is contained within waking consciousness
The same misattribution occurs in waking as in dream
mv-k06-v858.inference: Waking conventional activity is structurally analogous to dream, since both involve taking the self's display as other.

mv-k06-v859.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v859.question: What difference remains between dream and waking on this view?
premises: An objection asks what difference there would then be between dream and waking
The answer will be given later
Alternatively, for the free Lord nothing is impossible to express
mv-k06-v859.inference: The apparent objection does not limit the free Lord, whose expression can encompass both dream and waking.

mv-k06-v860.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v860.question: What is the real basis of the distinction between injunction and restatement?
premises: The difference between injunction and restatement arises only by the order of cognition
One may say all is God or God is all
In reality these are one and the same
mv-k06-v860.inference: Injunction and restatement differ only in cognitive sequence, not in the underlying reality.

mv-k06-v861.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v861.question: How did Narayana express the identity of God and the universe?
premises: In reality the universe is like jar and pot, a matter of mere synonymy
The difference is only in what is to be expressed
Glorious Narayana declared to them 'you indeed are that'
mv-k06-v861.inference: The scriptural identity statement rests on the real non-difference of God and the universe.

mv-k06-v862.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v862.question: How can injunction and restatement operate if there is no difference?
premises: An objection asks how injunction and restatement are possible in non-difference
The example given is 'this toothy one is Caitra'
In that example the toothy one is first restated
mv-k06-v862.inference: The objection challenges whether logical roles of restatement and injunction can arise without real difference.

mv-k06-v863.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v863.question: What absurdity follows if restatement and injunction imply real difference?
premises: If after restating the toothy one the part 'Caitra' is enjoined as different

And Caitra would be other than the toothy one
mv-k06-v863.inference: Treating injunction and restatement as requiring real difference leads to an impossible split of one referent.

mv-k06-v864.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v864.question: What is the correct relation between the restated and enjoined terms?
premises: A case like 'the pot is Caitra' would not count as injunction and restatement
Injunction and restatement require identity of referent
Therefore the one who is Caitra is the same as the toothy one
mv-k06-v864.inference: Injunction and restatement operate on one and the same referent, not on different entities.

mv-k06-v865.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v865.question: When are injunction and restatement legitimately used?
premises: The distinction of injunction and restatement is real in use but arises only from cognition
It is employed for those who do not yet know synonymous terms
Examples include tree and earth-grower, jar and pot, and the statement that the Great Lord is all this world
mv-k06-v865.inference: Injunction and restatement serve to reveal identity to those who have not yet recognized synonymous expressions of the same reality.

mv-k06-v866.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v866.question: What is the nature of the state established by the union of enclosure?
premises: By the union of enclosure a certain state is established
That state is perfectly full
Within it stand hundreds of phases of dissolution and creation
mv-k06-v866.inference: The state of mutual enclosure is a plenitude that internally contains countless cycles of creation and dissolution.

mv-k06-v867.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v867.question: How do some practitioners approach that plenary state?
premises: Some are minded to worship that plenary state part by part

These divisions are modes of engaging the same state
mv-k06-v867.inference: Practitioners approach the one plenary consciousness through graduated numerical differentiations.

mv-k06-v868.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v868.question: How is the one consciousness differentiated into multiple forms?
premises: Consciousness is divided by various sequences into wheels of consciousness
The one consciousness becomes twofold as knowing and acting
That same consciousness then becomes threefold
mv-k06-v868.inference: The divisions of practice are structured unfoldings of the one consciousness into functional modes.

mv-k06-v869.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v869.question: How do the fourfold and fivefold divisions of consciousness arise?
premises: With the assistance of the unfolding power consciousness is also spoken of as fourfold
Through ascent in the bliss of the power of consciousness it is declared fivefold
These are further articulations of the same consciousness
mv-k06-v869.inference: The fourfold and fivefold forms arise from the same consciousness through unfolding and blissful ascent.

mv-k06-v870.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v870.question: How far do the numerical differentiations of consciousness extend?
premises: Consciousness is contemplated as sixfold through the worship taught as the six vowels
It extends up to a twelvefold form
These forms apply in the creation of consciousness and in domains of equal scope
mv-k06-v870.inference: The one consciousness unfolds into multiple ordered forms, from sixfold to twelvefold, within the same field of manifestation.

mv-k06-v871.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v871.question: How does consciousness conceive emanation and attain redness?
premises: Consciousness can conceive emanation one by one through a threefold nature.
Consciousness can also conceive emanation in the triad through a fourfold nature.
In that process consciousness attains the state called redness.
mv-k06-v871.inference: Consciousness generates emanation through structured multiplicities and thereby enters the colored phase of manifestation.
uncertainties: The exact referents of the triad and fourfold nature are not specified in this verse.

mv-k06-v872.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v872.question: What happens when consciousness conceives maintenance and dissolution?
premises: Consciousness conceives maintenance and dissolution.
In some cases it may produce doubt.
That doubt and the portion of being are withdrawn again from the withdrawal of its own self.
mv-k06-v872.inference: The phases of maintenance and dissolution include the arising and retraction of doubt within consciousness itself.

mv-k06-v873.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v873.question: How does consciousness act when reflecting on its role as withdrawer?
premises: Consciousness reflects on its own withdrawer-hood.

By its own freedom it does not desire either a quick resolution or suppression.
mv-k06-v873.inference: As withdrawer, consciousness freely refrains from hastily resolving or suppressing merit and demerit.
uncertainties: The precise scope of drutaṃ is context-dependent and could qualify resolution rather than action in general.

mv-k06-v874.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v874.question: What does consciousness withdraw in this phase of reabsorption?
premises: Consciousness devours the wheel of rays consisting of faculties and parts of awareness.

mv-k06-v875.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v875.question: Where is the constructed measure-part withdrawn after the previous reabsorption?
premises: After withdrawing the previous elements, consciousness withdraws the constructed measure-part.

Even what is beyond all is taken within the unlimited abode.
mv-k06-v875.inference: The process of withdrawal culminates by dissolving constructed measure into an unconstructed and unlimited inner ground.
uncertainties: The subject carrying out the withdrawal remains implicit as consciousness.

mv-k06-v876.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v876.question: How should the universe be led and re-emanated in this practice?
premises: That totality should be led through the door of the eye.
The universe should be led in that same way to the stated extent.
Then emanation should be conceived again by such sequential practice.
mv-k06-v876.inference: The contemplative method alternates between leading the universe inward and conceiving its emanation again in ordered sequence.

mv-k06-v877.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v877.question: What is the nature of the twelve-spoked wheel described here?

mv-k06-v878.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v878.question: How does this wheel expand across different orders of manifestation?

It expands through various orders while devouring object, measure, and subject.
mv-k06-v878.inference: The same wheel unfolds in multiple ordered and nonordered configurations and encompasses all poles of cognition.

mv-k06-v879.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v879.question: Can the divisions of this wheel ever be counted?
premises: This wheel contains endless rays and spokes.
The divisions of the wheel depend on that endless structure.
What depends on an endless structure cannot be fully enumerated.
mv-k06-v879.inference: The divisions of the wheel are uncountable because they arise from an endless array within it.

mv-k06-v880.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v880.question: What analogy illustrates the wheel's shifting appearances?

They shine even though they are not ultimately of that fixed nature.

mv-k06-v881.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v881.question: How does the lord of the wheel appear in relation to subtle consciousness?
premises: The lord of the wheel is full of subtle consciousness that is unopened and dissolved.
He shines in a manner comparable to the peacock-feather analogy.
His appearance is variegated by activities of closing and opening.
mv-k06-v881.inference: The lord of the wheel manifests diverse activities while remaining grounded in subtle, unmanifest consciousness.

mv-k06-v882.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v882.question: What causes the wheel to vary from one spoke to a thousand spokes?
premises: The wheel's manifestation is linked to closing and opening.
For some it turns through closing and for others through opening.
This variation ranges from a one-spoked wheel to a thousand-spoked wheel.
mv-k06-v882.inference: The wheel's manifold configurations arise from differing dynamics of closing and opening.

mv-k06-v883.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v883.question: Is that wheel innumerable, mutually nested, or simply one space expanding?
premises: The wheel may be conceived as innumerable.
The wheel may be conceived as mutually nested within itself.
The wheel may be conceived as not a wheel but as one expanding space.
mv-k06-v883.inference: The nature of the wheel admits multiple alternative descriptions of its structure and unity.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'that wheel' depends on the preceding verses.

mv-k06-v884.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v884.question: How does that space manifest in relation to infinite wheels and spaces?
premises: That reality may shine forth as containing infinite true wheels.
That reality may shine forth as containing infinite spaces.
That reality may be called one great space.
mv-k06-v884.inference: The same reality can be described as containing infinite wheels, containing infinite spaces, or as one great space.

mv-k06-v885.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v885.question: How does the consciousness principle manifest its many forms without losing unity?
premises: One space gleams as white, blue, and red without ceasing to be one space.
Clouds appear in many ways while arising in that same space.
The autonomous consciousness principle vibrates forth in its own forms beyond construction and enumeration, yet those forms are not anything separate from it.
mv-k06-v885.inference: Multiplicity of appearance does not compromise the unity and autonomy of the consciousness principle.

mv-k06-v886.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v886.question: How was this principle of varied form transmitted to the speaker?
premises: The speaker's lord, seated in the heart, himself realized this principle.
That lord described this principle of varied form.
The teaching came through the successive lineage of teachers.
mv-k06-v886.inference: The doctrine of the varied yet non-separate principle is grounded in direct realization and transmitted through the guru lineage.

mv-k06-v887.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v887.question: Why did the Lord teach the construction of various maṇḍalas?
premises: Some people do not have the capacity to attain firm grounding in that doctrine.
The Lord intends to awaken those people.
The Lord therefore taught various constructions of maṇḍalas.
mv-k06-v887.inference: The maṇḍala teachings are a pedagogical means for those unable to grasp the doctrine directly.

mv-k06-v888.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v888.question: How do mudrās, maṇḍalas, mantras, and tantras function as teaching aids?
premises: A child is trained in letters by lines and conventional signs in sequence.
Similarly, a practitioner is engaged through mudrās, maṇḍalas, mantras, and tantras.
This engagement leads into one's own full and priceless abode.
mv-k06-v888.inference: Ritual and scriptural forms are sequential pedagogical devices guiding one to the full inner reality.

mv-k06-v889.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v889.question: Why does ritual teaching present divisions of near and far if reality is partless?
premises: In this domain something shines forth by that will alone as far or near, according to the gradation of those who resort to it.
That reality remains untouched and established in a partless state.
Thus the division found in the section on ritual action appears in many ways.
mv-k06-v889.inference: Ritual divisions reflect the gradation of practitioners, not a division in the partless reality itself.

mv-k06-v890.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v890.question: What is the goddess who shines forth as the described principle?
premises: The principle that was described participates in valid cognition.
That principle is the goddess who is both supreme and non-supreme.
She shines forth in various ways.
mv-k06-v890.inference: The supreme-and-non-supreme goddess is the manifest form of the principle established by valid cognition.

mv-k06-v891.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v891.question: How are the supreme, knower, and known aspects distinguished within this reality?
premises: Within this same reality there is a supreme part.
There is also a knower part and a known part.
This division was previously made clear by us.
mv-k06-v891.inference: The one reality is articulated into supreme, knower, and known aspects as previously explained.

mv-k06-v892.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v892.question: What form does the knower aspect take when situated in the supreme part?
premises: The knower part is situated in many ways within the supreme part.
Because of that situation, it becomes predominant as both supreme and non-supreme.
In that state it takes the form of a lord of mantras.
mv-k06-v892.inference: When the knower aspect abides in the supreme, it manifests as the mantreśa level characterized by the supreme-and-non-supreme.

mv-k06-v893.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v893.question: How are the mantra and balanced knower levels distinguished by predominance?
premises: When the lower aspect predominates, that level is called mantra.
There is also a knower who is characterized as supreme-and-non-supreme.
In that knower the supreme-and-non-supreme aspects are balanced in predominance.
mv-k06-v893.inference: The mantra level is marked by predominance of the lower aspect, while another knower level is marked by a balanced supreme-and-non-supreme state.

mv-k06-v894.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v894.question: How do vijñānākala and pralayākala arise from the same knower?
premises: The balanced supreme-and-non-supreme knower is declared vijñānākala.
That vijñānākala has an awakened supreme aspect.
Through predominance of the lower aspect, that same knower is pralayākala.
mv-k06-v894.inference: Vijñānākala and pralayākala are two states of the same knower distinguished by the relative predominance of supreme and lower aspects.

mv-k06-v895.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v895.question: How is the lower knower called sakala further divided into multiple states?
premises: The lower knower is called sakala.
This sakala knower is distinguished by divisions such as higher-lower and so on.
Even this sakala knower has a manifold state.
mv-k06-v895.inference: Therefore the sakala, though defined as the lower knower, is itself internally differentiated into many modes.

mv-k06-v896.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v896.question: How many divisions of the knower are recognized when examined in detail versus in principal classification?
premises: When examined, the state of the knower extends into countless divisions of knowers.
A principal classification is also possible.
In that principal classification, seven divisions of knowers are proclaimed.
mv-k06-v896.inference: Therefore the divisions of the knower are innumerable in analysis but are taught as seven in their chief forms.

mv-k06-v897.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v897.question: What is the status of the knowers' own powers in relation to the means of knowledge?
premises: The knowers' own powers fall within the domain of the means of knowledge.
Power is understood as fitness for activity.
This fitness for activity belongs to those powers.
mv-k06-v897.inference: Therefore the powers of the knowers function as the means of knowledge because their essence is the capacity to act.

mv-k06-v898.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v898.question: How does being active establish instrumentality and the divisions of knower and means of knowledge?
premises: Being in an active state is the same as being an instrument.
Distinctions arise between the possessor of power and the powers.
From these distinctions arise the divisions of knower and means of knowledge.
mv-k06-v898.inference: Therefore instrumentality is grounded in activity, and from the differentiation of power and its possessor the knower-means structure emerges.
uncertainties: The final compound śaktimacchakktibhedān contains internal sandhi; analyzed as a fused form without splitting the token.

mv-k06-v899.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v899.question: Why is the object of knowledge said to have a fourteen-fold nature?
premises: The object of knowledge is said to have a fourteen-fold nature.
Knower, means of knowing, and object of knowing are distinguished.
These three are proclaimed as one underlying reality.
mv-k06-v899.inference: Therefore the fourteen-fold object of knowledge is taught within a framework where knower, means, and object are ultimately one.
uncertainties: The derivation of the number fourteen is not explicit in this verse alone.

mv-k06-v900.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k06-v900.question: How does the one reality become a fifteen-fold structure when differentiated by its own principles?
premises: From the preceding account, the one reality is described as fifteen-fold.
That one reality is grouped in fives together with prakṛti.
When differentiated one by one, each division takes the form of its own principle.
mv-k06-v900.inference: Therefore the single reality unfolds into a fifteen-fold structure through fivefold grouping and further differentiation into its own tattvas.
uncertainties: The exact referent of the fivefold grouping with prakṛti is not fully specified in this verse alone.

mv-k07-v901.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v901.question: By what order is the infinity of difference now to be reckoned?
premises: The endlessness of difference has been set forth concisely and at length.
What follows is its sequential reckoning beginning with the water-principle.
The marker moreover signals a new movement from exposition to enumeration.
mv-k07-v901.inference: The verse closes the bheda-infinity exposition and opens the ordered reckoning of divisions from water upward.
uncertainties: Scope of root-to-end left open between tattva series and adhvan stations.
Why water rather than earth opens the series, earth perhaps treated in the preceding kanda.

mv-k07-v902.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v902.question: What is taught as fifteenfold, and how does the sakala stand within it?
premises: Manifold is the upsurge of variety sprung from difference and its subdivisions.
From earth to the end of the pradhāna-principle the course has been taught fifteenfold.
The sakala, whose very nature spans puruṣa to kalā, is neither true knower nor means of knowledge.
mv-k07-v902.inference: The fifteenfold lower course is enumerated, and the bound souls knowerhood within it is refused at the supreme level.
uncertainties: Whether the opening line closes the preceding movement or opens this verse.
The precise level at which the sakala knowerhood is refused.

mv-k07-v903.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v903.question: Where does each bound-soul class hold its own nature?
premises: The thirteenfold nature is therefore established here as the frame.
In the night-state the layākala keeps his own nature.
In the middle stands the vijñānākala-nature, and in the vidyā-domain the mantra-become-nature.
mv-k07-v903.inference: The soul-classes are stationed across night, middle, and vidyā-domain stations.
uncertainties: The thirteenfold count left unanalyzed, ten senses plus three inner organs presumed.
The optative-like bhavel read as would-be against a possible print slip.

mv-k07-v904.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v904.question: How does the Śiva-state flash forth, and whence the numbered divisions?
premises: In the Īśa domain the Mantreśa class abides, and in the most auspicious abode stands devotion to that Lord.
Each prior stage therein discloses its own knower-measure order, so that with no other knower the ever-one self-luminous Śiva-state flashes forth.
From the Mantreśa-Īśas however come divisions by number: three, five, seven, nine, three.
mv-k07-v904.inference: The one self-luminous Śiva-state emerges through the ordered knower-system, then differentiates into numbered Mantreśa groups.
uncertainties: Exact syntactic joints of the long compounds left open.
The referents of the 3-5-7-9-3 counts read as group-numbers, specific groups unidentified.

mv-k07-v905.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v905.question: Why does the separateness of śakti from its holder not amount to difference?
premises: Śakti is indeed undivided from the power-holder.
Thereby this separateness does not indeed amount to difference.
Where knowerhood is absent no śakti exists, so such a nature is not power-endowed.
mv-k07-v905.inference: Śakti, knower, and power-holder entail one another, so their separateness is not difference.
uncertainties: The segmentation of tenaiti as tena-plus-eti against tena-plus-iti.
The exact scope of our in ca no.

mv-k07-v906.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v906.question: How is the light that shines as earth itself Lord Śiva?
premises: Whatever light shines without difference from the earth-principle is in question.
That very light is Lord Śiva here.
For earth is brahman, the supreme.
mv-k07-v906.inference: The earth-principle is sealed as non-different from Śiva: earth is the supreme Absolute.
uncertainties: The gender crossing in earth-is-brahman left as predicate-noun usage.
Whether here scopes the whole seal or the Śiva-identity alone.

mv-k07-v907.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v907.question: Who are the Mantramaheśvaras?
premises: Certain ones impel, from Śivas will, those intent on granting earth-principle powers.
Those impellers are named by the correlative: they are the Mantramaheśvaras.
mv-k07-v907.inference: Mantramaheśvaras are those who, by Śivas will, move the bestowers of earthly powers.
uncertainties: Whether the intent ones are deities or yogins left open.
The exact scope of earth-principle powers.

mv-k07-v908.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v908.question: What do the impelled Mantreśas and their mantras do?
premises: The Mantreśas stand impelled by the higher lords.
Their mantras plainly speak that yoga.
They have cultivated earth-abiding yoga through the Śiva-science.
mv-k07-v908.inference: Impelled Mantreśas proclaim and practice the earth-yoga by Śiva-knowledge.
uncertainties: The antecedent of thereof carried from the preceding verse.

mv-k07-v909.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v909.question: How do the dualist philosophers fall short?
premises: They rank with the Pāśava, Sāṃkhya, Vaiṣṇava and kindred dualists.
They have never attained the firm abode.
They possess vijñānākala-nature only.
mv-k07-v909.inference: Dualist schools rank as vijñānākalas who miss the firm abode.
uncertainties: The implied subject carried from context.
The firm abode read as the Śiva-state, presumed.

mv-k07-v910.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v910.question: Who are the pralayakevalas?
premises: They enjoyed just such principles and reached dissolution at the kalpas end.
They abide as in deep sleep.
They are here called pralayakevalas.
mv-k07-v910.inference: Kalpa-end dissolvers resting in sleep-like abeyance are the pralayakevalas.
uncertainties: The scope of just-such left to context.
Whether the sleep simile marks state or simile only.

mv-k07-v911.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v911.question: How is the dissolution of principles in deep sleep established?
premises: In deep sleep the dissolvedness in the principles is plainly observed.
Otherwise whence this fixed conjunction with dreaming.
mv-k07-v911.inference: Observed dissolution plus the dream-return argument establish tattva-dissolution in sleep.
uncertainties: The exact dream-mechanics behind the otherwise-argument left implicit.

mv-k07-v912.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v912.question: How is deep sleep itself shown to be variegated?
premises: Deep sleep too shines forth as varied, pure and impure and the rest.
This follows from observing variety in such memories as I-did-not-sleep and happily.
mv-k07-v912.inference: Memory-variety proves deep sleep variegated, pure and impure.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of the negative memory report left open.
Whether pure-impure grades states or recollections.

mv-k07-v913.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v913.question: Who are to be known here as sakalas?
premises: Persons carry massed malas mixed with the māyā-karma upsurge.
They climb upon the earth-principle.
mv-k07-v913.inference: Earth-climbing souls with māyā-karma-mixed malas are the sakalas.
uncertainties: Exact force of climbing-upon left open between ascent and station.

mv-k07-v914.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v914.question: What is called the seven of the śaktis?
premises: Within just this sevenfold order each ones own task is settled.
Whatever agitation attends that settling is called the śakti-seven.
mv-k07-v914.inference: The śakti-seven is the agitation in settling the sevenfold task-order.
uncertainties: The sevenfold group left to context, soul-classes presumed.

mv-k07-v915.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v915.question: How do Śivas three śaktis take subject-object form?
premises: Śiva himself is of unfallen consciousness-nature.
His three śaktis are in question.
They have assumed subject-and-object form by force of autonomy.
mv-k07-v915.inference: Autonomy turns the three śaktis into the subject-object polarity while Śiva stays unfallen.
uncertainties: The three unnamed here, will knowledge and action presumed.
Exact joint of assumed within the long compound.

mv-k07-v916.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v916.question: How is the one inert human thing settled amid seven and seven?
premises: By excess of the subject-share and upsurge of the object-share come seven and seven.
Yet it is one thing, merely inert, human-natured.
mv-k07-v916.inference: The seven-and-seven reduce to one inert human nature, settled threefold per tattva with the next verse.
uncertainties: Correlative closed with the next verse.

mv-k07-v917.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v917.question: How is the one nature settled, and what are moments in the ungraspable?
premises: Its nature is therefore settled threefold per tattva.
In the ungraspable object the verse asks what, and answers: the sixteen tuṭis are moments.
mv-k07-v917.inference: The one nature stands threefold per tattva, and tuṭi-time is fixed at sixteen moments in the ungraspable.
uncertainties: The threefold referents presumed subject-object polarities.

mv-k07-v918.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v918.question: How are the moments reckoned, and what is the first?
premises: They are severally reckoned from the two-and-a-quarter-finger entrance.
Therein the first is of the very taste of partless supreme nondualism.
mv-k07-v918.inference: Moment-reckoning starts from the finger-measure, and the first moment tastes partless nondualism.
uncertainties: The finger-measure physiology left unanalyzed, prāṇa-course presumed.
The they-subject carried from the preceding moments.

mv-k07-v919.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v919.question: How are the last and penultimate moments conceived?
premises: The last is not distinctly conceived apart from object-nature identity.
The penultimate is fully conceived as grasper of its nature.
mv-k07-v919.inference: The last moment merges with the object while the penultimate holds the grasper.
uncertainties: Exact nuance of fully against distinctly.

mv-k07-v920.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v920.question: What is the first seven that has gone imageless?
premises: There the first seven has gone to imagelessness.
It is skilled in covering the shade of sequentially unfolding thought-portions.
mv-k07-v920.inference: The first seven, imageless, covers the shadow of unfolding vikalpa.
uncertainties: The mechanism of shade-covering left unanalyzed.

mv-k07-v921.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v921.question: What do the wise know as Śiva-nature, and what is the second seven?
premises: The wise know that very nature as Śiva consisting of supreme śakti.
The second seven therein consists of the mixed plane.
mv-k07-v921.inference: Śiva-nature is supreme-śakti while the second seven is the parāpara plane.
uncertainties: The planes mapped to stations left open.
The knower-subject of the wise left generic.

mv-k07-v922.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v922.question: How is difference made to appear?
premises: What is sung as vikalpa — thus difference is made to appear.
For that, in this subtle consciousness, they are intent on impelling.
mv-k07-v922.inference: Named vikalpa, difference appears through the intent impelling within subtle consciousness.

mv-k07-v923.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v923.question: What form do they experience, and what is held of the tuṭis?
premises: Whatever form they experience — what is the point of boastings about it.
But what is held: even the tuṭis in the lessening of difference that comes from sequence.
mv-k07-v923.inference: Experience outruns boasting while the held view dissolves even tuṭis as difference lessens.
uncertainties: Elliptical syntax with the boastings-target unclear.
Exact construction of the held-view clause.

mv-k07-v924.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v924.question: How does diminution of conceptualization become characterized?
premises: diminution of conceptualization is characterized by absence of conceptualization
one afflicted by long suffering later attains happiness
the comparison illustrates conceptual diminution
mv-k07-v924.inference: conceptual diminution is recognized by the absence of conceptualization, like relief after prolonged suffering

mv-k07-v925.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v925.question: How do people behave when established in awareness beyond conceptualization?
premises: One who attains happiness forgets earlier suffering through resting in happiness.
Likewise, people established in awareness beyond conceptualization do not dwell on conceptual thought.
mv-k07-v925.inference: Absorption in non-conceptual awareness naturally displaces conceptual activity, just as present happiness displaces past suffering.

mv-k07-v926.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v926.question: What happens when conceptualization dissolves and one attends to that state?
premises: Those resting on the strength of conceptualization do not claim the non-conceptual state.
Through the dissolution of conceptualization, awareness becomes barren of thought and true in the ultimate sense.
In that condition the manifestness of awareness's own nature is attained.
mv-k07-v926.inference: For those who strive with attention, the fading of conceptualization reveals the ultimately true, self-manifest nature of awareness.

mv-k07-v927.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v927.question: What is meant by attentiveness in the relation of grasper and grasped?
premises: There is a relation between the grasped, the grasper, and their awareness.
Attentiveness can be directed within that relation.
Such attentiveness is defined by its connection with the desired result.
mv-k07-v927.inference: Attentiveness in the grasper-grasped relation is the focused awareness that brings about the intended fruit.

mv-k07-v928.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v928.question: Why do the worlds display such manifold diversity?
premises: The divisions within that awareness are abundant.
The worlds attain variegation from this abundance of divisions.
No transgression of this explanatory principle is accepted.
mv-k07-v928.inference: The diversity of worlds is explained by the multiplicity of divisions within awareness, without invoking any other principle.

mv-k07-v929.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v929.question: Can time and space be established as ultimately real principles?
premises: Reality appears as both sequential and non-sequential.
Time has already been refuted as an independent principle.
Space likewise cannot be established as ultimately real by reasoning.
mv-k07-v929.inference: Neither time nor space has ultimate reality; their apparent status does not withstand rational examination.

mv-k07-v930.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v930.question: What could produce the cognition of before and after if no single real principle does so?
premises: No single entity produces the cognition of before and after.
Difference due to limiting conditions is not itself an independently real thing.
A cognition of sequence cannot be grounded in what is not ultimately real.
mv-k07-v930.inference: The cognition of before and after cannot be validly postulated as arising from an ultimately real time or from mere adjuncts.

mv-k07-v931.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v931.question: How does the supreme Lord relate to distinctions of superiority and to space and time?
premises: Relative superiority is expressed in terms of qualities.
The supreme Lord declared the principle behind such distinctions.
The sphere of space and time is fashioned by the Lord's own bliss.
mv-k07-v931.inference: Distinctions of quality and the frameworks of space and time arise within the supreme Lord's own blissful manifestation.

mv-k07-v932.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v932.question: Why are absorptions described as threefold in this variegated reality?
premises: The nature of reality is variegated.
Practitioners seek to enter into that reality.
The means of entry differ.
mv-k07-v932.inference: Because the means differ for those entering this variegated reality, absorptions are described as threefold.

mv-k07-v933.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v933.question: What are the three means of absorption and how is the third classified?
premises: The Śāmbhava means is described as methodless.
The next means is based on consciousness.
The Āṇava means is based on the inert and is regarded as manifold.
mv-k07-v933.inference: The three means are Śāmbhava, Śākta or consciousness-based, and Āṇava, with the Āṇava admitting many subdivisions.
uncertainties: The text gives cidupāya rather than the explicit name śākta, though the identification is standard in this context.

mv-k07-v934.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v934.question: How can a consciousness-based means operate through apparently inert supports?
premises: Even in the non-inert, an appearance of inertness can arise.
This appearance arises through the power of supreme lordship.
Channels, senses, and external supports can serve as loci for that appearance.
mv-k07-v934.inference: Because inert-seeming supports appear within consciousness by the Lord's power, they can function as instruments of the consciousness-based means.

mv-k07-v935.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v935.question: What characterizes the waking state in terms of sense activity?
premises: Sense functioning can be taken as the basis of experience.
On that basis there is apprehension of external forms.
This apprehension is clear, present, and repeatedly continuous.
mv-k07-v935.inference: The waking state is defined as the clear and repeatedly continuous apprehension of external forms through sense functioning.

mv-k07-v936.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v936.question: How is dream distinguished, and what kind of experience belongs to the layākala?
premises: Dream is a construction produced by one's own imagination.
Dream is the reverse of the waking state.
The layākala has experience under the force of karma tending toward dissolution.
mv-k07-v936.inference: Dream is internally constructed and opposed to waking, while the layākala's experience is determined by dissolving karma rather than stable manifestation.

mv-k07-v937.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v937.question: Why is the layākala's experience unstable, and what defines sleep for the jñānākala?
premises: The layākala's experience would not be stable because there is no night-like obscuration to fix it.
Deep sleep is marked by non-awareness of pleasure and other contents.
For the jñānākala, experience is limited by mere impurity and amounts only to bare experience.
mv-k07-v937.inference: Instability in the layākala comes from lack of obscuring fixation, while the jñānākala's sleep-like condition is defined by impurity and mere, contentless experience.

mv-k07-v938.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v938.question: Who abides in the fourth state amid differentiated inert and non-inert entities?
premises: Entities appear as differentiated, both inert and non-inert.
Such differentiation is treated as something made or intended.
In the fourth state, three groups abide: mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords.
mv-k07-v938.inference: Within the fourth state, differentiated manifestation is still present, and it is inhabited by the three hierarchic groups of mantra, mantra-lords, and mantra-overlords.

mv-k07-v939.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v939.question: When do differentiated entities become non-different?
premises: Entities can become capable of admitting a share of Bhairava-awareness.
When that happens, their separate essence melts away.
With the loss of separate essence, they become non-different.
mv-k07-v939.inference: Entities become non-different to the extent that they can receive Bhairava-awareness and their separate essence dissolves.

mv-k07-v940.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v940.question: How should the waking state be identified within the fifteenfold scheme?
premises: Entities capable of full non-difference would abide in the state beyond the fourth.
Within the fifteenfold scheme, each level has its own modes.
Whatever form is clear and distinct at a given level is to be regarded as waking.
mv-k07-v940.inference: In the fifteenfold analysis, the waking state is defined functionally as whichever form is most clear and manifest at that level.

mv-k07-v941.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v941.question: How are dream and deep sleep distinguished from waking in this scheme?
premises: The same form that is clear in waking may appear as unstable.
An unstable appearance of that form is dream.
An unclear appearance is deep sleep.
mv-k07-v941.inference: Waking, dream, and deep sleep are distinguished by degrees of clarity and stability in the appearance of the same underlying form.
uncertainties: The final clause 'tat puro 'pi yat' is compressed; its syntactic role is slightly unclear in isolation.

mv-k07-v942.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v942.question: What is the fourth state in relation to waking, dream, and deep sleep?
premises: Waking, dream, and deep sleep form a triad.
There is a continuity by whose power this triad is held together.
That continuity runs through all differences like a thread through a garland.
mv-k07-v942.inference: The fourth state is the unifying continuity that pervades and connects the three states across all differences.

mv-k07-v943.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v943.question: What distinguishes the state beyond the fourth from the fourth state?
premises: The fourth state unifies the triad of waking, dream, and deep sleep.
There is a further state shining with the fullness of nonduality.
That further state melts away all distinctions.
mv-k07-v943.inference: The state beyond the fourth is the plenary nondual radiance in which all distinctions are dissolved, and this schema should be applied universally.

mv-k07-v944.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v944.question: How should the four-state schema be applied to different levels such as the layākala?
premises: Each level has its own proper form.
What counts as waking, dream, and so on is relative to that level.
The wise should trace the full sequence in every case.
mv-k07-v944.inference: The four-state schema is relative and must be applied contextually, with each level's own form determining what counts as waking, dream, sleep, and beyond.

mv-k07-v945.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v945.question: How do the four states map onto the powers within the one supreme Lord?
premises: Even within the one full Lord, the states can be distinguished.
Consciousness corresponds to the state beyond the fourth.
Bliss corresponds to the fourth, will to the seed-like deep sleep, and further powers follow.
mv-k07-v945.inference: The four-state schema is mapped onto the Lord's powers, with cit as beyond the fourth, ānanda as the fourth, and icchā as the seed-ground of deep sleep.

mv-k07-v946.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v946.question: How do knowledge and action map onto dream and waking, and what further yogic designations arise here?
premises: Knowledge corresponds to the dream-functioning state.
Action corresponds to the waking state.
In this same framework arise yogic designations such as piṇḍastha and others.
mv-k07-v946.inference: The mapping of the Lord's powers to the four states extends to yogic stages, with jñāna as dream-like and kriyā as waking-like.

mv-k07-v947.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v947.question: Why do additional classifications like sarvatobhadra arise in the expanded scheme?
premises: Classifications such as sarvatobhadra are constructed by discriminative knowers.
In each individual case the fourfold structure is present.
When the scheme is expanded, further subdivisions arise from that fourfold presence.
mv-k07-v947.inference: Additional yogic classifications arise because the fourfold structure recurs in every case and is elaborated by reflective analysis.

mv-k07-v948.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v948.question: How do multiplicity and unity resolve in the supreme Bhairava?
premises: The scheme can be seen as fourfold in one locus.
It can then be seen as threefold and then as one.
Beyond these reductions stands the one Lord Bhairava, in whom all forms flash forth.
mv-k07-v948.inference: The progressive reduction from fourfold to threefold to one culminates in the one Bhairava, who contains and manifests all forms.

mv-k07-v949.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v949.question: How is the one reality related to the entire path from Śiva to the individual?
premises: There is one reality that pervades all levels from Śiva down to the individual.
This same reality constitutes the entire path.
The entire path abides in non-difference from Bhairava.
mv-k07-v949.inference: The one all-pervading reality is identical with the entire path and remains non-different from Bhairava.

mv-k07-v950.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v950.question: How does the one reality manifest as the path of mantras?
premises: The reality manifests by virtue of its own freedom.
In manifesting, it assumes autonomy.
When abiding in the nature of the knowing subject, it is recognized as the path of mantras.
mv-k07-v950.inference: Through its own freedom, the reality appears as autonomous and, in the subject's mode, is recognized as the mantra path.

mv-k07-v951.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v951.question: How does the same reality become the paths of phonemes and words?
premises: In the form of valid cognition, the reality is declared to be the path of phonemes.
When it assumes the form of the means of knowledge, it becomes the path of words.
mv-k07-v951.inference: The same reality appears as the phoneme path in the mode of cognition and as the word path in the mode of the cognitive instrument.

mv-k07-v952.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v952.question: How does the reality become the path of limited powers while still linked to the knower?
premises: The reality does not abandon its immersion in the form of the means of knowledge.
It moves toward objecthood through association with conceptualization.
In that state, joined with the knower, it is the path of limited powers.
mv-k07-v952.inference: Retaining its role as cognitive instrument while taking on objecthood through conceptualization, the reality becomes the kalā path in relation to the knower.

mv-k07-v953.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v953.question: When is the reality understood as the paths of principles and worlds?
premises: In a pure connection with objecthood, the reality is to be understood as the path of principles.
When connected with serving as the support of that grossness, it is described as the path of worlds.
mv-k07-v953.inference: The same reality appears as the tattva path in pure objecthood and as the bhuvana path when it supports gross manifestation.

mv-k07-v954.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v954.question: Under what condition does the expressible state become absorbed in conscious awareness?
premises: The state of the expressible can be swallowed by the reflective awareness of consciousness.
This occurs when that state is intent on cognition and protection dependent on Śiva's knowledge and action.
mv-k07-v954.inference: When oriented toward Śiva's powers of knowledge and action, the expressible state is absorbed into conscious reflective awareness.

mv-k07-v955.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v955.question: How does the Śiva-natured mantra path first arise?
premises: The reality possesses skill in the eager play of all its powers.
From that skill, the mantra path arises forcefully and quickly.
This first arising is of the nature of Śiva.
mv-k07-v955.inference: Through the playful skill of all its powers, the Śiva-natured mantra path arises first and swiftly.

mv-k07-v956.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v956.question: Why are the powers unrestricted for the one resting in pure consciousness?
premises: There is one whose relish is repose in surging consciousness alone.
That state has the capacity for all naming.
From that capacity, the powers are unrestricted.
mv-k07-v956.inference: Because pure conscious repose entails the capacity to name all, its powers operate without restriction.

mv-k07-v957.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v957.question: What range of objects do the emanated powers encompass within consciousness?
premises: Powers are emanated whose operations extend from self-coemergent meanings down to the earth.
These operations occur within the play of consciousness.
They encompass corresponding objects within their own self-nature.
mv-k07-v957.inference: The emanated powers span the full range of objects, from subtle self-arising meanings to gross earth, all within consciousness.

mv-k07-v958.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v958.question: Do beings without linguistic convention still possess real cognitive awareness?
premises: Infants and even animal knowers do not partake in linguistic convention.
They apprehend objects reflectively.
In doing so, they bear a real consciousness in the form of valid cognition.
mv-k07-v958.inference: Even without conventional language, infants and animals possess real cognitive awareness.

mv-k07-v959.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v959.question: How do pre-conventional beings attain varied subjecthood?
premises: Even pre-conventional beings possess their own consciousness.
This consciousness has an uncontrived formative essence and is both differentiated and undifferentiated.
Relying on this consciousness, they attain varied subjecthood.
mv-k07-v959.inference: By relying on their innate, both-differentiated-and-undifferentiated consciousness, pre-conventional beings attain varied forms of subjecthood.

mv-k07-v960.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v960.question: What happens when linguistic conventions become rooted in innate phonemic consciousness?
premises: There is an uncontrived consciousness of infinite phonemes.
Linguistic conventions can become firmly established in that consciousness.
When so established, those conventions attain a non-conventional mode of operation.
mv-k07-v960.inference: Conventions grounded in innate phonemic consciousness transcend mere conventionality in their operation.

mv-k07-v961.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v961.question: Why can linguistic conventions not find stable rest without innate consciousness?
premises: Many conventions can be made without this innate consciousness.
Such conventions depend on other conventions.
Dependence on further conventions prevents stable rest in the mind.
mv-k07-v961.inference: Without grounding in innate consciousness, conventions cannot achieve stable mental rest because they require endless further conventions.

mv-k07-v962.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v962.question: How could a child be instructed in convention if conventions lack a stable foundation?
premises: Conventions without innate grounding lead to infinite regress.
Infinite regress destroys the root of understanding.
Instruction of a child in convention presupposes a stable foundation.
mv-k07-v962.inference: If conventions rested only on other conventions, infinite regress would make it impossible to instruct a child in them.

mv-k07-v963.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v963.question: What is the nature of the phonemic ground that makes convention possible?
premises: Conventions require a stable, non-regressive ground.
There is an infinite, non-māyic collection of phonemes of this kind.
This phonemic collection is always accompanied by conscious reflective awareness and continually unfolds.
mv-k07-v963.inference: The stable ground of convention is an infinite, non-māyic phonemic totality that perpetually unfolds with conscious reflective awareness.

mv-k07-v964.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v964.question: What is the relationship between non-māyic and māyic phonemes?
premises: The māyic phonemes arise from the non-māyic phonemic source.
The non-māyic phonemes are the power behind the māyic phonemes.
mv-k07-v964.inference: Māyic phonemes originate from the non-māyic phonemic totality, which constitutes their underlying potency.

mv-k07-v965.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v965.question: Why does hearing another's speech fail to produce subjecthood in some listeners?
premises: When others' utterances are heard, a listener's own cognition may remain veiled.
A person whose own cognition is veiled remains dull with respect to that meaning.
Such a person does not attain subjecthood in relation to that meaning.
mv-k07-v965.inference: Mere hearing of others' speech does not confer subjecthood if one's own cognition does not awaken to the meaning.

mv-k07-v966.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v966.question: What enables a listener to attain subjecthood through heard speech?
premises: A listener may have their own cognition enter into awareness.
That cognition, containing differentiation, enters the mass of māyic phonemes within oneself.
Through this entry, the listener attains subjecthood.
mv-k07-v966.inference: Subjecthood arises when one's own differentiated cognition awakens and engages the māyic phonemes from within.

mv-k07-v967.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v967.question: What determines the degree of aesthetic wonder in cognition?
premises: The uncreated, innate form can predominate to varying degrees.
The degree of aesthetic wonder corresponds to that predominance.
mv-k07-v967.inference: The more the uncreated innate form predominates, the greater the gradation of aesthetic wonder that arises.

mv-k07-v968.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v968.question: What results when the surge of the innate form becomes great in intuitive insight?
premises: The innate form can surge to a great degree.
Some become established in the nature of flash insight.
Such establishment leads to excellence in poetry and eloquence.
mv-k07-v968.inference: When the surge of the innate form is great, those established in intuitive insight certainly attain complete poetic and eloquent excellence.

mv-k07-v969.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v969.question: Why are the phonemes contemplated and kept secret in the perfection of speech?
premises: The perfection of speech depends on the phonemes.
Therefore the phonemes are objects of contemplative practice.
For that reason they are kept secret and spoken only by the initiated.
mv-k07-v969.inference: Because phonemes are the basis of perfected speech, they are contemplatively cultivated and transmitted under secrecy.

mv-k07-v970.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v970.question: What occurs when the Lord's constant repose projects many phonemes at once?
premises: The Lord has a constant repose.
From that repose, many phonemes can be projected simultaneously.
These phonemes are well established in fulfilling portions of experience.
mv-k07-v970.inference: The Lord's abiding repose simultaneously projects multiple phonemes that are structured to fulfill experiential portions.
uncertainties: The gerund 'udṛṅkya' is morphologically unusual; taken here as 'having projected forth'.

mv-k07-v971.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v971.question: How does the path of words become the first sprout of worldly convention?
premises: The path of words resorts to the level of the knowable object.
At that level it enters the mass of conventions bound to transmigratory life.
In that mass it functions as the first sprout.
mv-k07-v971.inference: When the word path takes support in objectivity, it becomes the initial sprout of the aggregate of worldly conventions.
uncertainties: The compound 'saṃsāramṛtasaṃketasaṃghāte' is compact; interpreted as conventions inert within transmigratory existence.

mv-k07-v972.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v972.question: How are objecthood, subjecthood, and measure related to the thirty-six principles?
premises: Objecthood, subjecthood, and the state of being the measure have been described.
These modes pertain to the collection of thirty-six principles.
mv-k07-v972.inference: It is concluded that objecthood, subjecthood, and measure are modes within the thirty-sixfold system of principles.

mv-k07-v973.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v973.question: How does all this appear in the unchanging supreme Lord?
premises: All this shines forth in the unchanging supreme Lord.
It appears there in the manner of a reflection.
It does not appear as something external to him.
mv-k07-v973.inference: The universe appears within the supreme Lord as reflection, not as an external reality.

mv-k07-v974.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v974.question: Where and how do differentiated bodily cognitions appear to worldly beings?
premises: Such divided cognitions of various bodies appear to worldly beings.
They appear in the sky of consciousness, in Śiva alone.
This is like the appearance of a snake and so on in a rope.
mv-k07-v974.inference: The differentiated world of embodied experience appears within consciousness alone, like a snake seen in a rope.

mv-k07-v975.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v975.question: What kind of bodily existence can be established after death if prior embodiment is dreamlike?
premises: The established view before the death of the body belongs to the sphere of dream.
Another body and related experiences arise after death.
The nature of that post-death bodily arising is therefore questionable.
mv-k07-v975.inference: If embodied life before death is dreamlike, the status of another body arising after death cannot be taken as independently real.
uncertainties: The verse is compressed and may be read as a rhetorical challenge rather than a direct assertion.

mv-k07-v976.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v976.question: How do particular details arise in a dream without being independently produced?
premises: In a dream, particulars appear by the force of the unfolding of mere appearance.
Their manifestation comes from appearance itself, not from separate production.
Therefore those particulars are not produced as independent realities.
mv-k07-v976.inference: Dream particulars are manifestations of appearance, not independently generated entities.

mv-k07-v977.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v977.question: How can the varied levels of manifestation be contained within consciousness?
premises: Some śālagrāma stones naturally contain varied forms within themselves.
Consciousness has a variegated inner nature.
The inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward are contained within consciousness.
mv-k07-v977.inference: The manifold levels of manifestation are inner differentiations within consciousness, not external additions to it.

mv-k07-v978.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v978.question: Do cities, oceans, mountains, and other forms act as independent causes or effects?
premises: Cities, oceans, mountains, and similar forms follow the will of consciousness.
They do not operate by themselves.
They do not independently possess the nature of existent or nonexistent causes and effects.
mv-k07-v978.inference: The apparent causal structure of the world depends on the will of consciousness rather than on independent entities.
uncertainties: The compound sadasadrūpakāraṇākaraṇātmakāḥ is dense and allows slight variation in unpacking.

mv-k07-v979.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v979.question: Does the Lord remain free both within established order and beyond it?
premises: A long-established rule may be cut off or set in motion.
Even where no rule has yet taken root, activity may arise.
In both cases the Lord remains independent.
mv-k07-v979.inference: The consciousness-sky Bhairava is sovereign over both the maintenance and suspension of order.

mv-k07-v980.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v980.question: What causes differentiation within the realm of beings despite nondifference with Bhairava?
premises: The true state shares nondifference with Bhairava, full of one consciousness alone.
Within that state, the reflective awareness 'I am thus' may fail to occur.
That non-recognition differentiates the realm of beings.
mv-k07-v980.inference: Differentiation arises from the absence of reflective recognition, not from any real division in consciousness.

mv-k07-v981.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v981.question: Is any agent other than independent awareness established as the creator of manifestation?
premises: In a dream, no other agent is established by any means of knowledge.
Dream creation belongs to one's own awareness.
The world's creation should be understood in the same way as arising from independent self-awareness.
mv-k07-v981.inference: Creation is the free activity of self-awareness, not the work of another agent.

mv-k07-v982.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v982.question: What recognition arises for one who plays within the mind's variegated display?
premises: One may sport within the mind's variegated city and garden of appearances.
Such a one can recognize the true identity behind those appearances.
The recognition is that 'I alone abide as all these beings, which are consciousness only.'
mv-k07-v982.inference: True recognition sees all manifested beings as the self's own consciousness-only forms.

mv-k07-v983.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v983.question: Where do the varied experiences of birth and death actually appear?
premises: The sense 'I am born' and 'I am dead' arises as a reflective appearance.
The diverse forms of birth and death appear in the unborn and deathless reality.
They appear on the wall of the mind as self-imagined projections.
mv-k07-v983.inference: Birth and death are imagined appearances within the unborn, deathless consciousness.

mv-k07-v984.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v984.question: Are this world and the other world truly different realities?
premises: The distinction between this world and the other world is only a matter of awareness.
Even apparent divisions of time, part, awareness, and place do not create real difference.
The underlying reality remains non-differentiated.
mv-k07-v984.inference: World-distinctions are modes of awareness within an undivided reality.
uncertainties: The compound akālakalāsaṃviddeśabhede is compact and its internal relations are interpretively dense.

mv-k07-v985.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v985.question: Could any material object be perceived if creation were not consciousness-made?
premises: Suppose this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness.
Perception would then have to arise from within that material creation.
No one could perceive even a single mountain from within such a merely material creation.
mv-k07-v985.inference: Because perception occurs, creation cannot be merely material; it must be consciousness-made.

mv-k07-v986.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v986.question: What ultimately supports the elements and subtle elements in their mutual dependence?
premises: The elements, subtle elements, and related classes can be examined as support and supported.
Such examination cannot rest in another material support without regress.
Ultimately the supporting principle is the consciousness-power that is Śiva's own nature.
mv-k07-v986.inference: The final support of all dependent manifestation is Śiva's consciousness-power.

mv-k07-v987.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v987.question: Why is cognition identified as the creative agent and called the common ground?
premises: Cognition itself is the creative agent in this mode of manifestation.
That cognition is manifestation and is Śiva in his own self.
Because it is the shared basis of manifestation, it is called the common power.
mv-k07-v987.inference: Creative cognition is Śiva's own power and the common ground of all manifestation.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of sādhārasaṃjñitā may be 'called common' or 'called the common basis'.

mv-k07-v988.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v988.question: Why does even an apparently unsupported imagined appearance not collapse?
premises: An imagined appearance may seem to have no support.
Yet it does not fall away into collapse.
This is because the universe rests in its own supporting power.
mv-k07-v988.inference: All appearances, even imagined ones, are upheld by the self-supporting power of consciousness.

mv-k07-v989.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v989.question: How does the dense sense of ego give rise to the levels of manifestation and culminate in Bhairava identity?
premises: From the fixation of the dense sense 'I' arise the states beginning with earth.
This same process extends through the levels of manifestation.
At its culmination, the recognition 'I am consciousness' is realized as Bhairava identity.
mv-k07-v989.inference: The spectrum from gross egoity to earth and back to pure recognition culminates in the realization of Bhairava identity.

mv-k07-v990.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v990.question: Do the varied appearances in Śiva truly arise and pass away?
premises: Colors like blue appear in a jewel or rainbow as expressions of light.
So too varied appearances manifest in Śiva.
In ultimate truth, these appearances have no real arising or dissolution.
mv-k07-v990.inference: Appearances in Śiva are like colors in light: manifest without ultimate origination or destruction.

mv-k07-v991.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v991.question: Can creation be properly located within space and time?
premises: It is incoherent to say that creation occurs in space or in time.
The Lord whose nature is consciousness is the creator.
Space and time themselves are part of that creation.
mv-k07-v991.inference: Creation cannot be placed within space and time, because space and time arise from the conscious Lord's creative act.

mv-k07-v992.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v992.question: How do dreams reveal the relativity of space and time within waking assumptions?
premises: What is assumed to be waking occurs within limited space and a limited watch of time.
Within that same span, separate dreams can occur.
Those dreams have their own varied measures of space and time.
mv-k07-v992.inference: The measures of space and time are not fixed by waking assumptions, since distinct dream worlds generate their own.

mv-k07-v993.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v993.question: Is a moment a fixed unit of time if many actions occur within it?
premises: A so-called moment is not regarded as any fixed thing.
Even within a single moment of action, many swift actions can occur.
Therefore the moment cannot be an ultimate, indivisible unit.
mv-k07-v993.inference: The moment is not an absolute temporal atom but a relative measure within experience.

mv-k07-v994.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v994.question: What is the limitation of those who reduce manifestation to momentary contraction?
premises: Some accept that the contraction of beings ends in a moment.
This view narrows reality to a constricted channel.
Such thinkers rely on an emptiness-based outlook.
mv-k07-v994.inference: Reducing manifestation to momentary contraction reflects a constricted, emptiness-leaning perspective rather than the full view of consciousness.
uncertainties: The metaphor nālyā is somewhat interpretive; it suggests a narrow tube or channel.

mv-k07-v995.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v995.question: Who has the sovereign power to make the existent appear empty and the nonexistent appear manifest?
premises: The same sovereign power can reduce existent beings to emptiness.
That same power can make what is nonexistent appear clearly.
This capacity belongs to the Lord because of his independence.
mv-k07-v995.inference: The supreme Lord's freedom alone accounts for the appearance of existence and nonexistence.
uncertainties: The token tahtāsataḥ is unusual in form; taken here as tathā+asataḥ in sense.

mv-k07-v996.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v996.question: Is the universe-form a property of the supreme Lord or of any separate entity like earth?
premises: The supreme Lord is proclaimed in this way as having the universe as his form.
No separate entity such as earth and the rest is independently tenable as the basis of that form.
Therefore universe-form belongs to the supreme Lord alone.
mv-k07-v996.inference: The universe is the form of the supreme Lord, not of any independently real separate entity.

mv-k07-v997.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v997.question: Why is the critique of external objects not examined again here?
premises: This point has already been stated earlier.
It is therefore not examined again in detail.
Many refutations of external objects have already been composed.
mv-k07-v997.inference: Because the refutation of external objects was already established earlier and elaborated by many, it need not be reexamined here.

mv-k07-v998.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v998.question: How can karma still be connected with its fruit in birth and death?
premises: An objection is raised about how karma can yield fruit across birth and death.
The previously stated freedom of consciousness seems to be forgotten.
The question challenges the compatibility of karmic fruition with consciousness's freedom.
mv-k07-v998.inference: If consciousness is truly free, the mechanism by which karma produces fruit in birth and death must be explained.

mv-k07-v999.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v999.question: How does the freedom of consciousness account for what appears?
premises: This consciousness is free.
As it makes things appear, so they truly appear.
It contains all forms within itself, and this is determined.
mv-k07-v999.inference: Because free consciousness manifests appearances according to its own nature, those appearances are real as its self-expression.

mv-k07-v1000.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1000.question: How is the whole creation present in each smallest unit?
premises: Sweetness pervades every atom of sugarcane completely.
In the same way, each ultimate atom contains the state of all creation.
The analogy shows total presence within each part.
mv-k07-v1000.inference: Just as sweetness pervades every part of sugarcane, the entirety of creation abides in each ultimate atom.

mv-k07-v1001.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1001.question: Why do some learned people dispute this teaching?
premises: Some learned people do not know the root principle.
They dispute the teaching presented here.
Their effort serves to protect their own mental constructions.
mv-k07-v1001.inference: Those who dispute this do so not from insight into the root principle but to defend their own imagined views.

mv-k07-v1002.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
