mv-k07-v1002.question: What causes the mistaken idea that this is located in some particular place?
premises: People imagine this to be located in breath, space, consciousness, the external, or somewhere else.
Such localization is a delusion.
The delusion arises from ignorance and from the apparent absence of freedom due to restriction.
mv-k07-v1002.inference: The belief that reality is confined to a particular locus is a delusion produced by ignorance and restrictive limitation.

mv-k07-v1003.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1003.question: How does birth appear in relation to self-awareness and freedom?
premises: The awareness of one's own consciousness appears here as birth.
Before that appearance, consciousness does not manifest in a form fit for freedom.
Birth is thus tied to a particular mode of appearing awareness.
mv-k07-v1003.inference: Birth is the appearance of self-awareness in a limited mode, not the original free form of consciousness.

mv-k07-v1004.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1004.question: What is previous karma and how can it be destroyed?
premises: Former consciousness is here called previous karma.
A consciousness that obstructs that former consciousness can arise.
Such obstructing consciousness brings about the destruction of karma.
mv-k07-v1004.inference: Previous karma is a prior mode of consciousness, and a stronger opposing consciousness can dissolve it.

mv-k07-v1005.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1005.question: How can something not actually done still appear to yield fruit?
premises: In a dream, what was not done can appear as done by me.
That appearance can be experienced as fruit-giving.
The same account applies to karma in the waking state.
mv-k07-v1005.inference: Karmic fruition depends on the mode of consciousness in which an act appears, as shown by the dream analogy.

mv-k07-v1006.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1006.question: Who ceases to undergo the fruit of past karma?
premises: A higher consciousness can arise that burns up the fruit of accumulated past karma.
Even a single such consciousness may arise in someone.
That person no longer undergoes karmic fruit in the usual way.
mv-k07-v1006.inference: One in whom a higher consciousness arises that consumes past karmic fruit is no longer bound to experience that fruit.

mv-k07-v1007.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1007.question: What further effect follows from the vivid arising of many consciousnesses?
premises: The clear flashing of many consciousnesses can turn disrepute into repute.
This transformation can yield abundant fruit.
The result is compared to a seed watered by a river in the sky.
mv-k07-v1007.inference: When many vivid consciousnesses arise, even adverse outcomes can be transformed into abundantly fruitful ones.
uncertainties: The long compound in token 2 is transmitted as a single fused form; internal segmentation is interpretive.

mv-k07-v1008.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1008.question: How does the degree of awareness affect the fruit of karma?
premises: Karma flashing forth in slight awareness yields small fruit.
Karma not flashing forth in awareness is fruitless.
This principle concerns one's own consciousness.
mv-k07-v1008.inference: The fruition of karma depends on the degree to which it is present in one's own consciousness.

mv-k07-v1009.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1009.question: What determines whether consciousnesses are small or great in effect?
premises: Smallness and greatness are conceived among consciousnesses.
These differences belong to the doer of karma.
They take shape according to how firmly consciousness is established.
mv-k07-v1009.inference: The lesser or greater force of consciousness depends on the degree of its establishment in the karmic agent's awareness.
uncertainties: The segmentation of saṃvittirūḍhyā follows the transmitted fused form; internal analysis is interpretive.

mv-k07-v1010.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1010.question: When does a consciousness fail to produce its corresponding fruit?
premises: A consciousness may not arise by itself as pregnant with a particular fruit.
It may also fail to do so through association with a subject grasping another fruit.
In such cases the corresponding fruition does not take shape.
mv-k07-v1010.inference: A specific karmic fruit arises only when consciousness is formed for that fruit and not redirected by another subject's orientation.
uncertainties: Token 3 is an editorial insertion in the source and is kept exactly as given.

mv-k07-v1011.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1011.question: Can another subject's intention determine the fruit experienced by someone else?
premises: The fruit is known in the consciousness of a particular subject.
Another subject may form an intention regarding that fruit.
Such an external intention cannot ultimately govern the other's experience.
mv-k07-v1011.inference: Karmic fruit belongs to the consciousness of its own subject and cannot be decisively imposed by another subject's intention.

mv-k07-v1012.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1012.question: What does the awakened one do to constructions centered on karmic fruit?
premises: The awakened one unfolds the power of maintenance in relation to creation for the senses.
Such awakening involves knowledge of how creation operates.
The awakened one contracts constructions that depend on grasping at fruit.
mv-k07-v1012.inference: Awakening contracts and dissolves the mental constructions that fixate on karmic fruit.
uncertainties: The form akṣāyai is transmitted as given; its precise relation to the senses is interpretive.

mv-k07-v1013.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1013.question: Why did the ancients teach that helping others should be done?
premises: This creation is seen from a standpoint other than the limited fish-like view.
The ancients understood this broader perspective.
With that intention, they taught that helping others should be done.
mv-k07-v1013.inference: The ancients taught compassion because they saw creation from a wider, non-limited perspective.
uncertainties: The fish/non-fish contrast is transmitted tersely; its exact illustrative force is interpretive.

mv-k07-v1014.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1014.question: How is help said to extend even to the dead?
premises: Help is said to extend even to one who has died.
This is done through offerings such as rice-balls.
Through such acts, union with a body is said to be given again.
mv-k07-v1014.inference: Ritual help for the dead is explained as providing the conditions for renewed bodily association.

mv-k07-v1015.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1015.question: What motive is imagined behind undertaking difficult austerity for others?
premises: One may accept afflictions upon oneself.
The intention is that others should not be harmed.
This motive is conceived as the fruit of difficult austerity.
mv-k07-v1015.inference: Difficult austerity is imagined to bear fruit when one willingly suffers so that others may be spared harm.
uncertainties: The form pīḍayan is transmitted as given; its exact finite analysis is interpretive.
The segmentation of kṛcchrādes follows the transmitted form and is somewhat uncertain.

mv-k07-v1016.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1016.question: How should prohibitions like the uneatability of garlic be understood?
premises: The uneatability of garlic and similar things is stated in scripture.
Such a rule is to be understood as a command.
It is presented as not requiring an external reason for people to accept it.
mv-k07-v1016.inference: Certain dietary prohibitions function as authoritative commands rather than as conclusions from independent causal reasoning.

mv-k07-v1017.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1017.question: Why do differing judgments arise about what is eatable or uneatable?
premises: Rules about eatability and uneatability vary in cases like swans and other birds.
Such variation fits a difference in understanding or convention.
Otherwise there would be no basis for the difference at all.
mv-k07-v1017.inference: Differences in dietary judgments are intelligible as differences in understanding or convention, not as fixed by nature alone.
uncertainties: The form nna is transmitted as given; it is taken as a negation in context.

mv-k07-v1018.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1018.question: Where is the connection between action and fruit ultimately established?
premises: Connections with fruit are conceived in both seen and unseen domains.
These are arranged through conceived divisions and sequences.
That arrangement is now established on the ground of consciousness.
mv-k07-v1018.inference: The linkage of action and fruit, in both visible and invisible spheres, is ultimately grounded in consciousness.

mv-k07-v1019.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1019.question: Does a body in the other world really arise from ritual offerings, and are beings otherwise unconnected?
premises: A doctrine holds that a body in the other world comes from the rice-ball offering and not otherwise.
This implies a specific account of how embodied beings are related.
The verse questions whether beings are mutually unconnected apart from such ritual linkage.
mv-k07-v1019.inference: The claim that postmortem embodiment depends on ritual offerings raises the problematic implication that beings lack mutual connection otherwise.
uncertainties: The final token is punctuation as transmitted; the verse reads as a probing or skeptical question.

mv-k07-v1020.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1020.question: What is the effect of masses of scripture on ignorant minds regarding karmic fruit?
premises: Masses of scriptures plant stakes of doubt.
These doubts take root in the ground of ignorant minds.
From there they grow into fixed conclusions about karmic fruit.
mv-k07-v1020.inference: For ignorant minds, scriptural proliferation can entrench doubt and harden it into rigid doctrines about fruit.

mv-k07-v1021.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1021.question: How does the belief in a rice-ball giver shape one's imagined afterlife state?
premises: A person imagines having a ritual giver of rice-balls.
Through the sequence of rice-ball offerings, one imagines obtaining bodily enjoyment.
This imagined ritual support produces the sense of being complete and well-established.
mv-k07-v1021.inference: The conviction of ritual support generates a corresponding experience of bodily completeness in the afterlife imagination.
uncertainties: The token prapnobh/m(?)yavayavābhogaṃ is textually uncertain in the source.

mv-k07-v1022.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1022.question: What heavenly condition is imagined through unseen rites performed by others?
premises: Unseen ritual actions are imagined as performed by sons, disciples, oneself, or others.
These actions are believed to secure a share in heaven.
The result is imagined as complete enjoyment and stable well-being.
mv-k07-v1022.inference: Belief in unseen rites performed by related agents produces the conviction of a stable and pleasurable heavenly state.

mv-k07-v1023.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1023.question: What fearful afterlife is imagined when ritual support and rescue are absent?
premises: A person imagines having no one to offer rice-balls.
The same person judges himself to be a great wrongdoer with no savior anywhere.
This conviction leads to the imagination of falling into a hellish ocean.
mv-k07-v1023.inference: The absence of imagined ritual and moral support produces a corresponding vision of helpless descent into hell.

mv-k07-v1024.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1024.question: How do such hopes and fears in awareness come to fruition?
premises: Thoughts arise such as the hope that a savior will appear somewhere and sometime.
These are expansions of cognition, not merely external events.
The expansion of cognition bears fruit in a corresponding way.
mv-k07-v1024.inference: Cognitive expansions, whether hopeful or fearful, actualize themselves as corresponding experiences.

mv-k07-v1025.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1025.question: What happens if no external ritual agent exists for the imagined afterlife?
premises: An external performer of rice-ball rites may not actually exist.
The cognition still flashes forth in a particular form.
The experiencer undergoes the fruit fashioned by that cognition.
mv-k07-v1025.inference: The experienced afterlife result depends on the form of cognition, not on the presence of an external ritual agent.

mv-k07-v1026.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1026.question: What can destroy the deeply hardened belief in such afterlife constructions?
premises: The mistaken belief is hardened by doubt like diamond-hard plaster.
Such a fixation cannot be removed by ordinary means.
The fire of Bhairava-awareness alone can burn it completely and instantly.
mv-k07-v1026.inference: Only the liberating fire of Bhairava-consciousness can uproot the hardened delusion of afterlife constructions.

mv-k07-v1027.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1027.question: What realization burns up the entire dream-house of worldly experience?
premises: The world is like a dream-house contained within varied consciousness.
A fire is needed to burn that dream-house.
The realization 'I alone am Śiva' flashes forth as that fire.
mv-k07-v1027.inference: The identity-realization 'I am Śiva' is the fire that consumes the entire dreamlike world.

mv-k07-v1028.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1028.question: Why does the deluded person take the varied world-cycle as real?
premises: A deluded person's consciousness is variegated by karmic cognitions.
What appears is fundamentally a construction of resolve.
The deluded person mistakes that construction for a real, varied world-cycle.
mv-k07-v1028.inference: Delusion consists in taking a resolve-constructed world, shaped by karmic cognition, to be objectively real.

mv-k07-v1029.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1029.question: Why might a child who dies be reborn again as an infant?
premises: A child who dies may lack other developed impressions.
Firm worldly impressions may still remain latent.
Rebirth follows the dominant latent impressions.
mv-k07-v1029.inference: A deceased child without other impressions may be reborn as an infant because firm worldly impressions remain latent.

mv-k07-v1030.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1030.question: How do latent impressions unfold again into later stages of life?
premises: Latent impressions continue to operate after rebirth.
Development proceeds through stages such as youth.
The sequence of those impressions drives that progression again.
mv-k07-v1030.inference: The unfolding of life stages after rebirth follows the sequence of latent impressions.
uncertainties: The tokens tānyau and (?) are textually unclear in the source.

mv-k07-v1031.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1031.question: How do impressions lead a being to identify with various transmigrations and even inert states?
premises: Cognition shaped by impressions makes one identify with particular transmigrations.
An impression of inertness can make a being become inert.
Even in that state, association with subtle elements like space and wind continues.
mv-k07-v1031.inference: Impression-shaped cognition drives identification with transmigratory forms, including states of inertness.

mv-k07-v1032.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1032.question: How can a being pass through vegetal and embryonic forms in transmigration?
premises: Association with earth and water can lead to existence as flower and fruit.
When consumed, that existence can pass into the form of seed.
Through that seed-form, the being can return to a womb state.
mv-k07-v1032.inference: Transmigration can proceed through elemental, vegetal, and reproductive transformations driven by continuing impressions.

mv-k07-v1033.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1033.question: Where do the varied cycles of transmigration actually occur?
premises: The being repeatedly takes varied world-cycles to be real.
This taking-to-be-real is driven by dwelling in one's own impressions and tendencies.
The conscious subject in whom this occurs is Śiva.
mv-k07-v1033.inference: The varied cycles of transmigration occur in the one conscious locus, Śiva, as experiences shaped by impressions.

mv-k07-v1034.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1034.question: What kinds of experiences does the self-fashioned consciousness undergo?
premises: Consciousness experiences heavens, hells, and other realms.
These experiences are fashioned by its own freedom.
They may appear in earthlike, waterlike, or mixed forms.
mv-k07-v1034.inference: The realms and forms experienced in transmigration are self-fashioned manifestations of free consciousness.

mv-k07-v1035.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1035.question: How does awareness appear as worlds and as pleasure or pain?
premises: Awareness shines by its own nature in the form of worlds.
Wherever it becomes fixed, that fixation occurs in that very locus.
From its own impressions it experiences pleasure and other feelings there.
mv-k07-v1035.inference: World-appearance and felt experience arise from awareness itself through fixation shaped by its own impressions.

mv-k07-v1036.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1036.question: Why is the experiencer's world not publicly visible and not ultimately located in space or time?
premises: The experiencer knows, but is not seen by another in that same experiential form.
The experiencer may know others differently.
In ultimate truth, no independent place or time exists to fix these experiences.
mv-k07-v1036.inference: Experiential worlds are privately constituted in awareness and lack ultimate grounding in independent space or time.

mv-k07-v1037.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1037.question: Why does the doctrine of difference fail to establish real spatial distinction?
premises: If space itself is taken as the common place, everything would collapse into one place.
If difference is explained by limiting conditions, those conditions still require spatial distinction.
The distinction of limiting conditions would itself depend on further distinction.
mv-k07-v1037.inference: In a doctrine of difference, spatial distinction cannot be grounded without circular dependence on limiting conditions.

mv-k07-v1038.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1038.question: What kind of difference, if any, can coherently explain distinction?
premises: Spatial difference collapses into mutual dependence.
Mutual dependence cannot establish any real difference of place.
Only difference of intrinsic nature could coherently serve as a differentiator.
mv-k07-v1038.inference: If difference is to be coherent, it must be intrinsic difference of nature rather than spatial difference.

mv-k07-v1039.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1039.question: Why does intrinsic difference also fail in the light of nondual consciousness?
premises: Intrinsic difference was proposed as the only coherent differentiator.
In realities whose nature is one light, such intrinsic difference does not exist.
This has been established by reflective insight, which some lack.
mv-k07-v1039.inference: Because all is of the nature of one light, intrinsic difference cannot ultimately exist, though this is missed without reflective insight.

mv-k07-v1040.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1040.question: What happens to those who lack reflective insight into nondual consciousness?
premises: Some people lack the reflective vision that sees the one light.
They are made doubtful by floods of scriptures that generate doubt.
They become absorbed in constructions imagined like inert beings in their own dreams.
mv-k07-v1040.inference: Without reflective insight, people are overwhelmed by doubt-producing scriptural constructions and become identified with dreamlike projections.

mv-k07-v1041.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1041.question: Why do seeming scriptures create doubt in those without awakening?
premises: Those devoid of awakening are made to grasp doubt by seeming scriptures.
This doubt is ultimately futile.
Awareness may remain hidden for long but can still awaken.
mv-k07-v1041.inference: Seeming scriptures only trouble those lacking awakening, while awareness itself can awaken even after long latency.

mv-k07-v1042.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1042.question: Why do mental constructions still seem to bear fruit in experience?
premises: Mental constructions and similar projections appear to bear fruit.
This happens mostly through constructions of mind and related faculties.
Underlying them is the sovereignty of freedom that manifests multiplicity.
mv-k07-v1042.inference: Mental constructions bear experiential fruit because consciousness freely manifests multiplicity through them.

mv-k07-v1043.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1043.question: How does a fashioned appearance become an embodied experience of disturbance?
premises: Whatever is fashioned in awareness becomes that experiencer's embodied form.
This can occur under the influence of reversed or distorted appearances.
Such distortion may be tainted by sensations like cold and others.
mv-k07-v1043.inference: A mentally fashioned appearance can manifest as an embodied condition, especially when distorted by adverse sensations.

mv-k07-v1044.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1044.question: How is bodily disturbance described when the body's vital mechanism is altered?
premises: The subtle channels and related bodily structures can be afflicted.
The body is likened to a great bellows-machine driven by the wheel of vital winds.
When this mechanism goes awry, contraction, bursting, striking, and similar disturbances arise.
mv-k07-v1044.inference: Bodily suffering is explained as the malfunction of the body’s wind-driven mechanism affecting its channels.

mv-k07-v1045.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1045.question: What happens to the body and experience when the vital breath breaks apart?
premises: The vital breath can become disjoined from its normal functioning.
When the breath breaks apart, the body appears as inert matter.
A new sphere of experience arises according to the sequence of prior latent impressions.
mv-k07-v1045.inference: At the disruption of the vital breath, the body falls into inert appearance and consciousness passes into another experiential domain shaped by prior impressions.
uncertainties: The exact scope of adhikāra here, whether a new life-domain or a new experiential jurisdiction, is context-dependent.

mv-k07-v1046.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1046.question: What kinds of experience can arise in that post-disruption state?
premises: In that same state, one may construct an experience called the other world.
Alternatively, one may experience a stone-like insentient condition.
Alternatively, one may awaken again to ordinary awareness.
mv-k07-v1046.inference: The state following the breath's disruption can manifest as an other-world experience, as inert stupor, or as a return to waking awareness.
uncertainties: Whether pāṣāṇatāṃ refers to literal insentience, deep coma, or a metaphorical rigidity is not fully explicit.

mv-k07-v1047.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1047.question: How does an experience come to count as another world or as heaven and liberation?
premises: The designation 'this is another world' depends on a subject's firm conviction.
Heaven, liberation, and similar states become established in a person's mind in specific ways.
What is firmly settled in consciousness determines how such states are taken.
mv-k07-v1047.inference: Other-world status and states like heaven or liberation are constituted by the way they become firmly established in consciousness.
uncertainties: The verse spans into the next verse for its full consequence; the syntactic completion is carried forward.

mv-k07-v1048.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1048.question: What forms of experience appear outwardly as a result of settled inner conviction?
premises: What is firmly established in consciousness appears outwardly for that subject.
Even in that projected domain there is manifold variety.
Bondage, liberation, happiness, heaven, suffering, and inert states can all appear there.
mv-k07-v1048.inference: The outwardly appearing world, including its highest and lowest states, is a varied manifestation shaped by consciousness.

mv-k07-v1049.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1049.question: What is the ultimate nature that manifests all these varied experiential states?
premises: Consciousness alone manifests independently in these ways.
This independent manifestation is of the nature of Śiva.
In a being composed of parts, the sense of 'I' abides only to a limited extent.
mv-k07-v1049.inference: The diverse appearances of experience are the free self-manifestation of consciousness whose nature is Śiva, though finite beings know this 'I' only in a limited way.

mv-k07-v1050.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k07-v1050.question: How does Bhairava's universal I-sense relate to the way imagined objects appear real?
premises: Bhairava's I-sense abides in a form whose nature is the whole universe.
A child can perceive a goblin even in an empty place.
What is thus perceived can appear to produce real effects.
mv-k07-v1050.inference: Just as a child's cognition can make an unreal figure appear effectively real, consciousness in its universal Bhairava-form freely manifests appearances with seeming reality.

mv-k08-v1051.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1051.question: How can an embodied and divided deity be invoked and act effectively?
premises: Meditation and worship take diverse forms.
An embodied and divided deity can be invoked.
Such invocation can produce effective action in an instant.
mv-k08-v1051.inference: The variety of meditation and worship is effective because an embodied, divided deity can be invoked and act immediately.

mv-k08-v1052.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1052.question: Does the claim that a god comes and acts fit the true nature of reality?
premises: The report that a god comes and acts may suit scriptural statements.
The ultimate nature is formless and beyond such limitations.
A doctrine must fit that ultimate nature to be fully valid.
mv-k08-v1052.inference: The coming-and-going account is only scripturally suitable, while the formless nature is what truly fits.

mv-k08-v1053.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1053.question: What is the true source of the appearance of division?
premises: The self alone has that ultimate nature.
The self appears in divided forms.
This appearing as division is the very nature of consciousness.
mv-k08-v1053.inference: Division is not external to the self but is consciousness manifesting according to its own nature.

mv-k08-v1054.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1054.question: When is karmic differentiation treated as an impurity and when is it not?
premises: Scripture defines karmic impurity as being seized by division.
Initiation and ritual action operate within differentiated forms.
In the context of initiation, that differentiation is not treated as impurity.
mv-k08-v1054.inference: Karmic division counts as impurity in bondage but not in the liberating use of initiation and ritual.

mv-k08-v1055.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1055.question: What is initiation in its essential nature?
premises: Initiation is directed toward burning away the whole division-made world of transmigration.
Its true function is not merely external ritual.
In reality it consists in true consciousness of that liberating kind.
mv-k08-v1055.inference: Initiation is essentially the true consciousness that destroys division-based transmigration.

mv-k08-v1056.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1056.question: What is realized when the domain of division is pacified in the supreme teaching?
premises: The supreme teaching states that one who knows thus knows in truth.
This knowledge arises in the yoga of realization.
In that yoga the sphere of division becomes quieted.
mv-k08-v1056.inference: True knowledge in the supreme doctrine consists in realization when division is pacified.

mv-k08-v1057.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1057.question: If the self is one with Śiva, what meaning do bondage and liberation have?
premises: In realization the self alone is Śiva, the one reality.
From that standpoint bondage and liberation lose their ultimate distinction.
Teaching still speaks of initiation to lead one into that great consciousness.
mv-k08-v1057.inference: Bondage and liberation are pedagogical distinctions used to guide entry into the nondual consciousness where self is Śiva.

mv-k08-v1058.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1058.question: How does action-based initiation remove karmic and other impurities?
premises: There is an initiation whose nature is action.
Its purpose is the removal of karmic and other impurities.
It operates within actions compelled by a fixed force fashioned by nature.
mv-k08-v1058.inference: Action-based initiation works by transforming karmic actions that are otherwise governed by fixed necessity.

mv-k08-v1059.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1059.question: How can the fruition of karma be experienced simultaneously through initiation?
premises: Initiation can bring about the experience of karma for the initiate.
This fruition can occur simultaneously through mantra power.
The limiting determinations of breath, space, limited agency, and time are thereby engaged.
mv-k08-v1059.inference: Mantra power in initiation can compress and resolve karmic fruition across the usual limiting paths.
uncertainties: The exact scope of deśakalākālādhvaniścayāḥ is compressed in the compound and follows traditional Trika categories.

mv-k08-v1060.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1060.question: Across what range are the initiate's births and experiences unfolded?
premises: The initiate's births are unfolded across the whole cosmic range.
That range extends from earth up to Śiva.
Within that range occur birth, experience, authority, and dissolution.
mv-k08-v1060.inference: Initiatory transformation encompasses the full spectrum of existence from the lowest to the highest level.

mv-k08-v1061.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1061.question: How does initiation block all prior karmic powers between guru and disciple?
premises: The initiate is elevated from one level and established in another.
Guru and disciple meet in a state grounded in settled consciousness and free of karmic mind.
Initiation operates through a non-conceptual transmission between them.
mv-k08-v1061.inference: Mutual non-conceptual initiation between guru and disciple restrains all prior karmic powers.
uncertainties: niṣkarmacetor is metrically compressed; taken as a genitive dual/collective sense in context.

mv-k08-v1062.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1062.question: Do external Śaiva ritual forms fully eliminate the obscurity of division?
premises: Śaiva ritual employs substances like rice, sesame, ghee, and oblations.
These forms are fashioned according to Śaiva necessity and operate at a clear level.
Even so, division continues to operate.
mv-k08-v1062.inference: External ritual forms do not completely uproot the obscurity of division because differentiation still persists.
uncertainties: niśāprapañco is metaphorical; interpreted as the expanse of obscurity rather than literal night.

mv-k08-v1063.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1063.question: How is the entire network of principles divided in the state of difference?
premises: Even in difference, this pure factor destroys merit that would produce future transmigration.
Because of that, the entire network of principles is classified by pure and other states.
The classification of all principles is therefore only twofold.
mv-k08-v1063.inference: The whole set of principles is divided into pure and impure solely because the pure factor blocks future transmigratory merit.

mv-k08-v1064.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1064.question: Why does a manifold expanse of ritual restriction arise from the pure reality?
premises: The pure shines as filled with the three powers and as paired.
Because of this, ritual action is conceived in many ways.
The expanse of restriction arises through conceived operations and yields limited forms of enjoyment.
mv-k08-v1064.inference: The manifold system of ritual restriction is a differentiated projection of the pure reality shaped by conceived ritual operations.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of yāmalaṃ in this doctrinal context is interpretive.

mv-k08-v1065.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1065.question: What ritual complex becomes capable of yielding results in this system?
premises: An assemblage of seals and mandalas is practiced together with mantras and tantras.
In that context, yoga and related practices are included.
Such a complex becomes fit to give results.
mv-k08-v1065.inference: The combined ritual complex of seals, mandalas, mantras, tantras, and yoga is what produces the promised fruits.

mv-k08-v1066.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1066.question: How do those fixed on attaining liberation conceive the highest fruit?
premises: Some practitioners are established in a narrowed desire for attaining liberation as a fruit.
They take unlimitedness itself as the fruit in this context.
Their conception of the goal is therefore framed as an attained result.
mv-k08-v1066.inference: Even those seeking the highest liberation still conceive unlimitedness as a fruit to be attained.

mv-k08-v1067.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1067.question: Can ritual conception apply where the unlimited supreme nondual reality is known?
premises: In the unlimited and unbroken, no conception of sacrifice and the like applies.
Those whose vision transcends all that have no such ritual framing.
Even so, when the supreme nondual reality is known, desire for a fruit may still arise in some.
mv-k08-v1067.inference: Ritual conception is incompatible with the unlimited nondual, yet knowledge of that reality does not automatically abolish all fruit-seeking.
uncertainties: The token anantānav/yacchede contains an editorial slash whose exact intended segmentation is uncertain.

mv-k08-v1068.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1068.question: Why is the full hierarchical teaching presented if the highest reality transcends fruit-seeking?
premises: Because of the freedom of consciousness's own nature, some still desire fruits.
Aiming at those seekers, the teaching presents the whole system.
The presentation extends from earth up to Śiva for their fulfillment.
mv-k08-v1068.inference: The graded scriptural system is taught out of consciousness's freedom to accommodate those who still seek fruits.

mv-k08-v1069.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1069.question: Why does this teaching present the whole range up to Śiva without rejecting other manifestations?
premises: The text on concentrations teaches the range up to Śiva through many divisions.
Unlike in other systems, nothing manifested here is denied its reality.
For those abiding in the level of truth, nothing can fall into a merely rejectable level.
mv-k08-v1069.inference: Because all manifestations are grounded in truth, the teaching can include the whole range without treating any part as ultimately rejectable.

mv-k08-v1070.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1070.question: How is the culminating principle related to the Śiva-state and to the differentiated world?
premises: The principle that appears as the culmination of the seventeen sections is determined as the unsurpassed Śiva-state for those desiring attainment.
All that is taught here in the Jagadānanda appears as of opposing nature.
This entire expanse stands here because it is animated by difference.
mv-k08-v1070.inference: The culminating principle is identified with the unsurpassed Śiva-state, while the differentiated expanse is presented as its opposition-shaped manifestation for seekers.
uncertainties: jagadānande may refer to a textual section or to bliss in the world; the reference is context-dependent.

mv-k08-v1071.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1071.question: How is Maheśvara approached in the second section of the teaching?
premises: The second section presents Maheśvara as established as the self of all.
He is approached through gradual knowledge and yoga.
He is also approached through concentrations.
mv-k08-v1071.inference: In the second section, Maheśvara is worshiped as the universal self through graded knowledge, yoga, and concentrations.

mv-k08-v1072.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1072.question: What is expounded in the eighteenth chapter regarding the principles?
premises: The eighteenth chapter takes up the sequence of principles.
That sequence is presented with the net of duality, impurity, māyā, and so on removed.
The principle is fully expounded there.
mv-k08-v1072.inference: The eighteenth chapter fully expounds the purified sequence of principles beyond duality, impurity, and māyā.

mv-k08-v1073.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1073.question: Why are practices like breath control described as to be abandoned here?
premises: Breath control and similar practices are described as to be abandoned in this context.
They do not function as a means to supreme knowledge.
What is not a means to the highest knowledge is set aside at this level.
mv-k08-v1073.inference: Practices such as breath control are rejected here because they do not serve as means to supreme knowledge.

mv-k08-v1074.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1074.question: How could consciousness established within itself be produced by external practice?
premises: What is firmly established within consciousness cannot be transferred into the body of breath and mind.
If one still insists, a method of practice and yoga may be proposed.
But those who try to refine consciousness by practice face insoluble questions about what, where, from where, and how they would do it.
mv-k08-v1074.inference: Because consciousness is already inwardly established, attempts to produce or refine it through external practice are fundamentally doubtful.

mv-k08-v1075.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1075.question: Why is repeated practice unsuitable for the supreme nondual reality?
premises: Repeated practice means doing something again and again.
Such practice arises from distinctions of space and time and from connection with appearance and otherness.
The path of body, mind, breath, and senses is the domain of such distinctions.
mv-k08-v1075.inference: Therefore repeated practice belongs to the differentiated domain and cannot reach the undivided supreme reality.

mv-k08-v1076.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1076.question: How do seekers become established in the Bhairava reality?
premises: The Bhairava reality is a form dense with pure light.
Some seekers wish to enter that reality.
Resting in knowledge that shines once is sufficient for establishment.
mv-k08-v1076.inference: Therefore seekers become established in the Bhairava reality through a single resting in luminous knowledge, not through repeated practice.

mv-k08-v1077.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1077.question: What practice is declared supreme in this context?
premises: In this context a supreme and universally helpful limb is declared.
That limb is concentration.
Concentrations determined through that door may take on that same nature.
mv-k08-v1077.inference: Therefore concentration, when grounded in this realization, is the supreme and universally helpful practice.

mv-k08-v1078.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1078.question: How can confidence be placed in reasoning that lacks firm grounding?
premises: An opponent claims reasoning is ungrounded.
If reasoning is ungrounded, confidence in it seems impossible.
The same charge of groundlessness could apply to the opponent's own statement.
mv-k08-v1078.inference: The objection from groundlessness is unstable because it threatens to undermine itself.

mv-k08-v1079.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1079.question: How can scripture alone decide truth when scriptures conflict?
premises: Some hold that scripture alone is the valid means of knowledge.
There exist hosts of scriptures that contradict one another.
A contradictory set cannot by itself settle what is certain.
mv-k08-v1079.inference: Therefore scripture alone cannot serve as the final criterion when conflicting scriptures are present.

mv-k08-v1080.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1080.question: Can majority acceptance establish scriptural validity?
premises: One might propose acceptance by the great multitude as the cause of validity.
A great multitude opposed to that position is also possible.
A criterion that can be matched by its opposite lacks firm grounding.
mv-k08-v1080.inference: Therefore majority acceptance does not securely establish validity.

mv-k08-v1081.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1081.question: Is ordinary perception a secure final authority?
premises: Perception in cases like taste is sometimes overruled.
Appeal to later cognitions to correct perception can continue without end.
A criterion open to endless regress is not final.
mv-k08-v1081.inference: Therefore ordinary perception is not an unquestionable final authority.

mv-k08-v1082.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1082.question: How could practical life proceed if self-awareness were overruled?
premises: The opponent's critique would overrule even self-awareness.
Practical dealings depend on some trusted awareness.
A person skilled in managing differences still needs a basis for action.
mv-k08-v1082.inference: If self-awareness were overruled, coherent practical life would become impossible.

mv-k08-v1083.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1083.question: Why does the Trika position not fall into groundlessness?
premises: The Trika position rests on the all-full supreme ocean of Bhairava.
That ocean is present everywhere.
What is grounded everywhere cannot become ungrounded at some time or place.
mv-k08-v1083.inference: Therefore the Trika position does not suffer from groundlessness.

mv-k08-v1084.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1084.question: For whom does reasoning lose its charge of groundlessness?
premises: Reasoning is accused of groundlessness in general.
Some have crossed the ocean of reasoning and received the supreme nectar of awareness.
For such knowers, reasoning is no longer cut off from its ultimate ground.
mv-k08-v1084.inference: Therefore reasoning is not ungrounded for those established in the supreme nectar of awareness.

mv-k08-v1085.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1085.question: Why do ordinary forms of reasoning fail to reach Śiva?
premises: All parts of reasoning can operate without touching self-awareness.
Without self-awareness, reasoning lacks its highest ground.
Śiva is the final fruit only when that ground is reached.
mv-k08-v1085.inference: Therefore reasoning that does not touch self-awareness does not attain Śiva as its final fruit.

mv-k08-v1086.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1086.question: What is the true aim of scripture and where do the deluded go astray?
premises: The meaning of all scripture has non-difference as its essence.
Difference may be brought forth within scripture for the sake of attaining non-difference.
Those of deluded intellect take delight in that difference itself.
mv-k08-v1086.inference: Therefore the deluded mistake a provisional teaching of difference for scripture's final aim.

mv-k08-v1087.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1087.question: Does reasoning have any use even within non-difference?
premises: Reasoning is skilled at cutting down arguments rooted in difference.
The ultimate teaching is non-difference.
A tool suited to difference may or may not serve non-difference.
mv-k08-v1087.inference: The question arises whether reasoning retains any usefulness in the domain of non-difference.

mv-k08-v1088.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1088.question: What is the supreme means to the nonduality that graces the universe?
premises: Even reasoning is not truly fitting in the vision of supreme nonduality.
Supreme nonduality is of the nature of grace to the universe.
A means suited to that reality must itself be immediate and living.
mv-k08-v1088.inference: Therefore the text declares the Heart, whose nature is vibration, as the supreme means to that nonduality.

mv-k08-v1089.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1089.question: What is the self-reflective awareness that arises in the Heart?
premises: The Heart is made of awareness.
In it arises a self-reflective awareness that is the wonder of full consciousness.
That awareness can suddenly dissolve the outward flashing of the universe.
mv-k08-v1089.inference: The Heart's self-reflective awareness is an immediate, all-at-once absorption of universal manifestation into full consciousness.

mv-k08-v1090.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1090.question: What is the universal vibration described in this teaching?
premises: There are first and last moments in the grasping of things.
In those moments a state appears that is full of surging bliss.
That bliss is identified with the bliss of the whole world.
mv-k08-v1090.inference: This state is called the universal vibration.

mv-k08-v1091.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1091.question: How does the Heart's flashing lead into the triad of powers?
premises: The Heart's flashing forth is manifest as pure being.
This flashing belongs to the abode of emission.
Recognition of that flashing corresponds to entry into the triad of powers.
mv-k08-v1091.inference: To the extent one recognizes the Heart's flashing as being, one enters the triad of powers.

mv-k08-v1092.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1092.question: How is the Heart defined and from where is it emitted?
premises: The Heart is the supreme nectar of Bhairava awareness.
It is situated on the trident of the powers of will, knowledge, and action.
From the supreme abode it is emitted outward.
mv-k08-v1092.inference: The Heart is both the nectar of Bhairava awareness and the emissive center of the three powers.

mv-k08-v1093.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1093.question: How does the universe arise from the supreme Self?
premises: The universe flashes forth in the lordly supreme Self.
That universe is of the nature of consciousness.
It is situated on the trident of the three powers and proceeds by the path of emission on the Śāmbhava level.
mv-k08-v1093.inference: The universe is a conscious emission from the supreme Self through the three powers on the Śāmbhava path.

mv-k08-v1094.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1094.question: What is the Heart that always shines forth?
premises: The emitted reality is proclaimed as pure being.
The Heart is full and of the nature of 'I'.
Its shining is the flashing of the union of Śiva and Śakti.
mv-k08-v1094.inference: The Heart is the ever-shining fullness of being, identical with the 'I' as the flashing union of Śiva and Śakti.

mv-k08-v1095.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1095.question: What cosmic processes appear within the Heart?
premises: The Heart is the locus described as 'here'.
Creation, dissolution, and maintenance occur in countless sequences.
These sequences are associated with Hara, Viṣṇu, and the lotus-born creator.
mv-k08-v1095.inference: All cosmic cycles of creation, maintenance, and dissolution shine forth eternally within the Heart.

mv-k08-v1096.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1096.question: How is the Heart's vibration revealed to one not ready for the prior method?
premises: Some may not be able to enter immediately through the previously stated collection of reasonings.
Such a person still needs access to the Heart's vibration.
The śākta means provides an alternative path.
mv-k08-v1096.inference: For one unable to enter by the prior reasoning, the Heart's vibration is revealed through the path of the śākta means.

mv-k08-v1097.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1097.question: What practice leads the practitioner into the Heart's inner path?
premises: The breath can be impelled at the tip of the trident.
That impelling opens access to the path of the Heart.
Within that path one may rest in the moon-digit of consciousness.
mv-k08-v1097.inference: By impelling the breath at the trident's tip and resting in the inner moon-digit of consciousness, the practitioner enters the Heart's path.
uncertainties: The exact yogic referent of 'tip of the trident' is technical and context-dependent.

mv-k08-v1098.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1098.question: What must be abandoned to move beyond the lower states?
premises: There are states beginning with absence of bliss.
These states are situated amid the five elements.
Progress requires suddenly abandoning that level.
mv-k08-v1098.inference: By abruptly abandoning the elemental level and its joyless states, the practitioner moves beyond them.

mv-k08-v1099.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1099.question: How should one progress through the stages of bliss toward the peaceful ground?
premises: One intent on complete rest should abandon the former stage and ascend to the higher stage.
The ground consisting of innate bliss follows the peaceful state.
Progression through stages is oriented toward that innate-bliss ground.
mv-k08-v1099.inference: Therefore the practitioner should sequentially transcend lower stages to reach the innate-bliss ground that leads to peace.

mv-k08-v1100.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1100.question: What gives rise to the states of nirānanda and parānanda?
premises: Nirānanda and parānanda are connected with puruṣa and the unborn principle.
Bliss expands from the experience of undivided and divided masses of objects.
The character of these two states arises from that expansion of bliss.
mv-k08-v1100.inference: Therefore nirānanda and parānanda arise from the bliss generated by experiencing undivided and divided objects in relation to puruṣa and the unborn.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'ajāta' (unborn) is context-dependent and may indicate a specific tattva.

mv-k08-v1101.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1101.question: Where and how does the state of great bliss manifest?
premises: A wondrous state of great bliss follows a leftward course.
This state shines forth in the great abode of Bhairava.
That abode is consciousness which has assumed all.
mv-k08-v1101.inference: Therefore the state of great bliss manifests in the all-encompassing consciousness of Bhairava through a leftward mode.
uncertainties: The technical sense of 'vāmācārā' (leftward course) may carry ritual or energetic connotations.

mv-k08-v1102.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1102.question: How does great bliss continue within the all-encompassing triad?
premises: Great bliss becomes consciousness-bliss.
It proceeds again within a specific triad.
That triad has assumed all the right, left, and upper aspects.
mv-k08-v1102.inference: Therefore great bliss, transformed into consciousness-bliss, continues to unfold within the triad that integrates right, left, and upper.

mv-k08-v1103.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1103.question: In what modes can phenomena appear within the triad that grasps duality and nonduality?
premises: The triad in every way grasps both duality and nonduality.
Phenomena may appear as undivided.
Phenomena may appear as divided or as both divided and undivided.
mv-k08-v1103.inference: Therefore within the triad that comprehends duality and nonduality, phenomena can manifest as undivided, divided, or both.

mv-k08-v1104.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1104.question: How do beings arise in relation to the fivefold bliss and universal bliss?
premises: Beings are joined with the fivefold states of bliss beginning with innate bliss.
There is a state of intense universal bliss.
Beings arise from that state of intense universal bliss.
mv-k08-v1104.inference: Therefore beings, structured by the fivefold bliss states, arise from the state of intense universal bliss.

mv-k08-v1105.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1105.question: What distinguishes the states of innate bliss and nirānanda?
premises: Innate bliss is founded only on resting in the subject aspect.
Nirānanda arises from resting only in emptiness.
Each state is defined by its specific locus of rest.
mv-k08-v1105.inference: Therefore innate bliss and nirānanda are distinguished by whether rest occurs in the subject aspect or in mere emptiness.

mv-k08-v1106.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1106.question: How does supreme bliss arise in relation to the field of objects?
premises: Supreme bliss arises from resting in the domain of the object.
The object field can be filled on all sides with the collision of infinite objects.
Resting in that fully filled object field gives rise to supreme bliss.
mv-k08-v1106.inference: Therefore supreme bliss fully arises when awareness rests in the object domain, even when it is filled with infinite objects.

mv-k08-v1107.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1107.question: What defines the state called great bliss?
premises: The means of knowing can be engaged in savoring.
All masses of knowers and knowns can be apprehended and devoured.
A state skilled in that devouring arises through such savoring.
mv-k08-v1107.inference: Therefore the state called great bliss is defined by savoring through the means of knowing and devouring the apprehension of all knowers and knowns.

mv-k08-v1108.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1108.question: When does consciousness-bliss arise in its unconditioned fullness?
premises: One may attain a rest that is unconditioned and utterly full.
Consciousness-bliss is not nourished by the inert.
Such rest corresponds to that consciousness-bliss.
mv-k08-v1108.inference: Therefore when unconditioned and utterly full rest is attained, consciousness-bliss arises, independent of the inert.

mv-k08-v1109.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1109.question: What characterizes the reality in which consciousness-bliss shines?
premises: In that reality there is no divided state having an inert form.
In that reality there is no division whatsoever.
That reality shines forth on all sides.
mv-k08-v1109.inference: Therefore the locus of consciousness-bliss is an undivided, non-inert reality that shines everywhere without limitation.

mv-k08-v1110.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1110.question: What did the teacher identify as the abode of universal bliss?
premises: There is a reality of unstruck awareness nourished by supreme nectar.
The teacher declared that reality to be the abode of universal bliss.
This identification is presented as authoritative.
mv-k08-v1110.inference: Therefore the abode of universal bliss is unstruck awareness nourished by supreme nectar, as taught by the guru.

mv-k08-v1111.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1111.question: How should one establish rest where contemplative practices do not primarily apply?
premises: There are states where contemplation and similar practices have no primary applicability.
Rest must still be established in such states.
The yoga of heart-utterance provides the method for establishing that rest.
mv-k08-v1111.inference: Therefore where contemplative practices do not primarily apply, rest should be established through the yoga of heart-utterance.

mv-k08-v1112.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1112.question: What is the complete rest attained there called, and how is it brought about?
premises: Complete rest can be attained in that state.
That complete rest is called supreme nonduality.
It arises through the application of the breath-staff and the equalizing of before and after.
mv-k08-v1112.inference: Therefore the complete rest attained there is supreme nonduality, realized by equalizing before and after through the breath-staff practice.
uncertainties: The technical meaning of 'prāṇadaṇḍa' (breath-staff) is practice-specific.

mv-k08-v1113.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1113.question: How is the yogin's ground distinguished from that of the ordinary person?
premises: The yogin abides on a ground described as sprinkled by the mansion of the pendant lotus tetrad.
Bondage and liberation are divided for the ordinary person.
The yogin's realization is situated elsewhere than that division.
mv-k08-v1113.inference: Therefore the yogin stands on a consecrated inner ground beyond the ordinary division of bondage and liberation.
uncertainties: The imagery of 'catuṣkikāmbujālambilambikāsaudha' is esoteric and may refer to a specific yogic diagram.

mv-k08-v1114.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1114.question: By what nature does the yogin operate in this realization?
premises: The yogin operates by an unsurpassed nature.
That nature functions through the activity of speech.
It is united with the dissolution and flourishing of the supreme I in reflective consciousness.
mv-k08-v1114.inference: Therefore the yogin acts from the unsurpassed nature that expresses itself through speech and the play of supreme I-consciousness.

mv-k08-v1115.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1115.question: What illuminates and fills the field of experience in this yogic process?
premises: A sun whose nature is the true twelve phases is present.
That sun is emptied of the force of effort.
By it the entity is illuminated, filled, and fully pervaded.
mv-k08-v1115.inference: Therefore the effortless sun of the twelve phases illuminates, fills, and pervades the field of experience.
uncertainties: The 'twelve phases' likely refer to a specific esoteric solar or energetic schema.

mv-k08-v1116.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1116.question: What happens to the phases when the fire of awakening is entered?
premises: An agent possessing the sixteen named phases enters the fire of awakening.
The phases are slowed by the power of devouring that.
That agent completely releases the phases.
mv-k08-v1116.inference: Therefore entry into the fire of awakening by the sixteen-phased power leads to the complete release of the phases.
uncertainties: The identity of the 'sixteen named phases' is technical and context-dependent.

mv-k08-v1117.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1117.question: What is attained by the one who has internalized all principles and reached emission?
premises: The agent has internalized infinite principles from ka to kṣa on all sides.
That agent has attained emission while remaining in an unchanged state.
Four life-giving powers are attained in that condition.
mv-k08-v1117.inference: Therefore the one who has internalized all principles and attained emission in an unchanged state obtains the four life-giving powers.
uncertainties: The 'four life-giving powers' are not named explicitly in this verse.

mv-k08-v1118.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1118.question: What inner stance characterizes the yogin in relation to the beingness of all things?
premises: The yogin is joined to the heart where reflection on the essence of beingness is absent.
The yogin rests upon the eye of the yogin lineage fit for outward emission.
This stance concerns the beingness of all beings.
mv-k08-v1118.inference: Therefore the yogin abides in a non-reflective heart-essence while resting in the lineage-eye that governs outward emission.
uncertainties: The phrase 'yogikulanetra' is esoteric and may denote a specific lineage center or faculty.

mv-k08-v1119.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1119.question: What stairway of powers is always established in the state of Rudra-union?
premises: A stairway-garland of powers is always established in the state of Rudra-union.
That stairway extends through consciousness, breath, quality, and body.
This structure is presented as permanently established.
mv-k08-v1119.inference: Therefore in the state of Rudra-union there is an ever-established stairway of powers spanning consciousness, breath, quality, and body.

mv-k08-v1120.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1120.question: How is the ground of emission approached through the power of vibration?
premises: Release occurs through emission moving within the womb of vibration.
After that release, the ground of emission is embraced.
That ground enjoys the state of the fish-womb.
mv-k08-v1120.inference: Therefore by vibratory emission one releases and embraces the emission-ground characterized by the fish-womb state.
uncertainties: The term 'matsyodaradaśā' is a technical yogic image whose precise referent is contextual.

mv-k08-v1121.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1121.question: What supreme phase is reached upon ascending the ground of the trident?
premises: One ascends the ground of the trident connected with the three channels.
There is a supreme phase that is present in all, pervading all, and life-giving to all.
Ascending that ground gives access to that supreme phase.
mv-k08-v1121.inference: Therefore by ascending the trident-ground connected with the three channels, one reaches the supreme all-pervading, all-vivifying phase.

mv-k08-v1122.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1122.question: What is the nature of the upper stairway of powers reached in this ascent?
premises: The ascent reaches a stairway-garland of powers ending in the brow-center, bindu, and nāda.
This stairway expands and contracts.
It resorts to unity in sequence.
mv-k08-v1122.inference: Therefore the upper stairway of powers, culminating in brow-center, bindu, and nāda, dynamically expands and contracts while maintaining sequential unity.

mv-k08-v1123.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1123.question: How is the goddess characterized in her rhythmic activity?
premises: The goddess contracts and expands like the alternating flow of a she-donkey and a mare.
She repeatedly dissolves and creates streams of beings.
She is full of these dissolving and emerging streams of existence.
mv-k08-v1123.inference: The goddess is the dynamic power whose rhythmic contraction and expansion continually dissolves and manifests the totality of beings.
uncertainties: The exact ritual or physiological sense of rāsabhī-vaḍavā-āsrāva is not fully explicit in the verse alone.

mv-k08-v1124.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1124.question: Where is the goddess established and what does she unify?
premises: The goddess unifies the great root spike into a single emissive abode.
She rests in the heart of Bhairavī.
Bhairavī is characterized as nourishing all beings.
mv-k08-v1124.inference: The goddess is the unified emissive ground of the root power, established in Bhairavī's heart as the nourisher of all beings.
uncertainties: The technical referent of mahāmūlaśūla may depend on the surrounding tantric context.

mv-k08-v1125.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1125.question: What supreme qualities define this goddess?
premises: She earns the supreme name through the bold act of filling all.
She is without beginning and end.
She is inclined toward the whole universe.
mv-k08-v1125.inference: This goddess is the timeless, all-filling supreme power whose nature is oriented toward the universe.

mv-k08-v1126.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1126.question: What does one gain after attaining this goddess?
premises: The goddess is the moonlight of the consciousness-moon in the space of heart-awareness.
She is the ruler of the triad.
Having attained her, one obtains and also causes others to obtain.
mv-k08-v1126.inference: Attaining the goddess who rules the triad and illumines heart-awareness yields complete attainment for oneself and for others.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tritaya (triad) is context-dependent in Trika usage.

mv-k08-v1127.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1127.question: What happens when a yogi seeks to enter the supreme by contemplative means?
premises: The yogi uses means situated in the contemplative body.
The supreme reality is present as the goal.
When the yogi desires to enter that supreme, he first trembles.
mv-k08-v1127.inference: The initial approach to the supreme through contemplative embodiment produces a trembling in the yogi.

mv-k08-v1128.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1128.question: Why does the yogi tremble when approaching the supreme?
premises: For hundreds of past births the yogi has been certain of identity with the body.
He imagines consciousness and body to be one like water and dust.
This ingrained identification resists the entry into the supreme.
mv-k08-v1128.inference: The trembling arises because long-established body-identification conflicts with the dissolution of the assumed unity of consciousness and body.

mv-k08-v1129.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1129.question: Into what does the yogi first enter and by what process?
premises: The goal is the perfectly full conscious self.
That self is free from māyā known as difference.
Entry occurs first through the process of overpowering by one's own power.
mv-k08-v1129.inference: The yogi's initial entry is into undivided, full consciousness, achieved by the force of his own awakened power.

mv-k08-v1130.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1130.question: What state arises before firm establishment in the supreme self?
premises: A sleep-like state may arise for the yogi.
That state loosens immersion in the body.
It appears as trembling until firm establishment in the supreme self arises.
mv-k08-v1130.inference: Before stable absorption in the supreme self, the yogi passes through a trembling, sleep-like loosening of bodily fixation.

mv-k08-v1131.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1131.question: What is the unmanifest sign described in this state?
premises: This is an unmanifest sign.
Its nature consists of man, power, and Śiva.
In it this universe is dissolved and it is understood as standing within.
mv-k08-v1131.inference: The unmanifest sign is the triadic ground of man, power, and Śiva in which the universe is inwardly dissolved.

mv-k08-v1132.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1132.question: How does absorption become clear in relation to the paths and the body?
premises: The whole aggregate of paths has already been determined as situated in the body.
That same reality unfolds from within.
By the force of its unfolding, absorption may become clear.
mv-k08-v1132.inference: Absorption becomes explicit when the path-structure already present in the body unfolds from within.

mv-k08-v1133.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1133.question: What arises in the mind-principle when it vibrates in a special way?
premises: The mind-principle abides in a state of special vibration.
From the fullness of Śakti's radiance, consciousness-bliss arises.
That consciousness-bliss internalizes the supreme essence of mantra-power.
mv-k08-v1133.inference: Special vibration of the mind-principle yields consciousness-bliss charged with the inner essence of mantra-power through Śakti's radiance.

mv-k08-v1134.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1134.question: How is the manifest-unmanifest sign characterized in scripture?
premises: This sign consists of man and power.
It is both manifest and unmanifest.
Scripture describes it as flowering with the sap of the fruit of accomplishment.
mv-k08-v1134.inference: The manifest-unmanifest sign, composed of man and power, is taught as the source that yields the fruit of accomplishment.

mv-k08-v1135.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1135.question: How is the manifest sign distinguished and how do the three signs relate?
premises: The manifest sign is said to consist only of man.
The unmanifest and mixed signs were described as involving Śiva and Śakti.
This threefold division is an arrangement of one single vibration.
mv-k08-v1135.inference: The three signs are not separate realities but three structured modes of one vibration.

mv-k08-v1136.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1136.question: What is the value of external liṅga worship without knowledge of this inner sign?
premises: Some worship an external fixed liṅga with a heart separated from knowledge of this sign.
Such worship is mere effort.
Mere effort without that knowledge does not yield the intended fruit.
mv-k08-v1136.inference: External liṅga worship is fruitless when disconnected from knowledge of the inner sign.

mv-k08-v1137.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1137.question: Under what condition does the manifest self-sign arise?
premises: The manifest sign is called the sign of the self.
It rests on the human form.
It arises when the external universe is filled with non-difference from the body.
mv-k08-v1137.inference: The manifest self-sign appears when embodied identity expands to pervade the external universe without difference.

mv-k08-v1138.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1138.question: What happens to the first sign when the yogi is absorbed in great bliss?
premises: The yogi becomes absorbed on the ground of great bliss.
From that absorption the first sign responds.
The first sign comes directly face-to-face.
mv-k08-v1138.inference: Absorption in great bliss makes the primal sign immediately present to the yogi.
uncertainties: The referent of ādyaṃ liṅgam (first/primal sign) is interpreted from the preceding triadic sequence.

mv-k08-v1139.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1139.question: Where should the practitioner abide and what is that place?
premises: One should always abide in this sign.
Abiding there means being intent on resting in worship.
This sign is the heart of the yoginīs, the temple of supreme bliss.
mv-k08-v1139.inference: Stable worship consists in continual abiding in the inner sign, which is the yoginīs' heart and the abode of supreme bliss.

mv-k08-v1140.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1140.question: What do the wise attain in that abode of bliss?
premises: The place contains the bliss-abodes of the previously taught seed, womb, parts, and emission.
In that place the wise gather an indescribable attainment.
That attainment is identity with the reality there.
mv-k08-v1140.inference: In the inner bliss-abode of seed, womb, and emission, the wise realize an ineffable identity.
uncertainties: The technical mapping of bīja, yoni, aṃśa, and visarga follows prior doctrine not fully spelled out in this verse.

mv-k08-v1141.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1141.question: How do the deities abide in that bliss-filled abode?
premises: The whole host of deities abides there.
They abide without effort.
Their nature is eternally arisen consciousness in a bliss-filled abode.
mv-k08-v1141.inference: In that supreme abode the deities are effortlessly present as ever-risen consciousness.

mv-k08-v1142.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1142.question: How can contraction and expansion appear in Lord Bhairava?
premises: Lord Bhairava appears as contraction and its opposite.
In reality contraction and expansion are not present in him.
Yet that appearance shines.
mv-k08-v1142.inference: The play of contraction and expansion is a luminous appearance within Bhairava, not a real limitation of him.

mv-k08-v1143.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1143.question: What renews the universe in that supreme state?
premises: A stream of bliss arises from the impact of consummation.
This universe is sprinkled by that stream of bliss.
Being so sprinkled, the universe casts off oldness.
mv-k08-v1143.inference: The bliss of consummation continually renews the universe by removing its worn-out condition.

mv-k08-v1144.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1144.question: Is deliberate effort required to enter that ever-present reality?
premises: Effortful striving treats entry as a task to be accomplished.
That reality is ever risen like the sun.
An ever-risen sun does not need to be examined by a lamp.
mv-k08-v1144.inference: Because the supreme reality is always already manifest, forced effort is not the true means of entering it.

mv-k08-v1145.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1145.question: In what two modes may the yogi be established?
premises: The yogi may be established in his own self on the level of Śiva's conscious vibration.
Or he may engage the special streams of external beings.
In that external engagement he delights the circle of yoginīs.
mv-k08-v1145.inference: The yogi's realization can abide inwardly in Śiva-vibration or outwardly in the yoginī-delighting play of manifested beings.

mv-k08-v1146.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1146.question: What is the supreme seal that remains even without external objects?
premises: Even in the absence of an object such as a pot, a state remains.
That state consists of the appearance of universal vibration.
It is the supreme Bhairava seal with inward focus and outward gaze.
mv-k08-v1146.inference: The supreme Bhairava seal is the abiding state of universal vibration that persists beyond dependence on particular objects.

mv-k08-v1147.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1147.question: What does the supreme Śaiva goddess resort to after that state?
premises: The supreme Śaiva goddess resorts to a further domain.
That domain is fashioned by the play of her freedom.
That domain consists of manifold efficacies.
mv-k08-v1147.inference: After the prior state, the supreme Śaiva goddess turns to the stream of phenomena created by her autonomous play and filled with diverse efficacies.
uncertainties: The antecedent of yad/tataḥ depends on the immediately preceding verses (1145–1146).

mv-k08-v1148.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1148.question: How does the goddess abide within the stream of phenomena?
premises: The goddess enters the stream of phenomena.
She is joined to the savor of eager, awakening reflective awareness.
She touches the true ground of particular vibration, which is Śakti.
mv-k08-v1148.inference: Within the stream of phenomena, the goddess abides by contacting Śakti as the true ground of particular vibration, infused with eager reflective savor.

mv-k08-v1149.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1149.question: What effect does this presiding power have on one's own mantras?
premises: The mantras are presided over by this power.
In its manifestation the mantras become active.
They attain the state of possessing autonomy even amid various accomplishments.
mv-k08-v1149.inference: When empowered by this Śakti, one's own mantras gain autonomy and function freely even in diverse accomplishments.
uncertainties: The fused token svamantrāstatprakāśane contains internal sandhi; analyzed as a single surface unit per instruction.

mv-k08-v1150.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1150.question: What stance does the yogin attain toward manifestation?
premises: The yogin becomes firmly established in activity beyond rejection and acceptance.
All that appears shines forth through its connection with universal manifestation.
What shines forth does so as consciousness itself.
mv-k08-v1150.inference: Established beyond acceptance and rejection, the yogin recognizes all manifestation as shining forth in the nature of consciousness.

mv-k08-v1151.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1151.question: What does the yogin abandon when seeing the visible as non-different from consciousness?
premises: The yogin sees the visible from a mode of non-difference.
This seeing arises from the wonder of consciousness.
He abandons the timid state caused by wretched craving for practical efficacy.
mv-k08-v1151.inference: Seeing the visible as non-different through the wonder of consciousness, the yogin gives up the anxious dependence on practical efficacy.

mv-k08-v1152.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1152.question: What level does the yogin enter after abandoning that timid state?
premises: The yogin abandons the timid, efficacy-craving state.
As long as he remains in that abandonment, a transition occurs.
He effortlessly enters the Bhairava-like Śāmbhava and supreme level.
mv-k08-v1152.inference: By remaining free of anxious craving, the yogin effortlessly enters the Bhairava Śāmbhava, the supreme level.
uncertainties: chāṃbhavabhūmikām shows an initial consonant variation from expected śāmbhava; transcribed exactly as given.

mv-k08-v1153.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1153.question: How does everything appear to one whose awareness is entered by this state?
premises: The yogin's awareness is entered by the supreme Bhairava state.
He sees everything as pervaded by the nature of light.
Consciousness itself shines as that light.
mv-k08-v1153.inference: For one entered by this state, all things are seen as pervaded by light because consciousness alone shines.

mv-k08-v1154.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1154.question: Why can the unmanifest not become manifest through connection with something else?
premises: What is unmanifest does not become manifest merely by connection with something to be manifested.
This point has already been explained at length.
The reason is given as previously established.
mv-k08-v1154.inference: Manifestation cannot be produced in the unmanifest by external relation, as has already been demonstrated.

mv-k08-v1155.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1155.question: What inner condition characterizes the yogin in this intense practice?
premises: All mental activities dissolve through union with great audacity.
The mind becomes filled by a concentrated mass of its own rays.
These two descriptions characterize the same yogin.
mv-k08-v1155.inference: The yogin's state is marked by dissolution of all activities and saturation of the mind by concentrated self-radiance.
uncertainties: svaraśmyogha contains internal sandhi (sva-raśmi-ogha) within the single token; analyzed without splitting the row.

mv-k08-v1156.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1156.question: What happens when the yogin remains without thought and without clearly seen difference?
premises: The yogin thinks of nothing.
He abandons the state of clearly seen difference.
As long as he remains thus, the previously described levels respond.
mv-k08-v1156.inference: Remaining thought-free and beyond clearly seen difference brings the previously described levels into presence.

mv-k08-v1157.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1157.question: Which levels and faculties come into play in this state?
premises: The previously described levels come into presence.
