These levels are the sole causes for burning away worldly intoxication.
The divine aggregate of senses, once overgrown by difference, is also involved.
mv-k08-v1157.inference: The liberating levels and the divine senses, freed from the dominance of difference, present themselves to the yogin.
uncertainties: The phrase saṃsārasadmadāhaikahetavaḥ can be read as burning worldly intoxication; the exact nuance of sat-mada is context-sensitive.

mv-k08-v1158.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1158.question: Under what condition does the inward-turning sense aggregate become fruitful?
premises: The sense aggregate becomes an instrument of play that nourishes freedom.
It can remain fruitful in inward turning.
This fruitfulness occurs when it stands inwardly for even one moment.
mv-k08-v1158.inference: When the senses, as instruments of freedom's play, remain fruitfully turned inward for a moment, a transformative result follows.

mv-k08-v1159.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1159.question: What happens to the universe when awareness rises through that inward door?
premises: Awareness rises through the door of inward turning.
Its great flame melts the universe's apparent solidity.
The universe then comes to rest in supreme bliss.
mv-k08-v1159.inference: Through inwardly risen awareness, the universe is dissolved and comes to rest in the ocean of supreme bliss.

mv-k08-v1160.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1160.question: What result comes from resting in the savor of that bliss?
premises: The yogin rests in drinking the savor of supreme bliss.
He satisfies the goddesses of awareness.
This leads to freedom from fear of death and birth.
mv-k08-v1160.inference: By abiding in that blissful savor and satisfying the powers of awareness, the yogin soon becomes free from fear of death and birth.

mv-k08-v1161.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1161.question: How does awareness return to its own mass-like nature after congealing into body and world?
premises: Awareness congeals and takes on the form of body, senses, and known objects.
By the proper method, that congealed state dissolves.
When dissolved, awareness becomes its own dense mass of consciousness.
mv-k08-v1161.inference: Awareness that has congealed into body, senses, and objects returns, through dissolution, to its own dense conscious nature.

mv-k08-v1162.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1162.question: What method leads to the awareness of Bhairava's bliss?
premises: Minds overpowered by external objects undergo outward emergence by a certain method.
That same method can be applied in reverse.
The very same method yields awareness of Bhairava's bliss.
mv-k08-v1162.inference: The same method by which consciousness is drawn outward to objects can lead to the awareness of Bhairava's bliss.

mv-k08-v1163.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1163.question: How is the consciousness-made state established through the yoginī transmission?
premises: The same method is received through the lineage of the yoginī's mouth.
Through it the entry of impurity is shaken off.
The state that remains is made of consciousness.
mv-k08-v1163.inference: Received through the yoginī-mouth transmission, that method removes impurity and establishes the consciousness-made state.

mv-k08-v1164.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1164.question: What inner structures are affected when the yogin slightly opens the mouth of awareness?
premises: The yogin slightly opens the mouth of awareness.
All inner circles connected with senses and channels depend on this opening.
Their traversal is activated by that opening.
mv-k08-v1164.inference: A slight opening of the mouth of awareness activates all inner circles and channels of the senses.
uncertainties: The referent of sarvā is syntactically compressed; taken as all the cakra-structures implied by the compound.

mv-k08-v1165.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1165.question: What kind of expansion occurs when consciousness turns toward itself?
premises: The inner structures are activated by the opening of awareness.
Because of turning toward consciousness, they expand suddenly.
That expansion consists in the absence of difference among grasped objects.
mv-k08-v1165.inference: When consciousness turns toward itself, the system expands into a state where differences among grasped objects fall away.

mv-k08-v1166.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1166.question: What breaks the difference between grasper and grasped?
premises: The relation between grasper and grasped appears as a difference.
That difference is split at once.
The splitting occurs through attainment of the lineage rooted in the yoginī's mouth.
mv-k08-v1166.inference: The subject-object difference is immediately broken through the yoginī-mouth transmission.

mv-k08-v1167.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1167.question: What seals the yogin in this realization?
premises: An experience-giving seal acts immediately.
By it the yogin is wholly sealed.
He becomes absorbed in direct Bhairava, the consciousness-form presiding over all.
mv-k08-v1167.inference: The immediate seal of direct experience absorbs the yogin wholly in Bhairava as the all-presiding consciousness.
uncertainties: tandritaḥ is read as absorbed/entranced; nuance depends on tantric usage.

mv-k08-v1168.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1168.question: What does the yogin obtain when sealed in this wonder-filled absorption?
premises: The yogin is entered by wonder.
He obtains awareness of his own self.
That awareness remains even amid the arising and passing of various objects.
mv-k08-v1168.inference: In wonder-filled absorption, the yogin gains self-awareness that does not depart despite changing phenomena.

mv-k08-v1169.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1169.question: Why does water in a low tank not flow elsewhere by effort?
premises: Water situated low in a tank does not flow elsewhere.
Even effort cannot make it flow out.
It is incapable because it only fills that limited place.
mv-k08-v1169.inference: Like low tank-water, a limited state cannot overflow elsewhere because it is only sufficient to fill itself.

mv-k08-v1170.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1170.question: What happens when the inner source fills the system abundantly?
premises: The inner door can pour in a stream of water.
When filled by that inner stream, the system overflows.
The resulting streams flow in all directions.
mv-k08-v1170.inference: When filled from the inner source, consciousness overflows outward in streams facing all directions.
uncertainties: The compound tvantaḥdvāravāridhārasaṃpūritaṃ is read as tu + antaḥ-dvāra-vāri-dhārā-saṃpūritaṃ; internal sandhi is within the single token.

mv-k08-v1171.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1171.question: How does consciousness manifest beings without division?
premises: Consciousness opens forth by its own forceful surge.
It makes the portions of beings shine.
It shines them without division and as non-different from itself.
mv-k08-v1171.inference: Self-manifesting consciousness reveals all beings as undivided and identical with itself.

mv-k08-v1172.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1172.question: What happens when consciousness does not sink into closure?
premises: Consciousness may for a moment not become an object of closing.
From that, māyā dissolves.
When māyā dissolves, the Bhairava level shines forth.
mv-k08-v1172.inference: A brief non-closure of consciousness dissolves māyā and reveals the Bhairava state.

mv-k08-v1173.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1173.question: What is the source of the appearance of division?
premises: A limitation born of conceptualization may afterward show division.
That very showing of division is māyā.
Māyā belongs to the free one and reveals a vision of difference.
mv-k08-v1173.inference: The appearance of division is māyā, a power of the free absolute that manifests difference.

mv-k08-v1174.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1174.question: Can māyā arise for one established in pure opening?
premises: For one established only in the opening of consciousness, māyā is rootless.
What is rootless cannot arise.
In the method of the unsurpassed self, much explanation is unnecessary.
mv-k08-v1174.inference: In the unsurpassed self, māyā cannot arise for one abiding in pure opening.

mv-k08-v1175.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1175.question: Can any limb of yoga truly serve as a means here?
premises: In reality no limb of yoga has the status of a means.
The own nature of this reality is without form.
It is without form because it is free from limitation.
mv-k08-v1175.inference: Since the reality is formless and unlimited, no yogic limb can function as a true means to it.

mv-k08-v1176.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1176.question: Why is the means here also not a means?
premises: This means is also a non-means because it blocks effortful activity.
It is devoid of exhalation and inhalation practices.
It is devoid of regulation of body and breath.
mv-k08-v1176.inference: The so-called means transcends ordinary technique by abandoning effortful bodily and breath controls.
uncertainties: The exact analysis of tanuvātanauḥ is compressed in the transmitted form.

mv-k08-v1177.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1177.question: How can the mind cross over while immersed in objects?
premises: The self may be sinking in the ocean of difference.
Even then, this mind can carry the self across.
This occurs even while the mind is in an object-bound taste.
mv-k08-v1177.inference: The mind, rightly oriented, can rescue the self from difference even amid sensory immersion.

mv-k08-v1178.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1178.question: Why does forcibly restraining the mind fail to soften it inwardly?
premises: A gourd without holes does not become inwardly soft.
Some people restrain the mind's own path as one restrains a horse.
Such forced restraint does not produce inner receptivity.
mv-k08-v1178.inference: Forcible suppression of the mind does not create inner openness, just as a sealed gourd does not soften.

mv-k08-v1179.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1179.question: What happens to the mind when it is forcibly broken?
premises: For those who practice breaking the mind, it runs off by countless wrong paths.
The mind keeps asking what this is.
Even in pain, the mind mostly longs restlessly.
mv-k08-v1179.inference: Suppressing the mind scatters it into wrong paths and restless craving rather than settling it.

mv-k08-v1180.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1180.question: How does knowledge produce dispassion even toward pleasure?
premises: Through knowledge one may become dispassionate even toward pleasure.
Knowledge clarifies this and that as they are.
The teacher has instructed this in many ways in his own teaching.
mv-k08-v1180.inference: True dispassion arises from knowledge, as the teacher repeatedly taught.

mv-k08-v1181.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1181.question: What makes the activities of the senses fall away naturally?
premises: Sense activities fall away through indifference and dispassion alone.
When they are forcibly controlled, they do not settle.
As long as they are controlled by force, they act turbulently.
mv-k08-v1181.inference: Natural dispassion quiets the senses, while forcible control agitates them.

mv-k08-v1182.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1182.question: Is forced sensory withdrawal a true release from bondage?
premises: There is a so-called withdrawal applied to the net of the senses.
When bondage is already firmly established, such withdrawal is imposed on it.
That imposed withdrawal becomes a binding like diamond cement.
mv-k08-v1182.inference: Forced pratyāhāra, applied over established bondage, strengthens bondage rather than removing it.

mv-k08-v1183.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1183.question: How can one know inner ease amid objects and experiences?
premises: One may be amid objects, their enjoyment, and the pleasure or pain arising from them.
Even while immersed in mind, one may not enter them with fear.
In that state, one knows the inner ease of the dissolution of mental activities.
mv-k08-v1183.inference: Freedom from fearful identification allows one to know inner stillness even amid experience.
uncertainties: The backslash tokens are preserved as editorial line-break markers from the source list.

mv-k08-v1184.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1184.question: What reality should be accepted when senses and objects are fully present?
premises: The self shines in the heart as the great light of consciousness.
The senses and objects such as taste may still be present and active.
A yogi can abide clearly in a state whose arising is barren of difference and filled with fullness.
mv-k08-v1184.inference: Even amid active senses and objects, the yogi should accept the nondual reality of consciousness.

mv-k08-v1185.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1185.question: Is non-discrimination only bondage or also a means to liberation?
premises: It is commonly said that non-discrimination is supreme bondage.
That common saying is only a partial report.
Non-discrimination itself can become the supreme stairway to gaining liberation.
mv-k08-v1185.inference: Non-discrimination is not merely bondage; rightly understood, it can serve as the path to liberation.

mv-k08-v1186.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1186.question: Where can deliberate concentration truly be placed?
premises: One is told to abandon deliberate concentrations.
In the full, concentration is not fitting.
In the not-full, concentration does not attain true being.
mv-k08-v1186.inference: Deliberate concentration cannot establish truth in either fullness or incompleteness, so it should be abandoned.

mv-k08-v1187.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1187.question: Where can the yogi realize fullness amid all states of activity?
premises: Wherever union with bliss arises, there the own nature is full.
If the delusion of difference is known, one may reach peace there.
Even in waking and all states, the yogi can become lord of the great wheel of consciousness while active.
mv-k08-v1187.inference: Recognizing bliss and dispelling the delusion of difference allows the yogi to realize fullness in every state.
uncertainties: The two '---' tokens mark a lacuna in the transmitted text.
The fragmentary sequence 'te veti' is preserved as given and may be textually uncertain.

mv-k08-v1188.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1188.question: Why do people attain the supreme in different ways?
premises: One person digging a well feels accomplished only when water is reached.
Another is satisfied with water already at hand.
The attainment of the supreme likewise follows varied ways.
mv-k08-v1188.inference: The method of attaining the supreme differs according to readiness and circumstance.

mv-k08-v1189.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1189.question: How can a person be freed from the bondage of difference?
premises: This reality is without means.
Ordinary thinking relies on the connection of means and goal.
The question remains how a person is freed from the bondage of difference.
mv-k08-v1189.inference: Since the reality is beyond means, liberation from difference cannot be explained by ordinary means-and-goal logic.

mv-k08-v1190.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1190.question: Why does the scripture teach means if the reality is without means?
premises: The reality itself is without means.
Still, instruction can operate by relational functioning.
This scripture therefore teaches means in many ways.
mv-k08-v1190.inference: Scriptural means are taught provisionally, by relation, even though the ultimate reality is beyond means.

mv-k08-v1191.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1191.question: How do provisional means lead the deluded toward the real?
premises: Children are led clearly into the real nature of sound through written letters.
The letters are provisional aids, not the final reality.
In the same way, the deluded are led gradually by provisional means.
mv-k08-v1191.inference: Provisional means function pedagogically to lead the unprepared toward the real.

mv-k08-v1192.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1192.question: Why does a nondual scripture still teach worship and meditation?
premises: The supreme reality is nondual.
Even so, provisional instruction is needed for that purpose.
Therefore this scripture respectfully teaches worship, meditation, and related practices.
mv-k08-v1192.inference: Nondual teaching can include provisional practices as skillful means for realization.

mv-k08-v1193.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1193.question: How can any pleasing sensory state become a path to realization?
premises: Anything that delights the mind may arise in any state of the senses.
That delight can be joined to the abode of true awareness.
It can be joined to the opening of Brahman.
mv-k08-v1193.inference: Any mind-delighting sensory experience can become a support for realization when joined to the abode of awareness.

mv-k08-v1194.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1194.question: How does ordinary experience become effortless worship of the supreme powers?
premises: Absorption in true being follows the self.
That absorption supports the rite of worship of the wheel of supreme Kula powers.
Through this, experience naturally becomes an instrument without effort.
mv-k08-v1194.inference: When grounded in absorption in true being, experience effortlessly becomes worship of the supreme powers.

mv-k08-v1195.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1195.question: How does the yogin perform continuous inner worship of the deity?
premises: The yogin makes the support-ground washed by a moment of sprinkling with the essence of wonder.
The yogin offers flowers of innate nature taken from the mind, bearing their own fragrance.
The offering proceeds by the method of the priceless vessel of one's own heart full of bliss-nectar.
The worship takes place in the temple of the body together with the goddess.
mv-k08-v1195.inference: Therefore the yogin worships the deity day and night through an internalized ritual using the body's own faculties and states.
uncertainties: The exact parsing of devārcaye as a denominative or compound verb is interpretive but does not affect the sense.

mv-k08-v1196.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1196.question: What manifests when one abides anywhere in one's own reflective awareness?
premises: One may stand anywhere in this manner.
Such standing is by the nature of one's own reflective awareness.
In that very place the entry of the three powers occurs.
mv-k08-v1196.inference: Therefore the entry of the three powers shines forth threefold wherever one abides in one's own reflective awareness.

mv-k08-v1197.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1197.question: How does the threefold shining expand into a fuller state of repose?
premises: The shining manifests ninefold.
This arises from the stated twelve wheels.
The repose occurs in a single moment.
mv-k08-v1197.inference: Therefore the repose of that ninefold shining, arising from the twelve wheels, occurs in a single moment and has a state of one hundred and eight.

mv-k08-v1198.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1198.question: How is the yogin's speech understood in relation to this unified state?
premises: That state is clearly discerned as one alone, numbering a hundred.
In this way the yogin's expression arises within that state.
Whatever speech of this yogin may occur is included in that discernment.
mv-k08-v1198.inference: Therefore any speech whatsoever of the yogin is understood as belonging to that single unified state.
uncertainties: The compound kiṃcanaitasya is taken as kiṃcana + etasya; the fused surface is preserved as one token.

mv-k08-v1199.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1199.question: How does the yogin's speech function as mantra practice on the unsurpassed path?
premises: Whatever speech arises from the yogin belongs to the unified state.
That speech becomes mantra practice on the unsurpassed path.
This occurs constantly without depending on the presence of inner fuel.
mv-k08-v1199.inference: Therefore the yogin's speech itself becomes continuous mantra practice on the unsurpassed path without requiring any inner fuel.

mv-k08-v1200.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k08-v1200.question: What happens when all beings are understood to enter that blazing awareness?
premises: A fire blazes with hundreds of front flames spreading from all the masses of senses.
All beings may be considered to enter there.
This entry is presented as a matter of reflective understanding.
mv-k08-v1200.inference: Therefore, if the entry of all beings into that blazing awareness is reflectively understood, that very locus is the site of universal absorption.

mv-k09-v1201.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1201.question: What is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition?
premises: Entities suddenly and forcibly lose their gross form by being burned up.
By their own nature they attain unity with the blazing light of great awareness.
This attainment of unity with awareness-light is identified as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.
mv-k09-v1201.inference: The supreme offering is the sudden dissolution of gross forms into the blazing light of awareness.

mv-k09-v1202.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1202.question: Why do entities offered into the fire of awareness kindle that fire?
premises: Entities properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness abandon division and difference.
By their own power those same entities kindle that fire of awareness.
The abandonment of difference and the kindling occur together in the act of offering.
mv-k09-v1202.inference: Entities offered into awareness both lose their separateness and intensify the fire of awareness by their own power.

mv-k09-v1203.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1203.question: What becomes fit for meditation in this system of manifestation?
premises: By its own will and by the force of the nature of creation, consciousness manifests a sense-object in front.
Whatever sense-object is thus manifested becomes available for meditation.
Meditation is grounded in what is freely manifested, not in an abstract formlessness alone.
mv-k09-v1203.inference: Any sense-object freely manifested by the creative nature of consciousness is fit to serve as an object of meditation.

mv-k09-v1204.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1204.question: Why is a particular form established as an object of meditation within formless consciousness?
premises: The abode of consciousness is formless yet consists of all forms.
Those who seek specific results require a determinate focus for meditation.
Therefore some particular form is established as the object of meditation for such seekers.
mv-k09-v1204.inference: Within formless, all-form consciousness, a particular form is posited as the meditation object for result-seeking practitioners.

mv-k09-v1205.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1205.question: How can a particular form be sought within a nondual fullness?
premises: Reality is nondual and full, yet practical action still occurs within it.
A person fetching water sets aside other forms and seeks a pot.
The selection of a particular form does not negate the underlying fullness.
mv-k09-v1205.inference: Seeking a particular form within nondual fullness is analogous to choosing a pot to fetch water without denying the fullness of reality.

mv-k09-v1206.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1206.question: What causes a particular form to generate a particular conception of result?
premises: The supreme Lord's restrictive unfolding operates within the fullness of consciousness.
Through that unfolding, some particular form becomes salient.
That particular form gives rise to a corresponding conception of a specific result.
mv-k09-v1206.inference: The Lord's self-restriction makes a particular form produce a particular conception of fruit for the practitioner.

mv-k09-v1207.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1207.question: What kind of meditation unfolds for one who desires no particular result?
premises: Some practitioners act from the fullness of consciousness rather than from desire for a result.
Such a practitioner does not wish for any specific fruit.
For that person, meditation naturally takes the form of all forms at all times.
mv-k09-v1207.inference: One established in full consciousness experiences meditation as the spontaneous unfolding of all forms, without restriction to a particular object.

mv-k09-v1208.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1208.question: How does experience arise for a Kula yogin intoxicated by the Bhairava essence?
premises: The Kula yogin reels from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence.
In that state, experiences arise spontaneously and unpredictably.
Whatever arises, and in whatever manner it arises, is part of that reeling absorption.
mv-k09-v1208.inference: For the Kula yogin intoxicated by Bhairava essence, any experience arises spontaneously in whatever form it takes.

mv-k09-v1209.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1209.question: What is recognized as the seal in the unsurpassed teaching?
premises: A bodily absorption arises whose nature is delight and melting.
This absorption takes the whole world as its seal.
In the unsurpassed teaching, that world-embracing absorption is identified as the true seal.
mv-k09-v1209.inference: The true seal in the unsurpassed teaching is the bodily absorption of delight and melting that embraces the world.

mv-k09-v1210.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1210.question: In whose heart does this rare method of yoga abide?
premises: This method of yoga abides in the heart of only some rare person.
It becomes present when the wheel of consciousness becomes clear.
Such clarity arises quickly for one who is in his final birth.
mv-k09-v1210.inference: This yoga method abides in the heart of a rare person whose consciousness-wheel clears, especially one nearing final birth.

mv-k09-v1211.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1211.question: What happens to one in whom this yoga has matured, even while still embodied?
premises: Such a person may still be seen by ordinary people and remain in the condition of bodily bondage.
When yoga has matured in him, his state changes inwardly.
He attains an extraordinary awareness in an instant.
mv-k09-v1211.inference: Even while outwardly embodied and observed, one in whom yoga has matured instantly attains a special awareness.
uncertainties: The phrase 'na kṣaṇāt kām api saṃvidam' is syntactically compressed; the sense taken is that he attains an incomparable awareness in a moment.

mv-k09-v1212.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1212.question: What did the earlier teachers affirm about this state of yoga?
premises: The earlier teachers considered this very yogic state.
They strongly affirmed a specific consequence of it.
That consequence is the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.
mv-k09-v1212.inference: The earlier teachers held that in this yoga the delusions of worldly experience cease to be present.

mv-k09-v1213.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1213.question: What is the stance toward rival philosophical and scriptural systems in this context?
premises: Multiple rival systems are enumerated, including Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, worldly, Pancaratra, ritual, and Siddhanta views.
The verse dismisses further engagement with them.
The dismissal implies they are insufficient for the matter at hand.
mv-k09-v1213.inference: For the present yogic realization, reliance on these rival philosophical and scriptural systems is unnecessary.

mv-k09-v1214.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1214.question: How do practitioners of different systems operate within their own frameworks?
premises: Different practitioners cultivate portions of knowledge and action suited to them.
They are established in their own respective procedures.
They act according to what is fitting within those procedures.
mv-k09-v1214.inference: Each system's adherents function coherently within their own procedures according to their own sense of appropriateness.

mv-k09-v1215.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1215.question: What extensive preparatory process was carried out in the Shambhava branches?
premises: A sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was performed.
This sequence was carried out by many branches of the Shambhava teaching.
The process was very extensive.
mv-k09-v1215.inference: The Shambhava tradition developed an extensive preparatory sequence of practices across its many branches.
uncertainties: The agricultural imagery (sowing, implanting, digging) may be metaphorical for spiritual preparation; taken literally in gloss and metaphorically in sense.

mv-k09-v1216.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1216.question: What is the unsurpassed fruit of the extensive Shambhava process?
premises: The prior extensive Shambhava process is likened to cultivating a tree of consciousness-Bhairava.
That cultivation yields a fruit.
The fruit is identified as unsurpassed, beyond external observances from life-stage duties to ascetic marks.
mv-k09-v1216.inference: The unsurpassed fruit of the Shambhava cultivation is the realization of consciousness-Bhairava, not mere external observances.

mv-k09-v1217.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1217.question: What happens to worldly pageantry for those resting in this yoga beyond ritual difference?
premises: In this state, no difference is found between acts done and acts not done.
Practitioners come to rest in that yoga.
For those resting there, the pageantry of worldly existence loses its hold.
mv-k09-v1217.inference: For those who rest in the yoga where done and undone make no difference, the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.

mv-k09-v1218.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1218.question: Why does worldly existence dissolve when one savors the nectar of awareness?
premises: Worldly existence is compared to a mass of snow in the great summer.
When the juicy nectar of awareness is savored, a transformative condition is present.
Under that condition, worldly existence melts away by itself.
mv-k09-v1218.inference: Savoring the nectar of awareness causes worldly existence to dissolve spontaneously, like snow in summer heat.

mv-k09-v1219.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1219.question: How fully are the countless raptures of this realization presented here?
premises: Great raptures flow forth from this realization in countless numbers.
Their manifestations were already explained at length previously.
In this treatment by Abhinavagupta, only some of them are determined and set forth.
mv-k09-v1219.inference: Although the raptures of this realization are innumerable and previously detailed, only a few are definitively presented here.
uncertainties: The compound 'atrābhinavagupte' may refer to Abhinavagupta's present exposition or to a context within his teaching; taken as a locative reference to his treatment here.

mv-k09-v1220.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1220.question: Who is capable of delighting in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava?
premises: In the fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee is the true connoisseur, not the fly.
The worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava is similarly subtle and discriminating.
One deluded by duality cannot delight in it, but a rare fit person can.
mv-k09-v1220.inference: Only a rare connoisseur, not one deluded by duality, delights in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava.

mv-k09-v1221.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1221.question: Why is no purification required for one established in this realization?
premises: For one established in this state, no purification needs to be performed anywhere.
The world is understood as having Bhairava as its very nature.
If the world is Bhairava in nature, nothing in it can be truly impure.
mv-k09-v1221.inference: Because the world is of the nature of Bhairava, no purification is necessary for one established in that realization.

mv-k09-v1222.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1222.question: What logical problem arises if one tries to purify an allegedly impure mass of beings?
premises: If the mass of beings is taken as impure, some means of purification must be proposed.
Any proposed purifier would itself require justification or purification.
This leads to infinite regress and futile mutual dependence.
mv-k09-v1222.inference: Attempting to purify an allegedly impure world produces infinite regress and futile mutual dependence.

mv-k09-v1223.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1223.question: Why is purity not an independent reality if it depends on removing impurity?
premises: If impurity is concealed or removed, what is called purity also dissolves.
That shows purity is constituted by opposition to impurity.
What depends on an opposite is not established by its own nature, unlike blue.
mv-k09-v1223.inference: Purity is not an intrinsic nature but a relative designation dependent on the opposition of impurity.

mv-k09-v1224.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1224.question: Why is there no insistence on grasping or rejecting sense objects for one established in supreme Bhairava consciousness?
premises: Purity and impurity are not intrinsic realities but relative designations.
For one whose nature is supreme Bhairava consciousness, sense objects do not bind by their own status.
Enjoyership surges forth spontaneously from that consciousness itself.
mv-k09-v1224.inference: Because enjoyership arises spontaneously from supreme Bhairava consciousness, there is no insistence on either grasping or rejecting sense objects.

mv-k09-v1225.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1225.question: Does any alternative path achieve coherence once this path is rejected?
premises: Everything established here fits coherently by this path.
Rejecting this path leaves no alternative framework.
No other proposed path attains logical coherence.
mv-k09-v1225.inference: Therefore the stated path alone is coherent and alternatives fail.

mv-k09-v1226.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1226.question: How can initiation that cuts away impurities be possible in the dualist view?
premises: Initiation is defined as that which cuts away impurities.
The dualists hold a view of real difference.
The possibility of such cutting must be explained within that view.
mv-k09-v1226.inference: Initiation as removal of impurities is difficult to justify on the dualist position.

mv-k09-v1227.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1227.question: How can impurity cover a self whose nature is consciousness and all-pervading?
premises: Impurity is supposed to cover the self.
The self is of the nature of consciousness.
An all-pervading being cannot undergo a covering action.
mv-k09-v1227.inference: The covering of a conscious, all-pervading self by impurity is incoherent.

mv-k09-v1228.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1228.question: Can light ever be covered by darkness given light's nature?
premises: Light is never covered by darkness.
The arising of light is itself the act of destroying darkness.
What destroys darkness cannot be concealed by it.
mv-k09-v1228.inference: Consciousness, like light, cannot be covered by impurity.

mv-k09-v1229.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1229.question: How can obstruction-type covering apply to an all-pervading being that does not move?
premises: Covering is defined as obstruction of something that moves, like rays.
The all-pervading self does not have motion.
Obstruction presupposes motion.
mv-k09-v1229.inference: Covering as obstruction cannot apply to the all-pervading self.

mv-k09-v1230.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1230.question: Is covering merely concealment of knowability rather than alteration of nature?
premises: Covering by a cloth conceals a pot's knowability.
Such covering does not alter the pot's own nature.
Concealment of knowability is distinct from change of essence.
mv-k09-v1230.inference: If covering means only concealment of knowability, it does not change the self's nature.

mv-k09-v1231.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1231.question: Can selves of conscious nature be covered by concealment of knowability?
premises: Selves, being of the nature of consciousness, do not admit knowability as objects.
Covering as concealment of knowability presupposes object-knowability.
Applying such covering to selves is not even verbally coherent.
mv-k09-v1231.inference: The notion of covering selves by concealment of knowability is incoherent.

mv-k09-v1232.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1232.question: If atomic selves are knowable to the Lord, does that contradict their conscious nature?
premises: An opponent claims the atomic selves are knowable to the Lord.
What is of the nature of consciousness is not an object of knowledge.
Making consciousness an object would conceal its conscious nature.
mv-k09-v1232.inference: The claim that conscious selves are knowable to the Lord is problematic.

mv-k09-v1233.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1233.question: What does the phrase 'awareness is knowable' resemble in its self-contradiction?
premises: The expression 'awareness is knowable' treats consciousness as an object.
This is like saying 'my mother is barren'.
Both expressions are internally self-contradictory.
mv-k09-v1233.inference: Calling consciousness knowable is a self-contradictory statement.

mv-k09-v1234.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1234.question: Does the Lord's failure to know covered selves harm omniscience or the selves?
premises: If the Lord does not know covered atomic selves, his omniscience is impaired.
The selves themselves suffer no loss from not being known.
The problem falls on the doctrine of omniscience, not on the selves.
mv-k09-v1234.inference: The dualist account threatens the Lord's omniscience rather than explaining the selves' condition.

mv-k09-v1235.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1235.question: Does covering by impurity obstruct omniscience the way covering obstructs ordinary seeing?
premises: When a blue object is uncovered, the knower sees it; when covered, seeing does not occur.
By analogy, one might claim impurity obstructs omniscience.
The analogy assumes the knower is subject to obstruction.
mv-k09-v1235.inference: The opponent argues that impurity could obstruct even an omniscient knower by analogy with perception.

mv-k09-v1236.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1236.question: Why does the perceptual analogy fail to show obstruction of the true knower?
premises: In ordinary perception, a cloth obstructs outgoing rays of sight.
The obstruction affects the rays, not the knower's essence.
There is no possibility of covering the conscious knower itself.
mv-k09-v1236.inference: The analogy from perception does not establish that the knower can be covered.

mv-k09-v1237.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1237.question: Can a non-pervading impurity cover an all-pervading reality?
premises: Impurity is said to be non-pervading.
The self or consciousness is pervading.
A non-pervading thing cannot by its nature make an all-pervading space non-empty.
mv-k09-v1237.inference: A non-pervading impurity cannot coherently cover an all-pervading reality.

mv-k09-v1238.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1238.question: If impurity produces no real effect on the self, how can it be capable of covering?
premises: The self is not subject to modification by impurity.
If impurity produces no effect, it cannot act on the self.
Covering requires the capacity to produce an effect.
mv-k09-v1238.inference: If impurity does not affect the self, it cannot coherently cover it.

mv-k09-v1239.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1239.question: Is covering merely the bare coexistence of impurity with the atomic self?
premises: An opponent defines covering as the mere existence of impurity.
On this view, the atomic self is called covered simply by having impurity as a second.
This reduces covering to coexistence rather than an action.
mv-k09-v1239.inference: The opponent redefines covering as mere association with impurity.

mv-k09-v1240.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1240.question: Does defining covering as mere impurity-existence absurdly imply covering of Shiva?
premises: If covering is only the mere existence of impurity, the definition is too broad.
By that reasoning, even those of the stated nature could be said to have covering.
The definition would absurdly extend covering to Shiva.
mv-k09-v1240.inference: The mere-existence definition of covering leads to an absurd overextension.

mv-k09-v1241.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1241.question: If the self covered by impurity does not know impurity, must another impurity be posited?
premises: A self covered by impurity would not know that impurity.
Non-awareness of impurity would itself need explanation.
Positing another impurity to explain this leads to regress.
mv-k09-v1241.inference: The covering account risks an infinite regress of impurities.

mv-k09-v1242.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1242.question: If the self knows impurity without vidya and kala, does that imply omniscience?
premises: An opponent suggests the self might simply know impurity.
Knowing impurity without vidya and kala would imply omniscience.
If impurity were known, the self could abandon it by various means.
mv-k09-v1242.inference: Allowing the self to know impurity directly creates further doctrinal problems.

mv-k09-v1243.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1243.question: If the self could abandon known impurity by contrived means, what covering would remain?
premises: If impurity were known, the self could abandon it by various contrived means.
Abandoning impurity would remove its covering effect.
This undermines the claim that impurity necessarily covers the self.
mv-k09-v1243.inference: The knowability of impurity would make its covering effect eliminable by the self.

mv-k09-v1244.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1244.question: How would the self become knower and doer of objects if impurity were removed by itself?
premises: Ordinary knowing and doing concern objects like pots.
The opponent appeals to vidya and kala as the basis of limited knowing and doing.
The question is how these arise if impurity alone explains bondage.
mv-k09-v1244.inference: The account of impurity must also explain the emergence of limited agency and knowledge.
uncertainties: The dual future form bhaviṣyataḥ is metrically/contextually unusual; taken as future sense.

mv-k09-v1245.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1245.question: Who is deceived by the claim that inert maya and its products can manifest consciousness?
premises: Maya is of an inert nature.
Kala and the other limiting factors arise from maya.
Those with deluded understanding are misled by this account, not the wise.
mv-k09-v1245.inference: The dualist appeal to inert maya and its products is a deception for the deluded.

mv-k09-v1246.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1246.question: How can the non-conscious manifest all-pervading consciousness with limiting qualities?
premises: What is non-conscious cannot manifest consciousness.
Consciousness is all-pervading.
Limiting qualities like finitude cannot properly qualify all-pervading consciousness.
mv-k09-v1246.inference: The dualist account cannot explain how inert factors manifest and limit consciousness.

mv-k09-v1247.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1247.question: Can the Lord manifest consciousness through kala and vidya if qualification suits only partite things?
premises: Being qualified is fitting only for things that have parts.
All-pervading consciousness is not partite.
An opponent suggests the Lord could manifest consciousness through kala and vidya.
mv-k09-v1247.inference: The appeal to divine manifestation through limiting instruments does not resolve the problem of qualifying consciousness.

mv-k09-v1248.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1248.question: If God can manifest consciousness fully, why would liberation from eternal impurity be delayed?
premises: God could manifest consciousness in all ways without incapacity.
If impurity is eternal and God insists on it, liberation is unexplained.
Divine capacity and eternal bondage are in tension.
mv-k09-v1248.inference: The dualist account cannot explain delayed liberation if God is both capable and related to eternal impurity.

mv-k09-v1249.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1249.question: Why is the claim that mala's obstructing power sometimes ceases and sometimes operates rejected?
premises: The opponent claims impurity has an obstructing power.
That power is said to cease in some cases and operate in others.
Such selective operation is declared foolish speech.
mv-k09-v1249.inference: The doctrine that mala's obstructing power alternates arbitrarily is untenable.

mv-k09-v1250.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1250.question: If insentient things cannot deliberate, how can mala's power vary without God as cause?
premises: Insentient things lack deliberation.
Without deliberation, selective cessation or operation cannot occur.
The opponent may therefore admit God as the cause even there.
mv-k09-v1250.inference: To explain mala's varying operation, the opponent is pushed to make God the cause.

mv-k09-v1251.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1251.question: For what reason would God activate mala's power or make it cease again?
premises: If God causes mala's power to operate, a motive is required.
If God causes it to cease after activation, a motive is required.
No such motive has been established.
mv-k09-v1251.inference: Making God the controller of mala's power raises an unanswered problem of divine motive.

mv-k09-v1252.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1252.question: If God acts from autonomy, why posit mala or its maturation at all?
premises: The opponent may answer that God acts from sheer autonomy.
If autonomy is sufficient, the plenary principle alone can be accepted.
Positing darkness-like impurity and its maturation becomes unnecessary.
mv-k09-v1252.inference: Appealing to divine autonomy undermines the need for mala and the doctrine of its ripening.

mv-k09-v1253.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1253.question: Why does the doctrine of mala's maturation contradict mala's supposed permanence?
premises: Maturation involves connection with another state.
Acquiring another state destroys a thing's fixed nature.
Therefore the claim that souls act from impurity under God's will is undermined.
mv-k09-v1253.inference: If mala matures, it cannot be eternally fixed, so explanations built on its fixed connection fail.

mv-k09-v1254.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1254.question: What follows for the claim that creation favors the soul desirous of enjoyment?
premises: The opponent says the bound soul, intent on enjoyment, is favored by creation.
The preceding arguments undermine the basis of that claim.
A doctrine whose basis is undermined is struck at the root.
mv-k09-v1254.inference: The view that creation is a favor to the enjoyment-seeking soul is fundamentally refuted.

mv-k09-v1255.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1255.question: How is mala understood if the Lord is fully autonomous?
premises: The knowers understand mala as mere play of self-concealment.
The all-pervading Lord is autonomous.
An autonomous Lord can manifest anything within himself.
mv-k09-v1255.inference: Mala is not an independent substance but the Lord's free play of self-concealment.

mv-k09-v1256.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1256.question: If karma is accepted, how can a universal dissolution still be explained?
premises: The opponent also accepts karma as a principle.
Karma's connection with souls may still be present.
A universal dissolution is nevertheless asserted.
mv-k09-v1256.inference: The acceptance of karma creates a difficulty for explaining a total dissolution.

mv-k09-v1257.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1257.question: How are great dissolution and great creation possible if karma persists?
premises: Great dissolution and great creation are asserted.
The opponent replies that karma becomes restrained by God's will.
This reply must explain how restraint occurs.
mv-k09-v1257.inference: The appeal to God's will shifts the problem to how karma is restrained.

mv-k09-v1258.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1258.question: Does God restrain karma by its own inactivity or by depending on another karma?
premises: Either God restrains karma through karma's inactivity or by relying on another karma.
These are mutually distinct explanatory options.
If the first option is taken, a problematic possibility follows.
mv-k09-v1258.inference: The attempt to explain restraint forces a dilemma with undesirable consequences.

mv-k09-v1259.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1259.question: What happens to God's sovereignty if karma, not God, explains cosmic cycles?
premises: If the proposed divine control is impossible, God's sovereignty is undermined.
Creation, dissolution, and related processes would then arise from karma alone.
A God without effective control is not sovereign in that respect.
mv-k09-v1259.inference: Explaining cosmic cycles by karma alone displaces the Lord's sovereignty.

mv-k09-v1260.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1260.question: If God restrains karma without regard to karma, why would he not restrain it always?
premises: Suppose God restrains karmas independently of karma itself.
An independent restrainer has no karmic reason to restrain only sometimes.
Therefore perpetual restraint would follow.
mv-k09-v1260.inference: Divine independence in restraining karma leads to the absurdity of permanent restraint.

mv-k09-v1261.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1261.question: Can producing enjoyment be karma's intrinsic nature if it depends on another condition?
premises: The opponent claims karma's nature is to produce enjoyment.
A nature that depends on another condition is not intrinsic.
The proposed karmic nature is said to depend on another condition.
mv-k09-v1261.inference: Producing enjoyment cannot be karma's intrinsic nature if it is externally conditioned.

mv-k09-v1262.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1262.question: What counts as the true intrinsic nature of karmas?
premises: The intrinsic nature of things is independent of other conditions.
Karmas must be assessed by what they are without external dependence.
What karmas are apart from the Lord's direction would be their own form.
mv-k09-v1262.inference: Only the form karmas have independently of the Lord's direction could be their true nature.

mv-k09-v1263.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1263.question: Why would God awaken karmas dissolved in pralaya or still continuing?
premises: Some karmas are dissolved in universal dissolution, others continue.
If God awakens them, a purpose for that awakening is required.
The text challenges what is accomplished by those karmas.
mv-k09-v1263.inference: Divine awakening of karmas lacks a clear justification.
uncertainties: The form dṛsṛṣṭair is read as transmitted; its exact intended form is uncertain.

mv-k09-v1264.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1264.question: If karmas are for mala's maturation, what can they do to an all-pervading self?
premises: One might claim karmas awaken for the maturation of impurity.
The doctrine of mala's maturation has already been rejected.
The self is all-pervading, so karma's effect on it is problematic.
mv-k09-v1264.inference: Neither mala-maturation nor action on an all-pervading self justifies awakening karmas.

mv-k09-v1265.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1265.question: Where has this issue been examined, and what analogy illustrates divine agency?
premises: The examination has already been elaborated at length.
The potter analogy uses clay, stick, wheel, and threads.
In that analogy, the intelligent Lord stands as the true agent.
mv-k09-v1265.inference: The prior detailed analysis supports locating true agency in the intelligent Lord rather than in inert instruments.

mv-k09-v1266.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1266.question: Where does the potter's agency stand in cases like naturally sprouting seeds?
premises: The potter analogy is used to explain agency.
Some effects, like sprouting in uncultivated seeds, occur without such instrumental crafting.
Agency must be located where it actually operates.
mv-k09-v1266.inference: The analogy shows that human-like instrumental agency does not explain all production.

mv-k09-v1267.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1267.question: What principle explains distinguishing good and bad deeds by their fruits if causality is inconsistently assigned?
premises: One might grant causality at an earlier stage but deny it later.
Such selective assignment lacks a clear principle.
Good and bad deeds are distinguished by differences in their fruits.
mv-k09-v1267.inference: The distinction of deeds by their fruits requires a coherent account of causality.

mv-k09-v1268.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1268.question: If God is autonomous, why would his will unfold as harmful to others?
premises: Good and bad deeds are distinguished by their fruits.
One might attribute this distinction to God's will alone.
An autonomous God would then be responsible for adopting a will that harms others.
mv-k09-v1268.inference: Attributing moral differentiation to God's autonomous will raises the problem of divine cruelty.

mv-k09-v1269.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1269.question: How can a God full of compassion will harm, and can karma's nature explain the fruits instead?
premises: God is described as always filled with compassion.
A compassionate God should not adopt a will that harms others.
The opponent replies that karma gives such fruits by its own nature.
mv-k09-v1269.inference: The appeal to God's compassion conflicts with harmful divine will, prompting a shift to karma's nature.

mv-k09-v1270.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1270.question: Why would God promulgate varied scripture if karma operates by its own nature?
premises: Expiation and similar acts are said to pacify karma.
God is portrayed as considering this and teaching accordingly.
He promulgates scripture with varied instructions.
mv-k09-v1270.inference: The role of expiation and divine teaching complicates the claim that karma functions purely by its own nature.

mv-k09-v1271.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1271.question: What principle justifies saying karmas have such a nature by themselves?
premises: One may claim Śaiva teaching or karmas simply have such a nature.
The text asks what principle supports that claim.
Ordinary people infer a seed's nature from repeated observation.
mv-k09-v1271.inference: Appealing to 'own nature' is insufficient unless grounded in a valid principle of knowing.
uncertainties: The opening token śaivaṃ, may refer to Śaiva scripture or to a Śaiva explanation; the syntax is compressed.

mv-k09-v1272.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1272.question: Can the Lord's action ever be explained without his own will?
premises: Ordinary people know regularities from the usage and observation of earlier generations.
The Lord is not limited in the same way as ordinary knowers.
Divine action cannot be separated from the Lord's own will.
mv-k09-v1272.inference: Unlike ordinary empirical inference, the Lord's causality is never without his own will.

mv-k09-v1273.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1273.question: If the Lord observes the diversity of karmic fruits, can individual selves still be agents?
premises: The Lord has observed the skillful diversity of the fruits of actions.
If the Lord were the sole doer of all, individual selves could not be doers in any way.
If individual selves are not doers, the Lord would not be an all-doer with respect to action-barren beings.
mv-k09-v1273.inference: Therefore the Lord's all-doership cannot exclude the agency of individual selves.

mv-k09-v1274.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1274.question: Is the concept of karma coherent when viewed from a dualistic standpoint?
premises: From a dualistic viewpoint, the notion called karma is not well-reasoned.
Only a brief summary of this issue is given here.
A fuller elaboration has been shown elsewhere.
mv-k09-v1274.inference: Therefore the dualistic account of karma is rejected here in brief, with detailed refutation deferred.

mv-k09-v1275.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1275.question: How can the one conscious Lord be called connected with diverse karma?
premises: The Lord is one and his nature is consciousness.
By his own nature he is indeed the doer of all.
Because of the diversity of manifestations he is spoken of as connected with karma.
mv-k09-v1275.inference: Therefore karma-connection is a way of speaking about the diverse expressions of the one autonomous conscious Lord.

mv-k09-v1276.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1276.question: What follows if Maya, the cause of the universe, is taken to be eternal?
premises: Maya is established as the cause of the universe.
Maya contains within itself the tattva-elements ending with earth.
The hypothesis under examination is that Maya is eternal.
mv-k09-v1276.inference: If Maya is eternal in this explicit form, consequences for cosmic dissolution must be examined.

mv-k09-v1277.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1277.question: Why would cosmic dissolution never occur if Maya's manifestation is always present?
premises: If Maya is eternally manifest, dissolution would never occur.
Manifestation is not known apart from being an object of cognition.
Cognition requires an object to be grasped.
mv-k09-v1277.inference: Therefore the status of manifestation depends on its being cognized, not on mere eternal existence.

mv-k09-v1278.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1278.question: Can the Lord remain the cause if the universe is not grasped by his supreme knowledge?
premises: The universe's graspability by the Lord's supreme knowledge is everlasting.
If that graspability did not exist, the Lord's causality would be undermined.
Causality here is tied to the Lord's knowing.
mv-k09-v1278.inference: Therefore the Lord's causality depends on the eternal presence of the universe in his supreme knowledge.

mv-k09-v1279.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1279.question: Is the Lord's creation of the world like a potter clearly making a pot?
premises: A potter clearly produces a pot using external instruments.
One might compare the Lord's creation to that process.
The Lord does not depend on a distinction between inner and outer instruments.
mv-k09-v1279.inference: Therefore the potter analogy fails to capture the Lord's mode of creation.

mv-k09-v1280.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1280.question: Why is graded cognition appropriate for a potter but not for the Lord?
premises: In pot-making, cognition that is clear, unclear, and so on is fitting.
The Lord possesses clear, noble, prior cognition.
The Lord's cognition is not subject to the same gradations as a craftsman's.
mv-k09-v1280.inference: Therefore the Lord's creative knowledge differs fundamentally from finite instrumental cognition.

mv-k09-v1281.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1281.question: What part would remain unknown if manifestation were required even in the cause?
premises: Even where dependence on manifestation is posited, the question of unknown parts arises.
For proponents of satkarya, the effect is already clearly present in the cause.
If the universe is clearly established in the cause, no part is left unknown.
mv-k09-v1281.inference: Therefore the satkarya view implies the universe's clear presence in its cause, challenging the need for manifestation-based knowing.
uncertainties: deśe may mean 'place' or 'doctrinal position'; rendered as 'view' to fit the argumentative context

mv-k09-v1282.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1282.question: Is it coherent for the universe to be clearly present in Maya alongside pervasive Siva and selves?
premises: If the universe were clearly present in Maya, that would be incongruous.
Siva and the selves are pervasive.
Pervasive realities cannot be mutually contained alongside the tattvas in the same way.
mv-k09-v1282.inference: Therefore the model of the universe being clearly located in Maya together with pervasive principles is incoherent.

mv-k09-v1283.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1283.question: How can pervasive realities coexist without their pervasiveness being concealed?
premises: If multiple pervasive realities coexist, their pervasiveness would be concealed.
The supreme expansion of consciousness is its pervasion.
In the realm of division, this pervasion is spoken of in differentiated terms.
mv-k09-v1283.inference: Therefore apparent coexistence of pervasives is explained as differentiated expression of consciousness's pervasion.

mv-k09-v1284.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1284.question: What prior analyses support the account of Maya's coverings and effects?
premises: The group of coverings born of Maya has been examined before.
The collection of instruments has been examined before.
The group of effects has also been discussed before.
mv-k09-v1284.inference: Therefore the present argument rests on previously established analyses of coverings, instruments, and effects.

mv-k09-v1285.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1285.question: What becomes of the universe if it lacks grounding in the state of Siva?
premises: The universe does not shine forth if it is devoid of resting on Siva's state.
Without that grounding, claims about its autonomy are empty.
This conclusion should be firmly understood.
mv-k09-v1285.inference: Therefore the universe's manifestation and autonomy depend on its grounding in Siva.

mv-k09-v1286.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1286.question: If impurity and related bonds are absent, how can initiation and its roles be coherent?
premises: Initiation presupposes something to be purified, such as impurity.
If impurity and so on are absent, the roles of initiation, initiator, and recipient lose their basis.
Without that basis, the ritual structure does not fit.
mv-k09-v1286.inference: Therefore initiation is unintelligible if the conditions it addresses are denied.

mv-k09-v1287.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1287.question: How can the installation of the entire path in ritual loci be justified if its basis is denied?
premises: Initiation involves installing the entire path in the disciple, path, fire, vessel, mandala, and ritual implements.
Such installation presupposes a real structure of the path and its purification.
If that structure is denied, the ritual installation lacks justification.
mv-k09-v1287.inference: Therefore the ritual placement of the entire path becomes problematic under the opponent's assumptions.

mv-k09-v1288.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1288.question: Can mere conceptualization establish the full purifier-purified structure of initiation?
premises: The full extent of the path cannot simply be present as assumed.
An objection claims the purifier-purified relation is established by the power of conception.
The text questions whether such a declaration suffices.
mv-k09-v1288.inference: Therefore the appeal to mere conception is introduced as a contested basis for initiation.

mv-k09-v1289.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1289.question: If mere imagination produced real results, what absurd consequence would follow?
premises: The opponent suggests imagined ritual structures could be effective.
If imagination alone bore fruit, fantasy achievements would be real achievements.
People rich in fantasy would triumph by attaining heavenly sovereignty.
mv-k09-v1289.inference: Therefore mere imagination cannot be sufficient to produce real ritual fruit.

mv-k09-v1290.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1290.question: Do strong conceptions produce effects in the same way as meditation can counter poison?
premises: Some effects, like poison-destruction through meditation, seem to follow strong mental focus.
The question is whether ordinary conceived states bear fruit in the same way.
The analogy to meditation is raised as a possible counterexample.
mv-k09-v1290.inference: The objection suggests strong conception may be effective, but its scope and mechanism remain to be tested.

mv-k09-v1291.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1291.question: Why does meditation fail to produce results when it is mixed with doubt?
premises: Meditation is firmness of conception.
Meditation tainted by doubt does not bear fruit.
Doubt involves grasping two opposing alternatives.
mv-k09-v1291.inference: Therefore efficacy depends on undivided firmness of consciousness, not on conception as such.

mv-k09-v1292.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1292.question: If conception alone yields the result, why seek any external non-conscious entities?
premises: Suppose the desired fruit arises from the application of conception.
External entities not made of consciousness would then be unnecessary.
The opponent still seems to desire some external entities.
mv-k09-v1292.inference: Therefore reliance on conception undermines the need for external non-conscious ritual factors.

mv-k09-v1293.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1293.question: What remains if ritual consecration is reduced to conception alone?
premises: By conception alone, consecration of the pit, fire, guru, and disciple is posited.
That same consecration appears as the fruit.
What ultimately remains is that consciousness.
mv-k09-v1293.inference: Therefore the ritual process collapses into a mode of consciousness rather than external procedure.

mv-k09-v1294.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1294.question: What is initiation if its efficacy is grounded in autonomous consciousness?
premises: Autonomous consciousness manifests in a particular form.
That manifestation should be understood as initiation.
Beings are liberated by that initiation.
mv-k09-v1294.inference: Therefore initiation is fundamentally the liberating self-manifestation of autonomous consciousness.

mv-k09-v1295.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1295.question: Why does scripture not fix strict rules for the nature, taking, or measure of ritual substances?
premises: If initiation is grounded in autonomous consciousness, external ritual details are secondary.
Scripture does not determine any fixed sequence or rule regarding the essence, taking, or measure of substances like sesame and ghee.
This absence of strict regulation follows from the primacy of consciousness.
mv-k09-v1295.inference: Therefore ritual substances and procedures are not rigidly determinative when consciousness is primary.

mv-k09-v1296.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1296.question: If the supreme form partakes of all letters, why should mantras or initiation be strictly regulated?
premises: An objection asks what fixed rule there is in mantras.
The supreme form is declared to partake of all letters.
If so, initiation too would seem not to require fixed regulation.
mv-k09-v1296.inference: Therefore the universality of the supreme form challenges rigid ritual restrictions on mantras and initiation.

mv-k09-v1297.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1297.question: How does the approved burning of letters apply to those not yet firmly established?
premises: The burning of letters, as approved by the opponent, is beneficial in its own way.
Some practitioners have not yet attained firm establishment.
A rule that benefits the established may still apply differently to the unestablished.
mv-k09-v1297.inference: Therefore, with respect to those who have not attained firm establishment, a definite rule still holds.

mv-k09-v1298.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1298.question: Why does the stated mantric rule remain useful for practitioners?
premises: This mantric rule has been declared.
The rule attains practical usefulness.
Awakened mantras operate on the path of reflective awareness.
mv-k09-v1298.inference: Therefore, the mantric rule remains effective because awakened mantras function through reflective awareness.

mv-k09-v1299.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1299.question: How do mantras come to enter and empower the teacher?
premises: The light of consciousness is inherently autonomous.
From that autonomy, mantras are constituted of agency.
Identity with that agency can be applied to the teacher.
mv-k09-v1299.inference: Therefore, by the application of identity, agency-filled mantras enter that teacher.

mv-k09-v1300.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1300.question: What effect do the mantras have on instruments and ritual procedures?
premises: The mantras make the teacher autonomous.
Even instruments can attain agency.
Initiation and other rites are accepted procedures.
mv-k09-v1300.inference: Therefore, through this empowerment, initiation and other accepted rites become effective.

mv-k09-v1301.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1301.question: How can both injunction and prohibition be justified within this framework?
premises: Agents may perform prescribed acts or face prohibitions.
Both injunction and prohibition require a coherent basis.
In this nondual framework, all such determinations are grounded here.
mv-k09-v1301.inference: Therefore, both injunction and prohibition are established here, and all is enjoined within this very standpoint.

mv-k09-v1302.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1302.question: What happens to prohibition when viewed from the nondual path?
premises: From another standpoint, all this may appear prohibited.
A prohibition is meaningful only when clearly demonstrated.
One who rests on the nondual path sees beyond fixed oppositions.
mv-k09-v1302.inference: Therefore, once prohibition is shown in that limited way, its force is questioned for one established on the nondual path.

mv-k09-v1303.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1303.question: What remains when both injunction and prohibition are transcended?
premises: Even prohibition can be treated as an injunction from a limited standpoint.
That same prohibition can itself be negated.
Own-awareness is an overflowing ocean in itself.
mv-k09-v1303.inference: Therefore, beyond the play of injunction and prohibition, the ocean of own-awareness surges abundantly within itself.

mv-k09-v1304.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1304.question: How does this vision transform the universe and the sense of difference?
premises: The whole universe is seen as beautiful with the bliss of consciousness.
Difference appears as the opposite of that nondual bliss.
The surging of own-awareness dissolves limiting oppositions.
mv-k09-v1304.inference: Therefore, this vision reveals the universe as blissful and utterly dissolves the portion of difference opposed to it.

mv-k09-v1305.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1305.question: What radiates from the knowledge-moon arising from the Supreme Lord's mouth?
premises: Knowledge is likened to a moon rising from the Supreme Lord's mouth.
That moon emits rays in all directions.
The rays shine with the mass of their own light.
mv-k09-v1305.inference: Therefore, the knowledge-moon of the Supreme Lord spreads beautiful, self-luminous rays everywhere.

mv-k09-v1306.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1306.question: How is the poison affecting all beings transformed by Shiva's moon-rays?
premises: The poison called kālakūṭa afflicts the moon of all beings.
The rays of Shiva's moon fall upon it.
Mere contact with those rays melts the poison.
mv-k09-v1306.inference: Therefore, the deadly poison of all beings is transformed into an elixir by the rays of Shiva's moon.

mv-k09-v1307.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1307.question: What is the result of continually immersing in that transformative essence?
premises: One can plunge unceasingly into that essence.
Drinking that essence causes ecstatic reeling.
Becoming that essence removes impurity and suffering.
mv-k09-v1307.inference: Therefore, by immersing in and becoming that essence, we abide pure and freed from the threefold suffering.

mv-k09-v1308.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1308.question: What is meant by the Supreme Lord's mouth in this symbolic account?
premises: The Supreme Lord's mouth is identified with power.
That power is specifically the will.
Having arisen, that will assumes the function of the knowledge-moon in differentiated states such as Īśvara.
mv-k09-v1308.inference: Therefore, the Lord's mouth symbolizes the will-power that unfolds as the knowledge-moon across differentiated levels.
uncertainties: The exact internal analysis of īśvarādibhinnasthitivijñānaśaśāṅkaśaktivṛttam is compressed; the gloss follows the most plausible compound reading.

mv-k09-v1309.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1309.question: What does the spreading mass of rays from that moon represent?
premises: From that moon a fully spread mass of rays streams forth on all sides.
The Supreme Lord possesses a power consisting of action.
That power is identified as world-pervading.
mv-k09-v1309.inference: Therefore, the mass of rays is the Supreme Lord's own action-power, which consists of the world.

mv-k09-v1310.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1310.question: What is the ultimate reality expressed by this expansion of powers?
premises: This reality is full of the three powers.
It expands as the supreme Bhairava.
Nothing different from it can exist, and its own expansion is called victory.
mv-k09-v1310.inference: Therefore, the supreme Bhairava alone expands as the fullness of the three powers, and nothing exists apart from that expansion.

mv-k09-v1311.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1311.question: How does this doctrine account for the world's conquest and multiple scriptural expressions?
premises: From that supreme reality, these powers conquer the world.
The meaning becomes manifest and fitting.
A plurality of expressions can still point to one fullness.
mv-k09-v1311.inference: Therefore, the conquest of the world and the many scriptural expressions are compatible with the one fullness of that reality.
uncertainties: The final compound vākyabhedam is syntactically compressed; taken here as the doctrine accommodating divisions of statements within fullness.

mv-k09-v1312.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1312.question: What does this single verse ultimately reveal?
premises: The preceding teaching can be gathered into one verse.
That verse expresses Bhairava as consciousness itself.
Bhairava contains the entire sequence of beings.
mv-k09-v1312.inference: Therefore, this single verse clearly explains Bhairava himself as consciousness, full of the entire sequence of beings.

mv-k09-v1313.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1313.question: How can poison become a means to immortality in this teaching?
premises: Worldly existence is likened to poison.
Those whose vision is empowered by Garuda can use poison as medicine.
Right vision transforms what is normally harmful.
mv-k09-v1313.inference: Therefore, those established in the right vision can employ even poison and attain an immortal state.

mv-k09-v1314.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1314.question: What is established by self-luminous awareness in this teaching?
premises: The teaching has shown its point to this extent.
Own-awareness is self-luminous.
Nothing can be established apart from that awareness.
mv-k09-v1314.inference: Therefore, self-luminous own-awareness establishes everything, and apart from it nothing at all is possible.

mv-k09-v1315.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1315.question: What determines whether something is truly real in this system?
premises: Reality is measured by resting in own-awareness.
Dependence on another time undermines stable reality.
Own-awareness does not require temporal validation.
mv-k09-v1315.inference: Therefore, whatever rests in own-awareness is real, and reality cannot depend on another time.

mv-k09-v1316.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1316.question: If awareness is not bound by time, how does it relate to space and manifestation?
premises: The connection of awareness with time has been refuted at length.
Own-awareness remains the basis of manifestation.
Awareness can unfold appearances as space.
mv-k09-v1316.inference: Therefore, free from time, own-awareness functions by spreading out space in whatever way it manifests.

mv-k09-v1317.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1317.question: How is the reality of a thing tested according to this criterion?
premises: Awareness functions like a touchstone for testing appearances.
What cannot be placed upon that touchstone lacks confirmation.
Even scripture calls such a thing unreal and fit only for doubt.
mv-k09-v1317.inference: Therefore, whatever cannot be established in awareness is unreal and remains only an object of doubt.
uncertainties: The phrase saṃvidy akṣamayyāṃ is read as 'in awareness consisting of the senses/touchstone of the senses'; the metaphor is compressed.

mv-k09-v1318.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1318.question: What distinguishes valid scripture and method from mere talk?
premises: Speech that does not ascend to own-awareness is no better than idle talk.
Scripture and method claim authority.
Only what unfolds within awareness has genuine validity.
mv-k09-v1318.inference: Therefore, scripture and method are valid only insofar as they unfold within own-awareness.

mv-k09-v1319.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1319.question: Where do the world's appearances of arising and passing come from?
premises: All risings and settings of the world arise from the heart.
They are comparable to dream appearances emerging from deep sleep.
The scripture of own-awareness examines and explains them.
mv-k09-v1319.inference: Therefore, the world's cycles of arising and passing emerge from the heart of awareness, like dream from deep sleep, as understood by the scripture of own-awareness.

mv-k09-v1320.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1320.question: What processes make up the apparent functioning of the world in awareness?
premises: Perception depends on the totality of form, light, and attention.
