Creation, maintenance, and withdrawal describe cosmic functioning.
Closing and opening, and contraction, structure the experience of beings.
mv-k09-v1320.inference: Therefore, the world's apparent operations are configurations within awareness, from perception to contraction.

mv-k09-v1321.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1321.question: How does the triadic world-manifestation arise from consciousness?
premises: The abiding state takes the form of knower, known, and knowing.
This state belongs to perfectly full own-consciousness.
The fashioning of the manifold world occurs spontaneously from that consciousness.
mv-k09-v1321.inference: The entire triadic manifestation is the spontaneous, constant self-expression of perfectly full consciousness.

mv-k09-v1322.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1322.question: From what source does the determination of truth and falsity arise?
premises: Own-consciousness intrinsically takes the form of all beings, directions, places, and times.
The determination of truth and falsity is a cognitive act.
That determination arises from consciousness alone.
mv-k09-v1322.inference: Because consciousness pervades all forms, it alone is the source of discerning truth from falsity.

mv-k09-v1323.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1323.question: What did Utpaladeva teach about the status of external objects?
premises: Teacher Utpaladeva also taught this very point.
What appears outside may seem to be being or nonbeing.
Such appearance is grounded in own-consciousness as my seeing.
mv-k09-v1323.inference: Even the seemingly external world of being and nonbeing is established within own-consciousness.

mv-k09-v1324.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1324.question: How does the autonomous consciousness regulate itself across all beings?
premises: The principle 'let it see' expresses the regulation of the autonomous.
This regulation, called together with the senses, pervades from Shiva down to the worm.
Throughout this range it rests upon its own consciousness.
mv-k09-v1324.inference: The same autonomous self-awareness regulates and pervades all levels of existence from highest to lowest.

mv-k09-v1325.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1325.question: What distinguishes bondage from liberation in relation to consciousness?
premises: The same reality is worldly bondage in the limited condition and Shiva the supreme lord in truth.
Attaining rest in that consciousness changes one's condition.
One who has attained rest there is called liberated.
mv-k09-v1325.inference: Bondage and liberation are not different realities but different relations to the same supreme consciousness.

mv-k09-v1326.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1326.question: What sustains all beings from Brahma down to the immobile?
premises: All beings from Brahma to the immobile live by the grace of this consciousness.
This consciousness is always unobscured.
It should therefore be recognized as the sustaining reality.
mv-k09-v1326.inference: The ever-unobscured consciousness is the universal life-giving ground of all beings.

mv-k09-v1327.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1327.question: Does the shining goddess ever become separate from herself in her operations?
premises: The goddess shines forth everywhere.
She may establish the self in one place and fault it in another.
Nowhere is anything devoid of her.
mv-k09-v1327.inference: Even while performing diverse operations, the goddess never becomes separate from herself.

mv-k09-v1328.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1328.question: Do the goddess's acts of establishing and faulting alter her own nature?
premises: The goddess places things in various ways.
She does not undergo change.
She remains untouched by establishing, faulting, and otherness.
mv-k09-v1328.inference: The supreme goddess performs diverse operations without any alteration to her own nature.

mv-k09-v1329.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1329.question: Who is the primordial teacher behind this autonomous shining of consciousness?
premises: The goddess shines clearly in that very autonomous way.
The glorious great lord is the teacher even of earlier teachers.
This lord is identified with that autonomous consciousness.
mv-k09-v1329.inference: The autonomous, clearly shining consciousness is the glorious great lord, the primordial teacher of all.

mv-k09-v1330.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1330.question: What teaching did the great lord proclaim for the grace of the world?
premises: The great lord proclaimed this teaching out of grace for the world.
He criticized abiding in essenceless speech like the cawing of crows.
Those who honor their own consciousness and the instruction of the goddess-consciousness become liberated while living.
mv-k09-v1330.inference: Turning to one's own consciousness and heeding its immediate instruction leads to living liberation in any place.
uncertainties: sarva appears as a stem form where sarve might be expected; taken as m.nom.pl in context.

mv-k09-v1331.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1331.question: Why is consciousness itself called the true teacher in this doctrine?
premises: In this guiding principle, consciousness alone is called the teacher.
The teacher is so called because it swallows the universe.
It swallows the universe through the processes of creation and dissolution.
mv-k09-v1331.inference: Consciousness is the true guru because it emits and reabsorbs the entire universe.

mv-k09-v1332.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1332.question: What makes a relation with the teacher the supreme one?
premises: The primary, firm relation is called the supreme relation.
Through that relation, whatever is instructed becomes knowledge.
That knowledge is innately accomplished.
mv-k09-v1332.inference: The supreme relation to the teacher is the one through which instruction immediately becomes innately perfected knowledge.

mv-k09-v1333.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1333.question: From what abiding ground does the Tryambaka lineage proceed?
premises: Our lineage of teachers has an eternal abiding.
The division of the lineage beginning with Tryambaka proceeds from that abiding.
That abiding is the source of the tradition's continuity.
mv-k09-v1333.inference: The Tryambaka transmission stream proceeds from the eternal abiding of the teachers' lineage in consciousness.

mv-k09-v1334.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1334.question: How does the world appear once identity with ignorance perishes?
premises: It was said earlier that identity with ignorance perishes.
Own-consciousness takes on variety.
This world shines forth from that variety of own-consciousness.
mv-k09-v1334.inference: When ignorance dissolves, the world is seen to shine as the varied display of own-consciousness.

mv-k09-v1335.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1335.question: How should the diverse levels of scripture be understood in relation to the teacher?
premises: Scriptures range through intermediate, great-divine, divine, and other levels.
These teachings are rays of the teacher's own true speech.
They are fashioned by the teacher's own self.
mv-k09-v1335.inference: The confluence of diverse scriptures consists of self-fashioned rays of the teacher's own true speech.
uncertainties: The compound antarālamahaddivyādivyādi is compressed; the exact class boundaries follow the tradition's scriptural taxonomy.

mv-k09-v1336.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1336.question: Why is the present effort focused primarily on own-consciousness?
premises: The primacy of own-consciousness is manifest.
Authority may be traced to the teacher, scripture, or oneself.
This effort is made with own-consciousness as primary.
mv-k09-v1336.inference: Because own-consciousness is manifestly primary, the exposition rightly focuses its main effort on it.

mv-k09-v1337.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1337.question: How do teacher, scripture, and self-consciousness relate in producing realization?
premises: The teacher depends on the operation of scripture.
Scripture is established in one's own self-consciousness.
All of this attains accomplishment through self-consciousness and is never obstructed.
mv-k09-v1337.inference: Teacher and scripture are effective only because they are grounded in self-consciousness, which unfailingly accomplishes realization.
uncertainties: asahyatām is read as 'unbearableness' in the sense of not being able to be withstood or obstructed; the nuance is slightly compressed.

mv-k09-v1338.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1338.question: How should seekers of liberation direct their study and effort?
premises: This scripture should be practiced with effort.
Seekers of liberation are the intended audience.
Life should not be wasted in strained effort over other scriptures.
mv-k09-v1338.inference: Seekers of liberation should devote their effort to practicing this scripture rather than dispersing life in other teachings.

mv-k09-v1339.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1339.question: How does this teaching relate to views of difference and non-difference?
premises: There are views of non-difference and views of difference.
Both kinds of views come to fulfillment here alone.
Therefore this teaching deserves careful examination.
mv-k09-v1339.inference: Because both dualist and nondualist views find their fulfillment in this teaching, it should be thoroughly examined.

mv-k09-v1340.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1340.question: What is the effect of sustained practice of this scripture?
premises: One who recognizes the dream state becomes freed from sleep.
Practice of this scripture awakens the heart.
The awakened state becomes constant.
mv-k09-v1340.inference: Sustained practice of this scripture awakens the heart permanently, like recognizing a dream and waking from sleep.

mv-k09-v1341.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1341.question: What is the ultimate source of the scripture's authority?
premises: Own-consciousness is that very scripture.
Own-consciousness is free from dependence on anything else.
If self-derived authoritativeness is to be affirmed, it belongs to own-consciousness.
mv-k09-v1341.inference: The scripture's ultimate authority is the self-valid, independent authority of own-consciousness itself.

mv-k09-v1342.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1342.question: How are teaching, teacher, and taught unified in the highest state?
premises: Teaching, what is to be taught, and the teacher form a triad.
In the highest state this triad is not measured by time.
That state is beautiful with freedom and nonduality.
mv-k09-v1342.inference: In the timeless supreme state, the triad of teaching, taught, and teacher is unified in the beauty of freedom and nonduality.
uncertainties: tattatrākālakalitaṃ is a dense compound; the reading follows the sense of being beyond temporal division in that state.

mv-k09-v1343.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1343.question: Where did Shrikantha proclaim this intrinsic, never-departing state?
premises: There is an intrinsic state that never departs.
This state can be internalized.
Lord Shrikantha proclaimed it in the glorious Kirana scripture.
mv-k09-v1343.inference: The intrinsic, never-departing state of consciousness was authoritatively proclaimed by Shrikantha in the Kirana scripture.

mv-k09-v1344.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1344.question: Why does the teaching appear divided if its ultimate state is nondual?
premises: All this teaching is presented for the engagement of hearers.
It is differentiated according to differences of meaning.
This difference is constructed by metaphorical usage.
mv-k09-v1344.inference: The apparent divisions in the teaching are provisional, pedagogical constructions rather than ultimate differences.
uncertainties: The token 'śrot\rr' contains a backslash-r sequence as given in the source; it appears to be part of the transmitted form of śrotṝṇām split across tokens and is preserved exactly.

mv-k09-v1345.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1345.question: Should a difference of fruit be assumed in the Lord's teaching?
premises: A difference of fruit is not to be assumed here.
If a difference of fruit were assumed, it would be assumed falsely.
This teaching of the Lord would then be divided by distinctions of ten, eighteen, eight, and eight.
mv-k09-v1345.inference: Therefore no real difference of fruit should be posited in this teaching of the Lord.
uncertainties: The referents of the ten, eighteen, eight, and eight distinctions are not specified in this verse.

mv-k09-v1346.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1346.question: What is the single fruit and who is the qualified recipient of this teaching?
premises: This teaching has the single fruit of attaining the state of being Śiva.
It applies to the individual soul who is qualified and eager for attaining that state.
It proceeds with disregard for birth, family, caste, and similar distinctions.
mv-k09-v1346.inference: Therefore the teaching is directed to any eager qualified soul, without regard to social distinctions, for the sole fruit of Śiva-attainment.

mv-k09-v1347.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1347.question: How long is this teaching regarded as a single unified discourse?
premises: The teaching is set forth and attains unity of discourse.
As long as that unity of discourse continues, it remains operative.
Variety arises from the differing functions of subsidiary and principal parts.
mv-k09-v1347.inference: Therefore, despite variety in subsidiary and principal functions, the knowers regard this teaching as one so long as its unity of discourse holds.

mv-k09-v1348.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1348.question: What constitutes the unified structure of the Trika scripture in this context?
premises: The Trika scripture is identified as a unified whole.
The teacher in this context is of such a nature and nondual in essence.
The collection of subsequent textual portions and the sections belong to that same structure.
mv-k09-v1348.inference: Therefore the Trika scripture, its nondual teacher, and its subsequent sections form a single coherent framework.
uncertainties: The precise scope of 'subsequent textual portions' is not specified in this verse.

mv-k09-v1349.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1349.question: What remains the primary fruit even when differences due to māyā are clearly described?
premises: Accounts of difference produced by māyā may become clear in the teaching.
Such differentiated accounts do exist within the discourse.
Even so, the attainment of Śiva remains established as the primary final fruit.
mv-k09-v1349.inference: Therefore the clear presentation of māyā-based differences does not displace Śiva-attainment as the chief ultimate fruit.

mv-k09-v1350.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k09-v1350.question: Who is the true recipient of Śiva-hood despite sectional divisions in the teaching?
premises: The qualified person is indeed one and is the recipient of attaining Śiva-hood.
Even so, the teaching may arise in the form of limited sections.
Sectional presentation does not multiply the ultimate qualified recipient or the final attainment.
mv-k09-v1350.inference: Therefore, despite sectional divisions, there is one qualified recipient whose true attainment is Śiva-hood.

mv-k10-v1351.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1351.question: What kinds of fruit and opposing conditions determine a practitioner's qualification?
premises: The fruit may be clear and primary, or it may be a final fruit.
The fruit may belong to the principal element or to its auxiliary.
The fruit may arise in its opposite, in another side, or in another opposing condition.
mv-k10-v1351.inference: Qualification depends on the specific kind of fruit and the context in which that fruit appears.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic completion of the verse is carried into the following verse.

mv-k10-v1352.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1352.question: How do bodily suitability and prior preparation affect eligibility for practice?
premises: A person may become a receptacle for manifesting aspects of various opposing conditions.
Such eligibility depends on a suitably prepared body and related factors.
It also depends on one who shares in the appropriate preparatory conditioning.
mv-k10-v1352.inference: Eligibility is shaped by both the practitioner's embodied condition and their received preparation.
uncertainties: The referent of saṃskārabhāginaḥ could be the teacher, the student, or both in context.

mv-k10-v1353.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1353.question: How is the sequence of qualification determined for teacher and student?
premises: A corresponding sequence of qualification is declared for both teacher and student.
This sequence is illustrated by one who undertakes the death-destroying elixir procedure.
The analogy implies that prior preparation governs later ritual eligibility.
mv-k10-v1353.inference: The order of qualification for teacher and student follows the same logic of preparatory fitness as other regulated procedures.

mv-k10-v1354.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1354.question: Why must preparatory purification precede initiation and later ritual action?
premises: Preparatory conditioning is first obtained through purifying measures such as decoction, vomiting, and purging.
Initiation produces an alteration in the candidate.
That alteration should not occur later during the main ritual procedure.
mv-k10-v1354.inference: Purification must come before initiation so that disruptive change does not interfere with subsequent ritual performance.

mv-k10-v1355.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1355.question: Why are Vaishnavas and others restricted from certain Shaiva rites?
premises: Restriction of qualification arises from factors such as the practitioner's body and level of knowledge.
Vaishnavas and others are said to rely on the discipline suited to bound souls.
That discipline does not confer the preparation required for higher Shaiva rites.
mv-k10-v1355.inference: Because their conditioning belongs to the paśu level, Vaishnavas and others are not qualified for those rites.
uncertainties: The middle compound taddehavidaśādijaḥ is compressed and its exact member boundaries are interpretive.

mv-k10-v1356.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1356.question: How does qualification differ across the graded Shaiva scriptural domains?
premises: Those outside the Shaiva preparation are not qualified in the Shaiva scripture.
Shaivas qualified at one level are not thereby qualified in the left sphere.
Those of the left and right spheres are not thereby qualified in the Kula doctrine or the Trika.
mv-k10-v1356.inference: Qualification is graded and does not automatically transfer upward across scriptural domains.

mv-k10-v1357.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1357.question: What kind of teacher is fit to perform the highest initiatory rites?
premises: The revered Bhairava Kula states a standard for the teacher.
A fit teacher is one suited to the rite of the five initiations.
Such a teacher has either transcended the lower streams or is grounded in the Trika scripture.
mv-k10-v1357.inference: Only a teacher established beyond the lower streams or in the Trika is qualified for the highest initiatory rites.

mv-k10-v1358.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1358.question: How can qualification be both one and differentiated at the same time?
premises: At the level of reliance on the self-principle, qualification can be described as one.
Preparatory conditioning differs among practitioners.
Difference in preparation produces difference in qualification.
mv-k10-v1358.inference: Qualification is unitary in its basic locus but differentiated according to preparation.
uncertainties: saṃskārāśraya appears without an explicit case ending in the tokenized form; its relation is inferred from the compound context.

mv-k10-v1359.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1359.question: Why can Shiva be said to be the fruit of every scripture?
premises: The Svacchanda Tantra states that Shiva is the fruit in every scripture.
All scriptures arise from Shiva.
What arises from Shiva has Shiva's abode as its fruit.
mv-k10-v1359.inference: Because all scriptures originate in Shiva, their ultimate fruit is Shiva.

mv-k10-v1360.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1360.question: What higher knowledge is said to be inaccessible to Samkhya, Yoga, and Pancharatra?
premises: The same scripture again speaks in the section on discriminating higher principles.
It refers to something not known by the Samkhyas.
It refers to something not known by the great yogins or by the Pancharatrikas.
mv-k10-v1360.inference: There is a higher principle whose full discrimination lies beyond those systems.
uncertainties: The verse introduces a quotation whose completion continues in the next verse.

mv-k10-v1361.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1361.question: Why are the many rival schools said to fall short of knowing Shiva-tattva?
premises: The scripture challenges as many as three hundred and sixty-three disputants.
Those disputants discriminate only within a limited range.
Limited discrimination cannot grasp the full higher principle.
mv-k10-v1361.inference: The rival schools are rejected because their knowledge extends only to a partial domain.
uncertainties: The number three hundred and sixty-three is taken as a traditional count of rival views.

mv-k10-v1362.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1362.question: Can partial knowledge of a fragment amount to knowledge of unlimited Shiva-tattva?
premises: The rival schools know only a limited portion.
Unlimited Shiva-tattva cannot be constituted by a merely partial grasp.
An objection proposes that they might still posit Shiva's presence in that partial portion.
mv-k10-v1362.inference: A partial grasp does not by itself make them knowers of the unlimited Shiva principle.

mv-k10-v1363.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1363.question: Why is superimposing the whole of Shiva on a partial view not coherent?
premises: One might try to superimpose Shiva's presence on a mere part.
Such superimposition lacks clear coherence.
A sentence like 'Devadatta' refers to a complete individual, not to a fragment.
mv-k10-v1363.inference: Superimposing the whole on a part fails because meaning and reference require a coherent whole.

mv-k10-v1364.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1364.question: How could a hearer of a partial word recover the meaning of whole prior sentences?
premises: A hearer may grasp only a single limited word such as 'Devadatta'.
The full meaning belongs to entire previous sentences.
A partial word does not by itself contain that whole sentential meaning.
mv-k10-v1364.inference: One cannot legitimately superimpose the meaning of whole sentences onto a merely partial word.

mv-k10-v1365.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1365.question: Can full meaning be understood from a sentence if one is only hearing a partial word?
premises: Understanding of the full meaning would have to come from the sentence as a whole.
If one claims it comes merely from that partial word, the hearer is no longer just a word-hearer.
The limited part would then no longer remain merely limited.
mv-k10-v1365.inference: Full sentential understanding cannot be reduced to hearing a mere fragment without contradiction.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse for its full conclusion.

mv-k10-v1366.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1366.question: What kind of knowledge is required to understand the present Shaiva domain correctly?
premises: A merely partial element does not contain the full meaning.
The present domain concerns the meaning of the Shaiva scripture.
Correct understanding requires knowledge of that meaning in its complete form.
mv-k10-v1366.inference: In this domain, only complete knowledge of the Shaiva scriptural meaning is adequate.

mv-k10-v1367.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1367.question: Can other scriptural systems be construed as complete through the Shiva principle?
premises: One might try to interpret Yoga, Samkhya, Arhata, Nyaya, Pancharatra, Veda, and Smriti through the Shiva principle.
Such an interpretation would treat them as complete in that light.
The proposal raises the question of whether that completeness is actually present in them.
mv-k10-v1367.inference: The possibility of reinterpreting other systems through Shiva-tattva is entertained as an objection.

mv-k10-v1368.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1368.question: Why is reinterpretation through Shiva-tattva insufficient without proper preparation?
premises: One may grant a limited reinterpretation of other systems through Shiva-tattva.
That does not mean the full expansion of Shiva-tattva is present there.
Knowledge of Shiva-tattva must be preceded by the appropriate preparation.
mv-k10-v1368.inference: Without the requisite preparation, other systems cannot yield full knowledge of Shiva-tattva.

mv-k10-v1369.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1369.question: What happens if teacher and student lack the required preparation for Shiva-tattva?
premises: Knowledge of Shiva-tattva requires the proper preparation.
If that preparation is absent, both teacher and student incur a fault.
If that preparation is received, the scriptural meaning may indeed be understood in that way.
mv-k10-v1369.inference: The legitimacy of transmitting Shiva-tattva depends on the presence of the required preparation.

mv-k10-v1370.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1370.question: Does receiving higher preparation erase a practitioner's former sectarian identity?
premises: A person may receive higher and higher preparation.
Even so, he may continue to practice as a Vaishnava, Samkhya, or follower of Vedic tradition.
Former identity and new preparation do not automatically coincide.
mv-k10-v1370.inference: Higher preparation alone does not abolish a practitioner's continued adherence to a prior discipline.

mv-k10-v1371.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1371.question: How can strict sectarian restriction be justified within a nondual standpoint?
premises: If one remains Vaishnava and so on while claiming higher preparation, a serious transgression follows.
An objector asks how such a primary restriction can stand in the nondual state.
The objection challenges whether nonduality permits rigid sectarian boundaries.
mv-k10-v1371.inference: The text raises a tension between graded qualification and the claim of nonduality.

mv-k10-v1372.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1372.question: Who is actually committed to duality in this dispute about nonduality?
premises: The objector appeals to nonduality while insisting on sectarian identity.
That insistence is itself shaped by duality.
By clinging to that position, the objector resorts to duality.
mv-k10-v1372.inference: The objection fails because the objector's own stance is grounded in duality.

mv-k10-v1373.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1373.question: Why does claiming Vaishnava identity undermine the objection to Shaiva qualification rules?
premises: The objector says, 'Being a Vaishnava, why am I not qualified in the Shaiva domain?'
This claim presupposes a fixed dualistic identity.
Within duality, restriction operates by force of rule.
mv-k10-v1373.inference: The objector cannot appeal to nonduality while simultaneously insisting on a dualistic sectarian identity.

mv-k10-v1374.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1374.question: What follows from sectarian restriction, and how is a deity properly worshiped?
premises: Given the established rules of qualification, transgression would arise from violating them.
This consequence has already been demonstrated.
A deity is worshiped through identification with that deity.
mv-k10-v1374.inference: Because worship depends on identification, sectarian restriction and its consequences remain operative where dualistic identity persists.
uncertainties: The final tataḥ points forward to the next verse, so the argument continues beyond this unit.

mv-k10-v1375.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1375.question: How can someone identified with Vishnu properly worship Rudra?
premises: A worshipper who has attained identity with Vishnu faces a problem in worshipping Rudra.
The Gita teaches that whoever is devoted to a particular deity becomes identified with that deity.
mv-k10-v1375.inference: Because worship establishes identity with its object, identity with Vishnu appears incompatible with worship of Rudra.
uncertainties: The exact Gita passage alluded to by 'yo yac chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ' is not specified in the verse.

mv-k10-v1376.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1376.question: What result do identity-contemplation and mantras yield for a fruit-seeking practitioner?
premises: Practices of identity-contemplation and mantras produce their corresponding fruit.
A practitioner whose self is shaped by contemplation of a deity becomes aligned with that deity.
For one who desires a specific fruit, such practices grant the success sought.
mv-k10-v1376.inference: Identity-contemplation and mantra practice are effective for a fruit-seeker because they shape the practitioner into conformity with the contemplated deity.
uncertainties: The token '}}' appears to be an editorial or encoding artifact in the source and its exact intended reading is unclear.

mv-k10-v1377.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1377.question: Is someone seeking liberation through scripture fit for that limited application?
premises: A person who desires liberation may also seek liberation through a particular scripture.
Such a person can become overcome by contemplating the faults attributed to that path or object.
Fitness applies only within that limited scope of application.
mv-k10-v1377.inference: Even a seeker of liberation through scripture is only conditionally fit, because fault-contemplation restricts competence to that limited application.
uncertainties: The antecedent of 'tad' in 'taddoṣabhāvanākrāntaḥ' is context-dependent and could refer to a deity, path, or doctrine.

mv-k10-v1378.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1378.question: Who is primarily authorized in a given domain of teaching?
premises: A primary method is being stated.
A person may be established in a particular domain.
That person may have permanently attained identity with that domain.
mv-k10-v1378.inference: One who is established in a domain and has attained identity with it is authorized there.

mv-k10-v1379.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1379.question: Why should knowledge be received from such an authorized person?
premises: Knowledge is said to be received from that authorized person.
That person has attained identity with the domain.
This identity arises through the ordered practice of contemplating that domain.
mv-k10-v1379.inference: Because such a person has realized identity through contemplative practice, knowledge should be received from him.

mv-k10-v1380.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1380.question: How could a student initially connect the scripture by his own understanding?
premises: A student receives scripture in a sequential order from earlier to later.
At that initial stage the student relies on his own understanding.
The scripture contains an internally connected teaching.
mv-k10-v1380.inference: A student receiving scripture sequentially cannot at first reliably connect its coherent meaning by his own understanding alone.

mv-k10-v1381.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1381.question: What role remains for a human teacher when someone can unite the teaching by their own power?
premises: A person who strives to unite the teaching by himself is directly the supreme lord.
For such a person, a human teacher can do nothing further.
That same person is called the teacher of others.
mv-k10-v1381.inference: Self-sufficient realization makes one independent of an external teacher and qualifies one to teach others.

mv-k10-v1382.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1382.question: Why is a teacher defined as one who has attained identity with the teaching?
premises: People hold that knowledge is not obtained from anyone other than those who truly know.
A teacher is therefore understood through attained identity with that knowledge.
The designation 'teacher' rests on this attained identity.
mv-k10-v1382.inference: The title of teacher is grounded in realized identity with the knowledge, not merely in external transmission.

mv-k10-v1383.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1383.question: Does temporary contemplation of Shiva undermine the authority of a Vaishnava scriptural teacher?
premises: The realized teacher's identity holds only in the domain and to the extent where it is attained, not otherwise.
An objection arises that the meaning of Vaishnava scripture might be affected at the time of contemplating Shiva.
The objection assumes that shifting contemplative focus changes scriptural identity.
mv-k10-v1383.inference: The verse sets up the problem of whether contemplative identification transfers or cancels a teacher's scriptural authority.
uncertainties: The first clause is compressed; the exact scope of yāvati/yatraiva/tāvati depends on the surrounding argument.

mv-k10-v1384.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1384.question: Does contemplative identification destroy a teacher's authority like an actor losing a role?
premises: The objection claims that identity with another deity destroys teacherhood.
The reply calls this objection foolish talk.
In Rama-Ravana dramas, assumed roles do not become fixed ontological identities.
mv-k10-v1384.inference: Contemplative identification is not like a theatrical role-change that abolishes the teacher's underlying authority.

mv-k10-v1385.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1385.question: How does a Vaishnava's contemplative identification differ from an actor changing costume?
premises: An actor assumes otherness by changing costume and stage accessories.
A Vaishnava reflects 'I am Vishnu' or 'I am his servant' as contemplative identifications.
The comparison tests whether contemplative identity is merely external role-assumption.
mv-k10-v1385.inference: The verse contrasts theatrical role-change with contemplative identification to clarify the nature of religious identity.

mv-k10-v1386.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1386.question: If a contemplative identity can be reversed, does that make one of the cognitions false?
premises: A person may later say, 'Now I am not thus.'
Such a reversal raises the question of whether the earlier or later identification is coherent.
If two conflicting identifications are treated as fixed truths, one awareness becomes false knowledge.
mv-k10-v1386.inference: The problem is not contemplation itself but treating shifting identifications as mutually exclusive fixed truths.

mv-k10-v1387.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1387.question: Why must the teacher belong to the same scripture as the disciple?
premises: A disciple can become fallen through a cognition that shifts allegiance to another system.
Such a fall shows that scriptural alignment is not indifferent.
Therefore the primary rule is that each scripture has its own proper teacher.
mv-k10-v1387.inference: Because crossing scriptural allegiance can make a disciple fall, the governing rule is that a teacher must correspond to the disciple's own scripture.
uncertainties: The exact antecedent of yayā is implicit from the preceding verses rather than stated in this verse.

mv-k10-v1388.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1388.question: Who fails to grant the fruit of attainment according to the independent scriptures?
premises: The independent scriptures state a restriction on who can grant attainment.
A person devoted to another scripture is excluded from granting that fruit.
Even one merely absorbed in that other scripture is excluded.
mv-k10-v1388.inference: Only a teacher aligned with the relevant scripture can grant its fruit of attainment, not someone attached to a different scripture.

mv-k10-v1389.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1389.question: What common-world examples support the rule that worship follows the deity's own rite?
premises: In ordinary life there is a widespread convention that each deity is served by its own adherents.
Examples include Bhagavatas for Vishnu, Magas for the Sun, Shaiva ascetics for Shambhu, specialists for the Mothers, brahmins for Brahma, Shakyas for the Buddha, and naked ascetics for the Arhat.
The general rule is that those who worship a deity by its own method should perform that deity's rite.
mv-k10-v1389.inference: The restriction of ritual and teaching to the proper tradition is confirmed by both scriptural rule and common religious practice.
uncertainties: The syntax of the final relative-correlative clause is compressed and spans several listed examples.

mv-k10-v1390.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1390.question: Does the mere presence of a more knowledgeable teacher create multiple eligibilities?
premises: A teacher possessing higher knowledge may be present in the same place.
Such proximity does not by itself alter the disciple's proper qualification.
Eligibility is not multiplied merely because a superior knower is nearby.
mv-k10-v1390.inference: The presence of a higher knower does not override the established rule of scriptural eligibility.

mv-k10-v1391.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1391.question: What is the role of a teacher established in the full and real teaching?
premises: A teacher may be firmly established in this full awakening and real teaching.
Such a teacher directs the disciple toward progressively higher establishment.
The teacher's action is oriented to the disciple's ascent rather than to crossing scriptural boundaries.
mv-k10-v1391.inference: Within the true teaching, a fully established teacher guides the disciple upward through successive levels of realization.
uncertainties: The final token '(?)' marks an uncertain or incomplete reading in the transmitted text.

mv-k10-v1392.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1392.question: Why may a fully established teacher bestow grace on a partially prepared disciple?
premises: A disciple may be governed only by a partial share of spiritual disposition.
The teacher may act for the attainment of the disciple's fruit.
The teacher's fullness and higher functioning make such grace possible.
mv-k10-v1392.inference: Because the teacher operates from fullness, he can bestow grace even on a disciple whose readiness is partial.

mv-k10-v1393.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1393.question: How can there be a higher level if the teaching is nondual?
premises: An objector claims that in nonduality there can be nothing higher.
The reply states that those who think so are deluded by difference.
Difference itself is the lower state, not a limit on nonduality.
mv-k10-v1393.inference: Talk of higher and lower does not contradict nonduality, because lower levels are modes of difference within what nonduality contains.

mv-k10-v1394.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1394.question: Which other traditions are classed as followers of lower teachings in this context?
premises: The preceding argument distinguishes lower difference-bound states from the supreme teaching.
Various groups may abide in teachings oriented to bound souls.
These include Vaishnavas, Buddhists, Vedic ritualists, and Vedanta speakers.
mv-k10-v1394.inference: From the standpoint of this supreme teaching, those traditions are counted among disciplines that remain within lower, difference-bound frameworks.
uncertainties: The verse lists traditions as examples of paśuśāsana-vartins; the degree of polemical generalization is contextual.

mv-k10-v1395.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1395.question: Are followers of those other teachings ever authorized in the Lord's teaching?
premises: The listed traditions are treated as following other disciplines.
The Lord's teaching has its own rules of eligibility.
Scriptural discussions of eligibility state that such followers are not authorized there.
mv-k10-v1395.inference: Followers of those other teachings are never eligible within the Lord's teaching, as stated in scriptural determinations of qualification.
uncertainties: The subject of uktavān is not named in this verse and is supplied by context.

mv-k10-v1396.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1396.question: What should a disciple do if initiated by a teacher from the wrong tradition?
premises: A Vaishnava of deluded mind might give initiation to a Shaiva disciple.
Such a teacher acts improperly and deceptively across scriptural boundaries.
The disciple should reject that teacher and follow the proper course.
mv-k10-v1396.inference: An initiation given by a teacher outside the proper tradition is invalid, so the disciple must abandon that teacher and act according to what is proper.
uncertainties: The token chaivaṃ is a fused form; the intended recipient reading is clear from context but the sandhi is compact.

mv-k10-v1397.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1397.question: What kind of knowledge makes a teacher capable of giving liberation?
premises: It is stated here that a giver of liberation must possess well-practiced knowledge.
The relevant knowledge is supreme knowledge.
From supreme knowledge there is no falling away.
mv-k10-v1397.inference: A teacher can grant liberation only when grounded in supreme, firmly practiced knowledge from which no lapse occurs.

mv-k10-v1398.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1398.question: Why is there no falling away from supreme nondual realization?
premises: Supreme nondual realization is the highest knowledge.
From that realization there is no falling away at all.
Its functioning is filled with all knowledge established on the side of the Self.
mv-k10-v1398.inference: Because supreme nondual realization contains and stabilizes all knowledge in the Self, no lapse from it is possible.

mv-k10-v1399.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1399.question: How can this established meaning of the scripture ever fall away or shift its position?
premises: The meaning of the scripture is established by the power of śakti.
What is established by śakti's power is not subject to ordinary conditions of change.
Questions of how, who, from where, or where presuppose possible deviation.
mv-k10-v1399.inference: Therefore no deviation from this scriptural meaning is possible, because it stands firm through śakti's power.

mv-k10-v1400.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1400.question: Who is the one that abides in its own nature while containing all principles and names within itself?
premises: This reality inwardly contains all principles, letters, and related fullness.
It is designated by all names and has Bhairava as its nature.
Such a reality abides in its own essential form.
mv-k10-v1400.inference: Therefore the one who partakes of his own nature is none other than Bhairava, containing all within himself.

mv-k10-v1401.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1401.question: Why does the author say that sincere readers will recognize the authority of this exposition without need for praise?
premises: The supreme lord composed this scripture under the name Jñānacandra.
The author has explained it clearly and profoundly to establish the authority of his own tradition.
For minds that have entered this teaching, the greatness of its authority shines forth, exalted by universal nonduality.
mv-k10-v1401.inference: Therefore sincere readers will recognize its truth on their own, making self-praise unnecessary.

mv-k10-v1402.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1402.question: Toward which kinds of readers is argumentative effort worthwhile, and toward which is it futile?
premises: Those who investigate properly are auspicious and need no persuasive effort.
Those lame in the ascent of reflective awareness and hardened like stone cannot be reached by such effort.
Those barren of scripture provoke a violent agitation that, like the ocean at dissolution, whirls back within oneself.
mv-k10-v1402.inference: Therefore effort should not be wasted on the incapable or hostile, since their agitation only turns back upon the self.

mv-k10-v1403.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1403.question: Why should the fire of dissolution abandon its fierce display and become calm within itself?
premises: The cosmic fire is addressed as blazing with ostentatious flames and sparks.
There is nothing left for it to burn.
The universe has already been pervaded and dissolved into what is essentially its own light.
mv-k10-v1403.inference: Therefore the fire of dissolution should withdraw its fierce display and rest calmly in itself.

mv-k10-v1404.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mv-k10-v1404.question: Who composed this vārttika and in what place and on what text was it composed?
premises: The author identifies himself as the Kashmirian Abhinavagupta.
The work is composed in the eastern city named Pravarapura.
The composition is a vārttika on the great teaching beginning with the Mālinī.
mv-k10-v1404.inference: Therefore this verse serves as a colophon identifying Abhinavagupta of Kashmir as the composer of the vārttika on the Mālinīvijaya in Pravarapura.

mv-k01-v01.plain_english: May the first section shine, with its divine parents and heart as the family of supreme nectar.
mv-k01-v01.sanskrit_cite:

prathamaḥ kāṇḍaḥ

vimalakalāśrayābhinavasṛṣṭimahā jananī bharitatanuś ca pañcamukhaguptarucir janakaḥ /
tadubhayayāmalasphuritabhāvavisargamayaṃ hṛdayam anuttarāmṛtakulaṃ mama saṃsphuratāt // [AgMsv_1.1]

mv-k01-v02.plain_english: May that teacher conquer, whose shining rays of knowledge make our hearts blossom everywhere.
mv-k01-v02.sanskrit_cite:
yadīyabodhakiraṇair ullasadbhiḥ samantataḥ /
vikāsihṛdayāmbhojā vayaṃ sa jayatād guruḥ // [AgMsv_1.2]

mv-k01-v03.plain_english: He gave me floods of meanings, bright with reflection and streams, that destroy poverty.

mv-k01-v04.plain_english: May Shambhunatha, pure and skilled toward true devotees, be pleased with me through speech-flowers.
mv-k01-v04.sanskrit_cite:
śrīmatsumatisaṃśuddhaḥ sadbhaktajanadakṣiṇaḥ /
śambhunāthaḥ prasanno me bhūyād vākpuṣpatoṣitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.4]

mv-k01-v05.plain_english: I salute Shricukhala, greater than teachers, by whose purification I stand freed from grasping.
mv-k01-v05.sanskrit_cite:
gurubhyo 'pi garīyāṃsaṃ yuktaṃ śrīcukhalābhidham /
vande yatkṛtasaṃskāraḥ sthito 'smi galitagrahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.5]

mv-k01-v06.plain_english: May glorious great-minded Bhutiraja conquer, bolder than the guru in rescuing devotees.
mv-k01-v06.sanskrit_cite:
tato gurutaraḥ śrīmān bhūtirājo mahāmatiḥ /
jayatād bhaktajanatāsamuddharaṇasāhasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.6]

mv-k01-v07.plain_english: The joyful consciousness compositions arising from Shri Somananda and Utpala conquer, spreading in all directions.

mv-k01-v08.plain_english: The speech of teacher Shriman Lakshmanagupta conquers, teaching recognition that cuts the world cycle.

mv-k01-v09.plain_english: Even my bee-mind, intoxicated by the wonder of countless new tastes, is satisfied in supreme enjoyment.

mv-k01-v10.plain_english: Having attained unity with that in one's own self, various sound-riches indeed blossom from it.
mv-k01-v10.sanskrit_cite:
tadekamayatām āpya svātmany eva tathā sthitā /
tad asyāḥ pronmiṣanty eva vividhā nādasaṃpadaḥ // [AgMsv_1.10]

mv-k01-v11.plain_english: Requested by good disciples' ears, I explain sentence meaning again and again in Shrimanmalini, here and there.
mv-k01-v11.sanskrit_cite:
sacchiṣyakarṇamandrābhyām arthito 'haṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
vākyārthaṃ vartaye śrīmanmālinyāṃ yat kva cit kva cit // [AgMsv_1.11]

mv-k01-v12.plain_english: By fitness and abandoning the other, scripture and commentary circulate well in this mutual usage of expressed and expressor.
mv-k01-v12.sanskrit_cite:
aucityenetaratyāgād vācyavācakayor mithaḥ /
vartanāvarta etasmin sādhu śāstraṃ ca vārttikam // [AgMsv_1.12]

mv-k01-v13.plain_english: We bow day and night to those Abhinavaguptas, collections of Shiva moon rays, shining beyond all range.
mv-k01-v13.sanskrit_cite:
ye 'harniśaṃ prakāśante sarvasya ca na gocare /
numo 'bhinavaguptāṃs tāñ śivacandrāṃśusaṃcayān // [AgMsv_1.13]

mv-k01-v14.plain_english: The moon rays of knowledge born from Paramesha's face conquer, able to destroy opponents of world bliss.

mv-k01-v15.plain_english: From unrestrained true being, sharing one nature with beings, great knowledge born before has the glory of its rays.
mv-k01-v15.sanskrit_cite:
aniyantritasadbhāvād bhāvābhedaikabhāginaḥ /
yat prāg jātaṃ mahājñānaṃ tadraśmibharavaibhavam // [AgMsv_1.15]

mv-k01-v16.plain_english: Spread and such, it is free from maya's rejectable and acceptable, differentiated only by various thought rays.

mv-k01-v17.plain_english: That heart of the supreme lord has the nature of reflection; even there Maheshvara always acts by power made of his own self.
mv-k01-v17.sanskrit_cite:
abhimarśasvabhāvaṃ tad dhṛdayaṃ parameśituḥ /
tatrāpi śaktyā satataṃ svātmamayyā maheśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.17]

mv-k01-v18.plain_english: When, having reached contact, he would go to supreme absorption, then his supreme face becomes the seat of emission expansion.
mv-k01-v18.sanskrit_cite:
yadā saṃghaṭṭam āsādya samāpattiṃ parāṃ vrajet /
tadāsya paramaṃ vaktraṃ visargaprasarāspadam // [AgMsv_1.18]

mv-k01-v19.plain_english: The seed of all stands, beautiful world bliss rising from supreme expansion, by non-difference of future face.
mv-k01-v19.sanskrit_cite:
anuttaravikāsodyajjagadānandasundaram /
bhāvivaktrāvibhāgena bījaṃ sarvasya yat sthitam // [AgMsv_1.19]

mv-k01-v20.plain_english: That opinion, heart pulse vision supreme flow wave etc, is the supreme trika before, undivided from all powers.
mv-k01-v20.sanskrit_cite:
hṛtspandadṛkparāsāranirnāmormyādi tan matam /
etat paraṃ trikaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvaśaktyavibhāgavat // [AgMsv_1.20]

mv-k01-v21.plain_english: Here, from release of expansion and contraction doubt, only the three of will, knowledge, and action remain in absorption in own bliss.

mv-k01-v22.plain_english: Thus teachers described it in the Shaiva view: he stands absorbed in experience of consciousness bliss only.
mv-k01-v22.sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca guravaḥ śaivadṛṣṭāv itthaṃ nyarūpayan /
sa yad āste cidāhlādamātrānubhavatallayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.22]

mv-k01-v23.plain_english: That will, so much knowledge, and so much action indeed occur by harmony of three subtle powers.
mv-k01-v23.sanskrit_cite:
tad icchā tāvatī jñānaṃ tāvat tāvat kriyā hi sā /
susūkṣmaśaktitritayasāmarasyena vartate // [AgMsv_1.23]

mv-k01-v24.plain_english: Supreme in consciousness-form bliss would be undivided from that; but, it is asked, in such a world-self, from abandoning contraction?
mv-k01-v24.sanskrit_cite:
cidrūpāhlādaparamas tadābhinno bhaved iti /
nanu cedṛśi viśvātmabhūte saṃkocavarjanāt // [AgMsv_1.24]

mv-k01-v25.plain_english: How are scripture and other riches said to be rooted in conceptual construction? All this knowledge is made of consciousness radiance.
mv-k01-v25.sanskrit_cite:
vikalpakalpanāmūlāḥ kathaṃ śāstrādisaṃpadaḥ /
ucyate sarva evāyaṃ bodhaḥ saṃvitprabhāmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.25]

mv-k01-v26.plain_english: Because it is of the nature of light, awareness is essentially dense with conscious self-reflection; and that light which shines has reflective awareness as its very nature.
mv-k01-v26.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśarūpatāyogāc cidāmarśaghanātmakaḥ /
tatrāmarśasvabhāvo 'yaṃ yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.26]

mv-k01-v27.plain_english: Why should that very light not be the flood of scriptures? What need is there for other displays of reasoning? One who is pierced by the supreme goddess of speech would simply abide in that.
mv-k01-v27.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva kiṃ na śāstraughaḥ kim anyair yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
paravāgdevatāviddhas tatrāsau kevalaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.27]

mv-k01-v28.plain_english: But it is not variegated by masses of ordinary, māyic letters. As it is said in the revered Pratyabhijñā, what abides in the self shines forth of itself.
mv-k01-v28.sanskrit_cite:
na tu laukikamāyīyavarṇapuñjavicitritaḥ /
uktaṃ śrīpratyabhijñāyām ātmasaṃsthasya bhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.28]

mv-k01-v29.plain_english: Reflective awareness of will does indeed proceed and is not absent from that. The wise know reflective awareness to be the very nature of manifestation; otherwise, manifestation would not be what it is.
mv-k01-v29.sanskrit_cite:
asty eva na vinā tasmād icchāmarśaḥ pravartate /
svabhāvam avabhāsasya vimarśaṃ vidur anyathā // [AgMsv_1.29]

mv-k01-v30.plain_english: Even if light tinged by an object seems similar to jewels and the like, any reflective awareness at all belongs to the domain of the wonder of consciousness.
mv-k01-v30.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśo 'rthoparakto 'pi tulyo ratnādikair iti /
kiṃca yaḥ kaś canāmarśaś ciccamatkāragocaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.30]

mv-k01-v31.plain_english: When reflective awareness has joy, pain, and the like as its objects, it becomes clear through the surging inner grasp that arises within that reflection.

mv-k01-v32.plain_english: Afterward it attains full clearness. And so the teacher has said: pleasure and the like are established by one's own awareness and stand firm on that basis.
mv-k01-v32.sanskrit_cite:
paścāt susphuṭatām eti tathā ca gurur ūcivān /
yathā svasaṃvidā siddhaṃ sukhādi vyavatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.32]

mv-k01-v33.plain_english: For at the time of later determination it is not known in that same way by self-awareness; even so, it must necessarily be accepted as established by self-awareness.
mv-k01-v33.sanskrit_cite:
na hi vyavasthāsamaye vedyate tat svasaṃvidā /
tathāvaśyopagantavyaṃ svasaṃvitsādhanād iti // [AgMsv_1.33]

mv-k01-v34.plain_english: So too here: afterward, on the path where knowledge and the other powers rise, the level consisting of universal non-difference comes to be reflectively apprehended.
mv-k01-v34.sanskrit_cite:
evam atrāpi paścād yaj jñānādyullāsavartmani /
sarvābhedamayī bhūmir yāvad āmṛśyatāṃ vrajet // [AgMsv_1.34]

mv-k01-v35.plain_english: Then, because a noble reflective portion fitting that level becomes clear, that very primordial emission attains the status of scripture.
mv-k01-v35.sanskrit_cite:
tāvat taducitodāravimarśāṃśasphuṭatvataḥ /
tādṛk sa eva śāstratvaṃ prāgvisargaḥ prapadyate // [AgMsv_1.35]

mv-k01-v36.plain_english: This indeed would be fitting, for even in the unconditioned supreme meaning of scripture some trace of practice can be discerned.
mv-k01-v36.sanskrit_cite:
etad eva tu yuktaṃ syāt tathā hy anupadhau pare /
śāstrārthe 'pi samācāraleśaḥ ko 'pi vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.36]

mv-k01-v37.plain_english: That trace surely possesses the powers of knowledge and the rest that will arise in the abode of clearness; and from conditioning it becomes expanded into various manifold distinctions.
mv-k01-v37.sanskrit_cite:
sa nūnaṃ sphuṭatādhāmabhāvijñānādiśaktimān /
uparāgāt tatas tattadvaicitryaparibṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.37]

mv-k01-v38.plain_english: Just as a face appears in water, a mirror, a jewel, or a sword as trembling, round, subtle, long, and so on, so its manifestation varies with the medium.
mv-k01-v38.sanskrit_cite:
yathā mukhasya tadvyaktisthāne 'psu mukure maṇau /
khaḍge cañcalasadvṛttasūkṣmadīrghādikā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.38]

mv-k01-v39.plain_english: Thus, in the supreme form, the treasures of knowledge arise, beautiful with the unlimited triad of heart, seed, and self.
mv-k01-v39.sanskrit_cite:
tad itthaṃ parame rūpe prodbhūtā jñānasaṃpadaḥ /
anavacchinnahṛdayabījātmatrayasundarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.39]

mv-k01-v40.plain_english: But when Bhairava, expanded by power, desires to emit the floods of beings as inner waves of his own surging form,
mv-k01-v40.sanskrit_cite:
yadā tūcchaladākārasvataraṅgāntarātmakān /
visisṛkṣati bhāvaughān bhairavaḥ śaktibṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.40]

mv-k01-v41.plain_english: Then those very treasures of cognition, as if taking on a constraint of slight activity and practice born from that limiting condition,
mv-k01-v41.sanskrit_cite:
tadā tā eva vijñānasaṃpadas tadupādhijām /
īṣatkriyāsamācārayantraṇāṃ saṃśritā iva // [AgMsv_1.41]

mv-k01-v42.plain_english: having assumed all around an identity with the flood of those waves, still remain within awareness-Bhairava, who is beautiful with the bliss of the world.
mv-k01-v42.sanskrit_cite:
paritas tattaraṅgaughasātmatāṃ samupāśrite /
tathāpi jagadānandasundare bodhabhairave // [AgMsv_1.42]

mv-k01-v43.plain_english: In that powerful awareness, satisfied with the mere fullness of being, the state of the power-holder is set aside by its own full power alone.
mv-k01-v43.sanskrit_cite:
bhāvanirbharatāmātrasaṃtṛpte śaktiśālini /
pūrṇayā nijaśaktyaiva nyakkṛte śaktimatpade // [AgMsv_1.43]

mv-k01-v44.plain_english: Such a stream of knowledge, whose nature is reflective awareness, unfolds; and in it some delight arises through the teaching of enjoyment.
mv-k01-v44.sanskrit_cite:
tādṛg eva vimarśātmā jñānadhārā vijṛmbhate /
yasyāṃ bhogopadeśena ko 'pi hlādaḥ pravartate // [AgMsv_1.44]

mv-k01-v45.plain_english: For the fortunate, even the multitude of enjoyments, nourished by confidence in the practice of that awareness, becomes a state of supreme liberation.

mv-k01-v46.plain_english: Here it is said that the deity's delight in worship is full of the stirring arousal of its own primordial power, especially arising from among the Mothers.
mv-k01-v46.sanskrit_cite:
yatrocyate svaśaktyādikṣobhasaṃraṃbhanirbharā /
devasya yāgapriyatā viśeṣān mātṛmadhyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.46]

mv-k01-v47.plain_english: By the surge of sovereign power, this deity, whose greatness is cognition and who has obtained the name of the lordly state, has become manifested and unfolded.
mv-k01-v47.sanskrit_cite:
aiśvaryaśaktyudrekeṇa labdheśvarapadābhidhaḥ /
devo vijñānamahimā prodbhūto 'yaṃ prapañcitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.47]

mv-k01-v48.plain_english: Here too, in the joining and separating of infinite portions of beings, countlessness is attained because of the connection with the non-difference of the prior state.

mv-k01-v49.plain_english: Simply by force of that adjunct, devoid of the state of consciousness-knowledge, are spread the various powers of scripture, action, and knowledge.
mv-k01-v49.sanskrit_cite:
tadupādhivaśād eva saṃvijjñānapadojjhitāḥ /
tāyante vividhāḥ śāstrakriyājñānavibhūtayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.49]

mv-k01-v50.plain_english: This main world is discussed as fivefold, yet the truth remains undivided.
mv-k01-v50.sanskrit_cite:
mukhyas tv eṣa prapañco 'yaṃ pañcātmatvena carcitaḥ /
tathā ca vakṣyate tattvam abhinnam api pañcadhā // [AgMsv_1.50]

mv-k01-v51.plain_english: By active lordship, directing what lacks, desire cessation, and self-abiding, such sentence collections establish the point.
mv-k01-v51.sanskrit_cite:
savyāpārādhipatvena taddhīnaprerakatvataḥ /
icchānivṛtteḥ svasthatvād ityādyair vākyasaṃcayaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.51]

mv-k01-v52.plain_english: In this context, differences made by place, time, and art do not arise; granted, we say so.
mv-k01-v52.sanskrit_cite:
nanv etāvati sandarbhe deśakālakalākṛtāḥ /
bhedā na saṃbhavanty eva bāḍham om iti vacmahe // [AgMsv_1.52]

mv-k01-v53.plain_english: Here time principle is not merely a name, and even great time power does not expand.
mv-k01-v53.sanskrit_cite:
na hy atra kālatattvasya nāmamātraṃ vibhāvyate /
vaibhavy api mahākālī śaktir nātra vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.53]

mv-k01-v54.plain_english: Then, in the undivided self-full state, what is this grasp of speech reasoning?
mv-k01-v54.sanskrit_cite:
tarhy abhinne svasaṃpūrṇe tadā paścāt punar yadā /
parataś ceti ko nv eṣa vācoyuktiparigrahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.54]

mv-k01-v55.plain_english: Here we say truth indeed; in reality, in clear self, even in expanded principle creation and time.
mv-k01-v55.sanskrit_cite:
atra brūmaḥ satyam eva vastutas tu sphuṭātmani /
jṛmbhite tattvasarge 'pi kāle 'py unmiṣitātmani // [AgMsv_1.55]

mv-k01-v56.plain_english: For awareness, these prior and later alternatives do not exist, because time becomes a differentiator only as qualifier.
mv-k01-v56.sanskrit_cite:
bodhasya naiva santy etāḥ pūrvāparavikalpanāḥ /
kālo viśeṣaṇatvena yasmād bhavati bhedakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.56]

mv-k01-v57.plain_english: That qualifier is said to become knowability by difference, as a blue lotus.
mv-k01-v57.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣaṇaṃ ca tat proktaṃ samaśīrṣikayaiva yat /
bhedena vedyatām eti yathā nīlaṃ saroruhaṃ // [AgMsv_1.57]

mv-k01-v58.plain_english: Awareness is never knowable; knowability is appearing-ness by clarity grace.
mv-k01-v58.sanskrit_cite:
na ca bodhasya vedyatvaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
vedyatvaṃ bhāsamānatvaṃ tat prakāśaprasādataḥ // [AgMsv_1.58]

mv-k01-v59.plain_english: Clarity is that awareness; if another awareness stood, surely regress would proceed from clarity rules.
mv-k01-v59.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśaḥ sa sa bodhaś ca na ced bodhāntarasthiteḥ /
prakāśaniyamān nūnam anavasthā pravartate // [AgMsv_1.59]

mv-k01-v60.plain_english: Deluded ones who call awareness non-first-appearing and object-appearance-natured are cheated by their own words.
mv-k01-v60.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva vimūḍhā ye bodham aprathamānakam /
arthaprathātmakaṃ brūyuḥ svavacovañcitās tu te // [AgMsv_1.60]

mv-k01-v61.plain_english: Therefore time is not fit to differentiate awareness, nor is that time able to become differentiator of the knowable.
mv-k01-v61.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt kālo na bodhasya bhedakatvāya kalpate /
nāpi vedyasya kālo 'sau bhedakībhavituṃ kṣamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.61]

mv-k01-v62.plain_english: The universe is not different from awareness; otherwise it would not shine; pervaded by clarity, variegated being shines.
mv-k01-v62.sanskrit_cite:
viśvaṃ hi bodhābhinnaṃ tad atathātve na bhāsate /
prakāśena samāviṣṭaś citraṃ bhāvaḥ prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.62]

mv-k01-v63.plain_english: Thus universe clarity would be eternal for all; when clarity named awareness is present, it attains clarity-ness.
mv-k01-v63.sanskrit_cite:
viśvaprakāśa evaṃ syāt sarvasyaiva sadātanaḥ /
sati prakāśe bodhākhye sa prakāśatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_1.63]

mv-k01-v64.plain_english: Even if an unlit being is clarity-self and known, that unlit being is darkness as refuge here.
mv-k01-v64.sanskrit_cite:
aprakāśo 'pi bhāvaś cet prakāśātmā sa vedyate /
aprakāśas tv asau bhāva ity atra śaraṇaṃ tamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.64]

mv-k01-v65.plain_english: If an unlit being-self is made clarity-self, surely that being would be destroyed from loss of self-clarity.
mv-k01-v65.sanskrit_cite:
yaś cāprakāśo bhāvātmā prakāśātmā sa cet kṛtaḥ /
nūnaṃ sa bhāvo naṣṭaḥ syāt svāprakāśatvavicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.65]

mv-k01-v66.plain_english: Even rule cannot make clarity not of that form; but this being shines when clarity is present.
mv-k01-v66.sanskrit_cite:
nātadrūpaṃ prakāśaṃ ca kartuṃ vidhir api kṣamaḥ /
nanv etāvad idaṃbhāvaḥ prakāśe sati bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.66]

mv-k01-v67.plain_english: Let this be indeed; but thus unlit clarity-ness, of being and in unlit-ness, when made clear and present.
mv-k01-v67.sanskrit_cite:
astv etad eva kiṃtv ittham aprakāśaḥ prakāśatām /
bhāvasya cāprakāśatve prakāśībhāvite sati // [AgMsv_1.67]

mv-k01-v68.plain_english: Thus a separately manifested entity is not the state of things; enough of separate light, for shiva is so.
mv-k01-v68.sanskrit_cite:
naivaṃ prakāśito bhāva iti vastusthitir bhavet /
tad alaṃ vyatiriktena prakāśena śivas tathā // [AgMsv_1.68]

mv-k01-v69.plain_english: Therefore that light is sung as supreme shiva, whose inconceivable glory is swayed by freedom.
mv-k01-v69.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt prakāśa evāsau gīto yaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ /
sa evācintyamahimā svātantryoddāmaghūrṇitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.69]

mv-k01-v70.plain_english: So it shines through those natures in unfailing state; here all-knowingness is not suspected everywhere.
mv-k01-v70.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśate tathā tais taiḥ svabhāvair acyutasthitiḥ /
nātra sarvatra sarvajñabhāvaḥ kaś cana śaṅkyate // [AgMsv_1.70]

mv-k01-v71.plain_english: I, Caitra, know the pot not the cloth; but this one knows that; this one does not know the cloth; I know both pot and cloth.
mv-k01-v71.sanskrit_cite:
ahaṃ caitro ghaṭaṃ vedmi na paṭaṃ, veda taṃ tv ayaṃ. /
nāyaṃ vetti paṭaḥ, so 'haṃ jāne ghaṭapaṭāv iti // [AgMsv_1.71]

mv-k01-v72.plain_english: I will know or not; before, not knowing; not anywhere; gradually I know, simultaneously, devoid of both.
mv-k01-v72.sanskrit_cite:
vediṣyāmi na vā, pūrvam ajānāṃ naiva vā kva cit, /
krameṇa vedmi yugapad dvābhyām ubhayavarjitam. // [AgMsv_1.72]

mv-k01-v73.plain_english: I know all, yet I know nothing; I am not any entity-self; indeed not I; I am all always.
mv-k01-v73.sanskrit_cite:
sarvaṃ vedmi, na kiṃ cic ca jāne. naivāsmi kaś cana /
bhāvātmā, nanu naivāham. ahaṃ sarvaṃ ca sarvadā. // [AgMsv_1.73]

mv-k01-v74.plain_english: All am I alone; what else could all be? Thus one light unfolds.
mv-k01-v74.sanskrit_cite:
sarvam asmy aham evaikaḥ kiṃ sarvam itarad bhavet /
ityādir eka evāyaṃ prakāśaḥ pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.74]

mv-k01-v75.plain_english: If one were nonexistent, light would not then be supreme; how could it be? Alas fool, how is this to be instructed?
mv-k01-v75.sanskrit_cite:
nanv eko yady asaḥ kaś cit, prakāśo na tadā paraḥ /
kathaṃ bhaved. aho mūḍhaḥ kathaṃ vyutpādyatām ayam // [AgMsv_1.75]

mv-k01-v76.plain_english: One light shines in varied form from freedom; in reality it is neither varied nor unvaried, because of the fault of difference.
mv-k01-v76.sanskrit_cite:
ekaḥ prakāśaḥ svātantryāc citrarūpaḥ prakāśate. /
vastutaś ca na citro 'sau, nācitro bhedadūṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.76]

mv-k01-v77.plain_english: If cloth's light arose in pot's light, that would not be pot-light; it would be two lights.
mv-k01-v77.sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭaprakāśe vastrasya prakāśo yadi saṃbhavet /
nāsau ghaṭaprakāśaḥ syād dviprakāśo hy asau bhavet // [AgMsv_1.77]

mv-k01-v78.plain_english: Let that be or not; this is urged by you; light should not be as pot-self, so it stands.
mv-k01-v78.sanskrit_cite:
so 'pi cāstv eva, no nāsti tad idaṃ tvatpracoditam /
ghaṭātmanā prakāśo 'sya mā bhūd ity avatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.78]

mv-k01-v79.plain_english: That is improper, since light's cognition-nature is self-unfolding; if that is the definition, what is this vain word-net pomp?
mv-k01-v79.sanskrit_cite:
tac cāyuktaṃ prakāśasya bodhatvāt svātmajṛmbhaṇam /
lakṣaṇaṃ yadi tat ko 'yaṃ vṛthā vāgjālaḍambaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.79]

mv-k01-v80.plain_english: Limited light is the definition of inert; cognition is distinct from inert, because it is not measured.
mv-k01-v80.sanskrit_cite:
paricchinnaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam /
jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate // [AgMsv_1.80]

mv-k01-v81.plain_english: Therefore, since the sun's existence is established, what fool would say how this all-earth-bearing ray is?
mv-k01-v81.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād arkasya sadbhāve siddhe kaḥ khalu bāliśaḥ /
brūyāt katham ayaṃ svāṃśuśubhritāśeṣabhūr iti // [AgMsv_1.81]

mv-k01-v82.plain_english: Therefore, since light is established, all its variations are keepers of all enjoyment and conduct.
mv-k01-v82.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt siddhe prakāśe 'smin yāḥ prakāśavikalpanāḥ /
sarvās tāḥ sarvasaṃbhuktayoṣiccāritrapālanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.82]

mv-k01-v83.plain_english: If light were unestablished, who am I, what are you, what darkness? Nothing at all, or silence, or how?
mv-k01-v83.sanskrit_cite:
asiddhau ca prakāśasya ko 'haṃ kiṃ tvaṃ tamo 'pi kim /
na kiṃ cid api vā kiṃ syāt tūṣṇīṃ syād api vā katham // [AgMsv_1.83]

mv-k01-v84.plain_english: Therefore time cannot do anything to beings who share bhairava's light-identity.
mv-k01-v84.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt prakāśatādātmyalabdhabhairavabhāginām /
bhāvānām api kālo 'yaṃ na kiṃ cit kartum arhati // [AgMsv_1.84]

mv-k01-v85.plain_english: Alas, then how is the sequence of words like 'tad eti' made? Let it be heard; what was said is spoken again after separation.
mv-k01-v85.sanskrit_cite:
hanta tarhi kathaṃkāraṃ tadetyādivacaḥkramaḥ /
śrūyatām uktam apy etat punar nirbhajya bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_1.85]

mv-k01-v86.plain_english: The light that is this very one appears thus and thus; no other's light shines, but that alone shines.
mv-k01-v86.sanskrit_cite:
yaḥ prakāśaḥ sa evāyaṃ pratibhāti tathā tathā /
naiva cānyasya kasyāpi sa tu bhāty eva kevalam // [AgMsv_1.86]

mv-k01-v87.plain_english: That very one is supremely generous and illuminator of all; being free, his will-power is called freedom.
mv-k01-v87.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva paramodāraḥ sarvasyaivāvabhāsakaḥ /
svatantra iti tasyecchāśaktiḥ svātantryasaṃjñitā // [AgMsv_1.87]

mv-k01-v88.plain_english: Resting in self through absence of other, that very rest in self is called the god's bliss.
mv-k01-v88.sanskrit_cite:
sa ca svātmani viśrāntas tadanyābhāvayogataḥ /
svātmaviśrāntir evaiṣā devasyānanda ucyate // [AgMsv_1.88]

mv-k01-v89.plain_english: The greatness of his freedom, non-separate from own form, would illuminate confusions of beings in his own light-abode.
mv-k01-v89.sanskrit_cite:
svātantryamahimaivāsya svarūpād apṛthaksthitiḥ /
svaprakāśe nije dhāmni bhāsayed bhāvavibhramān // [AgMsv_1.89]

mv-k01-v90.plain_english: Illumination is called the power of action in scriptures, by which manifold principle-creation is divided.
mv-k01-v90.sanskrit_cite:
bhāsanā ca kriyāśaktir iti śāstreṣu kathyate /
yayā vicitratattvādikalanā pravibhajyate // [AgMsv_1.90]

mv-k01-v91.plain_english: When illumination does not shine, how is anything conceived? That knowing situated within it is remembered as knowledge-power.
mv-k01-v91.sanskrit_cite:
bhāsanānavabhāte ca kathaṃ nāma prakalpate /
tad asyāntaḥsthitaṃ bhānaṃ jñānaśaktir ahaṃ smṛtā // [AgMsv_1.91]

mv-k01-v92.plain_english: This much is the god's form from self alone; that is called opening, then five powers, then the all-pervading.
mv-k01-v92.sanskrit_cite:
etāvad asya devasya yad rūpaṃ svātmamātrataḥ /
sa unmeṣa iti proktaḥ pañcaśaktis tato vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.92]

mv-k01-v93.plain_english: Whether as three powers, one power, or god alone standing, that power then is the goddess determined in essence-scripture.
mv-k01-v93.sanskrit_cite:
triśaktir ekaśaktir vā devo vā kevalaḥ sthitaḥ /
śaktir evātha devī sā sāraśāstre nirūpyate // [AgMsv_1.93]

mv-k01-v94.plain_english: The world-substance will be said from 'said' onward as supreme; that one alone, being, goes to manyness, says the great lord.
mv-k01-v94.sanskrit_cite:
vakṣyate ca jagaddhātuḥ kathitetyāditaḥ param /
saivaikā saty anekatvaṃ gacchatīti maheśinā // [AgMsv_1.94]

mv-k01-v95.plain_english: This one, firmly bliss-rested in self, is described by sisterly word-arrangements by bhairava and others.
mv-k01-v95.sanskrit_cite:
sa cāyaṃ nirbharānandaviśrāntisvātmasusthitaḥ /
sodaryaiḥ śabdasaṃdarbhair bhāṣyate bhairavādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.95]

mv-k01-v96.plain_english: Whether near or far-going, in reality nothing of this is other; what word-collection could there be, or anything else, of the lord?
mv-k01-v96.sanskrit_cite:
savidhaṃ dūragaṃ vāpi yady apy asya na vastutaḥ /
śabdajātaṃ bhavet kiṃ cid anyad apy atha vā prabhoḥ // [AgMsv_1.96]

mv-k01-v97.plain_english: Thus the god illuminates thus and thus; then according to that, all this sequence of construction follows.
mv-k01-v97.sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca bhāsayaty eva deva eṣa tathā tathā /
tatas tadanusāreṇa sarvo 'yaṃ kalpanākramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.97]

mv-k01-v98.plain_english: Nor is that mere construction in such a state; then what ground? Thus the god's intentionality, or thus of those constructing.
mv-k01-v98.sanskrit_cite:
na ca tat kalpanāmātraṃ tathātve 'py atha kā kṣitiḥ /
tathā saṃkalpatāṃ devo yad vā kalpayatāṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.98]

mv-k01-v99.plain_english: Thus this light-self, beyond the thirty-seven-fold, doing manifold illumination, the lord illuminates time.
mv-k01-v99.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ caiṣa prakāśātmā saptatriṃśātmakāt paraḥ /
vaicitryabhāsanāṃ kurvan kālaṃ bhāsayati prabhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.99]

mv-k01-v100.plain_english: This very manifold illumination is declared as time-power; then according to the shining time-power.

mv-k01-v101.plain_english: From ours the coloring 'tad eti' and so on proceeds; that is not there; indeed what is not there, whence is that?
mv-k01-v101.sanskrit_cite:
āsmākīnāt tadetyādir uparāgaḥ pravartate /
na cāsau tatra nāsty eva tatra yan nāsti tat kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.101]

mv-k01-v102.plain_english: Let it be elsewhere; that stands under light's control. Indeed thus others are in the net of principles in pure-impure state.
mv-k01-v102.sanskrit_cite:
anyatra tanyatāṃ nāma tat prakāśavaśaṃ sthitam /
nanv evam apare tattvajāle śuddhetarasthitau // [AgMsv_1.102]

mv-k01-v103.plain_english: In the circle of principles, pure Bhairava existence makes no distinction remain.
mv-k01-v103.sanskrit_cite:
śuddhāśuddhapade vāpi vidyādau tattvamaṇḍale /
śuddhabhairavasadbhāvād aviśeṣo bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.103]

mv-k01-v104.plain_english: We dance, alas; the teaching must be explained with effort, since it turns in the heart of the long-lived one.
mv-k01-v104.sanskrit_cite:
narīnṛtyāmahe hanta yatnād vyākhyeyam eva naḥ /
āyuṣmato yad dhṛdaye svayaṃ viparivartate // [AgMsv_1.104]

mv-k01-v105.plain_english: In ultimate speech there is no pure-impure distinction; yet that distinction remains fixed in fools' minds.
mv-k01-v105.sanskrit_cite:
śuddhāśuddhavibhedo hi paramārthakathāsu no /
sa tu tatkṛta evāste mūḍhānāṃ dhiyi niścalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.105]

mv-k01-v106.plain_english: If the pure-otherness difference is unreal, then scripture disputes only the intended apparent distinction.
mv-k01-v106.sanskrit_cite:
nanu śuddhetaratvākhyo yadi bhedo na vāstavaḥ /
vyācikīrṣitam evaitac chāstraṃ vivadate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.106]

mv-k01-v107.plain_english: Impurity of principles is purified by initiation; hence difference-dominant positions are only local.
mv-k01-v107.sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhatvaṃ hi tattvānāṃ dīkṣayā śodhanaṃ tataḥ /
ityādi bahudhā bhedapradhānātra yataḥ sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.107]

mv-k01-v108.plain_english: In the nondual there is no duality at all; yet difference appears even in the all-pervading.
mv-k01-v108.sanskrit_cite:
ucyate nādvaye 'muṣmin dvaitaṃ nāsty eva sarvathā /
uktaṃ hi bhedavandhye 'pi vibhau bhedāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.108]

mv-k01-v109.plain_english: That is truly called bondage in samsara by maya, knowledge, and related terms; worldly beings are established as such.
mv-k01-v109.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva khalu saṃsāre māyāvidyādibhiḥ padaiḥ /
bandha ity ucyate tatra rūḍhāḥ saṃsāriṇo matāḥ // [AgMsv_1.109]

mv-k01-v110.plain_english: Following that thought gives these beings certainty of pure and impure; and this scripture properly teaches bhagavat yoga.
mv-k01-v110.sanskrit_cite:
taccintānusṛter eṣāṃ śuddhāśuddhādiniścayaḥ /
kiṃ ca śāstram idaṃ samyag bhagavadyogadeśakam // [AgMsv_1.110]

mv-k01-v111.plain_english: They call bhagavat yoga nondual and free from pairs; its teaching would be thus if difference still appears.
mv-k01-v111.sanskrit_cite:
bhagavadyogam advaitaṃ nirdvandvaṃ ca pracakṣate /
tasyopadeśa itthaṃ syād yadi yāvadvibhedavat // [AgMsv_1.111]

mv-k01-v112.plain_english: That is imagined and determined by separating; in nondual Bhairava all-pervading, entry and seating are considered.
mv-k01-v112.sanskrit_cite:
saṃbhāvyate tan nirbhajya nirbhajyaiva nirūpyate /
advaite bhairavavibhau yat praveśopaveśayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.112]

mv-k01-v113.plain_english: Habitual position is absent, for those two live by difference alone; therefore doubt of universal nonduality is removed.
mv-k01-v113.sanskrit_cite:
ābhyāsikī sthitir nāsti tau hi bhedaikajīvitau /
ataḥ saṃbhāvyanikhiladvaitaśaṅkāvyapohane // [AgMsv_1.113]

mv-k01-v114.plain_english: All effort unfolds for teachers and children; therefore duality is spread here by doubting and not doubting.
mv-k01-v114.sanskrit_cite:
gurūṇāṃ ca śiśūnāṃ ca yatnaḥ sarvo vijṛmbhate /
ato dvaitam ihāśaṅkyāśaṅkya sarvaṃ pratanyate // [AgMsv_1.114]

mv-k01-v115.plain_english: That is imagined as far as going, not neglected anywhere; if duality is unrefuted, then one being alone remains.
mv-k01-v115.sanskrit_cite:
tad yāvadgati saṃbhāvya na tu kutrāpy udāsyate /
tathā hi yadi nāmṛṣṭaṃ dvaitaṃ tarhy ekam eva sat // [AgMsv_1.115]

mv-k01-v116.plain_english: Consciousness-Brahman is enough; why is the thirty-fiveness of principles determined?
mv-k01-v116.sanskrit_cite:
cidbrahma tad alaṃ tattvasaṃkhyākalpananirṇayaiḥ /
pañcatriṃśatitā kasmāt tattvānāṃ tan nirūpyate // [AgMsv_1.116]

mv-k01-v117.plain_english: Therefore, having grasped duality's difference-nature as far as it goes, one who rejects it becomes fearless.
mv-k01-v117.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād dvaitasya bhedātmasthiter yāvadgati graham /
kṛtvā yas tatpratikṣepas tena niḥśaṅkatā bhavet // [AgMsv_1.117]

mv-k01-v118.plain_english: This indeed is teaching pierced in knowledge; as possible, it tears the diamond wings.
mv-k01-v118.sanskrit_cite:
etad eva ca vijñāne nirbhidyaivopadeśanam /
yathāsaṃbhavi yad vajrapakṣāṇāṃ tad vidāraṇam // [AgMsv_1.118]

mv-k01-v119.plain_english: Thus in the glorious hymn by Bhatta Narayana, salutation to you manifests and breaks worldly delusion.
mv-k01-v119.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi śrīmatā stotre bhaṭṭanārāyaṇena tat /
namas te bhavasaṃbhrāntabhrāntim udbhāvya bhindate // [AgMsv_1.119]

mv-k01-v120.plain_english: They reveal knowledge-bliss free from pairs, O god; the word free-from-pairs is made manifest as nondual.
mv-k01-v120.sanskrit_cite:
jñānānandaṃ ca nirdvandvaṃ deva vṛtvā vivṛṇvate /
nirdvandvam iti nirdvaitaṃ prakaṭīkriyate padam // [AgMsv_1.120]

mv-k01-v121.plain_english: Delusions are manifested, and the ca here is wonder-bringing; here nondual is spread before.
mv-k01-v121.sanskrit_cite:
udbhāvyante bhramāś ceti cakāro 'trādbhutāvahaḥ /
iha cādvaitam eveti purataḥ prataniṣyate // [AgMsv_1.121]

mv-k01-v122.plain_english: Path-purification and the like — its incongruence in dualism will be stated: not this without non-difference. But surely, what even without difference?
mv-k01-v122.sanskrit_cite:
adhvaśuddhyādikaṃ dvaite 'nupapattīti vakṣyate /
abhedena vinā naitan nanu bhedaṃ vināpi kim // [AgMsv_1.122]

mv-k01-v123.plain_english: True — but in the nondual principle even difference is not unfitting; for this is that supreme nondualism, which is no abandoning-and-grasping of difference.
mv-k01-v123.sanskrit_cite:
satyaṃ kiṃtv advaye tattve bhedo 'pi na na yujyate /
idaṃ hi tat parādvaitaṃ bhedatyāgagrahau na yat // [AgMsv_1.123]

mv-k01-v124.plain_english: But in difference, with world-beings settled each in its own nature — this word non-difference, I think, divides them out of sheer relish.
mv-k01-v124.sanskrit_cite:
bhede tu viśvabhāvānāṃ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ /
abheda iti śabdo 'yaṃ manye bhedayate rasāt // [AgMsv_1.124]

mv-k01-v125.plain_english: Enough of that — the matter at hand is answered: as the Lord indeed manifests the imagining of difference, so too surely does time expand likewise.
mv-k01-v125.sanskrit_cite:
tad alaṃ prakṛtaṃ nirūpyate parameśaḥ kila bhedakalpanām /
prakaṭīkurute yathā tathā nanu kālo 'pi vijṛmbhate tathā // [AgMsv_1.125]
