mv-k03-v403.plain_english: Thus it is also said there: in that sushiva covering on the path, Sadāśiva is first to be known.
mv-k03-v403.sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca tatraivoktaṃ tatsuśivāvaraṇe 'dhvani /
suśivāvaraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ tatra jñeyaḥ sadāśivaḥ // [AgMsv_1.404]

mv-k03-v404.plain_english: Joined with ten Śiva and endowed with eighteen Rudra, authority is in the Īśa principle, but the desire to grasp that is in Sauśiva.
mv-k03-v404.sanskrit_cite:
śivadaśakasaṃyukto rudrāṣṭādaśakānvitaḥ /
adhikāro hīśatattve tajjighṛkṣā tu sauśive // [AgMsv_1.405]

mv-k03-v405.plain_english: In the covering, from bindu in the enjoyment-abode, from the lord's abundance, there is a supreme triad of Bhairava knowledge in the power principle.
mv-k03-v405.sanskrit_cite:
varaṇe binduto bhogadhāmni vibhavato vibhoḥ /
bhairavākhyasya bodhasya śaktitattve paraṃ trayam // [AgMsv_1.406]

mv-k03-v406.plain_english: Therefore the position is above Īśvara and below the Sadāśiva station, as said by the sushiva covering in the glorious Svacchanda scripture.
mv-k03-v406.sanskrit_cite:
sthitis tasmād īśvarordhve sadāśivapadād adhaḥ /
suśivāvaraṇenoktā śrīmatsvacchandaśāsane // [AgMsv_1.407]

mv-k03-v407.plain_english: After that, in these Śiva-Rudra distinctions, enough; on the māyīya path, established by the Śivas, the one named Śiva is said.
mv-k03-v407.sanskrit_cite:
tadanantaram etāsu śivarudrabhidāsv alam /
māyīyādhvani kḷptāsu śivair uktaḥ śivābhidhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.408]

mv-k03-v408.plain_english: The difference, by Rudras and called Rudra, thus reaches variety; then, from the flourishing essence of rising action, it becomes gradually clear.
mv-k03-v408.sanskrit_cite:
bhedo rudraiś ca rudrākhya iti prāpto vicitratām /
tataḥ prodyatkriyāsāraprollāsāt kramaśaḥ sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.409]

mv-k03-v409.plain_english: The scriptural meanings that rest on Maya-born Vaikhari speech heard by all, and whose nature is letters, sentences, and words, are within the range of the world.

mv-k03-v410.plain_english: Having resorted to those various transmitters of the tantras, they proceed; therefore, at first, as long as they come through the Maya-born cavity of Vaikhari.
mv-k03-v410.sanskrit_cite:
samāśritya pravartante tāṃs tāṃs tantrāvatārakān /
tena prathamato yāvan māyīyāṃ vaikharīṃ darīm // [AgMsv_1.411]

mv-k03-v411.plain_english: This scriptural meaning, bound by Maya-born letters, has not arrived within as that which consists of the supreme speech-letters of essential awakening.
mv-k03-v411.sanskrit_cite:
māyīyavarṇasaṃdṛbdhaḥ śāstrārtho nāyam āgataḥ /
antaḥ sāravibodhaikaparavāṅmayavarṇakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.412]

mv-k03-v412.plain_english: The scriptural meaning, refined by the root impression of uncontrived supreme immersion, extends to the worldly level, yet it is in the supreme thirty-seventh lord.
mv-k03-v412.sanskrit_cite:
akṛtrimaparāveśamūlasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaḥ /
śāstrārtho laukikānto 'sti saptatriṃśe pare vibhau // [AgMsv_1.413]

mv-k03-v413.plain_english: For there, unreal beings have no reality anywhere at all; how could respect arise in a lordly nature overcome by disrespect?
mv-k03-v413.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāsatāṃ hi bhāvānāṃ kvāpi nāsty eva satyatā /
svāminy avinayākrāntaprakṛtau vinayaḥ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.414]

mv-k03-v414.plain_english: Therefore the entire meaning of scripture is established as the nature of the supreme principle; hence even these Vedas and others are Maya-born portions of teaching.
mv-k03-v414.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt samastaśāstrārthaḥ paratattvātmanā sthitaḥ /
ato vedādayo 'py ete māyīyāḥ śāsanāṃśavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.415]

mv-k03-v415.plain_english: They shine forth from the power of the Bhairava-sun alone, not from elsewhere; for apart from the reflective awareness of consciousness there could be no other cause anywhere at all.
mv-k03-v415.sanskrit_cite:
sphuranti bhairavādityaprabhāvād eva nānyataḥ /
na hi saṃvidvimarśāt syād anyat kvāpy eva kāraṇam // [AgMsv_1.416]

mv-k03-v416.plain_english: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness would be consciousness alone; therefore, since it is spoken of as both effect and cause, that status is applied only figuratively.
mv-k03-v416.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvinnāthasya saṃvit syāt saṃvid eva tathā yataḥ /
kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ceti tathātva upacāryate // [AgMsv_1.417]

mv-k03-v417.plain_english: For in the sequential transformation of a being with extended properties, at the beginning and at the end, consciousness alone appears as its very form.
mv-k03-v417.sanskrit_cite:
pariṇāme hi bhāvasya kramād vitatadharmaṇaḥ /
ādyantayoḥ saṃvid eva rūpatvenāvabhāsate // [AgMsv_1.418]

mv-k03-v418.plain_english: And if consciousness could endure division by time, then we would clearly be enjoying gravel bits of sky cut by a sharpened sword.
mv-k03-v418.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvic ca kālakalanāṃ saheta yadi tat sphuṭam /
bhuñjīmahi niśātāsicchinnā vyomāṃśaśarkarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.419]

mv-k03-v419.plain_english: Therefore all the scriptures, because they do not fall away from the form of consciousness and because consciousness is self-luminous, are in reality self-luminous.
mv-k03-v419.sanskrit_cite:
ataḥ samagraśāstrāṇi saṃvidrūpāparicyuteḥ /
saṃvidaḥ svaprakāśatvāt svaprakāśāni vastutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.420]

mv-k03-v420.plain_english: And it should not be said that the expressed ever stands apart from the expresser; for by autonomy the expresser alone appears as what will be expressed.
mv-k03-v420.sanskrit_cite:
na ca vācyaṃ pṛthag jātu vācakād vyavatiṣṭhate /
svātantryād abhidhātaiva bhāvivācyatayā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.421]

mv-k03-v421.plain_english: Sometimes the expressing aspect appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature; sometimes, instead, it appears as expressing a general flash.
mv-k03-v421.sanskrit_cite:
kadācid vācakāṃśas tu svarūpagrastavācyakaḥ /
nirbhāsate kadācit tu sāmānyollāsavācakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.422]

mv-k03-v422.plain_english: Sometimes it shines, qualified by near and countless qualifiers, with a surge of the clear expressed aspect of its own form.

mv-k03-v423.plain_english: Therefore sometimes there is orientation toward meaning, and likewise sometimes orientation toward the word's own form; sometimes a state in which the meaning is desired to be known, and sometimes a state consisting of rasa.
mv-k03-v423.sanskrit_cite:
tenārthaparatā jātu svarūpaparatā tathā /
bubhūtsitārthā kvāpi kvacid rasamayī daśā // [AgMsv_1.424]

mv-k03-v424.plain_english: A variegated state of words is observed, because they do not depart from the form of consciousness; since it flashes through the varied flashings of consciousness, what is wonderful about that?
mv-k03-v424.sanskrit_cite:
śabdānāṃ lakṣyate citrā saṃvidrūpānapāyataḥ /
saṃvidvicitrakacanaiḥ kacatīti kim adbhutam // [AgMsv_1.425]

mv-k03-v425.plain_english: Thus word, non-different from the Śiva-natured level of reflective awareness, becomes clear here and illuminates both itself and other. Valid cognition is nothing but reflective awareness whose essence is consciousness; anything else is called cognition only by figurative extension from that.
mv-k03-v425.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ śivātmakavimarśapadād abhinnaḥ śabdaḥ sphuṭatvata iha svaparaprakāśaḥ /
mānaṃ tad eva citisāravimarśamātram anyat punas tadupacāravaśāt tathā hi // [AgMsv_1.426]

mv-k03-v426.plain_english: That ultimate consciousness, whose nature is self-luminous, is called self-awareness, because the ordering of the entire universe rests on it.
mv-k03-v426.sanskrit_cite:
svaprakāśātmikā yeyaṃ saṃvittiḥ pāramārthikī /
tat svasaṃvedanaṃ proktaṃ yato viśvavyavasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.427]

mv-k03-v427.plain_english: This consciousness never goes beyond a nature whose very self is reflective awareness. Its reflective awareness is its supreme, full enjoyment, and that state is called paśyantī.
mv-k03-v427.sanskrit_cite:
sā caiṣā na vimarśātmasvarūpam ativartate /
vimarśo 'syāḥ paro bhogaḥ pūrṇaḥ paśyanty udāhṛtā // [AgMsv_1.428]

mv-k03-v428.plain_english: Understand that same goddess as parāparā, which is valid cognition. In that state the knowable object appears on the lower side and stands forth through identity with that cognition.
mv-k03-v428.sanskrit_cite:
parāparā saiva devī mānam ity avadhāryatām /
yatrāparāṃśagaṃ meyaṃ tādātmyād vyavatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.429]

mv-k03-v429.plain_english: For an object cannot be determined by a cognition that is entirely different from it; just as a crow cannot claim the whiteness that belongs to a swan.
mv-k03-v429.sanskrit_cite:
na hi bhinnena mānena meyasya syād vyavastitiḥ /
na hi haṃsasya śuklatve kākaḥ śvetatvam arhati // [AgMsv_1.430]

mv-k03-v430.plain_english: The teacher Śaṅkaranandana says the same thing: establishment does not arise merely because something is cognition, nor because it is other than cognition, nor because of sublation, nor because of non-establishment.
mv-k03-v430.sanskrit_cite:
etad eva tathā cāha guruḥ śaṅkaranandanaḥ /
na mānatvāt tato 'nyatvān na bādhād asthiteḥ sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.431]

mv-k03-v431.plain_english: A thing is established through properties that are inseparable from luminosity and fixed in existence; if it stood outside that, it could not attain establishment at all.
mv-k03-v431.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśenāvinābhūtaiḥ sattāyāṃ niyatātmabhiḥ /
dharmair bhāvo bahirbhāvān na bhāvaḥ siddhim ṛcchati // [AgMsv_1.432]

mv-k03-v432.plain_english: Therefore the triad of knower, cognition, and known, though appearing in those roles, is in essence nothing but consciousness and shines by its own nature as self-luminous.
mv-k03-v432.sanskrit_cite:
tena saṃvittikātmaiva mātṛmānaprameyatā /
gṛhṇatī svaprakāśatvaṃ svabhāvād eva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.433]

mv-k03-v433.plain_english: That consciousness, inwardly beautiful with mantra-natured verbal reflective awareness, is valid by itself, because it does not depend on anything else.
mv-k03-v433.sanskrit_cite:
sā cāntaḥsthitamantrātmaśabdanāmarśasundarā /
anapekṣānyavirahāt pramāṇaṃ svata eva hi // [AgMsv_1.434]

mv-k03-v434.plain_english: The various names of that same consciousness, arising in many modes from its own grace, were fashioned by different theorists.
mv-k03-v434.sanskrit_cite:
tasyā eva vicitrāṇi nāmāni bahubhaṅgibhiḥ /
tatprasādotthitāny eva vādinaḥ paryacīkḷpan // [AgMsv_1.435]

mv-k03-v435.plain_english: And so the teaching that perception rests on the sphere of the eye and other senses is now examined.
mv-k03-v435.sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca cakṣurādyakṣamaṇḍalīṭaṅkaniṣṭhitam /
pratyakṣam iti yad gītaṃ tat tāvat pravivicyate // [AgMsv_1.436]

mv-k03-v436.plain_english: If the senses cannot be established apart from consciousness, then the supposed identity of object and cognition would have to be treated like that of an external pot and so on.
mv-k03-v436.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvittivyatirekeṇa yady akṣāṇāṃ vyavasthitiḥ /
na syād arthapramāṇaikyaṃ tarhi bāhyaghaṭādivat // [AgMsv_1.437]

mv-k03-v437.plain_english: An objection says: the eye and other senses are instruments of the self, unlike a pot and so on; therefore things are cognized by those senses, not by pots and the like.
mv-k03-v437.sanskrit_cite:
nanv ātmanaś cakṣurādi karaṇaṃ na ghaṭādikam /
tasmāt tenaiva bhāvānāṃ mānaṃ na tu ghaṭādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.438]

mv-k03-v438.plain_english: If the self is taken as all-pervading, its contact is undifferentiated; and since the eye and other senses are not relevantly different in materiality from pots and the like, mere contact cannot explain their special role.
mv-k03-v438.sanskrit_cite:
vyāpakābhimatasyāsya saṃyoge cāviśeṣiṇaḥ /
bhautikatvāviśeṣeṇa ghaṭādyaiś cakṣurādinā // [AgMsv_1.439]

mv-k03-v439.plain_english: How could the self's need for an instrument be fulfilled in a determinate way? Only a specific contact, not a generic one, could be the basis for something becoming an instrument.
mv-k03-v439.sanskrit_cite:
ātmanaḥ karaṇākāṅkṣāpūraṇaṃ niyataṃ kutaḥ /
viśiṣṭa eva saṃyogaḥ karaṇatve nibandhanam // [AgMsv_1.440]

mv-k03-v440.plain_english: If one says the specific difference comes from various actions called merit and demerit, that explanation is devoid of the appearance of genuine reasoning.
mv-k03-v440.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣaḥ karmabhis tais tair dharmādharmagiroditaiḥ /
tad etad yuktisadbhāvapratibhāvikalātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.441]

mv-k03-v441.plain_english: One who, intent on evasion, speaks of cognition as arising from an all-pervading self in contact with all the senses deceives the deluded.
mv-k03-v441.sanskrit_cite:
bruvan vañcayate mugdhān palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ /
yac cāśeṣākṣasaṃyogivyāpakātmavaśotthitām // [AgMsv_1.442]

mv-k03-v442.plain_english: Mind is said to cut cognition at once; even there, mind-self alone is first fitted.
mv-k03-v442.sanskrit_cite:
yugapaj jñaptim ācchettuṃ mano nāma nigadyate /
tatrāpi brumahe pūrvaṃ manasātmaiva yujyate // [AgMsv_1.443]

mv-k03-v443.plain_english: Who would make self-mind union? If it is pervasive, all minds would go.
mv-k03-v443.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpy ātmamanoyogaṃ kaḥ kuryād iti carcyatām /
vyāpakatvād asau syāc cet sarvair eva mano vrajet // [AgMsv_1.444]

mv-k03-v444.plain_english: If one union arises, all would become omniscient, if own mind depends on presiding senses.
mv-k03-v444.sanskrit_cite:
ekasya jāte saṃyoge sarvaḥ sarvajñatām iyāt /
yadi svāntam adhiṣṭhātṛ cakṣurādyam apekṣate // [AgMsv_1.445]

mv-k03-v445.plain_english: Therefore presiding over objects is so many along the sense-particle path, illuminated by contact with fine sense particles.

mv-k03-v446.plain_english: Let one atom of an external object like a pot appear; but if mind-presiding arises in sense-range.
mv-k03-v446.sanskrit_cite:
bāhyasyārthasya kuṇḍāder aṇur eko 'vabhāsatām /
athāpi mānasādhiṣṭhā jātā ced akṣagocare // [AgMsv_1.447]

mv-k03-v447.plain_english: Power arises in its own domain; then eye-rays are emitted from the tiniest hole.
mv-k03-v447.sanskrit_cite:
tad etasya svaviṣaye śaktataivopajāyate /
tarhi sūkṣmatamacchidranissṛtā netraraśmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.448]

mv-k03-v448.plain_english: In the world-abiding flood they do not make valid cognition; senses grasp beings situated in a suitable place.
mv-k03-v448.sanskrit_cite:
viśvavartini bhāvaughe na pramāṃ kurvate kutaḥ /
yogyadeśasthitān bhāvān gṛhṇate 'kṣāṇi nanv alam // [AgMsv_1.449]

mv-k03-v449.plain_english: Suitability of place is to be examined; the place where cognition occurs is called suitable.
mv-k03-v449.sanskrit_cite:
yogyataiva hi deśasya kīdṛśīti vicāryatām /
yatrasthasya bhaved vittiḥ sa deśo yogya ucyate // [AgMsv_1.450]

mv-k03-v450.plain_english: Where would cognition occur? It is not shown; these logician-pretenders lack reasoned presentation.
mv-k03-v450.sanskrit_cite:
kutrasthasya bhaved vittir iti kiṃ vā na darśyate /
tad amī tārkikammanyā yuktyupanyāsavarjitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.451]

mv-k04-v451.plain_english: Why did it not stay silent before, and what do boasts avail for one barren of resolve?
mv-k04-v451.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvam eva kathaṃ tūṣṇīṃ nātiṣṭhan kiṃ vikatthanaiḥ /
ātmanaś cābhisaṃdhānavandhyasyaiva balādayam // [AgMsv_1.452]

mv-k04-v452.plain_english: Would the union of mind and sense-net be inconsistent, and does resolve arise toward its object?
mv-k04-v452.sanskrit_cite:
manokṣajālasaṃyogo bhavet kiṃ nāsamañjasaḥ /
abhisandhir athaitasya viṣayaṃ prati jāyate // [AgMsv_1.453]

mv-k04-v453.plain_english: If unknown, what resolve; if known, what purpose in sense-union; if remembered, it is shaped by the resolver.
mv-k04-v453.sanskrit_cite:
ajñāte ko 'bhisandhiḥ syāj jñāte ko 'rtho 'kṣasaṃyujā /
prajñāte smaryamāṇe ced abhisandhātṛbhāvitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.454]

mv-k04-v454.plain_english: The resolver's effort arises elsewhere, while senses rest on the mind-united self.

mv-k04-v455.plain_english: How do objects, by overtaking the eye sequence, extend knowerhood in the self?
mv-k04-v455.sanskrit_cite:
viṣayāḥ savidhībhūtanetrādyullaṅghanakramāt /
ātmany eva kathaṃkāraṃ pramātṛtvaṃ pratanvatām // [AgMsv_1.456]

mv-k04-v456.plain_english: If knowledge-made motherhood occurs in the self, how can motherhood be doubted for another?
mv-k04-v456.sanskrit_cite:
nanu jñānakṛto mātṛbhāvo vijñānam ātmani /
samavaiti tato 'nyasya kathaṃ mātṛtvaśaṅkanam // [AgMsv_1.457]

mv-k04-v457.plain_english: We say knowledge is there; why fear, O party-blind one, that reply was stated?
mv-k04-v457.sanskrit_cite:
etad eva vayaṃ brūmo jñānaṃ tatraiva vai kutaḥ /
bhayāt svapakṣapātāndhas tad evottaram abhyadhāt // [AgMsv_1.458]

mv-k04-v458.plain_english: As mind is cause in sense-self union, so let another cause be said in self-mind union.
mv-k04-v458.sanskrit_cite:
yathendriyātmasaṃyoge manaḥ kāraṇam ucyate /
tathaivātmamanoyoge kāraṇāntaram ucyatām // [AgMsv_1.459]

mv-k04-v459.plain_english: In such case there is regress damaging the root; otherwise mind-self union is assumed fixed.
mv-k04-v459.sanskrit_cite:
tathātve cānavasthaiva mūlakṣatikarī ca sā /
atha svāntātmasaṃyogo dhruva evābhyupeyate // [AgMsv_1.460]

mv-k04-v460.plain_english: Knowers would always be sleeping, drunk, fainted, unfortunate; this is not your desired knowledge, like a Buddhist disciple.
mv-k04-v460.sanskrit_cite:
jñātāraḥ syuḥ sadā suptamattamūrchitadurbhagāḥ /
na caitad bhavatāṃ jñānam abhīṣṭaṃ śākyaśiṣyavat // [AgMsv_1.461]

mv-k04-v461.plain_english: Therefore how is perceptibility from sense-range; then examination of these is extended.
mv-k04-v461.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt pratyakṣatā nāma katham indriyagocarāt /
atha pratyekam eteṣāṃ parīkṣeyaṃ pratanyate // [AgMsv_1.462]

mv-k04-v462.plain_english: There an atomic eternal all-object swift light non-material mind is proposed, but it does not attain reason-establishedness here.
mv-k04-v462.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāṇu nityaṃ sarvārthaṃ vegavallaghv abhautikam /
manas tac cāpi naiveha yuktisiddhatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_1.463]

mv-k04-v463.plain_english: If an atomic swift-moving mind repeatedly touched objects, the body would become a corpse.
mv-k04-v463.sanskrit_cite:
aṇu cec chīgrasaṃcāri mano yad viṣayān muhuḥ /
spṛśet tadaiva dehasya bhavec chavaśarīratā // [AgMsv_1.464]

mv-k04-v464.plain_english: Even in body-seated mind union, from knowledge union the soul would be only one atom, the rest like pot and wall.
mv-k04-v464.sanskrit_cite:
dehasthe 'pi manoyoge tatraiva jñānayogataḥ /
ekāṇumātraṃ jīvaḥ syāc chiṣṭaṃ syād ghaṭakuḍyavat // [AgMsv_1.465]

mv-k04-v465.plain_english: If union by mind is born somewhere in self-range, knowledge of the all-pervading self is inherent, hence motherhood.
mv-k04-v465.sanskrit_cite:
atha svāntena yogaś cej jātaḥ kvāpy ātmagocare /
tad vibhor ātmano jñānaṃ samavāyīti mātṛtā // [AgMsv_1.466]

mv-k04-v466.plain_english: Thus life in all bodies is not established; by this very reason, would pot and the like have life?
mv-k04-v466.sanskrit_cite:
jāteti sarvadehasthaṃ jīvanaṃ kiṃ na siddhyati /
enayaiva na kiṃ yuktyā ghaṭāder jīvanaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.467]

mv-k04-v467.plain_english: Knowledge born in the all-pervading self; from one part in body only, again in mind there would be a state with parts.
mv-k04-v467.sanskrit_cite:
vibhāv ātmani jātaṃ hi jñānaṃ tatraikadeśataḥ /
dehamātre punaḥ svānte bhavet sāvayavā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.468]

mv-k04-v468.plain_english: If mind were all-pervasive, all perception would occur simultaneously; if mind were eternal, knowledge would always occur.
mv-k04-v468.sanskrit_cite:
vibhutve mānasasya syād yugapat sarvavedanam /
nitye ca manasi jñānaṃ sarvadaiva bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.469]

mv-k04-v469.plain_english: Even liberation state arises possessing awareness union; yet self-mind union is denied in liberation—this is a great wonder.
mv-k04-v469.sanskrit_cite:
mokṣāvasthāpi vijñānayoginy evopajāyate /
muktau cātmamanoyogo nāstīty etan mahādbhutam // [AgMsv_1.470]

mv-k04-v470.plain_english: Why is the pervasiveness of one's own self restricted in liberation; if mind is non-material, how can it be all-object?
mv-k04-v470.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ hi vyāpakatā mokṣe svātmano vinirudhyate /
abhautikaṃ cet sarvārthaṃ kathaṃkāraṃ mano bhavet // [AgMsv_1.471]

mv-k04-v471.plain_english: It asks whether mind is material, since its luminous nature is desired from skill in manifesting distinct objects.
mv-k04-v471.sanskrit_cite:
viśiṣṭaviṣayavyaktikauśalād eva cakṣuṣaḥ /
taijasatvam abhīṣṭaṃ hi tan mano bhautikaṃ na kim // [AgMsv_1.472]

mv-k04-v472.plain_english: If mind grasps all objects, why are other sense-organs needed, since external objects already have sense-usefulness?
mv-k04-v472.sanskrit_cite:
sarvarthatve ca manasaḥ kim anyair akṣaḍambaraiḥ /
nanu bāhye 'sya viṣaye prāg asty akṣopayogitā // [AgMsv_1.473]

mv-k04-v473.plain_english: Thus mind's later state is in what sense perceives; it is said that, just as earlier, it is not grasped by sense.
mv-k04-v473.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hīndriyasaṃdṛṣṭe pāścātyā manasaḥ sthitiḥ /
atrocyate yathaiva prāg indriyeṇa na gṛhyate // [AgMsv_1.474]

mv-k04-v474.plain_english: If the particular is only inferred later, what is there to say; if only a universal was grasped earlier by those senses.
mv-k04-v474.sanskrit_cite:
tac cet svalakṣaṇaṃ paścād anuyantr iti kā kathā /
atha sāmānyamātraṃ tad gṛhītaṃ prāk tadindriyaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.475]

mv-k04-v475.plain_english: Then particular is fixed and mind determines particular; if not, why would mind grasp a universal?
mv-k04-v475.sanskrit_cite:
vyaktiniṣṭhaṃ tadānīṃ ca manasā vyaktiniścayaḥ /
nāstīti manasā kasmāt sāmānyagrahaṇaṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.476]

mv-k04-v476.plain_english: Without particular grasp, from where universal grasp? And if universal grasp occurs, mind's all-objectness is destroyed.
mv-k04-v476.sanskrit_cite:
vinā vyaktigraheṇaiva sāmānyagrahaṇaṃ ya[ku]taḥ /
sāmānyagrahaṇe cāsya sarvārthatvaṃ nirudhyate // [AgMsv_1.477]

mv-k04-v477.plain_english: Deprived of particular grasp, all words vanish; the speed attributed to it in that object is thereby challenged.
mv-k04-v477.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣagrahavandhyasya sarvaśabdavilopataḥ /
āśugāmitvam etasya yac coktaṃ tatra vastuni // [AgMsv_1.478]

mv-k04-v478.plain_english: For an object before the hand, a somewhat distant pot, and very distant Meru, how can going-agency be equal?
mv-k04-v478.sanskrit_cite:
puraḥsthite svahastādau kiṃcid dūragate ghaṭe /
atidūre ca mervādau kathaṃ tulyaiva gantṛtā // [AgMsv_1.479]

mv-k04-v479.plain_english: Because of prior light of swift-moving things, difference by near and far is manifested.
mv-k04-v479.sanskrit_cite:
āśusaṃcāriṇāṃ yasmāt kvāpi pūrvakatejasām (?) /
savidhāsavidhatvena viśeṣaḥ pravibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.480]

mv-k04-v480.plain_english: How could a non-elemental subtle thing grasp mountains and the like? Manifestation is established by the same through the same.
mv-k04-v480.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ cābhautikaṃ sūkṣmaṃ gṛhṇīyāt parvatādikam /
abhivyaktiḥ samānasya samānena vidhīyate // [AgMsv_1.481]

mv-k04-v481.plain_english: Let there be material intellect, then ego, then mind; even so, mind's atomicity is not established.
mv-k04-v481.sanskrit_cite:
nanv astu prākṛtī buddhis tato 'haṃkṛt tato manaḥ /
ittham apy aṇutā naiva manasaḥ saṃprasiddhyati // [AgMsv_1.482]

mv-k04-v482.plain_english: By pervasiveness the previous refutations remain; thus mind is not accepted by reason-parts for us.
mv-k04-v482.sanskrit_cite:
vyāpakatvena pūrvoktadūṣaṇāni sthitāny alam /
itthaṃ mano na yuktyaṃśair mānasāvarjanāya naḥ // [AgMsv_1.483]

mv-k04-v483.plain_english: Such as is desired by other instruments for dualist-deluded views, so participates in the manifestation of consciousness-self.
mv-k04-v483.sanskrit_cite:
yādṛg vādyantarair iṣṭaṃ dvaitavyāmūḍhadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
cidātmanaḥ prakāśasya tathābhāsanabhāginī // [AgMsv_1.484]

mv-k04-v484.plain_english: Let that mind be a power imagined by self-autonomy; where ear and space are, there all sound hearing would be.
mv-k04-v484.sanskrit_cite:
yā śaktis tan manas tv astu svasvātantryopakalpitam /
yatra śrotraṃ nabhas tatra sarvaśabdaśrutir bhavet // [AgMsv_1.485]

mv-k04-v485.plain_english: By eye and the rest perception is everywhere unobstructed because of space; obstruction by merit and demerit shows the opponent's reasoning is weak.
mv-k04-v485.sanskrit_cite:
cakṣurādyaiś ca sarvatra nirvibandhaṃ yato nabhaḥ /
dharmādharmair vibandhaś ca yuktyupanyāsavaikalī // [AgMsv_1.486]

mv-k04-v486.plain_english: How could deafness and the like arise, or how could they be treated? Thus grace comes by destroying the support of bondage.
mv-k04-v486.sanskrit_cite:
bādhiryādi kathaṃ ca syāt kathaṃ vā taccikitsanam /
bandhāśrayavighātena tadanugrahas tathā // [AgMsv_1.487]

mv-k04-v487.plain_english: A sense organ is inherent in its own parts; space is not dependent anywhere: this is the position.
mv-k04-v487.sanskrit_cite:
akṣaṃ svāvayaveṣv eva x x x samavāyinaḥ /
viśeṣeṇa nabho naiva kvāpy āśritam iti sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.488]

mv-k04-v488.plain_english: Conjunction occurs together with being; by grace and destruction let it be modified then.
mv-k04-v488.sanskrit_cite:
saṃyogitā tu \ldots sākaṃ bhāvena vartate /
tadanugrahaghātābhyām api vikriyatāṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.489]

mv-k04-v489.plain_english: Grace is grace and that is its support; thus this self-speech construction appears empty to us.
mv-k04-v489.sanskrit_cite:
yad anugrahas tad anugrahaḥ sa tadāśrayaḥ /
itīyaṃ svavacaḥkḷptir niḥsāraiva vibhāti naḥ // [AgMsv_1.490]

mv-k04-v490.plain_english: When asked what support these senses have, favor is named as support.
mv-k04-v490.sanskrit_cite:
āśrayadvārako 'kṣāṇām anugraha iti sphuṭam /
abhidhatsva ka eteṣām āśrayo 'stv iti codite // [AgMsv_1.491]

mv-k04-v491.plain_english: This reasoning that favor-union is support does not escape mutual dependence.
mv-k04-v491.sanskrit_cite:
yad anugrahayogo 'sya sa evāśraya ity ayam /
nyāyo 'nyonyasamālambī cakrakaṃ nātivartate // [AgMsv_1.492]

mv-k04-v492.plain_english: The touch said to be air-nature is distinguished while air's swift unobstructed state remains established.
mv-k04-v492.sanskrit_cite:
vāyuprakṛti yac coktaṃ sparśanaṃ tad vivicyate /
vāyor vegavatī tāvad aniruddhā sthitiḥ sthitā // [AgMsv_1.493]

mv-k04-v493.plain_english: If touch is not wall in the body-place, what order follows, while the eye is fiery light extended into external range?
mv-k04-v493.sanskrit_cite:
dehadeśe tataḥ sparśaḥ na kuḍya iti kaḥ kramaḥ /
cakṣuś ca taijasaṃ tejaḥ prasṛtaṃ bāhyagocare // [AgMsv_1.494]

mv-k04-v494.plain_english: This examines how objects, predominantly form, are known, and how invisible light could be driven by mind.
mv-k04-v494.sanskrit_cite:
arthān rūpapradhānāṃś ca vettīty etan nirūpyate /
adṛśyaṃ yadi tat tejaḥ preryate manasā katham // [AgMsv_1.495]

mv-k04-v495.plain_english: Driving never occurs without knowledge, and visual greatness is never known merely by sense.
mv-k04-v495.sanskrit_cite:
preraṇaṃ na hy avijñānaṃ kadācid upapadyate /
indriyeṇa na ca jñātaṃ kadācic cākṣuṣaṃ mahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.496]

mv-k04-v496.plain_english: Mind is not independent in what is sense-known, and undriven mind would see everywhere in every way always.
mv-k04-v496.sanskrit_cite:
na cāpīndriyavijñāte svatantraṃ bhavatāṃ manaḥ /
apreritaṃ ca tat paśyet sarvataḥ sarvathā sadā // [AgMsv_1.497]

mv-k04-v497.plain_english: Inconsistency would arise in activity or cessation, and the orb-arrangement is questioned if that greatness holds.
mv-k04-v497.sanskrit_cite:
āsamañjasyam eva syāt pravṛttau vā nivartane /
kiṃ ca golakasaṃsthānaṃ tāvac ca yadi tan mahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.498]

mv-k04-v498.plain_english: Grasping would be only of that gone-indeed, not from elsewhere anywhere; yet the opposite holds even in a closed orb.
mv-k04-v498.sanskrit_cite:
tāvatas tadgatasyaiva grahaḥ syān nānyataḥ kvacit /
tathaitad viparītaṃ tu golake 'pi nimīlite // [AgMsv_1.499]

mv-k04-v499.plain_english: When opened, grasping would occur everywhere in the object, and when the eye is opened with ray-circle extended.
mv-k04-v499.sanskrit_cite:
unmīlite vā sarvatra vastuni grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
unmīlite cakṣuṣi ca prasṛte raśmimaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.500]

mv-k04-v500.plain_english: There is no cloth-like covering in eye-closing, so closed-eyed object-sight would not occur.
mv-k04-v500.sanskrit_cite:
tasyāsti na paṭasyeva saṃvṛtir netramīlane /
tato nimīlitākṣasya vastudṛṣṭir na kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.501]

mv-k04-v501.plain_english: In dense sunlight there is bright light appearance for one with closed eyes and pressed eye-pair.
mv-k04-v501.sanskrit_cite:
ghane cātapamadhye 'sti vinimīlitacakṣuṣaḥ /
citratejovabhānaṃ tatpīḍitākṣayugasya ca // [AgMsv_1.502]

mv-k04-v502.plain_english: How would yogins' point-sight in darkness be, when even with opened eye there is no object-grasping anywhere?
mv-k04-v502.sanskrit_cite:
yogināṃ bindudṛg dhvānte kathaṃ tad vā bhaviṣyati /
bhaved unmīlite 'py akṣṇi na vastugrahaṇaṃ kvacit // [AgMsv_1.503]

mv-k04-v503.plain_english: By mind-seat union, atom-exceeding appearance and lamp-dependence of that too may be refuted.
mv-k04-v503.sanskrit_cite:
manodhiṣṭhānayogena paramāṇvadhikaprathā /
dīpāpekṣā ca yāmuṣya sāpi kiṃ na vibādhyate // [AgMsv_1.504]

mv-k04-v504.plain_english: Lamp-light helps mind, self, eye, and objects, but not individually; mind-fluctuation impression would be by that if.
mv-k04-v504.sanskrit_cite:
dīpaprakāśaḥ svāntātmanetrārtheṣūpakārakaḥ /
na pratyekaṃ manovṛtteḥ saṃskāras tena ced bhavet // [AgMsv_1.505]

mv-k04-v505.plain_english: When a lamp is imagined at night, form-grasping would occur; self-impression would be due to its all-pervadingness.
mv-k04-v505.sanskrit_cite:
dīpe saṃkalpyamane syād rātrau rūpaparigrahaḥ /
ātmanaḥ saṃskriyā cet syāt tasya sarvagatatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.506]

mv-k04-v506.plain_english: Form-awareness would always be; conjunction is impression, so for the formless eternal what other impression is called?
mv-k04-v506.sanskrit_cite:
sarvadā rūpasaṃvit syāt saṃyogaḥ saṃskriyā yataḥ /
amūrtasypi nityasya ko 'nyaḥ saṃskāra ucyate // [AgMsv_1.507]

mv-k04-v507.plain_english: If eye-help, then form in light-middle would never shine in a flame situated in the eye-place.
mv-k04-v507.sanskrit_cite:
netropakāraś cet tarhi netradeśasthite 'rciṣi /
tejomadhyagataṃ rūpaṃ na bhāseta kadācana // [AgMsv_1.508]

mv-k04-v508.plain_english: If the eye's rays reach the object, why should knowledge not arise in the self's own place?
mv-k04-v508.sanskrit_cite:
nanu tad vedyadeśe 'sau nāyanaḥ kiraṇavrajaḥ /
hanta tatraiva vijñānam ātmadeśe na kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_1.509]

mv-k04-v509.plain_english: Since the self is omnipresent and the instrument is there itself, talk of the body as support of enjoyment is vain.
mv-k04-v509.sanskrit_cite:
tatraivātmā vibhutvena tatraiva karaṇaṃ yataḥ /
tasmād bhogāśrayo deho jīvann iti vṛthoktayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.510]

mv-k04-v510.plain_english: Once the going of eye-rays is settled, clear perception begins from one's own hand along an uncovered forest path.
mv-k04-v510.sanskrit_cite:
nāyanānāṃ mayūkhānāṃ gantṛtve 'vasite sati /
anāvṛte 'raṇyamārge svahastāt prabhṛti sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.511]

mv-k04-v511.plain_english: How can perception of sun and moon arise, even if swift, when the stated difference concerns going far and near?
mv-k04-v511.sanskrit_cite:
arkacandrādisaṃdṛṣṭiḥ kathaṃ nāmopajāyatām /
śīghratve 'pi yataḥ proktabhedo dūrāvidūragaḥ // [AgMsv_1.512]

mv-k04-v512.plain_english: How can mind arise when lamp and eye illumination cover it; pure being would remain in that state.
mv-k04-v512.sanskrit_cite:
dīpanetrāvabhāsābhyāṃ channe tasmin kathaṃ matiḥ /
śuddha eva bhaved bhāve tābhyāṃ vyāmalatājuṣi // [AgMsv_1.513]

mv-k04-v513.plain_english: Blindness and its treatment are not a fault of fit support; if tongue is water-self, that water flows from the middle.
mv-k04-v513.sanskrit_cite:
andhatvaṃ tac cikitsā ca na yuktāśrayadūṣaṇā /
rasanā ca jalātmā cet taj jalaṃ srutimadyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.514]

mv-k04-v514.plain_english: Then how is its stability possible, and what various taste manifestation occurs, if one-taste union conflicts with not-one-taste station?
mv-k04-v514.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ sthairyaṃ kathaṃ tasya kā ca nānārasaprathā /
tasyaikarasatāyoge tasyā naikarasasthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.515]

mv-k04-v515.plain_english: One-taste cognition would not arise; when bile abounds, tongue function is bitter, and sweetness is not known as possible.
mv-k04-v515.sanskrit_cite:
na syād ekarasajñaptir yathā pittabhare sati /
tiktā rasanavṛttir no mādhuryaṃ viditaṃ kṣamā // [AgMsv_1.516]

mv-k04-v516.plain_english: Bitterness is bile-gone, not tongue-gone; then bile-hidden and tongue-path-goers are equal.
mv-k04-v516.sanskrit_cite:
nanu pittagataṃ taiktyaṃ na tv evaṃ rasanāgatam /
tarhi pittagūḍau tulyaṃ rasanāpathagāminau // [AgMsv_1.517]

mv-k04-v517.plain_english: Thus cognition would be simultaneous toward bitter and sweet; if tongue is tasteless, whence does it manifest taste?
mv-k04-v517.sanskrit_cite:
iti syād yugapaj jñaptis tiktamādhuryagocarā /
nīrasā rasanā cet sā rasābhivyañjikā kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.518]

mv-k04-v518.plain_english: If from nature, what is this water-ness grasp? Nose is earthly, so why is its hardness not seen?
mv-k04-v518.sanskrit_cite:
svabhāvād iti ced asyāḥ ko 'yam āmbhasatāgrahaḥ /
ghrāṇaṃ ca pārthivaṃ tasya kāṭhinyaṃ kiṃ na dṛśyate // [AgMsv_1.519]

mv-k04-v519.plain_english: If smell is quality-excessive, why does smell not shine? There is no valid cognition there in that way.
mv-k04-v519.sanskrit_cite:
nanu gandhaguṇodreki kiṃ sa gandho na bhāsate /
nāsti tatrendriyavyaktagandhavattve tathā pramā // [AgMsv_1.520]

mv-k04-v520.plain_english: Mind is smell-less and non-earth-self, yet smell-grasping-capable; such inference is not possible for you.
mv-k04-v520.sanskrit_cite:
nirgandham apṛthivyātmā mano gandhagrahakṣamam /
asty eva bhavatāṃ tena nānumā tādṛśā kṣamā // [AgMsv_1.521]

mv-k04-v521.plain_english: Therefore an elemental sense-aggregate does not fit; but in egoity there is pervasion and non-distinctness.
mv-k04-v521.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād indriyasaṃghāto bhautiko nopapadyate /
āhaṃkārikatāyāṃ tu vyāptṛtvam avibhinnatā // [AgMsv_1.522]

mv-k04-v522.plain_english: Body-support contradicts instrumentality and non-stability; speech and the five action-senses should be distinguished.
mv-k04-v522.sanskrit_cite:
dehāśrayavirodhaś ca karaṇatvena cāsthitiḥ /
vāgādi yac ca karmākṣapañcakaṃ tad vivicyatām // [AgMsv_1.523]

mv-k04-v523.plain_english: From navel to head, wind-strike-born; what distinction is speech-self? Such is said here.
mv-k04-v523.sanskrit_cite:
ānābher mūrdhaparyantaṃ yaḥ samīrābhighātajaḥ /
viśeṣaḥ ko 'pi vāgātmā sa tādṛg iha kathyate // [AgMsv_1.524]

mv-k04-v524.plain_english: Its work would be sound; who is the doer here, let be examined. The self has no doership, even in that state, due to omnipresence.
mv-k04-v524.sanskrit_cite:
tasya kāryaṃ bhavec chabdaḥ kartā ko 'tra vicāryatām /
ātmano naiva kartṛtvaṃ tathātve 'pi vibhutvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.525]

mv-k04-v525.plain_english: When I utter sound, why are you not speaker? Even in prakṛti this fault remains: doership is devoid of doership.
mv-k04-v525.sanskrit_cite:
mayā proccārite śabde tvaṃ vaktā kiṃ na jāyase /
prakṛtāv api doṣo 'yaṃ kartryāṃ kartṛtvavarjitā // [AgMsv_1.526]

mv-k04-v526.plain_english: There is no fixed state of the instrument when the vocal organ is the same — so how does the indistinct-and-distinct state arise in sounds?
mv-k04-v526.sanskrit_cite:
karaṇasya sthitir nāsti tulye vāgindriye sati /
kathaṃ cāsphuṭasuspaṣṭabhāvaḥ śabdeṣu jāyate // [AgMsv_1.527]

mv-k04-v527.plain_english: And how, in whispering, muttering, recollection and the like, is there sound-bound difference? If from effort — yet if effort too is an origination, whence then?
mv-k04-v527.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ copāṃśusaṃjalpasmṛtyādau śabdagā bhidā /
prayatnāc cet prayatno 'pi yady utpattis tataḥ katham // [AgMsv_1.528]

mv-k04-v528.plain_english: For a further distinction arises, not born of another quality, by which — through slack and intense effort — it is met.
mv-k04-v528.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣo jāyate hy anyo na hy anyaguṇasaṃbhavaḥ /
prayatnamāndyāmāndyābhyāṃ yena pratividhīyate // [AgMsv_1.529]

mv-k04-v529.plain_english: And the hand-organ gives nothing — whence then grasping by mouth and the rest? And what would be called grasping, if acceptance is what is meant?
mv-k04-v529.sanskrit_cite:
pāṇīndriyaṃ cādadānaṃ mukhādyair grahaṇaṃ kutaḥ /
grahaṇaṃ ca kim ucyeta svīkāro yadi saṃmataḥ // [AgMsv_1.530]

mv-k04-v530.plain_english: Acceptance, it is said, is the making-ones-own of what is not ones own; and if the word 'own' expresses the self — with the self as the root...
mv-k04-v530.sanskrit_cite:
asvasya svasya karaṇaṃ svīkāra iti bhaṇyate /
svaśabdaś cātmavācī cet tatrātmā prakṛtir yadi // [AgMsv_1.531]

mv-k04-v531.plain_english: Therefore nothing is non-radical, they say — so how indeed is there non-ownness? Then ego too would be the self — yet pot-making is not egoic.
mv-k04-v531.sanskrit_cite:
tan nāsty aprākṛtaṃ kiṃcid ity asvatatvaṃ kathaṃ kila /
ahaṅkāro 'py athātmā syān nāhaṃkārī kṛtir ghaṭe // [AgMsv_1.532]

mv-k04-v532.plain_english: Mine — this is faulted by that very fault; for all that is related to ego is indeed its own.
mv-k04-v532.sanskrit_cite:
ātmīyo 'yam anenaitad dūṣaṇenaiva dūṣitam /
ahaṃkārasya saṃbandhi sarvam eva hi tat svakam // [AgMsv_1.533]

mv-k04-v533.plain_english: For the pervading self there is nothing own or not-own; and likewise for the foot-organ too this same stride of argument holds.
mv-k04-v533.sanskrit_cite:
ātmano vyāpakasyāsti na svaṃ nāsvaṃ ca kiṃcana /
evaṃ pādendriyasyāpi samo 'yaṃ yuktivikramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.534]

mv-k04-v534.plain_english: And what is called going, by reaching from place to place — that is of abandoning-nature, established precisely by the absence of acceptance.
mv-k04-v534.sanskrit_cite:
deśād deśāntaraprāptyā gamanaṃ ca yad ucyate /
tattyāgarūpaṃ svīkārābhāvenaiva prasiddhyati // [AgMsv_1.535]

mv-k04-v535.plain_english: And this acceptance stands refuted — yet whatever share of acceptance there is in going, for that the hand-organ is the fit instrument, not the foot-named.
mv-k04-v535.sanskrit_cite:
svīkāro dūṣitaś caiṣa svīkārāṃśo 'pi yo gatau /
tasya pāṇīndriyaṃ yuktaṃ karaṇaṃ nāṅghrināmakam // [AgMsv_1.536]

mv-k04-v536.plain_english: For the common task of the senses thus arises in their tasks; therefore indeed, by the knowers of the great Nyaya, in the final view.
mv-k04-v536.sanskrit_cite:
indriyāṇāṃ hi sāṃkāryam evaṃ kāryeṣu jāyate /
ata eva mahānyāyavedibhiś carame naye // [AgMsv_1.537]

mv-k04-v537.plain_english: Proclaimed for the denial of going is the great pomp of true statements: the gone is not gone-to for now, the not-gone indeed is not gone-to.
mv-k04-v537.sanskrit_cite:
prokto gatiniṣedhāya bhūyān sadvākyaḍambaraḥ /
gataṃ na gamyate tāvad agataṃ naiva gamyate // [AgMsv_1.538]

mv-k04-v538.plain_english: Nothing free from gone-and-not-gone exists and the like, in one own view; and the anus-organ is not a mere hole — from the course of the belly-wind.
mv-k04-v538.sanskrit_cite:
gatāgatavinirmuktaṃ nāstītyādi svake naye /
pāyvindriyaṃ ca na cchidramātraṃ koṣṭhyamarutkramāt // [AgMsv_1.539]

mv-k04-v539.plain_english: Excretion, they say, is the common task — thereby stands just this position; and the sex-organ, whose task is declared...
mv-k04-v539.sanskrit_cite:
utsargaḥ kila sāṃkāryaṃ tena syād iyatī sthitiḥ /
upastham indriyaṃ yac ca tasya kāryaṃ nigadyate // [AgMsv_1.540]

mv-k04-v540.plain_english: It ceases is thus improper — inferential authoritativeness; for the difference-theorists, however, the two measures are simply incompatible.
mv-k04-v540.sanskrit_cite:
............................. /

śāmyatīti na yuktettham anumānapramāṇatā /
tadbhedavādināṃ tāvad dve māne naiva saṃgate // [AgMsv_1.604]

mv-k04-v541.plain_english: But this, from sound, is ascertained by the wise through inference; therefore this self-consciousness abides in self-luminosity.
mv-k04-v541.sanskrit_cite:
śabdādes tv anumānena sudhībhiḥ pariniścitam /
tasmāt svasaṃvid evaiṣā svaprakāśatayā sthitā // [AgMsv_1.605]

mv-k04-v542.plain_english: She shines forth with the expanses beginning with knower, measure, and object — the oceans upsurge of dense-wave play is moonlight, soft on unpierced lily-petals; the opening of supreme consciousness through the mixture of measure, object, and knower — that is, in the world, the manifold art of imagining.
mv-k04-v542.sanskrit_cite:
mātṛmānaprameyādiprapañcaiḥ sāvabhāsate /

samullāsaḥ sindhor bahalalaharīvibhramamayaḥ prakāśaḥ śāśāṅkaḥ kumudadalanirbhedasacivaḥ /
parasyāḥ saṃvitter mitiviṣayamātṛvyatikarair vikāso yaḥ seyaṃ jagati vividhā kalpanakalā // [AgMsv_1.606]

mv-k04-v543.plain_english: Therefore this very light, full of manifold power, itself shines in manifold form — everywhere, from every side.
mv-k04-v543.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt prakāśa evāyaṃ citraśaktisunirbharaḥ /
svayaṃ vicitrarūpeṇa bhāti viśvatra viśvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.607]

mv-k04-v544.plain_english: Then this clear shining, by way of world-form and the like, from own-power portion called imagining, shares the title perception.
mv-k04-v544.sanskrit_cite:
tad ayaṃ prasphuṭābhāso lokarūpādivartmanā /
svaśaktyaṃśād vikalpākhyāt pratyakṣavyapadeśabhāk // [AgMsv_1.608]

mv-k04-v545.plain_english: For thus: the god-of-gods portion is the opening of vision; breath throb is one-pointedness on that; being is the collection of its properties.
mv-k04-v545.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi devadevāṃśas tat samunmīlanaṃ dṛśaḥ /
prāṇaspandas tadaikāgryaṃ bhāvas taddharmasaṃcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.609]

mv-k04-v546.plain_english: All that shines, beginning with thus — that is clearly perception; but here there is no recourse through agent-act-part-instrumentality and the like.
mv-k04-v546.sanskrit_cite:
ityādi sarvaṃ yad bhāti tat pratyakṣam iti sphuṭam /
na tv atra kartṛkarmāṃśakaraṇatvādinā gatiḥ // [AgMsv_1.610]

mv-k04-v547.plain_english: But surely it exists in the later conceptual path — since the body-pot shining is clear, but afterwards it is unclear.
mv-k04-v547.sanskrit_cite:
nanv asāv asti pāścātye vaikalpikapathe tataḥ /
yato dehaghaṭābhāso sphuṭaḥ paścāt tu so 'sphuṭaḥ // [AgMsv_1.611]

mv-k04-v548.plain_english: But that very one of hidden form — toward pure-part self-consciousness; thence the body-pot shining; therein too this very procedure.
mv-k04-v548.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva cchannarūpas tu śuddhāṃśasvātmasaṃvidam /
tato dehaghaṭābhāsas tatrāpy eṣaiva vartanī // [AgMsv_1.612]

mv-k04-v549.plain_english: Even the shining of crores of beings in thousand-fold floods of bodies — yet therein too, before and after, if there is no such-like forth-arising...
mv-k04-v549.sanskrit_cite:
yāvatsahasradehaughabhāvakoṭyavabhāsanam /
tatrāpi ca purā paścān na tu tādṛkprathā yadi // [AgMsv_1.613]

mv-k04-v550.plain_english: It reaches the path of relishing — variegated clear-and-unclear; so much is this one alone, of manifest own-nature.
mv-k04-v550.sanskrit_cite:
āmarśapadavīṃ yāti tat spuṭāsphuṭacitritaḥ /
tāvān asāv eka eva svarūpaprasphuṭātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.614]

mv-k04-v551.plain_english: Śivas light comes. Variegated is this, not in reality — therein, from entry into the not-that-form, variety is considered.
mv-k04-v551.sanskrit_cite:
śivaprakāśa āyāti. /

\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ vicitro 'yaṃ na vastutaḥ /
tatrātadrūpasaṃveśād vaicityraṃ paricarcyate // [AgMsv_1.615]

mv-k04-v552.plain_english: But entry into the not-that-form in Śivas light is incoherent — or else, by force of the stated reasoning, nowhere is there variety.
mv-k04-v552.sanskrit_cite:
śivaprakāśe 'tadrūpapraveśas tu na saṃgataḥ /
yadi vā kathitanyāyabalāt kvāpi na citratā // [AgMsv_1.616]

mv-k04-v553.plain_english: But shining-as-variety gives birth to the variegated state; thus this Caitra of ours, being as it were variegated, is such.
mv-k04-v553.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃtu citratayābhāsaś citrabhāvaṃ prasūyate /
evaṃ caitro 'yam asmākaṃ citravadbhavann īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.617]

mv-k04-v554.plain_english: Enough of Mitra view of that! Seen — me, the seer of beings — seeing, he sees; who, this very one, is established in samadhi.
mv-k04-v554.sanskrit_cite:
maitreṇa tanmatenālaṃ dṛṣṭo māṃ bhāvadarśinam /
paśyan paśyati yaḥ so 'yaṃ samādhau pariniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.618]

mv-k04-v555.plain_english: But formerly this one enjoyed, bringing about this and that, through crores of births indeed; he will be freed by meditation-practice and the like — whoever has come by this path.
mv-k04-v555.sanskrit_cite:
prāk tv eṣa janmakoṭīṣu tattattāpādy abhuṅkta vai /
mokṣyate dhyānacaryādyair yo 'py etena pathāgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.619]

mv-k04-v556.plain_english: This one too — another — is a freedom-sharer, thus of unended rise: the light, one alone, which has long been undivided.
mv-k04-v556.sanskrit_cite:
so 'py anyo mokṣabhāg īttham aparyavasitodayaḥ /
prakāśa eka evāyaṃ yaś cirān na vibhidyate // [AgMsv_1.620]

mv-k04-v557.plain_english: Therefore indeed there is no difference which could split the nondual Great Lord, beautiful with the bliss of light.
mv-k04-v557.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva hi bhedo 'sti na kaścid yo maheśvaram /
advayaṃ saṃprabindhīta prakāśānandasundaram // [AgMsv_1.621]

mv-k04-v558.plain_english: Beginning with place, time, form, knowledge, property, and other adjuncts — agreed; if they shine as difference-makers, that shining is just so.
mv-k04-v558.sanskrit_cite:
deśakālākṛtijñānadharmopādhyantarādayaḥ /
saṃmatā bhedakatvena bhānti cet sā vibhā tathā // [AgMsv_1.622]

mv-k04-v559.plain_english: But if that shining is just such, then this nondualism is clear — while the mere word difference is devoid of shine.
mv-k04-v559.sanskrit_cite:
na ced vibhaiva sā tādṛk tad advaitam idaṃ sphuṭam /
bheda ity eṣa śabdas tu kevalaṃ pratibhojjhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.623]

mv-k04-v560.plain_english: Let there be difference-reckoning growing in shining — but by the stated reasoning it will be well-established right there.
mv-k04-v560.sanskrit_cite:
astu vā bhedakalanā pratibhāsaṃprarohiṇī /
uktanītyā tu tatraiva sapratiṣṭhā bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.624]

mv-k04-v561.plain_english: This pot and this cloth — the two differ mutually, differ from another knower too, and those two differ even from me.
mv-k04-v561.sanskrit_cite:
ayaṃ ghaṭaḥ paṭaś cāyaṃ tāv anyonyavibhedinau /
pramātrantarabhinnau ca tau matto 'pi vibhedinau // [AgMsv_1.625]

mv-k04-v562.plain_english: Thus this one light, of the nature of such relishing — but surely on this view this is partiality: how is nondualism yours?
mv-k04-v562.sanskrit_cite:
iti prakāśa eko 'yaṃ tathāmarśasvarūpakaḥ /
nanv evaṃ pakṣapāto 'yam advaitaṃ bhavatāṃ katham // [AgMsv_1.626]

mv-k04-v563.plain_english: Let difference be — having struck, what indeed is not endured? This is delighting deaf assemblies with song and music.
mv-k04-v563.sanskrit_cite:
bhedo 'py astu sa āhatya kiṃ nāma na viṣahyate /
seyaṃ badhiragoṣṭhīṣu gītavādyaprarocanā // [AgMsv_1.627]

mv-k04-v564.plain_english: For nondualism is not stated by us through exclusion of dualism entry — that would be reaching your side, for that dualism is blatant.
mv-k04-v564.sanskrit_cite:
na hy advayaṃ dvayāveśabādhenāsmābhir ucyate /
tvatpakṣopagamo hy eṣa syād dvayaṃ taddhi susphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.628]

mv-k04-v565.plain_english: This is dual, this is not, and this is dual-and-nondual — where all shines the same, that is called nondual.
mv-k04-v565.sanskrit_cite:
idaṃ dvaitam idaṃ neti tad idaṃ ca dvayādvayam /
iti yatra samaṃ bhāti tad advayam udāhṛtam // [AgMsv_1.629]

mv-k04-v566.plain_english: Well then, so be it — even difference; we are no lovers of mere words. Let it be — for us there is nothing to reject or accept, as with you here.
mv-k04-v566.sanskrit_cite:
nanv ittham astu bhedo 'pi na vayaṃ śabdakāmukāḥ /
astv asau na hi no heyam ādeyaṃ vā yathātra vaḥ // [AgMsv_1.630]

mv-k04-v567.plain_english: If you would cling to the all-favoring position, then resort to the supreme-nondual view — the great refuge.
mv-k04-v567.sanskrit_cite:
sarvānugrāhakaṃ pakṣam ālilambiṣase yadi /
paramādvayadṛṣṭiṃ tat saṃśrayeḥ śaraṇaṃ mahat // [AgMsv_1.631]

mv-k04-v568.plain_english: This principle will be in the eighteenth chapter — which is finally to be reached as supreme; let that ultimately be.
mv-k04-v568.sanskrit_cite:
etad aṣṭādaśe tattvam adhikāre bhaviṣyati /
yat tad ante paraprāpyaṃ tad astu paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.632]

mv-k04-v569.plain_english: But those who here have not come to rest resort to measured consciousness; they are in every way refuted by birth-death-born delusions.
mv-k04-v569.sanskrit_cite:
atra ye na hi viśrāntās te mitāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritāḥ /
sarvathaivāpabādhyante janmamṛtyūtthavibhramaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.633]

mv-k04-v570.plain_english: Therefore this one light alone is the Lord; directly — thus by that very light it shines.
mv-k04-v570.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt sa eka evāsau prakāśaḥ parameśvaraḥ /
pratyakṣam iti tenaiva prakāśenaiva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.634]

mv-k04-v571.plain_english: Therein all those views, like great rivers in the ocean, necessarily enter; unentered, they do not reach fulfillment.
mv-k04-v571.sanskrit_cite:
tatra tā dṛṣṭayaḥ sarvā mahānadya ivārṇave /
viśanty avaśyaṃ nāviṣṭāḥ prayānti kṛtakṛtyatām // [AgMsv_1.635]

mv-k04-v572.plain_english: For thus the mental apparatus, born of form, light, mind, and eye — together with knower and object, or excluding that, manifoldly.
mv-k04-v572.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi mānasāmagrī rūpālokamanokṣajā /
sākaṃ mātṛprameyābhyāṃ tadvarjaṃ vāpy anekaśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.636]

mv-k04-v573.plain_english: And let it make the measure known — nor does it abandon measureness; this perception-grounded supposition holds good now.
mv-k04-v573.sanskrit_cite:
jñātaṃ ca gamayen mānaṃ na cāpi ujjhati mānatām /
pratyakṣapādotprekṣeyam idānīm upapadyate // [AgMsv_1.637]

mv-k04-v574.plain_english: And since the measure grasping the ungrasped is ever fresh — by Bhairavas will this universe shines just so.
mv-k04-v574.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cānadhigatagrāhi mānaṃ navanavaṃ yataḥ /
bhairavecchāvaśād etad viśvaṃ bhāti tathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.638]

mv-k04-v575.plain_english: Displaying the thing, the measure clearly effects activity; it brings about just that thing through fitness for such shining.
mv-k04-v575.sanskrit_cite:
vastu pradarśayan mānaṃ pravṛttiṃ vidadhat sphuṭam /
prāpayaty eva tad vastu tathābhāsanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.639]

mv-k04-v576.plain_english: Even the true absolute is not simply this or nonexistence; consciousness shines ultimately through a clear non-one-sided view.
mv-k04-v576.sanskrit_cite:
sad apy ekāntato nedaṃ nāsac cetyādisaṃvidaḥ /
bhānty eva paramārthena tad anekāntadṛk sphuṭā // [AgMsv_1.640]

mv-k04-v577.plain_english: One being is the nature of all beings and all beings are the nature of one; this jain doctrine is fitting in our good view and is also stated in the Sri Sara scripture.
mv-k04-v577.sanskrit_cite:
eko bhāvaḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvaḥ sarve bhāvā ekabhāvasvabhāvāḥ /
arhadvādaḥ so 'yam asmadsudṛṣṭau yuktaś ca śrīsāraśāstre 'pi coktaḥ // [AgMsv_1.641]

mv-k04-v578.plain_english: Who is able to count measure and measured, this and that, in the world? This true opinion belongs to the blessed lord of speech, blissful consciousness; since he is silent, what else can anyone do here?
mv-k04-v578.sanskrit_cite:
idaṃ mānaṃ meyaṃ tad idam iti saṃkhyāṃ kalayituṃ svarūpaṃ vā śaktaḥ ka iva jagatīty etad api sat /
mataṃ vācāṃ patyur bhagavati cidānandasubhage yatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvād apara iha kaḥ kiṃ prakurutām // [AgMsv_1.642]

mv-k04-v579.plain_english: If appearance were without cause, there would be no space-time restriction; then whose greatness is such restriction of cause? This own nature of cause, how does it not restrain being itself in the supreme, by whom indeed is the supreme?
mv-k04-v579.sanskrit_cite:
ahetor bhāne syād yadi na tanudikkālaniyamas tato hetor īdṛṅ niyama iti kasyaiṣa mahimā /
svabhāvo 'yaṃ hetor atha vivṛtakaṇṭhaṃ katham asau na bhāvasyaivokto yamayati pare kena hi paraḥ // [AgMsv_1.643]

mv-k04-v580.plain_english: From own nature the self is supreme Shiva, as scripture says; the world-self expands in the entire world. Let it be not other than earth and so on; this element-consciousness is barren, free from space-time, birth, death, and loss.
mv-k04-v580.sanskrit_cite:
svabhāvāc cātmāsau paramaśiva ity āgamakathā nirukto viśvātmā jagati nikhile jṛmbhata iti /
dharādeś cānanyo bhavatu tad iyaṃ bhūtacititā sa vandhyo dikkālair jananamaraṇāpāyarahitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.644]

mv-k04-v581.plain_english: That is this world, then the other world also is this; why, because of cause, does time-measure not touch him? Therefore autonomy, rising bliss, supreme joy, glory, becoming ash, all impurity and bond-masses, is auspicious.
mv-k04-v581.sanskrit_cite:
tad asyāyaṃ lokas tadanu paraloko 'py ayam it grahaḥ kasmād dhetoḥ spṛśati na hi taṃ kālakalanā /
tataḥ svātantryodyatsukharasaparānandamahimābhavadbhasmībhūtākhilakaluṣapāśaughasubhagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.645]

mv-k04-v582.plain_english: The sankhya view is again discussed here greatly, covering all principles; it is seen from earth upward, enough, and that arises from the subtlest cause.
mv-k04-v582.sanskrit_cite:
sāṃkhyadṛk punar ihaiva bhūyasā carcyate nikhilatattvagocarā /
dṛśyate dharaṇīprabhṛty alaṃ tac ca sūkṣmatamakāraṇotthitam // [AgMsv_1.646]

mv-k04-v583.plain_english: The instrument for grasping that is again external tenfold and internal threefold; the cause of this is a mirror of pleasure, pain, and delusion.
mv-k04-v583.sanskrit_cite:
tadgṛhītikaraṇodyataṃ punar bāhyataḥ karaṇakaṃ daśātmakam /
āntaraṃ trividham asya kāraṇaṃ saukhyaduḥkhaparimohadarpaṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.647]

mv-k04-v584.plain_english: Such a three-guna thing, by inertness and difference, requires a supreme root cause; that is called enjoyable here, and dependence-nature does not mutually approach enjoyership.
mv-k04-v584.sanskrit_cite:
tādṛśaṃ triguṇam eva yad bhavet tat punar jaḍatayātha bhedataḥ / mūlakāraṇam apekṣate paraṃ sā niśeyam iha bhogyam ucyate /
tac ca bhoktṛ paratantratāmayam no parasparam upaiti bhoktṛtām // [AgMsv_1.648]

mv-k04-v585.plain_english: The body of enjoyable and enjoyer is not one, because of opposite qualities; therefore the enjoyer is only consciousness power, and mind is by consciousness nature.
mv-k04-v585.sanskrit_cite:
bhogyabhoktṛvapur ekam eva no jāghaṭīti hi viruddhadharmataḥ /
tena bhoktṛ citiśaktimātrakam tac cidātmamayatāvaśān manaḥ // [AgMsv_1.649]

mv-k04-v586.plain_english: How can the all-pervading pervader, the lord, go to enjoyership joined with difference? Therefore he may resort to a contracted condition made by his own mastery.
mv-k04-v586.sanskrit_cite:
vyāptṛ sarvagatam īśvaraṃ kathaṃ bhoktṛtāṃ vrajatu bhedasaṃgatām /
tena tannijavaśitvanirmitāṃ saṃkucatsthitijuṣaṃ daśāṃ śrayet // [AgMsv_1.650]

mv-k04-v587.plain_english: From absence of other cause and arts, this innate impurity of this is remembered; it appears threefold, and by its power this person is indeed called.
mv-k04-v587.sanskrit_cite:
anyakāraṇakalādyabhāvataḥ so 'yam asya sahajo malaḥ smṛtaḥ /
sa tridhā samavabhāti tadvaśād eṣa eva sa pumān udāhṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.651]

mv-k04-v588.plain_english: By dependence of enjoyership and by non-essentiality of this, the covering shines; not thus, it is named time, knowledge, arts, attachment, restriction.
mv-k04-v588.sanskrit_cite:
bhoktṛbhāvaparatantratāvaśā nāntarīyakatayāsya kañcukam /
bhāti naivam iti kālavitkalārāgasanniyatināmadheyakam // [AgMsv_1.652]

mv-k04-v589.plain_english: If this self again reveals its own form covered by own autonomy, by own strength, pure consciousness birth; agency indeed places all class of actions in own knowledge, seeing, may go to lordship: I, this all, true, exalted.
mv-k04-v589.sanskrit_cite:
yady ātmaiṣa punar nirargalanijasvātantryasaṃchāditaṃ svaṃ rūpaṃ vivṛṇoty alaṃ nijabalāt tacchuddhavitsaṃbhavaḥ /
kartṛtvaṃ kila kāryavargam akhilaṃ bodhe nidhāya svake paśyann īśvaratāṃ vrajed aham idaṃ sarvaṃ sadety uddhuraḥ // [AgMsv_1.653]

mv-k04-v590.plain_english: Having seen knower-ness with the eye throbbing in the hearts interior — in the clearly shining object the concealment of difference in own consciousness — since he fully sees, thereby may the thought of common-substratum-ness, swiftly attaining the unity-and-difference of I and knower, reveal the Sadāśiva-state.
mv-k04-v590.sanskrit_cite:
jñātṛtvaṃ hṛdayāntarasphuritadṛg dṛṣṭvā sphuṭābhāsini jñeye bhedatirodhitāṃ nijacitau yasmāt sa saṃpaśyati /
tenāsyedam ahaṃvidoḥ sarabhasaṃ bhedaikyam ājagmuṣī sāmānādhikaraṇyadhīḥ prakaṭayet sādāśivīṃ saṃsthitim // [AgMsv_1.654]

mv-k04-v591.plain_english: The whole object-effect merged within awakening — insofar as merged, from exuberant activity — in the interval of the flame-mass of awakening, that setting-forth as it were abandons its own form.
mv-k04-v591.sanskrit_cite:
jñeyaṃ kāryaṃ sarvam antar vibodhe yāval līnaṃ tāvad udriktavṛtteḥ /
bodhajvālāsaṃcayasyāntarāle tatprastyānaṃ svaṃ vapuḥ projjhatīva // [AgMsv_1.655]

mv-k04-v592.plain_english: This this-ness of melted mind — may it not melt away for us even in the prior stage; it is of equal lustre. That now: in the excess of the I-share the rule is boundless; in the spread of beings, this śakti — supreme in the self-proved self.
mv-k04-v592.sanskrit_cite:
idaṃbhāvaḥ so 'yaṃ vigalitumanā no vigalito bhavet prākkakṣyāyām api sa samakāntis tad adhunā /
ahaṃbhāgodreke vidhir anavadhir bhāvavisare tad eṣā śāktī bhūriṣir iti svasiddhātmani parā // [AgMsv_1.656]

mv-k04-v593.plain_english: It strives — may it melt from melted thought — from the conjunction of prior-and-later form; all this is called the śākta stage, being anointed with manifold consciousness-heaps.
mv-k04-v593.sanskrit_cite:
īhate galitumanvato galet tatra pūrvapararūpasaṃgateḥ /
śāktabhūmir akhileyam ucyate citracinnicayacarcitā satī // [AgMsv_1.657]

mv-k04-v594.plain_english: In principle after principle, by own will, the god of gods rests upon every stage — of full one-self, of full-consciousness-nature, glorious; in scripture declared Bhairava.
mv-k04-v594.sanskrit_cite:
tattve tattve svecchayā devadevaḥ sarvāṃ sarvāṃ bhūmim ālambamānaḥ /
pūrṇaikātmā pūrṇasaṃvitsvarūpaḥ śrīmāñ śāstre bhairavo niruktaḥ // [AgMsv_1.658]

mv-k04-v595.plain_english: This descent-of-power view is declared according to faint, middling, supreme, and intense distinction — but enough of those mutual divisions, which is the all-round vision of the self nature.
mv-k04-v595.sanskrit_cite:
śaktipātadṛg iyaṃ nirucyate mandamadhyaparatīvrabhedataḥ /
tatparasparabhidābhir apy alaṃ yā svarūpaparidṛṣṭir ātmanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.659]

mv-k04-v596.plain_english: But surely — does this Lord, full consciousness, ever reveal his own form? Or does he ever conceal it? For what indeed would be a causeless rule?
mv-k04-v596.sanskrit_cite:
nanu kiṃ kadācid ayam īśvaro nijarūpaṃ prakāśayati pūrṇacitiḥ /
kiṃ vā kadācid atha saṃvṛṇute nirhetuko hi niyamaḥ kila kaḥ // [AgMsv_1.660]

mv-k04-v597.plain_english: Endlessly declared before, they say: there is no other cause in regularities, even worldly ones — that very Great Lord, whose habit is ever-variegated shining-forth.
mv-k04-v597.sanskrit_cite:
uktam atra kila pūrvam anantaṃ nānyad asti niyameṣu nimittam /
laukikeṣv api sa eva maheśaś citracitraparibhāsanaśīlaḥ // [AgMsv_1.661]

mv-k04-v598.plain_english: From his autonomy — more now, no reply — we babble, mounted on the palace-course of the famed waves of the consciousness-ocean. Peace thereof; thereupon that — this one designated by the name bondage — thereby thus of fully-drunk relish: freedom, of the stated form.
mv-k04-v598.sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryād adhikam adhunā nottaraṃ bambhaṇīmaḥ saṃvitsindhoḥ prathitalaharīharmyadhārādhirūḍhiḥ /
śāntis tasyās tadanu tad ayaṃ bandhanāmnāpadiṣṭas tenaivetthaṃ parigataraso mokṣa ity uktarūpaḥ // [AgMsv_1.662]

mv-k04-v599.plain_english: Always, sometimes, now, beginning with that — of consciousness: the time-sport imaginings shining with his autonomy.
mv-k04-v599.sanskrit_cite:
sadā kadācid adhunā tadetyādi ca saṃvidaḥ /
tatsvātantryāvabhāsīyakālakelivikalpanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.663]

mv-k04-v600.plain_english: And the Lord is not touched by time-divisions — for they have no independent standing without the imagining of that.
mv-k04-v600.sanskrit_cite:
na ca kālakalābhiḥ sa spṛśyate parameśvaraḥ /
na hi tāsāṃ svatantrāsti sthitis tatkalpanāṃ vinā // [AgMsv_1.664]

mv-k05-v601.plain_english: Therefore, even in the self-created portion of being, which is essentially one's own nature, this clear appearance of dependence is manifested by the Lord alone.
mv-k05-v601.sanskrit_cite:
tena svasṛṣṭe bhāvāṃśe svarūpātmany api sphuṭam /
pāratantryāvabhāso 'yaṃ devenaivāvabhāsyate // [AgMsv_1.665]

mv-k05-v602.plain_english: The self-dependent supreme Lord fashions dependence; no other defining mark is stated for autonomy and dependence than this.
mv-k05-v602.sanskrit_cite:
pāratantryaṃ kalayati svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
svātantrye pāratantrye ca nānyal lakṣaṇam ucyate // [AgMsv_1.666]

mv-k05-v603.plain_english: For what has limited light is inert; therefore, if the limiter posited here is itself clearly something to be limited, a problem arises.
mv-k05-v603.sanskrit_cite:
paricchinnaprakāśo hi jaḍas tenātra yaḥ sthitaḥ /
paricchedaka eṣo 'pi paricchedyo yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.667]

mv-k05-v604.plain_english: Then, in grasping its form, light does not shine; for an external portion of being does not shine by itself.
mv-k05-v604.sanskrit_cite:
tad asya rūpagrahaṇe na prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
tathā hi bāhyo bhāvāṃśaḥ svayaṃ naiṣa prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.668]

mv-k05-v605.plain_english: Knowledge is of the nature of illuminating objects, yet if it is unmanifest, even its inherent self does not shine by its own nature.
mv-k05-v605.sanskrit_cite:
jñānam arthaprakāśātma tac cānābhātam eva hi /
tasyāpi samavāyy ātmā naiva bhāti svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_1.669]

mv-k05-v606.plain_english: Its instrument, such as the eye, does not shine by itself; and without consciousness there is no manifestation at all, even with light and other aids.
mv-k05-v606.sanskrit_cite:
tadīyakaraṇaṃ netraprabhṛty api na bhāsate /
ālokādeś ca vijñānād ṛte naivāvābhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.670]

mv-k05-v607.plain_english: But if, when knowledge arises, that luminosity of the object is its own power or property, then omniscience would follow throughout the whole universe.
mv-k05-v607.sanskrit_cite:
nanu jātaṃ yadi jñānam arthasyāsau prakāśatā /
śaktir dharmo yadi prāptaṃ sārvajñyaṃ viśvamaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.671]

mv-k05-v608.plain_english: Or if that so-called luminosity is taken as something else, it does not fit coherently anywhere among the known, the knower, and the means of knowing.
mv-k05-v608.sanskrit_cite:
anyad evātha tat kiṃcit prakāśatvābhiśabditam /
tan meyamātṛmāneṣu naiva kutrāpi saṃgatam // [AgMsv_1.672]

mv-k05-v609.plain_english: Therefore this whole universe would always remain unmanifest; and if an unmanifest being were to become illuminated, another difficulty follows.
mv-k05-v609.sanskrit_cite:
tataś cāprakaṭaṃ viśvaṃ sarvadaiva bhaved idam /
aprakāśasya bhāvasya yadi ca syād prakāśanam // [AgMsv_1.673]

mv-k05-v610.plain_english: By that much its own nature would be lost; and if the arising of knowledge is the manifestation of a being while it remains in its own nature, that must be explained.
mv-k05-v610.sanskrit_cite:
tāvataivāsya hīyeta svarūpaṃ parihānitaḥ /
jñānotpattiś ca bhāvasya svarūpasthasya cet prathā // [AgMsv_1.674]

mv-k05-v611.plain_english: If a being remains undifferentiated in its own nature, why would that manifestation not belong to the whole universe? Therefore the light of the universe rests in the limiter.
mv-k05-v611.sanskrit_cite:
aviśiṣṭe svarūpasthabhāve viśvasya sā na kim /
tasmāt prakāśo viśvasya paricchedakaniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.675]

mv-k05-v612.plain_english: If the limiter, differentiated by varied forms arising from the manifestation of its own freedom, were itself something to be limited, then a consequence follows.
mv-k05-v612.sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryāvabhāsotthacitrākāravibheditaḥ /
paricchedaka itthaṃ cet paricchedyo bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.676]

mv-k05-v613.plain_english: Then this root-destroying infinite regress would occur; therefore that limiter is said to be unlimited.
mv-k05-v613.sanskrit_cite:
mūlakṣatikarī seyam anavasthā patiṣyati /
ataś ca so 'paricchinnaḥ paricchedaka ucyate // [AgMsv_1.677]

mv-k05-v614.plain_english: Therefore it is not constructible and, as the scriptures say, not within the domain of time; for that reason the condition of being a knowable object is explained as belonging to time.
mv-k05-v614.sanskrit_cite:
akālpyas tena śāstreṣu tan na kālasya gocaraḥ /
tenāsya vedyadharmatvaṃ kālasya paribhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.678]

mv-k05-v615.plain_english: If time were to delimit the subject, then the stability of time would certainly depend on the subject and would require the subject's functioning.
mv-k05-v615.sanskrit_cite:
yadi kālaś ca mātāraṃ paricchindyāt tato dhruvam /
mātṛlagnaiva kālasya sthitir nirvāham icchati // [AgMsv_1.679]

mv-k05-v616.plain_english: And no other subject could be posited, because of infinite regress; to remove that regress, this subject must be accepted as free from the divisions of time.
mv-k05-v616.sanskrit_cite:
na ca mātrantaraṃ kiṃcit saṃbhaved anavasthiteḥ /
tāṃ hantuṃ vopagamyo 'sau mātā kālakalojjhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.680]

mv-k05-v617.plain_english: But if the limited subject is indeed dependent on that time, then how, in your view, can one and the same entity be both subject and object?
mv-k05-v617.sanskrit_cite:
ya eva tu paricchedyo mātā tallagna eva cet /
sa kālo mātṛmeyatve tarhy ekasya kathaṃ tava // [AgMsv_1.681]

mv-k05-v618.plain_english: For in the doctrine of difference your view is fixed in that way; but for us, who uphold non-difference, let there be no such refutation at all.
mv-k05-v618.sanskrit_cite:
bhedavāde hi bhavatāṃ niṣṭhitā matir īdṛśī /
abhedavādināṃ nas tu naiva kāpy astu khaṇḍanā // [AgMsv_1.682]

mv-k05-v619.plain_english: For those for whom the universe consists of the subject and the subject likewise consists of the universe, the supreme Lord is not entangled in the mire of the nets of time and limiting factors.
mv-k05-v619.sanskrit_cite:
viśvaṃ mātṛmayaṃ yeṣāṃ mātā viśvamayas tathā /
tan na kālakalājālajambālaiḥ parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.683]

mv-k05-v620.plain_english: For the light of the power of consciousness takes on a kind of tarnish; therefore it appears concealed at that time and later appears in manifest form.
mv-k05-v620.sanskrit_cite:
citiśaktiprakāśo hi mālinyam avalambate /
atas tadā saṃvṛto 'sau paścāt prakaṭarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.684]

mv-k05-v621.plain_english: Thus this unfolding, which designates that condition, belongs to that same reality alone; it is a certain creative construal of its own, whose nature is reflective awareness of its own form.
mv-k05-v621.sanskrit_cite:
iti tasyaiva jṛmbheyaṃ tathātvavyapadeśinī /
kalanaivāsya sā kācit svarūpāmarśanātmikā // [AgMsv_1.685]

mv-k05-v622.plain_english: In that construal the self regards itself as fit for union with Śiva; for through connection with variety it comes to regard itself in that way.
mv-k05-v622.sanskrit_cite:
śivayogārham ātmānaṃ yasyām ātmābhimanyate /
yato vaicitryayogena tathātmānaṃ sa manyate // [AgMsv_1.686]

mv-k05-v623.plain_english: Therefore the descent of power is taught here as ninefold; otherwise the Lord would have attachment or aversion somewhere, which he does not.
mv-k05-v623.sanskrit_cite:
śaktipātasya tenoktā navadhātra vyavasthitiḥ /
anyathā neśvarasyāsti rāgo dveṣo 'tha vā kvacit // [AgMsv_1.687]

mv-k05-v624.plain_english: For if this all-pervading Lord were to send down his own power in a fixed way anywhere, that would imply a motive; thus this descent of power of the great Lord is without external cause.
mv-k05-v624.sanskrit_cite:
yena kvāpy eṣa niyatāṃ svāṃ śaktiṃ pātayed vibhuḥ /
animittas tathā cāyaṃ śaktipāto maheśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.688]

mv-k05-v625.plain_english: By decay of attachment, equality of karma, weight of good deeds, ripening of impurity, union with a friend, devotion, feeling, and practice.
mv-k05-v625.sanskrit_cite:
tena rāgakṣayāt karmasāmyāt sukṛtagauravāt /
malapākāt suhṛdyogād bhakter bhāvāc ca sevanāt // [AgMsv_1.689]

mv-k05-v626.plain_english: From practice, breaking of latencies, ripening of impressions, decay of false knowledge, renunciation of karma, and falling away of desire.
mv-k05-v626.sanskrit_cite:
abhyāsād vāsanodbhedāt saṃskāraparipākataḥ /
mithyajñānakṣayāt karmasaṃnyāsāt kāmyavicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.690]

mv-k05-v627.plain_english: That power descends from equality of mind is said, but that is unreal; even there another cause must be sought.
mv-k05-v627.sanskrit_cite:
sāmyāc cittasya sā śaktiḥ patatīti yad ucyate /
tad asan /
nanu tatrāpi nimittāntaramārgaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.691]

mv-k05-v628.plain_english: From the absence of infinite regress and from avoiding mutual dependence, circularity, and similar faults.

mv-k05-v629.plain_english: In this view, even all doctrines have a fitting standing; in the all-enduring view, nothing is indeed faulted.
mv-k05-v629.sanskrit_cite:
asmiṃs tu pakṣe sarveṣāṃ pravādānām api sthitiḥ /
yuktā sarvaṃsahe pakṣe na kiṃcit kila duṣyati // [AgMsv_1.693]

mv-k05-v630.plain_english: Wise ones can join it themselves there; therefore separate joining is not said here, and this textual expansion is false.
mv-k05-v630.sanskrit_cite:
yuktiḥ sudhībhiḥ svayam eva tatra śakyeta saṃyojayitum tato na /
pṛthaktayā yojanam uktam atra yad granthato vistara eṣa mithyā // [AgMsv_1.694]

mv-k05-v631.plain_english: Therefore they approached independent Shiva-power; without her there is no liberation-state, so liberation-talks in other scriptures are in vain.
mv-k05-v631.sanskrit_cite:
upajagmur ato 'napekṣiṇīṃ śivaśaktiṃ na ca tāṃ vinā bhavet /
apavargapadaṃ yato mudhā paraśāstreṣu vimokṣasaṃkathāḥ // [AgMsv_1.695]

mv-k05-v632.plain_english: At the time of power-descent inquiry is proper, Lord, yet you never do it; the venerable Utpala teacher showed such inquiry there in his own scripture.
mv-k05-v632.sanskrit_cite:
śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit /
śrīmadutpalagurur nyarūpayat tatra tatra nijaśāstra īdṛśam // [AgMsv_1.696]

mv-k05-v633.plain_english: By his grace alone devotion is produced in men, by which they go to supreme perfection with mind gone to his state.
mv-k05-v633.sanskrit_cite:
tasyaiva hi prasādena bhaktir utpādyate nṛṇām /
yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatamānasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.697]

mv-k05-v634.plain_english: Thus in the puranas and scriptures first, that supreme power is declared independent, for in dependence there is lack of lordship.
mv-k05-v634.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ purāṇaśāstrādau śaktiḥ sā pārameśvarī /
nirapekṣaiva kathitā sāpekṣatve hy anīśatā // [AgMsv_1.698]

mv-k05-v635.plain_english: Only by blind views hidden by dualism does difficulty of capacity of this power arise, by rule of its sometimes standing.
mv-k05-v635.sanskrit_cite:
kevalaṃ bhedavādāndhyasthagitālasadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
duḥsamarthatvam etasyā niyamena kvacitsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.699]

mv-k05-v636.plain_english: Constantly considering karma, impurity, equality, and ripening in nets of such causes, the vain self is exhausted.

mv-k05-v637.plain_english: That is not for their benefit, like clinging to grass; therefore he indeed is endowed with such own autonomy.
mv-k05-v637.sanskrit_cite:
tat teṣāṃ nopakārāya kuśakāśāvalambanam /
tasmāt sa eva tādṛkṣasvasvātantryopabṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.701]

mv-k05-v638.plain_english: Then so it appears with such variety; thus all views are right here in the supreme Lord.
mv-k05-v638.sanskrit_cite:
tadā tathā tathetyādivaicitryeṇāvabhāsate /
tad itthaṃ sarvadṛṣṭīṇām atraiva parameśvare // [AgMsv_1.702]

mv-k05-v639.plain_english: Entry thus by others, enough, or with reasoning pomp; that own nature is here declared by the god of gods.
mv-k05-v639.sanskrit_cite:
anupraveśa ity anyair alaṃ vā yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
tad itthaṃ devadevena svasvarūpam ihoditam // [AgMsv_1.703]

mv-k05-v640.plain_english: Direct perception there is its measure, supreme among all measures; some held one such measure thus.
mv-k05-v640.sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣaṃ tatra tanmānaṃ sarvamānadhuroddhuram /
ekam evedṛśaṃ mānam iti kecit prapedire // [AgMsv_1.704]

mv-k05-v641.plain_english: From smoke fire, thus mostly; this is his manifestation, as of a pot fixed by seeing its first part.
mv-k05-v641.sanskrit_cite:
dhūmād agnir iti prāyas tasyaivaitad vijṛṃbhitam /
yathā ghaṭasya pūrvāṃśadṛṣṭaikapariniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.705]

mv-k05-v642.plain_english: Mother, grasping such form, having considered clear mind indeed, direct perception attains.
mv-k05-v642.sanskrit_cite:
mātā sphuṭāsphuṭākāratāvadarthāvalehinīm /
sphuṭām eva matiṃ matvā pratyakṣatvaṃ prapadyate // [AgMsv_1.706]

mv-k05-v643.plain_english: Not and inference in the final part; awareness is one indeed, because fire is known within smoke perception, so.
mv-k05-v643.sanskrit_cite:
na cānumānam antyāṃśe saṃvid ekaiva sā yataḥ /
dhūmādhyakṣapratītyantarniviṣṭāgniprathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.707]

mv-k05-v644.plain_english: One indeed, so far grasping an object part, mind arises; to that extent in part clear form is direct perception, thus let it be said.
mv-k05-v644.sanskrit_cite:
ekaiva tāvad arthāṃśalehinī jāyate matiḥ /
tāvaty āṃśe sphuṭākārā pratyakṣam iti bhāṣyatām // [AgMsv_1.708]

mv-k05-v645.plain_english: As variety of gems, so from establishment of impressions in eye, mind, light, object, etc., in awareness.
mv-k05-v645.sanskrit_cite:
yathā ratnādivaicityraṃ tathā saṃskārasaṃsthiteḥ /
netrātmamānasālokaviṣayādiṣu saṃvidi // [AgMsv_1.709]

mv-k05-v646.plain_english: Direct perception indeed in awareness appears as clear, so from establishment of such pervasion, light, and impression.
mv-k05-v646.sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣam eva saṃvittau sphuṭatvenāvabhāsate /
tathā tathāvidhavyāptidhāmasaṃkārasaṃsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.710]

mv-k05-v647.plain_english: At the end, so indeed that awareness having smoke-fire form, as firm impressions with clear marks immediately oneself.
mv-k05-v647.sanskrit_cite:
ante tathaiva sā vittir dhūmāgnyākārarūpiṇī /
yathā ca dṛḍhasaṃskārāḥ sollekhāḥ sapadi svayam // [AgMsv_1.711]

mv-k05-v648.plain_english: Gem etc. reality they see, obstructed by inner obstacle; so hungry selves quickly, very certain indeed.
mv-k05-v648.sanskrit_cite:
ratnāditattvaṃ paśyanti vighnāntaratirodhitaḥ /
tathā bubhukṣitātmānaḥ śīghram evātiniścitam // [AgMsv_1.712]

mv-k05-v649.plain_english: People take food to eat without any intervening inference of pervasion or the like; therefore what the opponents call mere conceptual construction is already answered and refuted.
mv-k05-v649.sanskrit_cite:
annādi gṛhṇate bhoktuṃ vyāptyādyavyavadhānataḥ /
tena pratyuktam eva syād yad āhuḥ parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.713]

mv-k05-v650.plain_english: In matters that have become well practiced, where awareness of invariable pervasion is already present, what use is there for a cognition pervaded by conceptual construction? We do not accept that.
mv-k05-v650.sanskrit_cite:
abhyasteṣv avinābhāvasvabhāvavyāptisaṃvidaḥ /
kiṃ hi tatkalpanāvyāptivitter iti na manmahe // [AgMsv_1.714]

mv-k05-v651.plain_english: Because this cognition arises very quickly, it is not clearly noticed; so the opponent infers that it must be conceptual construction. That is the move being stated here.
mv-k05-v651.sanskrit_cite:
āśūtpattivaśād asyā na khalv asty upalakṣaṇam /
anumīyata evaṃ sā tad eva parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.715]

mv-k05-v652.plain_english: Alas, these people who fancy themselves logicians, blinded by loyalty to their own side, have begun again and again to forget even what they themselves have accepted.
mv-k05-v652.sanskrit_cite:
aho svapakṣapātāndhāḥ svam apy upagataṃ muhuḥ /
amī vismartum ārabdhās tārkikammanyabuddhayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.716]

mv-k05-v653.plain_english: For in your own view, every cognition lasts only a moment and manifests its object simply by arising.
mv-k05-v653.sanskrit_cite:
kṣaṇāpavargiṇī buddhiḥ sarvaiva hi bhavanmatā /
utpattimātrayogena viṣayasyāvabhāsikā // [AgMsv_1.717]

mv-k05-v654.plain_english: If swift manifestation means nothing more than what happens in a moment, then in truth every cognition would be swiftly manifesting.
mv-k05-v654.sanskrit_cite:
na kṣaṇāc cāparaṃ kiṃcid āśubhāvitvam ucyate /
tat sarvam āśubhāvy eva vijñānam iti tattvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.718]

mv-k05-v655.plain_english: Then non-noticing would occur everywhere among all things; or else, in the case of unbroken seeing, what is known would have to range over a longer time.
mv-k05-v655.sanskrit_cite:
sarvatra bhāvajāteṣu bhaved anupalakṣaṇam /
athāvicchinnadṛṣṭīnāṃ drāghīyaḥkālagocaram // [AgMsv_1.719]

mv-k05-v656.plain_english: Then even on that view the object is manifested by mere arising; and if clarity of the object is also due simply to arising, that same fact must explain everything.
mv-k05-v656.sanskrit_cite:
jñātaṃ tenāpi tarhy artho janmamātreṇa bhāsyate /
yac cotpattivaśād eva viṣayasphuṭatātmakam // [AgMsv_1.720]

mv-k05-v657.plain_english: How can the fact that the experience is quicker make a difference, if that cognition is said to be self-luminous, even while being related to grasping?
mv-k05-v657.sanskrit_cite:
tasya śīghratarasthāsnubhāvo bhedāvahaḥ katham /
yat tat kila grahāpekṣaṃ svaprakāśam athāpi sat // [AgMsv_1.721]

mv-k05-v658.plain_english: If it becomes a means elsewhere, like lightning or a lamp, then the difference between lasting long or briefly may appear right there as a basis for difference.
mv-k05-v658.sanskrit_cite:
anyatropāyatāṃ yāti vidyuddīpādivat tathā /
tatraiva ciraśīghrasthabhāvo bhedāya bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.722]

mv-k05-v659.plain_english: And in inferences the grasping of pervasion and so on does not become clear again and again in such a way that it would be separately noticed.
mv-k05-v659.sanskrit_cite:
na ca kvāpy anumāneṣu vyāptyāder grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
punaḥ punaḥ sphuṭībhāvaṃ yāti yenopalakṣyate // [AgMsv_1.723]

mv-k05-v660.plain_english: Moreover, even if a clear series of successive cognitions of smoke and so on arises, how could that produce the manifestation of a single thing?
mv-k05-v660.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ ca kramikadhūmādijñānamālātmani sphuṭam /
uditāpi kathaṃ kuryād ekabhāvāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.724]

mv-k05-v661.plain_english: If one says the final connecting cognition will do this, that too is distinct and just like the earlier cognitions—so how could it unify them in that way?
mv-k05-v661.sanskrit_cite:
athāntyam anusandhānajñānam evaṃ kariṣyati /
tad api prāksthasaṃvittisamaṃ bhinnaṃ kathaṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.725]

mv-k05-v662.plain_english: If that final cognition is supposed to connect the earlier series of cognitions, but those earlier cognitions no longer exist, then no connection is possible once they have perished.
mv-k05-v662.sanskrit_cite:
tena prāktanavijñānamālāmanvasyate yadi /
tad asan na hi saṃdhānaṃ naṣṭāyām upapadyate // [AgMsv_1.726]

mv-k05-v663.plain_english: If one says that memory itself is the connection between cognitions, how could that memory arise at all in the absence of experience?
mv-k05-v663.sanskrit_cite:
atha smaraṇam eveha saṃdhānaṃ saṃvidāṃ bhavet /
tad apy anubhavābhāve kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.727]

mv-k05-v664.plain_english: And in your view there is no pair of cognitions existing simultaneously; so an experience of cognitions by awareness does not fit anywhere in that system.
mv-k05-v664.sanskrit_cite:
na ca jñāneṣv anubhavo yujyate saṃvidaḥ kvacit /
yugapaj jñānayugalaṃ nāstīti hi bhavanmatam // [AgMsv_1.728]

mv-k05-v665.plain_english: The relation of cognition and its object is observed only where two factors stand together at the same time, not where they arise successively as earlier and later and are therefore opposed.
mv-k05-v665.sanskrit_cite:
jñānajñeyātmatā dṛṣṭā yugapatsthitatājuṣoḥ /
na tu pūrvāparākārasamutpannavirodhinoḥ // [AgMsv_1.729]
