mv-k05-v666.plain_english: Therefore, even the cognition that seems to be preceded by a manifestation following pervasion is, in that very case, a non-sequential knowing of a directly perceptual kind.
mv-k05-v666.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād vyāptyanusārāvabhāsapūrvāpi yā matiḥ /
tatrāpy akramam evedaṃ pratyakṣamānavedanam // [AgMsv_1.730]

mv-k05-v667.plain_english: Just as someone suddenly awakened from deep sleep, with eyes just opening, acts to remove the dimness in the appearance of things, taking them directly...
mv-k05-v667.sanskrit_cite:
yathā jhaṭiti sauṣuptaprabuddhaḥ pronmiṣaddṛṣiḥ /
pratyakṣam iti bhāvāṃśadhyāmalatvanivṛtaye // [AgMsv_1.731]

mv-k05-v668.plain_english: While rubbing the eyes and so on, that person does not think, 'I am inferring these things.' Let the same be understood in this case as well.
mv-k05-v668.sanskrit_cite:
netrasaṃmārjanādīni vidadhannābhimanyate /
bhāvān anuminomīti tathaivātrāpi buddhyatām // [AgMsv_1.732]

mv-k05-v669.plain_english: And just as someone whose vision has just emerged from the delusion of deep sleep may, for that moment, forget himself and the place he is in...
mv-k05-v669.sanskrit_cite:
yathā ca ghanasauṣuptamohāvyutthitadarśanaḥ /
svātmānam atha tatsthānaṃ vismaraty eva tat kṣaṇaṃ // [AgMsv_1.733]

mv-k05-v670.plain_english: Then, when his own clear seeing is awakened through gathered effort, he recognizes, 'I am that one,' and in the ultimate sense this comes from awareness itself.
mv-k05-v670.sanskrit_cite:
atha prayatnasaṃbhāraprabuddhavimalasvadṛk /
so 'ham asmīti manvānaḥ saṃvitteḥ paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.734]

mv-k05-v671.plain_english: In all of this, the Lord Bhairava, whose very nature is consciousness, freely conceals and reveals his own form.
mv-k05-v671.sanskrit_cite:
tatra sarvatra nātho 'yaṃ bhairavaś citsvarūpakaḥ /
svātantryāt svaṃ vapur yāvad gūhate vivṛṇoti ca // [AgMsv_1.735]

mv-k05-v672.plain_english: To that extent ignorance arises, and knowledge arises; and that knowledge, by its clarity, should be understood as directly evident to all.
mv-k05-v672.sanskrit_cite:
tāvad ajñānam etasya vijñānaṃ copajāyate /
tac ca sphuṭatayā sarvapratyakṣam iti manyatām // [AgMsv_1.736]

mv-k05-v673.plain_english: When the word 'pot' is heard, a cognition arises of its broad base, belly, and other features; in that cognition, convention, memory, and similar factors are present in the same way.
mv-k05-v673.sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭaśabde śrute yā ca pṛthubudhnodarādidhīḥ /
tatrāpi khalu samketasmaraṇādi tathāvidham // [AgMsv_1.737]

mv-k05-v674.plain_english: Just as in examining a gem one awakens one's own clear awareness through assemblages of other cognitions, so that awareness stands forth distinctly.
mv-k05-v674.sanskrit_cite:
yathā ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ svāṃ saṃvittiṃ sphuṭātmikām /
samvidantarasaṃghātais tiṣṭhati pratibodhayan // [AgMsv_1.738]

mv-k05-v675.plain_english: Then, through the connection with the final awakened clear awareness, the reality of the gem shines forth; at that point the other cognitions have no further use.
mv-k05-v675.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ prabuddhacaramasphuṭasaṃvittiyogataḥ /
ratnatattvaṃ vibhāty atra nopayoge 'nyasaṃvidām // [AgMsv_1.739]

mv-k05-v676.plain_english: Those other cognitions exercised causality only for awakening that awareness; for in the very connection of its manifestation, they have no usefulness.
mv-k05-v676.sanskrit_cite:
tāḥ paraṃ tatprabodhāya kāraṇatvaṃ vitenire /
tasyaivāvabhāsayoge hi na tāsām upayogitā // [AgMsv_1.740]

mv-k05-v677.plain_english: From such an example as the knowledge of a child and a gem-cutter, in verbal cognition too there is indeed by itself one clear cognition of illumination.
mv-k05-v677.sanskrit_cite:
bālavaikaṭikajñānadṛṣṭāntād īdṛśāt svayam /
śābde 'pi khalu vijñāne sphuṭaivaikā prakāśadhīḥ // [AgMsv_1.741]

mv-k05-v678.plain_english: Therefore, when such a word is heard, whatever cognition arises immediately after in the manifestation of meaning, that cognition is of this extent and of such a character.
mv-k05-v678.sanskrit_cite:
atas tathāvidhe śabde śrute yat samanantaram /
arthāvabhāsane seyam iyatī matir īdṛśī // [AgMsv_1.742]

mv-k05-v679.plain_english: That meaning, of that extent, stands there like the prior and posterior parts of a pot. But surely that pot may be one whole composed of parts?
mv-k05-v679.sanskrit_cite:
arthaḥ sa tāvāṃs tatrāste ghaṭapūrvāparāṃśavat /
nanv asau ghaṭa ekaḥ syād avayavyātmakas tathā // [AgMsv_1.743]

mv-k05-v680.plain_english: But there is no unity of word and meaning, so how could there be such sameness? Alas, one whose eyes are clouded by the darkness of habitual grasping of difference!
mv-k05-v680.sanskrit_cite:
na tu śabdārthayor aikyaṃ tat kathaṃ sāmyam īdṛśam /
aho bhedagrahābhyāsatimirāvilalocanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.744]

mv-k05-v681.plain_english: Even with the application of the collyrium of true reasoning, he has not attained clear vision. This undivided Lord Bhairava assumes within himself the state of both the enjoyed and the enjoyer.
mv-k05-v681.sanskrit_cite:
sadyuktyañjanayoge 'pi na dṛṣṭiṃ vimalāṃ gataḥ /
abhinno bhagavān eṣa bhairavo bhogyabhoktṛtām // [AgMsv_1.745]

mv-k05-v682.plain_english: Having unified everything within himself, always full-bodied — when this has been established previously, what possibility remains for this question?
mv-k05-v682.sanskrit_cite:
ātmany evānusandhāya sarvadā pūrṇavigrahaḥ /
iti prasādhite pūrvaṃ kaḥ praśnasyāsya saṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.746]

mv-k05-v683.plain_english: Therefore, thus, in comparison and in other means of knowing as well, it is clearly the form of awareness-perception alone that appears everywhere.
mv-k05-v683.sanskrit_cite:
tad evam upamānādāv api mānāntare sphuṭam /
saṃvitpratyakṣarūpaiva sarvatra pratibhāsate // [AgMsv_1.747]

mv-k05-v684.plain_english: Even a blind person, perceiving each respective form through touch, sound, and so on, cognizes that clarity of just such a kind.
mv-k05-v684.sanskrit_cite:
andho 'pi sparśaśabdādyais tattadrūpaṃ vilokayan /
sphuṭatām eva tāṃ tāvat saṃvetti sa tathāvidhām // [AgMsv_1.748]

mv-k05-v685.plain_english: Thus those congenitally deaf apprehend an aspect of things clearly through form, touch, and so on; for them cognition is never unknown anywhere.
mv-k05-v685.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ jātijaḍā rūpasparśādyair abhimanvate /
sphuṭam eva hi bhāvāṃśaṃ teṣāṃ nājñātadhīḥ kvacit // [AgMsv_1.749]

mv-k05-v686.plain_english: Saying 'this is a lake of beauty, a shoot in the garden of youth,' a congenitally blind person is pleased from touching her limbs.
mv-k05-v686.sanskrit_cite:
iyaṃ lāvaṇyasarasī tāruṇyodyānakaṇḍalī /
iti tuṣyati jātyandhas tadaṅgaparimarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.750]

mv-k05-v687.plain_english: Saying 'ah, he sings with ornament,' a deaf person, merely by seeing the singer's face, is satisfied by that alone.
mv-k05-v687.sanskrit_cite:
aho nu sadalaṃkāraṃ gāyatīti jaḍo janaḥ /
gātur mukhaṃ vilokyaiva tāvatā parituṣyati // [AgMsv_1.751]

mv-k05-v688.plain_english: Thus perception alone expands without rival; therefore a brief consideration of its fruit and so on is now begun.
mv-k05-v688.sanskrit_cite:
iti pratyakṣam evaikaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate /
tad asya phalacintādi kartuṃ prastūyate manāk // [AgMsv_1.752]

mv-k05-v689.plain_english: That very cognition is surely of the nature of the essence of reflective awareness; therefore talk of difference is not at all well suited with regard to its fruit.
mv-k05-v689.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva khalu vijñānaṃ parimarśarasātmakam /
tasmād bhedakathā naiva phalaṃ prati susaṃgatā // [AgMsv_1.753]

mv-k05-v690.plain_english: Let avoidance and similar cognitions be the fruit; yet even that comes from manifestation. Or else, awareness is self-luminous and ultimate.
mv-k05-v690.sanskrit_cite:
hānādidhīḥ phalaṃ vāstu tasyā apy atha bhāsanāt /
yadi vā svaprakāśaiva saṃvittiḥ pāramārthikī // [AgMsv_1.754]

mv-k05-v691.plain_english: That indeed is the final fruit, well determined everywhere; joy and so on, which is spoken of everywhere here as the primary fruit, is included in it.
mv-k05-v691.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva paryanthaphalaṃ sarvatraiva suniścitam /
hlādādikaṃ phalaṃ mukhyaṃ yat sarvatreha gīyate // [AgMsv_1.755]

mv-k05-v692.plain_english: It comes to rest in that own awareness, in the full self. Therefore, thus, this perception fully expands on all sides.
mv-k05-v692.sanskrit_cite:
tatsvasaṃvidi viśrāntim abhyeti bharitātmani /
tad evam idam adhyakṣaṃ sarvataḥ pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.756]

mv-k05-v693.plain_english: For one devoted to the practice of this, what accomplishment does not arise? Beginning from kala and so on, through an inclination toward hearing what is spoken by Brahma and others...
mv-k05-v693.sanskrit_cite:
etadabhyāsaniṣṭḥasya keva siddhir na jāyate /
brahmādibhāṣitaśrautapraunmukhyena kalādikāt // [AgMsv_1.757]

mv-k05-v694.plain_english: Hearing-cognition from afar quickly arises; even in an aspect of a thing seen by the mind, the arising of clear cognition indeed occurs abundantly.
mv-k05-v694.sanskrit_cite:
dūrāc chravaṇavijñānam acirāt saṃpravartate /
manodṛṣṭe 'pi bhāvāṃśe sphuṭavṛttyudayo hy alam // [AgMsv_1.758]

mv-k05-v695.plain_english: What wonder is it if this arises when overcome by the power of one's own reflective awareness? So it is said in the Spanda scripture, even in an attentive mind.
mv-k05-v695.sanskrit_cite:
svavimarśabalākrānte kiṃ citraṃ yadi jāyate /
spandaśāstre tathā coktaṃ sāvadhāne 'pi cetasi // [AgMsv_1.759]

mv-k05-v696.plain_english: It shines forth ever more clearly — enough of much elaboration. In this way, this entire universe is indeed the perception of the supreme lord.
mv-k05-v696.sanskrit_cite:
bhūyaḥ sphuṭataro bhātīty alaṃ bahulavistaraiḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ viśvaṃ yat parameśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.760]

mv-k05-v697.plain_english: Even though the group of knowing subjects is undivided, there is no confusion of cognitions, because each cognition arises through its own distinct mode of manifestation.
mv-k05-v697.sanskrit_cite:
tat tato 'py avibhinnasya mātṛvargasya tat tathā /
na ca pratītisāṃkāryaṃ tathā bhāsanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.761]

mv-k05-v698.plain_english: Even when perception operates in the same field, the cognition of a pot and of a non-pot are not identical; thus perception itself shines forth unrivaled.
mv-k05-v698.sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣe 'pi same sāmyaṃ no ghaṭāghaṭasamvidoḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.762]

mv-k05-v699.plain_english: For that reason the object is not divided, and such nonduality of perception is recognized by one whose understanding is firmly established in the unifying insight.
mv-k05-v699.sanskrit_cite:
tato na bhidyate cārthaḥ pratyakṣādvaitam īdṛśam /
idaṃ sandhānakalikāpariniṣṭhitabuddhinā // [AgMsv_1.763]

mv-k05-v700.plain_english: Teacher Narasiṃha teaches the nonduality of perception, while some others claim that inference is the valid means of knowing for the entire universe.
mv-k05-v700.sanskrit_cite:
ācāryanarasiṃhena pratyakṣādvaitam ucyate /
anumānapramāṇatvaṃ viśvasmin kaiś cid ucyate // [AgMsv_1.764]

mv-k05-v701.plain_english: The all-knowing Lord, whose nature is nonconceptual and even perceptual, does not enter into ordinary practical usage.
mv-k05-v701.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi devaḥ sarvajño nirvikalpasvabhāvakaḥ /
sa cādhyakṣasvabhāvo 'pi nāyāti vyavahāryatām // [AgMsv_1.765]

mv-k05-v702.plain_english: How could practical activity, which is conceptual by nature, arise in the nonconceptual? In fact, all ordinary practical activity is carried on through conceptualization.
mv-k05-v702.sanskrit_cite:
avikalpe vikalpātmā vyavahāraḥ kathaṃ kila /
vikalpena ca sarvo 'yaṃ vyavahāro 'vatanyate // [AgMsv_1.766]

mv-k05-v703.plain_english: That very process would be inference, consisting of conceptual constructions such as the subject, its property, pervasion, and the apprehension of these, and so on.
mv-k05-v703.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva cānumānaṃ syāt tasyaitāḥ parikalpanāḥ /
pakṣataddharmatadvyāptitatpratītyādayo 'khilāḥ // [AgMsv_1.767]

mv-k05-v704.plain_english: But in reality there is only one ultimate cognition. Yet one may object: how could inference exist in the absence of perception, since it depends on it?
mv-k05-v704.sanskrit_cite:
vastutas tv eka evāsau pratyayaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
nanv adhyakṣaviyoge syād anumānaṃ kathaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.768]

mv-k05-v705.plain_english: It is true that inference depends on a connection determined by perception; but ultimately that rests on the one Lord who is the abode of omniscience.
mv-k05-v705.sanskrit_cite:
tatpratyakṣaparicchinnapratibandhanibandhanam /
satyaṃ kiṃtu ya eko 'sau devaḥ sarvajñatāspadam // [AgMsv_1.769]

mv-k05-v706.plain_english: Through immersion in that Lord, pervasion becomes possible in awareness; otherwise, even relations like fire and smoke, or knowledge of their absence, could not be established.
mv-k05-v706.sanskrit_cite:
tadāveśavaśād eṣā vyāptir bodhe 'vakalpate /
anyathā vahnidhūmādi tadabhāvādivedanam // [AgMsv_1.770]

mv-k05-v707.plain_english: The pattern of agreement and difference would not arise even over hundreds of ages; it arises because of similarity recognized by a primary cognition.
mv-k05-v707.sanskrit_cite:
anvayavyatirekātmā na syād yugaśatair api /
ata eva hi mukhyasya mānasya sadṛśatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.771]

mv-k05-v708.plain_english: Inference is said to set practical activity in motion; thus all knowing subjects everywhere depend on the awareness of the Lord.
mv-k05-v708.sanskrit_cite:
anumānam iti proktaṃ vyavahārapravartanam /
tad evam ete mātāraḥ sarvatreśvarasaṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.772]

mv-k05-v709.plain_english: They come to be knowers by depending on that awareness, and not otherwise; for how could this ignorant class of beings become knowers without entering into it?
mv-k05-v709.sanskrit_cite:
upajīvitum āyānti mātṛbhāvaṃ na cānyathā /
ajño hi jantuvargo 'yaṃ kathaṃ tadaniveśataḥ // [AgMsv_1.773]

mv-k05-v710.plain_english: One attains the nature of a knower through that awareness; without it, how could knowerhood arise? Therefore this being's connection with awareness is not hard to obtain.
mv-k05-v710.sanskrit_cite:
jñasvarūpatvam āpnoti tad vinā mātṛtā kutaḥ /
tasmād saṃvidi yogo 'sya sa ca nānena durlabhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.774]

mv-k05-v711.plain_english: In reality there is no one apart from awareness, for each knower has awareness as its lord; thus any position operates only as drawn from the Lord's perception.
mv-k05-v711.sanskrit_cite:
vastuto hi na kaś cit sa savinnātho hy asau tathā /
tad evaṃ pakṣam īśānapratyakṣākṣiptavṛttikam // [AgMsv_1.775]

mv-k05-v712.plain_english: The bound means of knowing is said to be dependent on another; for this ignorant, non-sovereign being does not control its own pleasure and pain.
mv-k05-v712.sanskrit_cite:
sāpekṣaṃ paratantre ca pāśavaṃ mānam ucyate /
ajño jantur anīśo 'yam ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.776]

mv-k05-v713.plain_english: The sage declared that the being moves only as impelled by the Lord; thus, for such a being, inference dependent on the Lord is the sole means of valid knowledge.
mv-k05-v713.sanskrit_cite:
īśvaraprerito yātīty ata eva munir jagau /
evam īśvarasāpekṣānumānaikapramāṇatā // [AgMsv_1.777]

mv-k05-v714.plain_english: This position was determined by the teacher named Lolaṭa and accepted by many; another thinker took it up and said, 'True, perceptual awareness also has validity.'
mv-k05-v714.sanskrit_cite:
nirṇītā lolaṭākhyena guruṇā lokasaṃmatā /
anyas tadgṛhya evāha satyaṃ vādhyakṣasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_1.778]

mv-k05-v715.plain_english: In practical life, perception has validity; but how can inference be certain knowledge when error is so easily possible in it?
mv-k05-v715.sanskrit_cite:
vyavahāre 'sti mānatvam anumā tu kathaṃ pramā /
sulabhavyabhicārāyām anumāyāṃ viniścitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.779]

mv-k05-v716.plain_english: Who, standing as a careful examiner, could rest confidently on agreement and difference, which depend on presence in similar and dissimilar cases?
mv-k05-v716.sanskrit_cite:
viśaṃśramītu ko nāma parīkṣakatayā sthitaḥ /
anvayo vyatirekaś ca yaḥ sapakṣetarasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.780]

mv-k05-v717.plain_english: What is seen at first does not produce certainty at that moment; therefore it should be rejected because of faults such as defects in the subject and its property.
mv-k05-v717.sanskrit_cite:
ādidṛṣṭas tadātve no viniścayavidhāyinau /
yais tu tasmād apāsyeta pakṣadharmādidūṣaṇāt [ṇam] // [AgMsv_1.781]

mv-k05-v718.plain_english: They would be trying to purify a heap of filth with piles of dust; therefore inference remains as doubt, serving only as an aid to action.
mv-k05-v718.sanskrit_cite:
varcaskakūṭe śuddhiṃ te kuryuḥ pāṃsukaṇoccayaiḥ /
tasmāt saṃśaya evāyaṃ pravṛttyaṅgatayā sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.782]

mv-k05-v719.plain_english: Because it manifests difference, that same doubtful cognition is called māyā; and for bound beings, the means of knowing is māyā itself, arising from māyā and consciousness.
mv-k05-v719.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva bhedābhāsitvān māyeti paribhāṣyate /
māyeva ca paśūnāṃ syān mānaṃ māyācidātakam // [AgMsv_1.783]

mv-k05-v720.plain_english: Reasoning, which considers the possibility that one side may hold, serves to guide engagement or withdrawal in action by weighing the greater force of benefit or harm.
mv-k05-v720.sanskrit_cite:
tarko vāpy ekapakṣāṃśasthitisaṃbhāvanātmakaḥ /
arthānarthabalīyastvāt pravṛttau [ttyai] vā nivṛttaye // [AgMsv_1.784]

mv-k05-v721.plain_english: He alone is all-powerful; what need is there of other displays of means of knowledge? Śiva alone is the one knower, whose own limb this world appears as such.
mv-k05-v721.sanskrit_cite:
prabhaviṣṇuḥ sa eveti kim anyair mānaḍambaraiḥ /
pramātā śiva evaiko yasyedaṃ svāṅgam īdrśam // [AgMsv_1.785]

mv-k05-v722.plain_english: As an object, it appears on all sides as having the nature of certainty; but every other being, the bound soul, dwells in the midst of the darkness of doubt.
mv-k05-v722.sanskrit_cite:
meyatvena samābhāti sarvato niścayātmakam /
anyaḥ punaḥ paśuḥ sarvaḥ saṃśayadhvāntamadhyagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.786]

mv-k05-v723.plain_english: Colored by an awareness like a flash of lightning, he reaches a certainty that one of two alternatives is true and the other not.

mv-k05-v724.plain_english: Even while finding it, he never gains firm grounding here in any way; therefore it is established that all practical activity proceeds from reasoning.
mv-k05-v724.sanskrit_cite:
vindāna eva labhate nātra rūḍhiṃ kathaṃ cana /
tad evaṃ tarkataḥ sarvo vyavahāra iti sthitam // [AgMsv_1.788]

mv-k05-v725.plain_english: Let this very knowledge be designated as an impure means of knowledge; its impurity is just this, that it does not conform to the real object.
mv-k05-v725.sanskrit_cite:
aśuddha saiva vidyeyam iti mānaṃ vidhīyatām /
aśuddhir iyatī tasyā yad vastv ananusāritā // [AgMsv_1.789]

mv-k05-v726.plain_english: But others, being certain that there is no activity for one who has no purpose, argued in this way that needfulness alone is the assisting factor.
mv-k05-v726.sanskrit_cite:
anye tv anarthino nāsti pravṛttir iti niścitāḥ /
arthitvam eva sacivam ity evaṃ paryacūcudan // [AgMsv_1.790]

mv-k05-v727.plain_english: Thus those who know the self as other declared that desire has the status of a means of knowledge; but others say that even doubt does not arise about an elephant that is not determined at all.
mv-k05-v727.sanskrit_cite:
rāgasya mānatām itthaṃ prāhur anyātmavedinaḥ /
anye tv āhuḥ saṃśayo 'pi na nāmāniścite gaje // [AgMsv_1.791]

mv-k05-v728.plain_english: When there is capability, desire may arise for activity; therefore people, having slightly noticed their own agency, always engage in action.
mv-k05-v728.sanskrit_cite:
śaktatve sati jāyeta rāgo vāpi pravṛttaye /
tataḥ svāṃ kartṛtām īṣad ālocya janatāḥ sadā // [AgMsv_1.792]

mv-k05-v729.plain_english: Thus they engage in action; this would be merely the unfolding of limited agency. Therefore, whether that object is so or not, by that power he takes himself to be an agent.
mv-k05-v729.sanskrit_cite:
pravartanta itītthaṃ syāt kalāyā eva jṛmbhitam /
tenārthaḥ sa tathā vāstu mā vābhūt svātmanas tayā // [AgMsv_1.793]

mv-k05-v730.plain_english: Considering himself an agent, this person engages in action everywhere; but others say that the practical activity consisting of action is beginningless.
mv-k05-v730.sanskrit_cite:
manvānaḥ kartṛtām eṣa sarvatraiva pravartate /
anye tv āhur anādir yo vyavahāraḥ kriyātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.794]

mv-k05-v731.plain_english: That very restriction abides as the impeller of the whole world; and that same thing is called scripture, namely the traditional course of conduct of the elders.
mv-k05-v731.sanskrit_cite:
niyatiḥ saiva viśvasya pravartakatayā sthitā /
sa eva cāgamo nāma vṛddhavyavahṛtikramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.795]

mv-k05-v732.plain_english: Therefore this complete determination of dharma and so forth does not come from perception or inference, which are for the most part deceptive.
mv-k05-v732.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ samagra evāyaṃ dharmādipariniścayaḥ /
na pratyakṣān nānumānād bhūyasā vipralambhakam // [AgMsv_1.796]

mv-k05-v733.plain_english: The mind of those inclined to examination comes to trust: children learn from others that food allays hunger and water allays thirst.
mv-k05-v733.sanskrit_cite:
matir abhyeti viśvāsaṃ parīkṣāpakṣaśālinām /
annaṃ kṣudhaṃ śamayate tṛṣaṃ vārīti bālakāḥ // [AgMsv_1.797]

mv-k05-v734.plain_english: Having ascertained it from elsewhere and not doubting that it is so, they also rely on that very source as the primary measure in other matters known by perception and so on.
mv-k05-v734.sanskrit_cite:
anyataḥ pariniścitya tathātvānatiśaṅkinaḥ /
anyadākṣādike 'py arthe tata evādyamānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.798]

mv-k05-v735.plain_english: Even examiners properly obtain certainty from what is declared by scripture; and so the sage said, regarding the pair, 'this is merit, this is demerit.'
mv-k05-v735.sanskrit_cite:
labhante niścayaṃ samyag āgamākhyāt parīkṣakāḥ /
tathā ca munir āhedaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpam iti dvaye // [AgMsv_1.799]

mv-k05-v736.plain_english: The purpose of a teaching text is small; that is not the purpose of scripture. For scripture is not merely a collection of books and written texts.
mv-k05-v736.sanskrit_cite:
śāstraprayojanaṃ svalpaṃ nāgamasya prayojanam /
āgamo hi na nāmaiṣa pustakagranthasaṃcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.800]

mv-k05-v737.plain_english: It is not merely the well-known, beginningless Veda and the like; rather, scripture is that established tradition itself, and that tradition has the nature of speech.
mv-k05-v737.sanskrit_cite:
kevalaṃ prathitābhikhyo 'nādir vedādikaḥ kila /
kiṃ tu prasiddhir evāsau sā ca śabdasvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.801]

mv-k05-v738.plain_english: That tradition, which in all systems never comes to be rejected, includes words for goats, shrines, matted hair, ashes, alms, staff, and water-pot.
mv-k05-v738.sanskrit_cite:
yā sarvadarśaneṣv eva na jātv āyāty apohyatām /
chāgaiś caityo jaṭā bhasma bhikṣā daṇḍaḥ kamaṇḍaluḥ // [AgMsv_1.802]

mv-k05-v739.plain_english: Net, heated stone, plucking of beard, hair, and body hair, fire, fuel, the piling of heaps of bricks, and the householder life.
mv-k05-v739.sanskrit_cite:
jālaṃ taptaśilā śmaśrukeśalomaviluñcanam /
agnir edhā iṣṭakaughacayanaṃ gṛhamedhitā // [AgMsv_1.803]

mv-k05-v740.plain_english: Apart from the course of established usage, what means is there for understanding, in terms of meaning, all such words and the assumed meanings of others?

mv-k05-v741.plain_english: Thus the wise have said that this scripture is a valid means of knowledge; for that established tradition is truly divine speech, since it does not deviate.
mv-k05-v741.sanskrit_cite:
ittham āgama evāyaṃ pramāṇam iti dhīdhanaiḥ /
uktaṃ satyaiva vāg aiśī prasiddhir avigānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.805]

mv-k05-v742.plain_english: Whether the well-known scripture in the world is reasonable or otherwise, it is an authority in both knowledge and ignorance; thus that is established.
mv-k05-v742.sanskrit_cite:
prasiddha āgamo loke yuktimān athavetaraḥ /
vidyāyām apy avidyāyāṃ pramāṇam iti tat sthitam // [AgMsv_1.806]

mv-k05-v743.plain_english: For the residents of the revered Bhūtaja, authoritativeness belongs to restriction; but others say that this distinct principle operating here is called time.
mv-k05-v743.sanskrit_cite:
prāmāṇyaṃ niyateḥ śrīmadbhūtajāntanivāsinām /
anye tv āhur viśeṣo 'yaṃ kālo nāmābhivartate // [AgMsv_1.807]

mv-k05-v744.plain_english: That present time operates with the nature of clear manifestation; but then it has an aspect whose clear nature belonged to the past and is now marked by non-clarity.
mv-k05-v744.sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭabhāvasvabhāvo 'sau vartamāno 'bhivartate /
vṛttasphuṭasvabhāvāṃśas tadā tv asphuṭatāmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.808]

mv-k05-v745.plain_english: The past is conceived through the assumption of a cause, while the future is conceived as what is to come; but neither of these is in any way independent, because they depend on each other.
mv-k05-v745.sanskrit_cite:
bhūtaḥ kāraṇakḷptyā tu bhāvy asau parikalpyate /
sa cāyaṃ na svatantro 'sti kaś cid anyonyasaṃśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.809]

mv-k05-v746.plain_english: Time cannot stand independently because it leads to infinite regress, because forms are seen to reverse, because it has no fixed measure, and because it depends on both the knower and the known.

mv-k05-v747.plain_english: Time has no coherent nature of its own, because it never appears without conditions and because it cannot be consistently established as one or many, permanent or impermanent.

mv-k05-v748.plain_english: If a single thing has a single limiting condition, its unity does not require time; and if difference belongs to action or to the condition itself, that is explained internally, so time serves no purpose.
mv-k05-v748.sanskrit_cite:
ekasyaikopadher aikyāt tirodher (?) upadherapi /
kriyāyāḥ svagate bhede kālasyānupayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.812]

mv-k05-v749.plain_english: Whether difference is produced by time itself or by something else through mutual dependence, the result is infinite regress; and since such conditioned difference is unreal and unsubstantial, it cannot establish time as truly real.

mv-k05-v750.plain_english: Because time cannot be established as an effect and a single undivided thing does not need it, the clear sense of the present and its enduring presence are given by consciousness itself.

mv-k06-v751.plain_english: Therefore, through the dissolution of past and future, and also through the dissolution of the present, this god, the lord of consciousness himself, fully makes time manifest.
mv-k06-v751.sanskrit_cite:
bhūtabhāvilayāt tasmād vartamānalayād api /
cinnātha eva devo 'sau kālam ābhāsayaty alam // [AgMsv_1.815]

mv-k06-v752.plain_english: Thus, for this consciousness whose nature is to manifest time, transmigration—containing the manifestation of its own nature—appears among beings as consisting of being and nonbeing within its own form.
mv-k06-v752.sanskrit_cite:
tad asya kālābhāsākhyā citsvarūpasya saṃsṛtiḥ /
svabhāva[svābhāsa]garbhā bhāveṣu bhāvābhāvamayī svake // [AgMsv_1.816]

mv-k06-v753.plain_english: Abiding in its own form is called the unfolding of knowerhood: 'this is not what I am', and 'I am what is not this', and also 'this is that'.
mv-k06-v753.sanskrit_cite:
rūpe sthitiḥ pramātṛtvasamullāso 'bhidhīyate /
idaṃ na yad ahaṃ cāhaṃ yan nedam idam apy adaḥ // [AgMsv_1.817]

mv-k06-v754.plain_english: The varied cognition expressed as 'this is not this' is the supreme appearing of nonbeing; but in that pure knowerhood there is no separate abiding of such distinctions.
mv-k06-v754.sanskrit_cite:
yan nedam iti citreyam abhāva[ābhāsa]syaiva mānatā /
parā pramātṛtā yāsau śuddhā tasyāṃ pṛthaksthiti // [AgMsv_1.818]

mv-k06-v755.plain_english: In that isolated aspect there is no cognition at all, so what use is that isolated state? But every worldly state of being a knower is of this differentiated kind.
mv-k06-v755.sanskrit_cite:
na mānam astīty atrāṃśe kiṃ tayā praviviktayā /
yas tu sāṃsāriko mātṛbhāvaḥ sarvo 'yam īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_1.819]

mv-k06-v756.plain_english: There, nonbeing becomes an object of cognition, and that happens through the grace of time; for this perfectly full reality bears the form of all things and the self of all.
mv-k06-v756.sanskrit_cite:
tatrābhāva[sa]sya mānatvaṃ sa ca kālaprasādataḥ /
tathā hi paripūrṇo 'sau sarvasarvātmarūpadhṛt // [AgMsv_1.820]

mv-k06-v757.plain_english: Where could the knower stand, where cognition, and where the known object? For if knower and the rest were absolutely real, their status could not be merely relative.
mv-k06-v757.sanskrit_cite:
kva mātā kva ca vā mānaṃ kva ca meyo 'vatiṣṭhatām /
mātrādīnāṃ hi satyatve na syād āpekṣikī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.821]

mv-k06-v758.plain_english: The being of the knower and the rest is conceived only from the known; whether their mutual form is absent or present, it cannot stand independently because of their incompatibility.
mv-k06-v758.sanskrit_cite:
meyād eva ca mātrāder bhāvo jātu prakalpate /
anyonyarūpasyālābhe lābhe vā tadayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.822]

mv-k06-v759.plain_english: This view fails because it would lead to overextension everywhere, would entail omniscience and the like, and because noncontributing factors do not manifest all at once.
mv-k06-v759.sanskrit_cite:
sarvatrātiprasaṅgāc ca sarvajñatvādiyogataḥ /
yugapac cāpy anullāsāt tattvasyānupakāriṇām // [AgMsv_1.823]

mv-k06-v760.plain_english: If knowerhood were produced by some other known object, then its own arising would depend on something else again, and so it would remain as if unarisen.
mv-k06-v760.sanskrit_cite:
anyameyādijanite mātṛtvādau tadanyataḥ /
tadbhāvasyāpy anutpannasamatvenaiva saṃsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.824]

mv-k06-v761.plain_english: Therefore this full consciousness, Shiva, dividing its own aspect, constructs the differentiated part beginning with 'not I' and also the object 'this'.
mv-k06-v761.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād pūrṇaś cidātmāsau śivaḥ svāṃśaṃ vikhaṇḍayan /
nāham ityādibhedāṃśa idam apy avakalpayet // [AgMsv_1.825]

mv-k06-v762.plain_english: The 'I' takes to itself, to that extent, the fullness of everything other; and from what is other there also arises the withdrawing sense of 'not I'.
mv-k06-v762.sanskrit_cite:
tadanyasarvapūrṇatvam aham ātmani tāvati /
tato 'nyato 'pi saṃhartā jāyate nāham ity api // [AgMsv_1.826]

mv-k06-v763.plain_english: These two parts mutually exclude each other; the own 'I' conceals the 'this' part, which stands in cognition, within its own 'I'-aspect.
mv-k06-v763.sanskrit_cite:
ubhau tau idam aṃśau cāpy apohati parasparam /
buddhistham idam aṃśaṃ svaṃ svāham aṃśe tirodadhat // [AgMsv_1.827]

mv-k06-v764.plain_english: It remains and does not dissolve it, just like a pot covered by a cloth; that same thing, though tied by convention, remains established in cognition.
mv-k06-v764.sanskrit_cite:
āste na drāvayaty enaṃ vastrāvṛtaghaṭādivat /
tad eva buddhisaṃsthāt tu samayāgrathitād atho // [AgMsv_1.828]

mv-k06-v765.plain_english: The 'this' arises from inner contraction that excludes the 'I'-part, and the 'I' arises from within through exclusion of the whole mass of 'thisness'.
mv-k06-v765.sanskrit_cite:
idam antarasaṃghātād ahamaṃśavyapohinaḥ /
ahamaṃśād idantaughavyapohād aham antarāt // [AgMsv_1.829]

mv-k06-v766.plain_english: From the exclusion of one's own 'I' and the exclusion of other and other 'I'-senses there arises manifestation; relying on which, the six deities of empty form proceed.
mv-k06-v766.sanskrit_cite:
vyapohātsvāhamo 'nyānyāhaṃvyapohasya bhāsanam /
ṣaḍdevatāḥ śūnyarūpā yadāśritya pravartate // [AgMsv_1.830]

mv-k06-v767.plain_english: The cognition 'that is indeed this' is called conceptual construction; and that is time, by which the universe is articulated through the arising of its own parts.
mv-k06-v767.sanskrit_cite:
tad evedam iti jñānaṃ vikalpa iti gīyate /
sa kālaḥ kalyate yena viśvaṃ nijakalodayāt // [AgMsv_1.831]

mv-k06-v768.plain_english: In that part there is this aspect of manifestation, self-luminous in the form of being; that is the very nature which animates all things.
mv-k06-v768.sanskrit_cite:
tad atrāṃśe ya eṣo 'sti bhāsāṃśaḥ svaprakāśakaḥ /
bhāvarūpatayā so 'yaṃ sarvānuprāṇanātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.832]

mv-k06-v769.plain_english: That is not defined as knower, nor as cognition, nor as known; but that aspect which, through connection with emptiness, appears as nonbeing has Rudra as its deity.
mv-k06-v769.sanskrit_cite:
na mātāsau na vā mānaṃ na ca meyaṃ nirucyate /
yas tv asau śūnyatāyogād abhāvo rudradaivataḥ // [AgMsv_1.833]

mv-k06-v770.plain_english: That very aspect becomes cognition; through its connection knowerhood is oriented, and from cognition the known stands apart. Thus it has been established.
mv-k06-v770.sanskrit_cite:
sa eva mānatām eti yadyogān mātṛtābhāvi[va]taḥ /
mānāc ca pṛthaṅmeyam ity evam upapāditam // [AgMsv_1.834]

mv-k06-v771.plain_english: In this way, the status of time as cognition was understood here by certain teachers who attended upon the revered guru feet known as Bhavatī.
mv-k06-v771.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ kālasya mānatvaṃ pratipede 'tra kaiś cana /
ye śrīmadbhavatītyākhyagurupādopasevinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.835]

mv-k06-v772.plain_english: Thus, in the individual self—shining with the joy of the glory of consciousness's nature and receiving knowerhood—there is declared the group of six called the sheaths.
mv-k06-v772.sanskrit_cite:
tad itthaṃ puṃsi ciddharmavibhavāmodaśālini /
mātṛtvadāyi yat proktaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ kañcukasaṃjñitam // [AgMsv_1.836]

mv-k06-v773.plain_english: Some have accepted that each one of them has the status of cognition, but others think that one of them functions with all the others as its assistants.
mv-k06-v773.sanskrit_cite:
tad ekaikasya mānatvaṃ ke cana pratipedire /
anye tv ekasya sarvānyasacivasyeti manvate // [AgMsv_1.837]

mv-k06-v774.plain_english: Others say that sometimes, somehow, somewhere, some one of them operates, and so on; others hold that they operate in pairs, and others by combinations of a triad and a pair.
mv-k06-v774.sanskrit_cite:
anye kadāpi kasyāpi kathaṃcit kva canetyādi /
anye dvayor dvayor anye trikadvayaniyogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.838]

mv-k06-v775.plain_english: Some say valid cognition comes from mutual favoring, others from mutual cognition, while others hold that primordial nature, whose essence is the balance of the qualities, alone is valid cognition.
mv-k06-v775.sanskrit_cite:
anyonyānugrahād anye bodhenānyonyato 'pare /
anye tu guṇasāmyātmaprakṛtim eva mānatām // [AgMsv_1.839]

mv-k06-v776.plain_english: They regard it as primary because of what is seen in sleep, intoxication, fainting, and similar states: wherever this knower stands as if asleep, that is taken to be the knower.
mv-k06-v776.sanskrit_cite:
mukhyatvena viduḥ suptamattamūrcchādidarśanāt /
sa yatraiva pramātāyaṃ yataḥ supta iva sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.840]

mv-k06-v777.plain_english: That alone is his knowerhood, because in such deep sleep cognition and object are not apprehended and there is mutual unchangeability.
mv-k06-v777.sanskrit_cite:
saivāsya mātṛtā mānameyayor apravedanāt /
anyonyam avikāryatvāt prasupte 'pi tathāvidhe // [AgMsv_1.841]

mv-k06-v778.plain_english: In that view, primordial nature alone conceives 'I know,' but the primary cognition is that which is the seeing belonging to spirit alone.
mv-k06-v778.sanskrit_cite:
kevalaṃ prakṛtiḥ seyaṃ jānāmīty abhimanyate /
tatra mukhyaṃ tu yan mānaṃ yatpuṃsaivānudarśanam // [AgMsv_1.842]

mv-k06-v779.plain_english: And that cognition is pure, unchanging, and free from the forms of being and nonbeing; some hold this view by relying on a Sāṃkhya covering.
mv-k06-v779.sanskrit_cite:
tac ca śuddhaṃ nirvikāraṃ sadasadrūpatojjhitam /
itthaṃ ke 'py abhimanyante sāṃkhyakañcukasaṃśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.843]

mv-k06-v780.plain_english: Others, living on knowledge in the house of the teacher Vayya, call the level of intellect itself the means of cognition, since it is colored by seer and seen.
mv-k06-v780.sanskrit_cite:
vayyābhidhānasya guror gṛhe jñānopajīvinaḥ /
anye dhībhūmim evāhur draṣṭṛdṛśyoparāgiṇīm // [AgMsv_1.844]

mv-k06-v781.plain_english: Some followers of Paramarshi say valid cognition is the collection of its modifications, while others hold it to be the class of properties counted as eight, beginning with merit.
mv-k06-v781.sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇaṃ pāramarṣeyāḥ kecit tadvṛttisaṃcayam /
dharmādikāṣṭasaṃkhyātaṃ dharmajātaṃ pare viduḥ // [AgMsv_1.845]

mv-k06-v782.plain_english: Others say it is the ego-sense alone, some say intellect, others mind, and some hold that this triad functions equally everywhere.
mv-k06-v782.sanskrit_cite:
anye 'haṃkāram evāhuḥ kecid dhiyam atho manaḥ /
kecid tritayam evedaṃ samaṃ sarvatra manvate // [AgMsv_1.846]

mv-k06-v783.plain_english: Others accept each one of the ten sense organs, while some accept all of them together, because they function everywhere without confusion.
mv-k06-v783.sanskrit_cite:
anye daśānām ekaikam indriyāṇām prapedire /
kecit samastāny etāni sarvatrākūṭavṛttitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.847]

mv-k06-v784.plain_english: For even a blind person has some domain of form, which produces a change when it reaches the hearing sense while the other senses remain in the same condition.
mv-k06-v784.sanskrit_cite:
andhasyāpi hi tat kiṃcidrūpāyatanam asti yat /
vikāram ekaśrotraspṛg akṣāntarasamasthiti // [AgMsv_1.848]

mv-k06-v785.plain_english: Hearing, 'It is dawn, and the sky is adorned with a cloudless expanse,' a blind person feels great satisfaction on a wintry day.
mv-k06-v785.sanskrit_cite:
prabhātaṃ pravilīnābhranabhomaṇḍalamaṇḍitam /
ity ākarṇya parāṃ tūṣṭiṃ yāty andho haimane dine // [AgMsv_1.849]

mv-k06-v786.plain_english: Even if he infers the comfort that comes from the removal of cold, still his own awareness does not directly reveal form.
mv-k06-v786.sanskrit_cite:
yady apy anumimīte 'sau śītavāraṇajaṃ sukham /
tathāpy asya svasaṃvittir na rūpānavabhāsinī // [AgMsv_1.850]

mv-k06-v787.plain_english: Others accept the subtle elements as the means of cognition, appealing to rules such as the claim that the eye-ray makes no contact.
mv-k06-v787.sanskrit_cite:
anye tanmātrarūpāṇāṃ mānatvaṃ pratipedire /
cakṣūraśmis tv asaṃsparśa ityādividhiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.851]

mv-k06-v788.plain_english: On that basis the invisibility of the eye and other senses is explained, but with respect to a yogin such invisibility is never explained.
mv-k06-v788.sanskrit_cite:
adṛśyatvaṃ cakṣurāder ata evopapadyate /
yoginaḥ praty adṛśyatvaṃ jātucin nopapadyate // [AgMsv_1.852]

mv-k06-v789.plain_english: Others declare the gross luminous elements to be valid cognition, while still others accept even the object of cognition as valid cognition.
mv-k06-v789.sanskrit_cite:
anye tu sthūlabhūtānāṃ jyotiṣāṃ mānatāṃ jaguḥ /
meyasyāpi pramāṇatvam apare pratipedire // [AgMsv_1.853]

mv-k06-v790.plain_english: The position is that whatever gives rise to knowerhood is valid cognition; and since a pot and such things do that, they too are regarded as valid cognition.
mv-k06-v790.sanskrit_cite:
yato bhavati mātṛtvaṃ tatpramāṇam iti sthitiḥ /
tadghaṭādyaiś ca yat tasmāt te 'pi mānam iti smṛtāḥ // [AgMsv_1.854]

mv-k06-v791.plain_english: And ordinary usage does not follow reality, for since it is formed by mere convention, it is mostly figurative.
mv-k06-v791.sanskrit_cite:
laukiko vyapadeśaś ca naiva vastvanusārataḥ /
sa hīcchāmātrakḷptatvāt prāyeṇaivopacārikaḥ // [AgMsv_1.855]

mv-k06-v792.plain_english: Asked, 'How do you know, sir?' and prompted, he replies, 'I know by this seen pot.'
mv-k06-v792.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ jānāsi bhoḥ so 'haṃ jānāmīti ca coditaḥ /
ghaṭenānena dṛṣṭena jānāmīty abhibhāṣate // [AgMsv_1.856]

mv-k06-v793.plain_english: Therefore, even if cognition is attributed to the object, that is not outside ordinary usage; and in a root-level doctrine of non-difference, even contradiction is not a fault.
mv-k06-v793.sanskrit_cite:
tasmān meye 'pi mānatvaṃ na hi nāma na laukikam /
abhedavāde mūlasthe virodho 'pi na dūṣaṇam // [AgMsv_1.857]

mv-k06-v794.plain_english: But those who say valid cognition is the totality of its factors clearly accept the cognitive status of the object and so on; if that status belongs even to the aggregate, how could it be otherwise?
mv-k06-v794.sanskrit_cite:
ye tu pramāṇam āhus tatsāmagrīṃ tair api sphuṭam /
arthāder mānatābhīṣṭā sā saṅghe 'py anyathā kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.858]

mv-k06-v795.plain_english: Others hold that every distinction of every measured thing has the status of cognition, arising in sequence everywhere and in some cases arising without sequence.
mv-k06-v795.sanskrit_cite:
anye tu sarvasyaiveyattāttabhedasya mānatām /
kramoditāṃ hi sarvatra kvacic cāpy akramoditām // [AgMsv_1.859]

mv-k06-v796.plain_english: In some cases they consider it to be full with a complete grasp of both sequence and nonsequence; for now that view is shown only by a brief indication.
mv-k06-v796.sanskrit_cite:
kvacit kramākramagrāsaparipūrṇatvabandhurām /
manvate tanmataṃ tāvad diṅmātreṇopadarśyate // [AgMsv_1.860]

mv-k06-v797.plain_english: First, through sudden contact with an appearing object, there is simply an inquiry on all sides into the intent concerning another seen thing.
mv-k06-v797.sanskrit_cite:
prathamaṃ meyayogena jhaṭiti pratibhāsinā /
anyārthadṛśyabhiprāyapracchanenaiva sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.861]

mv-k06-v798.plain_english: Finally there is knowerhood: first the unfolding of the eye, and then an inner brightness through the unfolding of the group of mind, ego, and intellect.
mv-k06-v798.sanskrit_cite:
mātṛtvaṃ caramaṃ tatra cakṣuṣaḥ pravijṛṃbhaṇam /
tato mano 'haṃdhīvargavijṛṃbhāntaḥsamujjvalam // [AgMsv_1.862]

mv-k06-v799.plain_english: Then comes the radiance of purified masculine consciousness, and after that the nights of time, limitation, attachment, impurity, and ignorance arise in sequence.

mv-k06-v800.plain_english: At the limited level, these factors may arise otherwise or together, in pairs or in threes, all at once, or even in combinations of four or five.
mv-k06-v800.sanskrit_cite:
anyathā vā samaṃ vāpi dvandvayogena vā triśaḥ /
sarvaśo vā catuṣpañcayogenāpy āṇave pade // [AgMsv_1.864]

mv-k06-v801.plain_english: There too, doubts arise concerning nonbeing, agency, attachment, proof, and reasoning, varied according to their different sequences.

mv-k06-v802.plain_english: After that, nonconceptual knowledge that reveals pure sovereignty becomes the valid means of knowledge in the final state of cognition.
mv-k06-v802.sanskrit_cite:
tatpṛṣṭe cāvikalpāsau śuddhaiśvaryāvabhāsikā /
vidyā pramāṇatām eti paryantapramitisthitau // [AgMsv_1.866]

mv-k06-v803.plain_english: Then, resting on the noble powers of knowledge and will of Sadashiva, that knower attains fullness, fulfilled in the path that culminates in Shakti.
mv-k06-v803.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ sadāśivodārajñānecchāśaktisaṃśraye /
sa mātā pūrṇatām eti śaktyantādhvasunirvṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.867]

mv-k06-v804.plain_english: Thus full knowerhood shines forth equally; yet differentiated forms of awareness arise from not being separated from the concealment of some part of that fullness.
mv-k06-v804.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ pūrṇaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ yataḥ samavabhāsate /
tadanyatamabhāgāṃśatirodhānaviyogajāḥ // [AgMsv_1.868]

mv-k06-v805.plain_english: The distinctions of clarity and otherness in awareness become countless; therefore those who do not know fail to recognize the state taught in the Shiva scriptures.
mv-k06-v805.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaḥ sphuṭatānyatvabhedān niḥsaṃkhyatāṃ gatāḥ /
ata eva hy ajānānaiḥ śivaśāstroditāṃ sthitim // [AgMsv_1.869]

mv-k06-v806.plain_english: In clear and unclear awareness, in memory and forgetfulness, and in states like deep sleep, reasoning and reflection cannot occur because of their rapidity.

mv-k06-v807.plain_english: Mental attention, mental impressions, and the postulation of unseen merit are merely words here; they do not provide a real meaning in this case.
mv-k06-v807.sanskrit_cite:
manovadhānaṃ saṃskāro dharmādyadṛṣṭakalpanam /
ity ete hi sphuṭaṃ śabdā nātra ko 'rthas tatri ... mā // [AgMsv_1.871]

mv-k06-v808.plain_english: When the group of higher and higher principles is established as the measure, the portion of lower and lower principles takes on the status of object.
mv-k06-v808.sanskrit_cite:
ūrdhvordhvatattvavrātasya mānatve ca nirūpite /
adharādharatattvāṃśo meyatām avalambate // [AgMsv_1.872]

mv-k06-v809.plain_english: There is no sequence here, for if there were interruption it would imply mediation; neither knowledge nor the intellect perceives that awareness.
mv-k06-v809.sanskrit_cite:
na cātrāsti kramaḥ kaś cid vyavadhāne hi saṃbhavāt /
na hi vidyā na bauddhī tām ālocayati saṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.873]

mv-k06-v810.plain_english: Knowledge is said to be discriminating and rests on the intellect, while the external sense faculty, whose nature is light, consists in perception.
mv-k06-v810.sanskrit_cite:
vidyā vivektrī proktā hi buddhipṛṣṭasamāśritā /
prakāśātmavapur bāhyam akṣam ālocanātmakam // [AgMsv_1.874]

mv-k06-v811.plain_english: They declare mind to be for conception, ego-making to be appropriating, intellect to be determining, and knowledge there to be discriminating.
mv-k06-v811.sanskrit_cite:
saṃkalpārthaṃ manaḥ prāhur abhimantrīm ahaṅkṛtim /
niścetrīṃ ca dhiyaṃ tatra vidyāṃ cāpi vivecikām // [AgMsv_1.875]

mv-k06-v812.plain_english: There attachment is coloring, limitation shows capacity, time delimits the agent, and restriction regulates.
mv-k06-v812.sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva rañjakaṃ rāgaṃ kalāṃ śaktatvadarśinīm /
kālaṃ vyavacchit kartāraṃ niyatiṃ ca niyāmikāṃ // [AgMsv_1.876]

mv-k06-v813.plain_english: Maya is reflective, manifests commonness with other knowers, and reflects the sphere of objects together with their various graspers.

mv-k06-v814.plain_english: Maya causes agitation and a fall from the enjoyment of fullness, while pure knowledge gives rest in fullness and has the nature of auspicious Shiva.

mv-k06-v815.plain_english: The power of will reflects a nature filled with knowledge and manifests the full being of the knower aspect.

mv-k06-v816.plain_english: Relying on these powers, this completely full state of the knower unfolds: first illumination and perception, then conception and intention.
mv-k06-v816.sanskrit_cite:
āśritya paripūrṇo 'yaṃ mātṛbhāvo vijṛmbhate ṝü /
prakāśālocane pūrvaṃ saṃkalpābhimate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.880]

mv-k06-v817.plain_english: Afterward come determination and subsequent seeing, then the pair of discrimination and nonattachment, followed by the delimitation of agency and the manifestation of commonness.

mv-k06-v818.plain_english: The presentation of the full object stirred by various reflections, together with awareness of full knowerhood, is indeed the Bhairava state.

mv-k06-v819.plain_english: Thus, as long as it manifests the object-domain in sixteen ways, this moon of consciousness is said to abide in sixteen phases.
mv-k06-v819.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ṣoḍaśadhā meyamayaṃ yāvat prakāśayet /
tāvad vijñānacandro 'sau prokto dvyaṣṭakalāsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.883]

mv-k06-v820.plain_english: First is the unsurpassed state, then bliss, will, and lordship, and after that arising, inclination, and immersion; thus a group of six is established.
mv-k06-v820.sanskrit_cite:
anuttarā sthitiḥ pūrvam ānandeccheśanāny ataḥ /
udayaś conatāveśa iti ṣaṭkaṃ vyavasthitam // [AgMsv_1.884]

mv-k06-v821.plain_english: Beginning from the unsurpassed and extending to the power of knowledge, will itself is established, and together with lordship it is established in relation to the power of action.
mv-k06-v821.sanskrit_cite:
anuttarāt samārabhya jñānaśaktyantam īdṛśam /
icchaiva tu kriyāśaktim īśanena samāsthitā // [AgMsv_1.885]

mv-k06-v822.plain_english: Taking up a subtle portion of light and stability, it attains a sixfold state; and the series beginning with will does so because of its connection with the prior unsurpassed and bliss.
mv-k06-v822.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśasthitileśāṃśaṃ gṛhṇatī ṣaṇṭhatāṃ gatā ṝü /
icchādi yac ca tatpūrvānuttarānandasaṃgateḥ // [AgMsv_1.886]

mv-k06-v823.plain_english: Through connection with that and what follows, a group of four juncture syllables arises. From that comes the attainment of awareness of one's own nature, and from that comes a state beginning with bindu.
mv-k06-v823.sanskrit_cite:
tadādiśleṣayogena saṃdhyakṣaracatuṣṭayam ṝü /
tataḥ svarūpasaṃvittilābhād bindvādikā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.887]

mv-k06-v824.plain_english: Then, in a form filled with the entire sequence, there arises the śākta visarga. This is indeed remembered as projection.
mv-k06-v824.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ samagrasaṃdarbhabharitākārarūpiṇi /
visargaḥ kila śākto 'sau vikṣepa iti yaḥ smṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_1.888]

mv-k06-v825.plain_english: The separation of visarga itself is called the seventeenth phase. In some cases that same phase is called the eighteenth, because of its connection with agitation.
mv-k06-v825.sanskrit_cite:
visargasyaiva viśleṣa iti saptadaśī kalā /
kvacid aṣṭādaśī saiva punaḥ prakṣobhayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.889]

mv-k06-v826.plain_english: Of the supreme akula, the supreme letter a in the form of supreme Bhairava, this is the highest supreme kaula power.
mv-k06-v826.sanskrit_cite:
anuttarasyākārasya parabhairavarūpiṇaḥ /
akulasya parā yeyaṃ kaulikī śāktir uttamā // [AgMsv_1.890]

mv-k06-v827.plain_english: That very power is visarga, and from it this world is born. Its capacity for agitation is the arising of the stir of agitation.
mv-k06-v827.sanskrit_cite:
sa evāyaṃ visargas tu tasmāj jātam idaṃ jagat ṝü /
tasya prakṣobhayogyatvaṃ prakṣobhakalanodayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.891]

mv-k06-v828.plain_english: Because agitation is not yet full, there is a bending into the sequence of that akula. This arises from the swaying reflection of the nature of the sixfold.

mv-k06-v829.plain_english: Because it is of supreme nature, this is the unfolding of the first alone. That very one is the Lord, inwardly always flashing forth.
mv-k06-v829.sanskrit_cite:
anuttarasvabhāvatvād ādyasyaiva vijṛmbhitam ṝü /
sa eva bhagavān antar nityaṃ prasphuradātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.893]

mv-k06-v830.plain_english: He has the middle power filled with all beings within, and he is beautiful with the bliss of the world rising from the nature of his own willed agitation.

mv-k06-v831.plain_english: He always flashes forth, beautiful with the rasa of full emission. That union of Śiva and Śakti is called love.
mv-k06-v831.sanskrit_cite:
nityaṃ sphurati saṃpūrṇavisargarasasundaraḥ ṝü /
śivaśaktyoḥ sa saṃghaṭṭaḥ sneha ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_1.895]

mv-k06-v832.plain_english: Right there, in the state of full emission, they practice the tradition of licking, churning, and so on in order to gain entry.
mv-k06-v832.sanskrit_cite:
atraiva pūrṇavaisargapade labdhuṃ praveśanam /
lehanāmanthanetyādisaṃpradāyam upāsate // [AgMsv_1.896]

mv-k06-v833.plain_english: For thus, having taken its stand in the middle channel, the supreme radiance vitalizes the whole body from the midst of agitated nectar.
mv-k06-v833.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi madhyamāṃ nāḍīm adhiṣṭhāyākhilaṃ vapuḥ /
prāṇayat paramaṃ tejaḥ prakṣubdhāmṛtamadhyataḥ // [AgMsv_1.897]

mv-k06-v834.plain_english: It moves into the state of emission and reaches the wonder of bliss. When merely incomplete it remains limited, but when full it is wholly of the Lord.
mv-k06-v834.sanskrit_cite:
visṛṣṭirūpatāṃ gacched yāty ānandacamatkriyām /
apūrṇā kevalaṃ sā tu pūrṇā tu bhagavanmayī // [AgMsv_1.898]

mv-k06-v835.plain_english: Therefore this single power of emission unfolds. Emission itself becomes agitated because of the doubling of effort.
mv-k06-v835.sanskrit_cite:
tena vaisargikī śaktir ekaiveyaṃ prajṛmbhate /
visarga eva prakṣubdhaḥ prayatnadviguṇatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.899]

mv-k06-v836.plain_english: The letter ha is indeed the producer of all consonants. And that same ha, through connection with bindu, returns to its own level.
mv-k06-v836.sanskrit_cite:
hakāro nāma viśveṣāṃ vyañjanānāṃ prasūtikṛt ṝü /
sa eva ca punarbinduyogāt svām eva bhūmikām // [AgMsv_1.900]

mv-k06-v837.plain_english: It resorts to the supreme level, which is accepted here as the I-sense. From that same locus arise ka, born of the letter a, and another born of the letter i.
mv-k06-v837.sanskrit_cite:
anuttarām āśrayate so 'haṃbhāva iheṣyate ṝü /
atraivāvarṇajaḥ kākhyas tadanyaś ca ivarṇajaḥ // [AgMsv_1.901]

mv-k06-v838.plain_english: From that, through the limiting condition of the shadow of the repha part and from the letter ṛ, arises the ṭa class. From that again, through dha and by the sequence of limiting shadow conditions, the next class proceeds.
mv-k06-v838.sanskrit_cite:
tata eva hi rephāṃśacchāyopādher ṛvarṇataḥ /
ṭavargas tata evātha dharāc chāyopadhikramāt // [AgMsv_1.902]

mv-k06-v839.plain_english: After that comes the ta class, and then ya, ra, and la beginning with u, and va, arising in order from the i-class and from u.
mv-k06-v839.sanskrit_cite:
tavargas tatparaḥ paścād uvarṇādyaralāś ca vaḥ /
ivarṇavargāc covarṇāt krameṇety ata eva hi // [AgMsv_1.903]

mv-k06-v840.plain_english: Thus the semivowels are reached, and from the letter i, in two divisions, comes the arising of śa, ṣa, and sa, joined with phases of pure limiting conditions.
mv-k06-v840.sanskrit_cite:
antaḥsthā ity aśītāś ca ivarṇād dviprabhedaśaḥ /
śaṣasānāṃ samudbhūtiḥ śuddhopādhikalāyujaḥ // [AgMsv_1.904]

mv-k06-v841.plain_english: For the universal emanation is indeed of will and is established in many ways. Therefore its having its own proper place is fitting.
mv-k06-v841.sanskrit_cite:
icchāyā eva viśvo hi prasavo bahudhā sthitaḥ ṝü /
ata eva hi sasthānabhāvo yuktatvam arhati // [AgMsv_1.905]

mv-k06-v842.plain_english: This womb-like resting state belongs to the living being, because that very state is explained here as the power of the supreme god.
mv-k06-v842.sanskrit_cite:
jīvasyaiveyam āśyānasthitir yonyatmikā yataḥ /
saivānuttaradevasya śaktir atra nirucyate // [AgMsv_1.906]

mv-k06-v843.plain_english: There, by the sequence of the levels of speech, the inner principles are arranged: in the a-class is the śiva principle, and in the group from ka to ha is the range extending up to śiva.
mv-k06-v843.sanskrit_cite:
tatraivantaḥsthatattvāni parāvāgbhūmikākramāt /
avarge śivatattvaṃ tu kādau hānte śivāntakam // [AgMsv_1.907]

mv-k06-v844.plain_english: Thus this enclosing union, the meaning of the thirty, has been explained. If the goddess-consciousness is clearly full and unlimited, then it is so.
mv-k06-v844.sanskrit_cite:
iti saṃpuṭayogo 'yaṃ triṃśakārtho nirūpitaḥ ṝü /
evaṃ pūrṇānavacchinnā ciddevī syād yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.908]

mv-k06-v845.plain_english: All would be in her, and she would be everywhere. Whoever sees me everywhere and sees all in me has that vision.
mv-k06-v845.sanskrit_cite:
sarvam asyāṃ bhaved eṣā sarvatra ca tathā bhavet ṝü /
yo māṃ paśyati sarvatra sarvaṃ ca mayi paśyati // [AgMsv_1.909]

mv-k06-v846.plain_english: For such a one I do not perish, and he does not perish for me. The sage spoke this, citing the words of teacher Arjuna in various places.
mv-k06-v846.sanskrit_cite:
tasyāhaṃ na praṇaśyāmi sa mametyapi tan muniḥ /
abhāṣatārjunācāryavacasā tatra tatra ca // [AgMsv_1.910]

mv-k06-v847.plain_english: If consciousness, whose nature is awareness, were cut off from all things, it would become a mere object, like a pot defined only by its own particular mark.
mv-k06-v847.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidātmā hi vicchinno yadi syāt sarvabhāvataḥ /
bhāva eva bhaved eṣa svalakṣaṇaghaṭādivat // [AgMsv_1.911]

mv-k06-v848.plain_english: Therefore, from the loss of its nature as consciousness, this consciousness perishes; for if one seeks to cut consciousness off, it flees away.
mv-k06-v848.sanskrit_cite:
ataś ca saṃvitsaṃvittvahāner eṣā praṇaśyati /
palāyate hi cit sā ced vyavacicchedayiṣyate // [AgMsv_1.912]

mv-k06-v849.plain_english: And the fact that the great mass of people does not see all things in me, though it has been declared so, is like trying to step on the shadow of one's own head while walking.
mv-k06-v849.sanskrit_cite:
nijottamāṅgcchāyeva svapadākramaṇakrame /
yac ca sarvaṃ mayi proktaṃ na paśyati mahājanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.913]

mv-k06-v850.plain_english: Because he abides in the midst of all, he is indeed established in me; yet, because he is not grounded in the light and treats it as unreal, he does not recognize this.
mv-k06-v850.sanskrit_cite:
sa sarvamadhyavartitvān mayi tāvat pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
evaṃ prakāśāniṣṭhatvād asyāsatsamatājuṣaḥ // [AgMsv_1.914]

mv-k06-v851.plain_english: The sage declared that this amounts to destruction by both paths; this, so far, is the order of reality which is called the enclosure.
mv-k06-v851.sanskrit_cite:
praṇāśa eveti muniḥ provācobhayavartmanā /
eṣa vastukramas tāvad yo 'yaṃ saṃpuṭa ucyate // [AgMsv_1.915]

mv-k06-v852.plain_english: From that very principle, in the abode of the seat that contains all the paths, consciousness attains the state of being supported and again becomes the support.
mv-k06-v852.sanskrit_cite:
tata eva samastādhvakalitāsanasadmani /
saṃvid ādheyatāṃ prāptā punar ādhāratāṃ gatā // [AgMsv_1.916]

mv-k06-v853.plain_english: And in the supreme worship the seat was spoken of again; therefore here, for those wishing to enter, the sage speaks according to the order of cognition.
mv-k06-v853.sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ cānuttare yāge punar evāsanaṃ /

\hspace{3cm} tataḥ /
atra tu pravivikṣūṇāṃ jñaptikramavaśān muniḥ // [AgMsv_1.917]

mv-k06-v854.plain_english: The Lord has indeed declared that the universe is not other than that, because the freedom of undivided consciousness shines forth on the path of difference.
mv-k06-v854.sanskrit_cite:
ūcivān bhagavān eva viśvaṃ tan nānyatheti yat /
abhinnasaṃvitsvātantryaṃ bhāsate bhedavartmani // [AgMsv_1.918]

mv-k06-v855.plain_english: This arrangement of the one to be taught and the teacher is extended; for one's own self is regarded as the teacher and as the supreme god.
mv-k06-v855.sanskrit_cite:
upadeśyopadeṣṭṛtvavyavastheyaṃ pratāyate /
svātmaiva hi gurur devaḥ para ity abhimanyate // [AgMsv_1.919]

mv-k06-v856.plain_english: One considers statements uttered by oneself as spoken by another; and the thing to be taught and that by which it is taught are likewise taken as distinct.
mv-k06-v856.sanskrit_cite:
svodīritāni vākyāni paroktānīti manyate /
pratipādyaṃ ca yad vastu yena ca pratipādyate // [AgMsv_1.920]

mv-k06-v857.plain_english: Indeed all that is of the nature of the self, yet one regards it as different, just as one experiences a lineage of instruction while situated in the dream state.
mv-k06-v857.sanskrit_cite:
tat sarvam ātmarūpaṃ hi bhedenaivābhimanyate /
yathā svapnapadāvasthām upadeśaparamparām // [AgMsv_1.921]

mv-k06-v858.plain_english: Just as a dull creature in a dream hears and regards what is spoken as coming from another, so too this entire ordinary activity contained within waking is regarded in the same way.
mv-k06-v858.sanskrit_cite:
ākarṇayaj jaḍo jantur anyoktam abhimanyate /
tathaiva jāgradgarbho 'yaṃ vyavahāraḥ samastakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.922]

mv-k06-v859.plain_english: If one asks what difference there would then be between dream and waking, that will be explained later; or else, what has not been spoken by the free Lord?
mv-k06-v859.sanskrit_cite:
ko bhedaḥ svapnajāgratsu tarhi syād iti cet punaḥ /
bhaṇiṣyate 'tha vā nāthe svatantre kin na bhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.923]

mv-k06-v860.plain_english: Thus the difference between injunction and restatement exists only by the order of cognition; whether one says 'all is God' or 'God is all', it is indeed one and the same.
mv-k06-v860.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ jñaptikrameṇaiva bhedo vidhyanuvādayoḥ /
sarvaṃ devo 'tha vā devaḥ sarvam ity ekam eva hi // [AgMsv_1.924]

mv-k06-v861.plain_english: In reality the universe is a matter of mere synonymy, like 'jar' and 'pot'; what differs is only the expression. Therefore glorious Narayana declared to them, 'You indeed are that.'
mv-k06-v861.sanskrit_cite:
vastutaḥ kumbhaghaṭavad viśvaṃ paryāyamātrakam /
vācya eṣāṃ tvam eveti tac chrīnārāyaṇo 'bhyadhāt // [AgMsv_1.925]

mv-k06-v862.plain_english: But surely, if there is non-difference, how can there be an arrangement of injunction and restatement? For example, 'this toothy one is Caitra' first restates the toothy one.
mv-k06-v862.sanskrit_cite:
nanv abhede kathaṃkāraṃ kḷptir vidhyanuvādayoḥ /
yo danturaḥ sa caitro 'yam iti danturam āditaḥ // [AgMsv_1.926]

mv-k06-v863.plain_english: If, after restating him, the part 'Caitra' is enjoined as something else, then the toothy one would be other than Caitra and Caitra other than the toothy one; how could that be?
mv-k06-v863.sanskrit_cite:
anūdya caitra ityaṃśo yadi nāma vidhīyate /
tad danturo 'nyaś caitrāc caitraś cānyas tataḥ katham // [AgMsv_1.927]

mv-k06-v864.plain_english: A case like 'the pot is Caitra' would not be injunction and restatement; therefore the situation is that the very one who is Caitra is the toothy one.
mv-k06-v864.sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭaś caitra itīdṛkṣā na syād vidhyanuvādatā /
tasmād ya eva caitro 'sau sa dantura iti sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.928]

mv-k06-v865.plain_english: The distinction between injunction and restatement is real in practice but arises only from cognition; it is used for those who do not yet know synonymous terms, as in 'this is a tree, an earth-grower' or 'a jar, a pot', and likewise in saying 'the Great Lord is all this world.'
mv-k06-v865.sanskrit_cite:
vāstavī jñaptimātrottho vidhir vidhyanuvādayoḥ /

ajñātaparyāyapadasthitīn prati prayujyate pādapa eṣa bhūruhaḥ /
kumbho ghaṭaś ceti tathaiva bhaṇyate maheśvaraḥ sarvam idaṃ jagat tv iti // [AgMsv_1.929]

mv-k06-v866.plain_english: In this way, by the union of enclosure, there is indeed a perfectly full state in which even hundreds of phases of dissolution and creation stand within.
mv-k06-v866.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ saṃpuṭayogena paripūrṇā hi yā sthitiḥ /
yasyāṃ saṃhārasṛṣṭyaṃśaśatāny antaḥsthitāny api // [AgMsv_1.930]

mv-k06-v867.plain_english: Some, wishing to worship that very state part by part, do so through divisions arising as one, twofold, four, six, twelve, and so forth.
mv-k06-v867.sanskrit_cite:
tām eva bhāgaśaḥ ke cid upāsitumanas tayā /
ekādidviguṇatvotthacatuḥṣaḍdvādaśādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.931]

mv-k06-v868.plain_english: By various sequences it divides itself through distinctions made of wheels of consciousness: the one consciousness becomes twofold as knowing and acting, and then that same consciousness becomes threefold.
mv-k06-v868.sanskrit_cite:
saṃviccakramayair bhedair bhindate vividhaiḥ kramaiḥ /
ekā saṃvid dvidhā saiva dṛkkriyātmā tridhātha sā // [AgMsv_1.932]

mv-k06-v869.plain_english: Then, through the assistance of the unfolding power, it is also spoken of as fourfold; and through ascent in the bliss of the power of consciousness, this same consciousness is declared to be fivefold.
mv-k06-v869.sanskrit_cite:
pronmeṣaśaktisācivyāc caturdhāpy atha gīyate /
cicchaktyānandarūḍhyā tu pañcadhāsau prabhāṣyate // [AgMsv_1.933]

mv-k06-v870.plain_english: It is sixfold through contemplation of the worship of consciousness taught as the six vowels, and extends up to twelvefold in the creation of consciousness and in domains of equal scope.
mv-k06-v870.sanskrit_cite:
ṣoḍhā tu svaraṣaṭkoktasaṃviccarcāvicāraṇāt /
yāvad dvādaśadhā saṃvitsṛṣṭyādau tulyagocare // [AgMsv_1.934]

mv-k06-v871.plain_english: Consciousness conceives emanation either one by one through a threefold nature, or in the triad through a fourfold nature, and in doing so it takes on redness.
mv-k06-v871.sanskrit_cite:
ekaikaśas tryātmakatvāt traye vā cāturātmyataḥ /
sṛṣṭiṃ kalayate saṃvit tatrābhyeti ca raktatām // [AgMsv_1.935]

mv-k06-v872.plain_english: Consciousness conceives maintenance and dissolution, and at times it may give rise to doubt; then, withdrawing that doubt and the portion of being, it returns again through the withdrawal of its own self.
mv-k06-v872.sanskrit_cite:
sthitināśaṃ kalayate kvāpi śaṅkāṃ prakalpayet /
tāṃ saṃhṛtya ca bhāvāṃśaṃ saṃhārāt svātmanaḥ punaḥ // [AgMsv_1.936]

mv-k06-v873.plain_english: Reflecting on its role as the withdrawer, consciousness considers merit and demerit within that state, and by its own freedom it does not wish for a quick outcome or for suppression.
mv-k06-v873.sanskrit_cite:
saṃhartrītvaṃ carcayate tadantaḥ puṇyapāpayoḥ /
na drutaṃ na nirodhaṃ vā svasvātantryeṇa vāñchati // [AgMsv_1.937]

mv-k06-v874.plain_english: Thus, devouring within itself the wheel of rays made of the faculties and portions of awareness, consciousness withdraws the suns that stand in the part of measurement.
mv-k06-v874.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ bodhāṃśakaraṇamarīcīcakram ātmani /
grasamānā saṃharate pramāṇāṃśasthitān ravīn // [AgMsv_1.938]

mv-k06-v875.plain_english: Then, having withdrawn the constructed part of measurement into the unconstructed heart, it takes even what is beyond all into the unlimited inner abode.
mv-k06-v875.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ kalpitamātraṃśaṃ saṃhṛtyākalpite hṛdi /
tatsarvātītam apy antar anavacchinnadhāmani // [AgMsv_1.939]

mv-k06-v876.plain_english: One should lead that universe through the door of the eye, lead it in that way as far as required, and then conceive emanation again, following this and similar sequential practice.
mv-k06-v876.sanskrit_cite:
nayet tan nayanadvārād viśvaṃ yāvat tathā nayet /
tataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ ca kalayed ityādikramayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.940]

mv-k06-v877.plain_english: This twelve-spoked wheel revolves at all times, and its gross form appears as the arrangements of months, zodiac signs, and the like.
mv-k06-v877.sanskrit_cite:
dvādaśāram idaṃ cakraṃ sarvadā parivartate /
yasyaitāḥ sthūlamātratvaṃ māsarāśyādisaṃpadaḥ // [AgMsv_1.941]

mv-k06-v878.plain_english: By the power of sequence and nonsequence, this arisen wheel expands in twos, in threes, and in many other ways, through various orders, devouring the object, the measure, and the subject.
mv-k06-v878.sanskrit_cite:
akramakramavaśād dviśas triśo bhūriśo 'tha vividhaiḥ kramākramaiḥ /
cakram etad uditaṃ vijṛmbhate meyamānamitimātṛbhakṣakam // [AgMsv_1.942]

mv-k06-v879.plain_english: Because this wheel rests on endless rays and spokes within it, the divisions of the wheel can never be counted.
mv-k06-v879.sanskrit_cite:
etaccakragatānantakiraṇārāsamāśrayāt /
cakrabhedo na saṃkhyātuṃ kadācid api śakyate // [AgMsv_1.943]

mv-k06-v880.plain_english: Just as on a peacock’s feather colors like white, yellow, and red seem to open and close and shine, even though they are not truly fixed in that way, so appearances can manifest dynamically.
mv-k06-v880.sanskrit_cite:
yathā hi varhiṇaḥ patre sitapītāruṇādikam /
pronmiṣan nimiṣac cātra bhāsate 'py atathātmakam // [AgMsv_1.944]

mv-k06-v881.plain_english: In the same way, the lord of the wheel shines, full of subtle consciousness that is unopened and dissolved, and made variegated by the activities of closing and opening.

mv-k06-v882.plain_english: Therefore, through the closing of some and the opening of others, the wheel turns forth in forms ranging from one spoke to a thousand spokes.
mv-k06-v882.sanskrit_cite:
tat kasyāpi nimeṣeṇa kasyāpy unmeṣayogataḥ /
ekāracakrāt prabhṛti sahasrāraṃ vivartate // [AgMsv_1.946]

mv-k06-v883.plain_english: Is that wheel innumerable, or mutually nested within itself, or not a wheel at all—does one space alone expand?
mv-k06-v883.sanskrit_cite:
tad asaṃkhyānam atha vāpy anyonyāśritagarbhakam /
na vā tac cakram atha kiṃ vyomaivaikaṃ vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.947]

mv-k06-v884.plain_english: That too shines forth as containing infinite true wheels, or as containing infinite spaces, or it is called the one great space.
mv-k06-v884.sanskrit_cite:
tad apy anantasaccakragarbhaṃ vāpi vibhāsate /
anantavyomagarbhaṃ vā mahāvyomaikam ucyate // [AgMsv_1.948]

mv-k06-v885.plain_english: Just as one space gleams as white, blue, and red, and just as clouds appear in many ways, so the autonomous principle of consciousness vibrates forth in many ways through its own forms, beyond construction and enumeration—and yet those forms are not anything separate from it.
mv-k06-v885.sanskrit_cite:
yathā vyomaivaikaṃ kacati sitanīlāruṇatayā yathā caite meghāḥ punar atha tathā bhānti bahudhā /
tathā saṃvittattvaṃ kalanaparisaṃkhyāvirahitaiḥ svatantraṃ svākāraiḥ sphurati na ca te ke cana tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.949]

mv-k06-v886.plain_english: Thus my lord, seated in my heart, having himself realized this principle of varied form, described it as transmitted through the successive lineage of teachers.
mv-k06-v886.sanskrit_cite:
iti tattvam idaṃ nyarūpayan mama nātho hṛdayasthitaḥ svayam /
pratipadya vicitrarūpakam gurusaṃtānaparamparāyitam // [AgMsv_1.950]

mv-k06-v887.plain_english: For those who do not resort to the capacity to attain firm grounding in that doctrine, the Lord indeed spoke the construction of various maṇḍalas for their awakening.
mv-k06-v887.sanskrit_cite:
tad amutra naye na ye prarūḍhiṃ pratipattuṃ kṣamatām upāśrayante /
nanu tatpratibodhanāya devo vividhāṃ maṇḍalakalpanām avocat // [AgMsv_1.951]

mv-k06-v888.plain_english: Just as a child is trained in the set of letters by lines and conventional signs in due sequence, so one is engaged, through mudrās, maṇḍalas, mantras, and tantras, in one's own full and priceless abode.
mv-k06-v888.sanskrit_cite:
bālo yadvat rekhayā varṇajāte svaiḥ saṃketair yojyate tatkrameṇa /
tadvanmudrāmaṇḍalair mantratantraiḥ pūrṇe svasmin yojyate dhāmny anarghe // [AgMsv_1.952]

mv-k06-v889.plain_english: Here too something shines forth by that will alone as far or near, according to the gradation of those who take refuge; yet it remains untouched and established in the partless state. Thus the division belonging to the section on ritual action appears in many ways.
mv-k06-v889.sanskrit_cite:
atrāpi kiñcana vibhāti tadicchayaiva dūraṃ tathā savidham āśritatāratamyam /
asaṃspṛg apy atha niraṃśapadapratiṣṭham itthaṃ kriyāpaṭalago bahudhaiva bhedaḥ // [AgMsv_1.953]

mv-k06-v890.plain_english: Thus the principle that was described as participating in valid cognition is that goddess, supreme and non-supreme, who shines forth in various ways.
mv-k06-v890.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ pramāṇatābhāgi yat tattvaṃ hi nyarūpyata /
parāparā bhagavatī seyaṃ bhāti tathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.954]

mv-k06-v891.plain_english: Right here, the supreme part, the knower part, and again the known part—this was previously made clear by us.
mv-k06-v891.sanskrit_cite:
tad atraiva parāṃśo yaḥ sa mātraṃśo 'paraḥ punaḥ /
meyāṃśa iti tat pūrvam evāsmābhiḥ prakāśitam // [AgMsv_1.955]

mv-k06-v892.plain_english: Because the knower part is situated in many ways within the supreme part, it becomes predominant as supreme-and-non-supreme and takes the form of a lord of mantras.
mv-k06-v892.sanskrit_cite:
mātraṃśo 'pi pare bhāge bahudhā yat sthitas tataḥ /
parāparatayodriktaḥ paro mantreśarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.956]

mv-k06-v893.plain_english: But when the lower aspect predominates, it is called mantra; and the knower who is supreme-and-non-supreme, with the supreme-and-non-supreme balanced in predominance—
mv-k06-v893.sanskrit_cite:
udriktāparabhāvas tu mantra ity abhidhīyate /
parāparas tu yo mātā samudriktaparāparaḥ // [AgMsv_1.957]

mv-k06-v894.plain_english: He is declared the vijñānākala, with the supreme aspect awakened; through the predominance of the lower aspect, that same one is the pralayākala.
mv-k06-v894.sanskrit_cite:
sa vijñānākalaḥ proktaḥ prabuddhaparabhāvakaḥ /
aparodrekayogena sa eva pralayākalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.958]

mv-k06-v895.plain_english: The lower knower is indeed called the sakala. Yet even he has a manifold state, distinguished by divisions such as higher-lower and so on.
mv-k06-v895.sanskrit_cite:
aparaḥ kila yo mātā sakalaḥ sa tu bhāṣyate /
parāparādibhedena tasyāpi bahudhā sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.959]

mv-k06-v896.plain_english: When examined closely, this gives rise to countless divisions of knowers. But in terms of the main classification, only seven divisions of the knower are proclaimed.
mv-k06-v896.sanskrit_cite:
vicāryamāṇā niḥsaṃkhyān mātṛbhedāṃs tanoty alam /
mukhyatvena tu saptaiva mātṛbhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.960]

mv-k06-v897.plain_english: Their own powers fall within the sphere of the means of knowledge. We understand power to be precisely this fitness for activity.
mv-k06-v897.sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇāṃśe patanty eva teṣām eva svaśaktayaḥ /
vyāpārayogitaivaiṣā śaktitvam iti manmahe // [AgMsv_1.961]

mv-k06-v898.plain_english: For being active is itself being an instrument. In this way, from the distinctions between the possessor of power and the powers, the divisions of knower and means of knowledge arise.
mv-k06-v898.sanskrit_cite:
yac ca vyāpriyamāṇatvaṃ karaṇatvaṃ tad eva hi /
evaṃ ca śaktimacchakktibhedān mātṛpramāṇajāḥ // [AgMsv_1.962]

mv-k06-v899.plain_english: The object of knowledge is said to have a fourteen-fold nature. This is taught because knower, means of knowing, and knowable, though distinguished, are proclaimed as one.
mv-k06-v899.sanskrit_cite:
caturdaśasvarūpaṃ ca prameyam iti bhāṣyate /
mātā mānaṃ ca meyaṃ ca yata ekaṃ prakīrtitam // [AgMsv_1.963]

mv-k06-v900.plain_english: From that, the one reality is described as fifteen-fold, grouped in fives together with prakṛti. Even there, when divided one by one, each division takes on the nature of its own principle.
mv-k06-v900.sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ pañcadaśātmaikam ekaṃ prakṛtipañcitam /
tatrāpy ekaikaśo bhede nijatattvasvarūpiṇi // [AgMsv_1.964]

mv-k07-v901.plain_english: The boundless manifold of difference, treated in brief and in full, is set forth; and now, in due order, comes the reckoning of its divisions from water onward, from root to end.

mv-k07-v902.plain_english: Great is the upsurge of manifold variety born of difference and its subdivisions. Thus from earth to the end of the pradhāna-principle the course has been taught fifteenfold, and the sakala, whose nature spans from puruṣa to kalā, is neither knower nor means of knowledge.
mv-k07-v902.sanskrit_cite:
bhūyān bhedaprabhedottho vaicitryavisarodayaḥ

evaṃ dharātaḥ prabhṛti pradhānatattvāntam uktaṃ daśapañcadhaiva /
puṃsaḥ kalāntaṃ sakalaḥ svarūpabhūto na mātā na ca mānarūpaḥ // [AgMsv_1.966]

mv-k07-v903.plain_english: The thirteenfold nature is therefore established here: in the night-state the layākala keeps his own nature, in the middle the vijñānākala-nature, and in the domain of vidyā the mantra-become-nature.
mv-k07-v903.sanskrit_cite:
trayodaśātmatvam ato 'tra niṣṭhitaṃ niśi svarūpaṃ tu bhavel layākalaḥ /
madhye tu vijñānakalasvarūpatā vidyāpade mantragatasvarūpatā // [AgMsv_1.967]

mv-k07-v904.plain_english: In the Īśa domain abides the class of Mantreśas; now, in the most auspicious abode, devotion to that Lord — and each prior stage therein reveals its own order of knower and measure — so that, with no other knower, the self-luminous state of Śiva flashes forth ever one; yet from the Mantreśa-Īśas issue divisions numbered three, five, seven, nine, and three.
mv-k07-v904.sanskrit_cite:
aiśe mantreśavargasthitir atha suśive dhāmni tannāthaniṣṭhā pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ ca tatra prakaṭayati nijāṃ mātṛmānavyavasthām /
tenānanyapramātṛ sphurati śivapadaṃ svaprakāśaṃ sadaikaṃ mantreśeśānatas tu triśaramuninavatryakṣasaṃkhyāvibhedāḥ // [AgMsv_1.968]

mv-k07-v905.plain_english: And śakti, for our part, is undivided from the power-holder; thereby this separateness does not indeed amount to difference. Where knowerhood is absent, moreover, no śakti exists — so such a nature is not endowed with power.
mv-k07-v905.sanskrit_cite:
śaktiś ca no śaktimato vibhinnā tenaiti no bhedam iyaṃ pṛthaktvam /
amātṛtāyāṃ na ca śaktir asti tena svarūpaṃ na hi śaktiyuktam // [AgMsv_1.969]

mv-k07-v906.plain_english: Whatever light shines here without difference from the earth-principle — that itself is Lord Śiva: earth is brahman, the supreme.
mv-k07-v906.sanskrit_cite:
dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
sa eva śivanātho 'tra pṛthivī brahma tatparam // [AgMsv_1.970]

mv-k07-v907.plain_english: Those who, from Śivas will, impel the ones intent on bestowing the powers abiding in the earth-principle — they are the Mantramaheśvaras.
mv-k07-v907.sanskrit_cite:
dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīr vitarītuṃ samudyatān /
prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.971]

mv-k07-v908.plain_english: The Mantreśas, being impelled, and the mantras clearly declaring it, having cultivated through the Śiva-science the yoga that abides in the earth-principle.
mv-k07-v908.sanskrit_cite:
preryamāṇās tu mantreśā mantrās tadvācakāḥ sphuṭam /
dharātattvagataṃ yogam abhyasya śivavidyayā // [AgMsv_1.972]

mv-k07-v909.plain_english: But not like the dualists — Pāśava, Sāṃkhya, Vaiṣṇava and the rest — who, never attaining the firm abode, possess but vijñānākala-nature.

mv-k07-v910.plain_english: Those who, through enjoyment of just such principles, reached dissolution at the kalpas end — abiding as in deep sleep, they are here the pralayakevalas.
mv-k07-v910.sanskrit_cite:
tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ /
sauṣuptāvasthitau yadvat te 'tra pralayakevalāḥ // [AgMsv_1.974]

mv-k07-v911.plain_english: In deep sleep the dissolvedness in the principles is indeed plainly seen — for otherwise, whence this fixed conjunction with dreaming, just so?
mv-k07-v911.sanskrit_cite:
sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭam eva hi lakṣyate /
anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃsṛṣṭir iyatī kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.975]

mv-k07-v912.plain_english: Deep sleep too shines forth varied — pure and impure and the rest — since variety is seen in such memories as I-did-not-sleep and happily.
mv-k07-v912.sanskrit_cite:
sauṣuptam api citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate /
asvāpsaṃ sukham ityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.976]

mv-k07-v913.plain_english: Here the persons, whose massed malas mix with the upsurge of māyā and karma, climbing upon earth, are to be known as sakalas.
mv-k07-v913.sanskrit_cite:
māyākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ /
dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ // [AgMsv_1.977]

mv-k07-v914.plain_english: Whatever agitation there is in settling each ones own task within just this sevenfold order — that indeed is called the seven of the śaktis; and thence.
mv-k07-v914.sanskrit_cite:
asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane /
prakṣobho yas tad evoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.978]

mv-k07-v915.plain_english: Śiva is of unfallen consciousness-nature; but his three śaktis — they have, by force of autonomy, assumed the form of subject and object.
mv-k07-v915.sanskrit_cite:
śivo 'vicyutacidrūpas tisras tacchaktayas tu yāḥ /
tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītṛgrāhyarūpikāḥ // [AgMsv_1.979]

mv-k07-v916.plain_english: By excess of the subject-share, by upsurge of the object-share — seven and seven — yet one thing, merely inert, human-natured.
mv-k07-v916.sanskrit_cite:
grahītṛbhāgodrekeṇa grāhyabhāgocchalatvataḥ /
sapta sapteti yat tv ekaṃ jaḍamātraṃ narātmakam // [AgMsv_1.980]

mv-k07-v917.plain_english: Its nature is therefore settled threefold, per tattva; and in the ungraspable object — what? — the sixteen tuṭis are moments.
mv-k07-v917.sanskrit_cite:
tatsvarūpaṃ tatas traidhaṃ pratitattvaṃ vyavasthitam /
kiṃ cārthe khalu nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ // [AgMsv_1.981]

mv-k07-v918.plain_english: They are severally reckoned from the two-and-a-quarter-finger entrance; and therein the first is of the very taste of partless supreme nondualism.

mv-k07-v919.plain_english: The last, though, is not distinctly conceived apart from identity with object-nature; the penultimate is fully conceived as the grasper of its nature.
mv-k07-v919.sanskrit_cite:
antyas tu grāhyatādātmyān na pṛthak pravibhāvyate /
upāntyas tatsvarūpasya grāhakaḥ paribhāvvyate // [AgMsv_1.983]

mv-k07-v920.plain_english: And the first seven there has gone to imagelessness — skilled in covering the shade of the sequentially unfolding portions of imagining.
