mv-k07-v920.sanskrit_cite:
ādyaṃ ca saptakaṃ tatra nirvikalpakatāṃ gatam /
kramonmiṣadvikalpāṃśacchāyācchādanakovidam // [AgMsv_1.984]

mv-k07-v921.plain_english: For the wise know that very nature as Śiva consisting of supreme śakti; the second seven therein consists of the parāpara plane.
mv-k07-v921.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ /
dvitīyaṃ saptakaṃ tatra parāparapadātmakam // [AgMsv_1.985]

mv-k07-v922.plain_english: Sung as vikalpa — thus difference is made to appear; for that, in this subtle consciousness, they are intent on impelling.
mv-k07-v922.sanskrit_cite:
vikalpa iti saṃgītam iti bhedo 'vabhāsyate /
tad asyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ // [AgMsv_1.986]

mv-k07-v923.plain_english: Whatever form they experience — what is there in boastings about it? But what is held: even the tuṭis, in the lessening of difference that comes from sequence.
mv-k07-v923.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vā vikatthanaiḥ /
kramāt tu bhedanyūnatve tuṭīnām api yo mataḥ // [AgMsv_1.987]

mv-k07-v924.plain_english: The diminution of conceptualization is characterized by the absence of conceptualization, just as one afflicted by long suffering later attains a state of happiness.
mv-k07-v924.sanskrit_cite:
vikalpasya ca nirhrāso nirvikalpopalakṣaṇam /
yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścād āttasukhasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.988]

mv-k07-v925.plain_english: Just as someone who has found happiness forgets earlier suffering by resting in that happiness, so people who are firmly established in awareness, even when conceptual thought has gone, no longer cling to it.
mv-k07-v925.sanskrit_cite:
vismaraty eva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā /
tathā gatavikalpe 'pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ // [AgMsv_1.989]

mv-k07-v926.plain_english: People who rely on conceptual thinking do not lay claim to that deeper state; but when conceptualization dissolves, awareness becomes free of thought and ultimately true, and its own nature shines forth. In this way, clear understanding arises for those who attend to it with effort.
mv-k07-v926.sanskrit_cite:
vikalpaviśrāntibalāt tāṃ vṛttiṃ nābhimanvate /

vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā /
saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvam itthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.990]

mv-k07-v927.plain_english: This attentiveness is said to occur in the relation between the grasped, the grasper, and their awareness, because in that context it is connected with the attainment of the desired result.
mv-k07-v927.sanskrit_cite:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā /
iyaṃ sā bhaṇyate tatra yatheṣṭaphalayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.991]

mv-k07-v928.plain_english: For this very reason, because of the abundance of its divisions, the worlds too become variegated; and no transgression of this explanation is accepted.
mv-k07-v928.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva hi tadbhedabāhulyād bhuvanāny api /
vicitratvaṃ prayāntīti na cātikrama iṣyate // [AgMsv_1.992]

mv-k07-v929.plain_english: This reality appears both with sequence and without sequence; but since time has already been refuted, and since the ultimate reality of space cannot be established by reasoning, neither can be taken as ultimately real.
mv-k07-v929.sanskrit_cite:
sakramākramam evedaṃ kālasya prākpradūsaṇāt /
diśaś ca paramārthatvaṃ naiva yuktyopapadyate // [AgMsv_1.993]

mv-k07-v930.plain_english: For no single thing produces the cognition of before and after, and difference based on limiting conditions is not itself a real entity; so how could that cognition be postulated as ultimately grounded?
mv-k07-v930.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvāparapratītiṃ hi naikā sā kurute tathā /
upādhibhedo no vastu tat kathaṃ sā prakalpyatām // [AgMsv_1.994]

mv-k07-v931.plain_english: The supreme Lord, who fashions the sphere of space and time out of his own bliss, declared the basis on which one thing is said to be superior to another by its qualities.
mv-k07-v931.sanskrit_cite:
yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭa ity ataḥ parameśvaraḥ /
abhāṣata nijānandakḷptadikkālamaṇḍalaḥ // [AgMsv_1.995]

mv-k07-v932.plain_english: Thus, for those who wish to enter into this variegated nature of reality, a threefold division of absorptions has been described, because the means differ.
mv-k07-v932.sanskrit_cite:
tad evaṃ tattvarūpe 'smin vicitre pravivikṣatām /
upāyabhedāt traividhyaṃ samāveśeṣu varṇitam // [AgMsv_1.996]

mv-k07-v933.plain_english: The Śāmbhava means is without method; next comes the means based on consciousness; and the Āṇava means, based on the inert, is also regarded as taking many forms.
mv-k07-v933.sanskrit_cite:
anupāyaḥ śāṃbhavo 'sau cidupāyas tataḥ param /
jaḍopāyas tv āṇavaḥ syāt sa cāpi bahudhā mataḥ // [AgMsv_1.997]

mv-k07-v934.plain_english: Even within what is non-inert, an appearance of inertness arises through the power of the supreme Lord, as in the channels, senses, and external supports; therefore these can still function as a means grounded in consciousness.
mv-k07-v934.sanskrit_cite:
ajaḍe 'pi jaḍābhāsaḥ pārameśvaryayogataḥ /
nāḍīkaraṇabāhyādes tena saṃvidupāyatā // [AgMsv_1.998]

mv-k07-v935.plain_english: When experience rests on the functioning of the senses and there is a grasping of external forms, that clear and repeatedly continuous condition is the waking state.
mv-k07-v935.sanskrit_cite:
tatrākṣavṛttim āśritya bāhyākāragraho hi yaḥ /
tajjāgratsphuṭam āsīnam anubandhi punaḥ punaḥ // [AgMsv_1.999]

mv-k07-v936.plain_english: Dream is a construction made by one's own imagination and is the reverse of waking; and the experience belonging to the layākala arises under the force of karma tending toward dissolution, but not in a stable way.
mv-k07-v936.sanskrit_cite:
ātmasaṃkalpanirmāṇaṃ svapno jāgradviparyayaḥ /
layākalasya yo bhogaḥ layakarmavaśān na tu // [AgMsv_1.1000]

mv-k07-v937.plain_english: That experience would not be stable, because there is no night-like obscuration; deep sleep is the non-awareness of pleasure and so on. For the jñānākala, due to mere impurity, there is only bare experience.
mv-k07-v937.sanskrit_cite:
sthiro bhaven niśābhāvāt suptaṃ saukhyādyavedane /
jñānākalasya malataḥ kevalād bhogamātrataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1001]

mv-k07-v938.plain_english: Inert and non-inert things appear as inherently distinct and differentiated; yet in the fourth state there abide the three groups: the mantra beings, their lords, and the overlords.
mv-k07-v938.sanskrit_cite:
bhedavantaḥ svato bhinnāś cikīrṣyante jaḍājaḍāḥ /
turye tatra sthitā mantratannāthādhīśvarās trayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1002]

mv-k07-v939.plain_english: To the extent that entities become capable of receiving a share of Bhairava-awareness, their own separate essence melts away and they become non-different by themselves.
mv-k07-v939.sanskrit_cite:
yāvad bhairavabodhāṃśapraveśanasahiṣṇavaḥ /
bhāvā vigaladātmīyasārāḥ svayam abhedinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1003]

mv-k07-v940.plain_english: They would abide in the state beyond the fourth. In this fifteenfold scheme, whatever form appears clear and distinct should be regarded as the waking state.
mv-k07-v940.sanskrit_cite:
turyātītapade saṃsyur iti pañcadaśātmake /
yasya yad yad sphuṭaṃ rūpaṃ taj jāgrad iti manyatām // [AgMsv_1.1004]

mv-k07-v941.plain_english: That same form, when it appears unstable, is dream of that kind; but when it appears unclear, that is deep sleep, including what appears before it.
mv-k07-v941.sanskrit_cite:
tad evāsthiram ābhāti svarūpaṃ svapna īdṛśaḥ /
asphuṭaṃ tu yad ābhāti suptaṃ tat tat puro 'pi yat // [AgMsv_1.1005]

mv-k07-v942.plain_english: The continuity by which the three states arise and are held together, like the thread in a garland, should be understood as the fourth state present through all differences.
mv-k07-v942.sanskrit_cite:
tritayasyānusaṃdhis tu yadvaśād upajāyate /
sraksūtratulyaṃ tatturyaṃ sarvabhedeṣu gṛhyatām // [AgMsv_1.1006]

mv-k07-v943.plain_english: But that which shines with the fullness of nonduality and melts away all distinctions is declared to be the state beyond the fourth; one should apply this understanding everywhere.
mv-k07-v943.sanskrit_cite:
yat tv advaitabharollāsi drāvitāśeṣabhedakam /
turyātītaṃ tu tat prāhur itthaṃ sarvatra yojayet // [AgMsv_1.1007]

mv-k07-v944.plain_english: For the layākala, its own form is waking, and the prior states are counted as dream and so on; the wise person should trace this whole sequence in every case.
mv-k07-v944.sanskrit_cite:
layākale hi svaṃ rūpaṃ jāgrattatpūrvavṛtti tu /
svapnādīti kramaṃ sarvaṃ sarvatrānusared budhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1008]

mv-k07-v945.plain_english: Even within the one full Lord, consciousness is said to be the state beyond the fourth, bliss is the fourth, and will itself is the seed-ground corresponding to deep sleep.
mv-k07-v945.sanskrit_cite:
ekatrāpi prabhau pūrṇe citturyātītam ucyate /
ānandas turyam icchaiva bījabhūmiḥ suṣuptatā // [AgMsv_1.1009]

mv-k07-v946.plain_english: Knowledge corresponds to the dream state, and action is remembered as the waking state; in this same context arise the yogic designations beginning with piṇḍastha.
mv-k07-v946.sanskrit_cite:
jñānaṃ tu svapnavṛttitvaṃ kriyā jāgrad iti smṛtā /
atraiva yogabhūmyutthāḥ saṃjñāḥ piṇḍasthatādayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1010]

mv-k07-v947.plain_english: Classifications such as sarvatobhadra are constructed by those who rely on discriminative analysis; because the fourfold structure is present in each case, further elaborations arise in the expanded scheme.
mv-k07-v947.sanskrit_cite:
sarvatobhadratādyās tu prasaṃkhyājñāninirmitāḥ /
ekaikatra catūrūpasadbhāvād vitate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1011]

mv-k07-v948.plain_english: In one place there is fourfoldness, then threefoldness, then oneness; yet the one Lord Bhairava remains, with all universal forms flashing forth within him.
mv-k07-v948.sanskrit_cite:
catūrūpatvam ekatra tritvaṃ paścād athaikatā /
ekas tu bhairavo nāthaḥ prollasadviśvarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1012]

mv-k07-v949.plain_english: The one reality, present in every state from Śiva to the limited individual, is this entire path itself, abiding in non-difference from Bhairava.
mv-k07-v949.sanskrit_cite:
ekaḥ śivādisakalaparyantasthitisaṃgataḥ /
so 'yaṃ samasta evādhvā bhairavābhedavṛttimān // [AgMsv_1.1013]

mv-k07-v950.plain_english: By its own freedom, that same reality shines forth as autonomous; when it abides in the form of the knowing subject, it is recognized as the path of mantras.
mv-k07-v950.sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryāt svatantratvam aśnuvāno 'vabhāsate /
so 'yaṃ mātṛsvarūpastho mantrādhveti vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_1.1014]

mv-k07-v951.plain_english: In the form of valid cognition, this reality is called the path of phonemes; when it takes the form of the means of knowledge, it becomes the path of words.
mv-k07-v951.sanskrit_cite:
pramārūpatayā so 'yaṃ varṇādhveti nirucyate /
pramāṇarūpatām etya prayāty eṣa padādhvatām // [AgMsv_1.1015]

mv-k07-v952.plain_english: Without abandoning its role as the means of knowledge, it moves toward objecthood through conceptualization; joined with the knower, it becomes the path of limited powers.
mv-k07-v952.sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇarūpatāveśam aparityajya meyatām /
gacchan saṃkalpanayogāt kalādhvā mātṛsaṃgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1016]

mv-k07-v953.plain_english: When it is purely connected with objecthood, it should be understood as the path of principles; when it serves as the support of that grossness, it is described as the path of worlds.
mv-k07-v953.sanskrit_cite:
śuddhe prameyatāyoge sa tattvādhveti gṛhyatām /
tatsthaulyādhāratāyogād bhuvanādhveti varṇitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1017]

mv-k07-v954.plain_english: For when the state of what can be expressed is swallowed by the reflective awareness of consciousness, it becomes intent on cognition and protection grounded in Śiva's knowledge and action.
mv-k07-v954.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā /
śivajñānakriyāyattamananatrāṇatatparā // [AgMsv_1.1018]

mv-k07-v955.plain_english: From its skill in the eager play of all its powers, the mantra path, whose nature is Śiva, first arises swiftly and with force.
mv-k07-v955.sanskrit_cite:
aśeṣaśaktipaṭalīlīlālāmpaṭyapāṭavāt /
mantrādhvā rabhasena drāk prāg udbhūtaḥ śivātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1019]

mv-k07-v956.plain_english: For the one who relishes repose in surging consciousness alone, the powers are unrestricted because of the capacity to name everything.

mv-k07-v957.plain_english: The powers are emanated with operations ranging from meanings that arise with the self down to the earth, encompassing all those objects within the play of consciousness in their own self.
mv-k07-v957.sanskrit_cite:
sṛṣṭāḥ svātmasahotthārthadharāparyantavṛttayaḥ /
svātmīye cidvilasite tāvato 'rthān nijātmani // [AgMsv_1.1021]

mv-k07-v958.plain_english: Infants and even animal knowers, who have no share in linguistic convention, still apprehend things and bear a real consciousness in the form of valid cognition.
mv-k07-v958.sanskrit_cite:
āmṛśantaḥ pramārūpāṃ satyāṃ bibhrati saṃvidam /
bālās tiryakpramātāro ye 'py asaṃketabhāginaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1022]

mv-k07-v959.plain_english: Even they, relying on this own consciousness of theirs—whose essence is an uncontrived impression and which is both differentiated and undifferentiated—attain a varied state of being knowers.
mv-k07-v959.sanskrit_cite:
te 'py akṛtrimasaṃskārasārām enāṃ svasaṃvidam /
bhinnabhinnām upāśritya yānti citrāṃ pramātṛtām // [AgMsv_1.1023]

mv-k07-v960.plain_english: If linguistic conventions become firmly established in this uncontrived consciousness of infinite phonemes, then even they come to operate in a non-conventional way.
mv-k07-v960.sanskrit_cite:
asyām akṛtrimānantavarṇasaṃvidi rūḍhatām /
saṃketā yānti cet te 'pi yānty asaṃketavṛttitām // [AgMsv_1.1024]

mv-k07-v961.plain_english: But without this innate consciousness, all the many conventions that are made could never find rest in the mind, because they would depend on yet other conventions.
mv-k07-v961.sanskrit_cite:
anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ /
naiva cetasi viśrāntiṃ saṃketāntarayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1025]

mv-k07-v962.plain_english: They would never find rest, because of infinite regress and because that would destroy the very root; so how, indeed, could a child even be instructed in a convention?
mv-k07-v962.sanskrit_cite:
vrajeyur anavasthānān mūlakṣatikaratvataḥ /
tatrāpi khalu saṃkete bālo vyutpādyatāṃ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1026]

mv-k07-v963.plain_english: Therefore, this infinite, non-māyic collection of phonemes, accompanied by the reflective awareness of consciousness, is always unfolding.
mv-k07-v963.sanskrit_cite:
tenānantas tv amāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ /
sa cidvimarśasacivaḥ sadaiva pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.1027]

mv-k07-v964.plain_english: And from that very source the māyic phonemes came into being; it is understood that those non-māyic phonemes are indeed their power.
mv-k07-v964.sanskrit_cite:
tata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire /
teṣāṃ te khalv amāyīyā vīryam ity avadhāryate // [AgMsv_1.1028]

mv-k07-v965.plain_english: For when others' utterances are heard, if one's own cognition remains veiled, that dull person does not become a knowing subject with respect to that meaning.
mv-k07-v965.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣv āvṛṇute nijā /
pramā yasya jaḍo nāsau tatrārthe yāti mātṛtām // [AgMsv_1.1029]

mv-k07-v966.plain_english: But if one's own cognition, bearing differentiation within it, enters into awareness within one's own mass of māyic phonemes, that person attains the state of being a knower.
mv-k07-v966.sanskrit_cite:
yasya tu svapramā bodhe praviśed bhedagarbhagā /
māyīyavarṇapuñje sve sa pramātṛtvam ṛcchati // [AgMsv_1.1030]

mv-k07-v967.plain_english: To the extent that the uncreated, innate form predominates, to that same extent a gradation of aesthetic wonder is produced.
mv-k07-v967.sanskrit_cite:
yathā yathā cākṛtakaṃ tadrūpam atiricyate /
tathā tathā camatkāratāratamyaṃ prakalpyate // [AgMsv_1.1031]

mv-k07-v968.plain_english: But when that surge becomes great, those established in the nature of intuitive insight certainly attain, in every way, excellence in poetry and eloquence.
mv-k07-v968.sanskrit_cite:
tadudrekamahattve tu pratibhātmani niṣṭhitāḥ /
dhruvaṃ kavitvavaktṛtvaśālitāṃ yānti sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1032]

mv-k07-v969.plain_english: Therefore, in the perfection of speech, the phonemes are contemplated; for that very reason they are kept secret and spoken only by one who maintains secrecy.
mv-k07-v969.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā /
teṣām eva tatas tena guptā guptena bhāṣitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1033]

mv-k07-v970.plain_english: Then, insofar as there is the Lord's constant repose, it projects many phonemes at once, well established in fulfilling the portions of experience.
mv-k07-v970.sanskrit_cite:
tato yāvadvibhoḥ śaśvadviśrāntir yugapadbahūn /
varṇān udṛṅkya bhogāṃśaparipūraṇasusthitān // [AgMsv_1.1034]

mv-k07-v971.plain_english: To that extent, this path of words, resting on the level of the object, becomes the first sprout within the mass of conventions bound up with worldly existence.
mv-k07-v971.sanskrit_cite:
tāvad eva padādhvāsau meyabhūmim upāśritaḥ /
saṃsāramṛtasaṃketasaṃghāte prathamāṅkuraḥ // [AgMsv_1.1035]

mv-k07-v972.plain_english: Thus it is ascertained that objecthood, the state of being the knower, and the state of being the means of knowledge all belong to the thirty-sixfold collection of principles.
mv-k07-v972.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ prameyatā mātṛbhāvo mānatvam apy atha /
ṣaṭtriṃśadātmanas tattvakalāpasyeti niścitam // [AgMsv_1.1036]

mv-k07-v973.plain_english: There, all this shines forth in the unchanging supreme Lord in the form of a reflection, and not as something external.
mv-k07-v973.sanskrit_cite:
tatra sarvaṃ vibhāty etat parameśitari dhruve /
pratibimbasvarūpeṇa na tu bāhyatayā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1037]

mv-k07-v974.plain_english: In the sky of consciousness, in Śiva alone, such divided cognitions of various bodies appear to worldly beings, just as a snake and the like appear in a rope.
mv-k07-v974.sanskrit_cite:
cidvyomny eva śive tattaddehādimatir īdṛśī /
bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ bhāti rajjau sarpādikā yathā // [AgMsv_1.1038]

mv-k07-v975.plain_english: Because the settled view before the body's death belongs to the realm of dream, what kind of other body or bodily arising after death could there really be?
mv-k07-v975.sanskrit_cite:
yataḥ prāgdehamaraṇasiddhāntaḥ svapnagocaraḥ /
dehāntarādir maraṇāt kīdṛg vā dehasaṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1039]

mv-k07-v976.plain_english: In a dream, particular details appear by the force of the unfolding of mere appearance, but they are not produced as independent realities in that way.
mv-k07-v976.sanskrit_cite:
svapne tu pratibhāmātrasāmānyaprathanād balāt /
viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante 'pi te tathā // [AgMsv_1.1040]

mv-k07-v977.plain_english: Just as some śālagrāma stones contain varied forms within them, so the inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward belong to the variegated heart of consciousness.
mv-k07-v977.sanskrit_cite:
sāligrāmopalāḥ kecic citrākṛtihṛdo yathā /
tathā māyādibhūmyantalekhāś citrahṛdayaś citaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1041]

mv-k07-v978.plain_english: Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like follow that will; they are not by themselves entities that independently function as existent or nonexistent causes and effects.

mv-k07-v979.plain_english: Whether by cutting off or setting in motion a long-established rule, or even where no rule has yet taken root, this Bhairava of the sky of consciousness remains independent.
mv-k07-v979.sanskrit_cite:
ciraprarūḍhe niyame samucchedāt pravartanāt /
arūḍhe 'pi svatantro 'yaṃ sthitaś cidvyomabhairavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1043]

mv-k07-v980.plain_english: In that state which shares nondifference with Bhairava, full of one consciousness alone, the absence of the recognition 'I am thus' is what differentiates the realm of beings.
mv-k07-v980.sanskrit_cite:
ekacinmātrasaṃpūrṇabhairavābhedabhāgini /
evam asmīty anāmarśo bhedako bhāvamaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.1044]

mv-k07-v981.plain_english: Just as no other agent is established in a dream by any means of knowledge, so too the creation should be understood as belonging to one's own independent awareness.
mv-k07-v981.sanskrit_cite:
sarvapramāṇair no siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā /
svasaṃvidaḥ svatantrāyās tathā sargo 'pi budhyatām // [AgMsv_1.1045]

mv-k07-v982.plain_english: One who plays in the mind's variegated city and garden knows: 'I alone abide as all these beings that have come to be, and they are nothing but consciousness.'
mv-k07-v982.sanskrit_cite:
cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍann evaṃ hi vetti yaḥ /
aham eva sthito bhāvair bhūtaiś cinmātrakair iti // [AgMsv_1.1046]

mv-k07-v983.plain_english: The varied experiences of 'I am born' and 'I am dead' appear in the unborn and deathless, on the wall of the mind, as projections of one's own imagination.
mv-k07-v983.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ jāto mṛto 'smīti janmamṛtyuvicitratāḥ /
ajanmany amṛtau bhānti cittabhittau svakalpināḥ // [AgMsv_1.1047]

mv-k07-v984.plain_english: Being this world or another world is only a matter of awareness; even amid apparent divisions of time, part, awareness, and place, it remains undivided.

mv-k07-v985.plain_english: If this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness, then no one could perceive even a single mountain from within it.
mv-k07-v985.sanskrit_cite:
abhaviṣyad ayaṃ sargo mūrtaś cen na tu cinmayaḥ /
tad avekṣyata tanmadhyāt kenaiko 'pi dharādharaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1049]

mv-k07-v986.plain_english: When one examines the elements, subtle elements, and the rest in terms of support and what is supported, in the end it is the consciousness-power, identical with Śiva's own nature, that upholds them.
mv-k07-v986.sanskrit_cite:
bhūtatanmātravargāder ādhārādheyacarcane /
ante saṃvinmayī śaktiḥ śivarūpaiva dhāriṇī // [AgMsv_1.1050]

mv-k07-v987.plain_english: Therefore cognition itself is the agent; that manifestation is Śiva in his own self. For that reason, this power is called the common ground.
mv-k07-v987.sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt pratītir evetthaṃ kartrī sā pratibhā śivaḥ /
atra svātmani te tena śaktiḥ sādhārasaṃjñitā // [AgMsv_1.1051]

mv-k07-v988.plain_english: Even what is imagined and seems without support does not fall away, because the universe rests in its own supporting power; reflect on it in this way.
mv-k07-v988.sanskrit_cite:
sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāram api naiva pataty adhaḥ /
svādhāraśaktau viśrānter viśvam itthaṃ vimṛśyatām // [AgMsv_1.1052]

mv-k07-v989.plain_english: From the fixation of the dense 'I' and so on arises the state beginning with earth, until at last the recognition 'I am consciousness' is fulfilled as the identity of Bhairava.
mv-k07-v989.sanskrit_cite:
asyā ghanāham ityādirūḍher eva dharāditā /
yāvad ante cidasmīti nirvṛttā bhairavātmatā // [AgMsv_1.1053]

mv-k07-v990.plain_english: Like blue and other colors in a jewel or in a rainbow's light, so appearances are in Śiva; but in ultimate truth they have no real arising or passing away.
mv-k07-v990.sanskrit_cite:
maṇāv indrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive /
paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayavyayayogitā // [AgMsv_1.1054]

mv-k07-v991.plain_english: To say that creation happens in space or in time is incoherent, for the creation of the conscious Lord includes space and time as well.
mv-k07-v991.sanskrit_cite:
deśe kāle 'tra vā sṛṣṭir ity etad asamañjasam /
cidātmano hi devasya sṛṣṭir dikkālayor api // [AgMsv_1.1055]

mv-k07-v992.plain_english: Within what is taken as waking, in a span of three and a half cubits and a single watch of time, separate dreams arise with their own varied measures of space and time.
mv-k07-v992.sanskrit_cite:
jāgarābhimate sārdhahastatritayagocare /
prahare ca pṛthaksvapnāś citradikkālamāninaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1056]

mv-k07-v993.plain_english: Therefore we do not regard a moment as anything fixed, for even within a single moment of action there are many swift actions.
mv-k07-v993.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcid api manmahe /
kriyākṣaṇe 'pi hy ekasmin bahvyaḥ santi drutāḥ kriyāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1057]

mv-k07-v994.plain_english: Therefore those who hold that the contraction of beings ends in a moment surely rely, through this narrow channel, on a view grounded in emptiness.
mv-k07-v994.sanskrit_cite:
tena ye bhāvasaṃkocaṃ kṣaṇāntaṃ pratipedire /
te nūnam anayā nālyā śūnyadṛṣṭyavalambinaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1058]

mv-k07-v995.plain_english: Therefore the one who, by his independence, is able to make existent beings appear empty and likewise make the nonexistent appear clearly is the supreme Lord.
mv-k07-v995.sanskrit_cite:
tad ya eva sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkatuṃ tahtāsataḥ /
sphuṭīkartuṃ svatantratvād īśaḥ sa parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.1059]

mv-k07-v996.plain_english: Thus the supreme Lord is proclaimed as having the universe as his form; no separate entity such as earth or the rest can be established as independently real in that way.
mv-k07-v996.sanskrit_cite:
tad itthaṃ parameśāno viśvarūpaḥ pragīyate /
na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāder upapannatā // [AgMsv_1.1060]

mv-k07-v997.plain_english: This has already been said before, so it is not examined again in detail; many refutations of external objects have already been composed.
mv-k07-v997.sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ caitat puraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate /
bahubhiś cāpi bāhyārthadūṣaṇā pravyaracyata // [AgMsv_1.1061]

mv-k07-v998.plain_english: But if things are so, how can karma be connected with its fruit in birth and death? Has the previously stated freedom of consciousness been completely forgotten?
mv-k07-v998.sanskrit_cite:
nanv itthaṃ janmamaraṇe karmaṇaḥ phalayogitā /
kathaṃ syāt kin nu pūrvoktaṃ citsvātantryaṃ suvisṛmtam // [AgMsv_1.1062]

mv-k07-v999.plain_english: For this free consciousness makes things shine forth just as it wills, and so they truly appear; it contains all forms within itself, and this is firmly established.
mv-k07-v999.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi citsvatantreyaṃ yathā bhāsayate tathā /
satyaṃ bhāty akhilākāragarbhā sā ceti niścitam // [AgMsv_1.1063]

mv-k07-v1000.plain_english: Just as sweetness is present in every atom of sugarcane in every way, so in each ultimate atom there abides a state consisting of the whole creation.
mv-k07-v1000.sanskrit_cite:
ikṣau pratyaṇu mādhuryaṃ yathā sarvātmanā tathā /
pratyekaparamāṇau hi sarvasṛṣṭimayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1064]

mv-k07-v1001.plain_english: But those learned people who do not know the root principle and dispute this are surely engaged only in protecting their own fantasy-kingdom.
mv-k07-v1001.sanskrit_cite:
ajñātatattvamūlās tu vivadante 'tra ye budhāḥ /
nūnaṃ nijamanorājyarakṣāyai te samudyatāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1065]

mv-k07-v1002.plain_english: The idea that this is located in breath, in space, in consciousness, in the external world, or anywhere at all is a delusion, arising from ignorance and swollen by the seeming absence of freedom produced by restriction.
mv-k07-v1002.sanskrit_cite:
prāṇe khe citi bāhye vā kutrāpīdam iti bhramaḥ /
ajñatvāt tanniyatyutthasvātantryābhāvajṛmbhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1066]

mv-k07-v1003.plain_english: Therefore, the awareness of one's own consciousness appears here as birth; but beforehand consciousness does not appear in a form suited to its freedom.
mv-k07-v1003.sanskrit_cite:
ataḥ svasaṃvidāmarśo janmatveneha bhāsate /
purastāt tu na saṃvittiḥ svātantryocitarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.1067]

mv-k07-v1004.plain_english: Here the former consciousness is called previous karma; therefore, a consciousness that obstructs that former consciousness brings about the destruction of karma.
mv-k07-v1004.sanskrit_cite:
prāktanī saṃvid eveha pūrvakarmeti bhāṣyate /
tatsaṃvidbādhikā saṃvitkarmakṣayakarī tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1068]

mv-k07-v1005.plain_english: Just as in a dream something not actually done can flash forth as 'done by me' and be seen to give fruit, the same is true of karma in the waking state.
mv-k07-v1005.sanskrit_cite:
akṛtaṃ ca yathā svapne mayā kṛtam iti sphuret /
phaladā dṛśyate saiva vārtā jāgrati karmaṇaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1069]

mv-k07-v1006.plain_english: And so, if even a single higher consciousness arises in someone, consisting in the burning up of the fruit of the mass of past karma, that person does not undergo that fruit.
mv-k07-v1006.sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca prācyakarmaughaphalasaṃploṣaṇātmikā /
yasyaikāpy uttarodeti saṃvit sa phalabhāṅ na hi // [AgMsv_1.1070]

mv-k07-v1007.plain_english: Moreover, through the clear flashing forth of many consciousnesses, even disrepute can become repute, bearing abundant fruit like a seed watered by the waters of a river in the sky.

mv-k07-v1008.plain_english: Thus karma that flashes forth in slight awareness yields little fruit, while what does not flash forth is indeed fruitless; this is the principle with regard to one's own consciousness.
mv-k07-v1008.sanskrit_cite:
evam alpaphalaṃ karma svalpasaṃvedane sphurat /
asphuran niṣphalaṃ tv eva nyāyaḥ so 'yaṃ svasaṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.1072]

mv-k07-v1009.plain_english: Even there, the smallness or greatness conceived among consciousnesses belongs to the doer of karma and takes that form according to how firmly it is established in consciousness.
mv-k07-v1009.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpy alpatvabhūyastve saṃvidāṃ ye prakalpite /
te karmakartuḥ saṃvittirūḍhyā tadrūpabhāginī // [AgMsv_1.1073]

mv-k07-v1010.plain_english: And if a consciousness does not arise by itself as pregnant with such a fruit, nor does so through association with a subject grasping another fruit, then that fruit does not arise in that way.
mv-k07-v1010.sanskrit_cite:
yā ca (yasya) saṃvit svayaṃ tādṛkphalagarbhā na jāyate /
nāpy anyaphalanirgrāhimātṛsaṃgatitas tathā // [AgMsv_1.1074]

mv-k07-v1011.plain_english: Even in the consciousness of another subject who knows the fruit, who could, to the very end, be capable of determining it through the intention of a different subject?
mv-k07-v1011.sanskrit_cite:
phalaveditur anyasya pramātur api saṃvidi /
anyapramātṛsaṃkalpād yāvadante sa ko 'py alam // [AgMsv_1.1075]

mv-k07-v1012.plain_english: The awakened one, unfolding the power of maintenance in creation, contracts the constructions that are based on grasping at fruit.
mv-k07-v1012.sanskrit_cite:
prabuddhaḥ sṛṣṭir akṣāyai sthitiśaktivijṛmbhakaḥ /
vidāḥ sma saṃkocayati phalālambanakalpanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1076]

mv-k07-v1013.plain_english: With the understanding that this creation is seen from a vision beyond the fish-like standpoint, the ancients taught that one should help others.
mv-k07-v1013.sanskrit_cite:
matsyād amatsyadṛṣṭyeyaṃ sṛṣṭir ity āśayena te /
paropakāraṃ kartavyam upādikṣan purātanāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1077]

mv-k07-v1014.plain_english: Thus this help is extended even to the dead: through offerings such as rice-balls, union with a body is given again.
mv-k07-v1014.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ nāmopakāro 'yaṃ mṛtasyāpi pratanyate /
piṇḍadānādinā bhūyo dīyate dehasaṃgamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1078]

mv-k07-v1015.plain_english: It is conceived that the fruit of this difficult austerity is the thought: better that afflictions fall upon oneself, but may they not harm others.
mv-k07-v1015.sanskrit_cite:
varaṃ svātmani saṃkleśāḥ paraṃ mā pīḍayan tv iti /
iti kalpitam etasya kṛcchrādes tapasaḥ phalam // [AgMsv_1.1079]

mv-k07-v1016.plain_english: The uneatability of garlic and such things is stated as a command of this kind; people are to accept it, indeed, as without further reason.
mv-k07-v1016.sanskrit_cite:
laśunādāvabhakṣyatvam uktam ājñeya īdṛśī /
akāraṇakam eveti gṛhṇantu kila jantavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1080]

mv-k07-v1017.plain_english: Therefore, in determining what is eatable or uneatable in cases like swans and other birds, a difference of understanding is fitting; otherwise, it would not be so at all.
mv-k07-v1017.sanskrit_cite:
tad evaṃ haṃsapakṣyādibhakṣyābhakṣyatvanirṇaye /
yujyeta bhinnabuddhitvam anyathā nna kathaṃ cana // [AgMsv_1.1081]

mv-k07-v1018.plain_english: Thus, in both the seen and the unseen, the connection with fruit, arranged through conceived divisions and sequences, is now firmly established on the ground of consciousness.
mv-k07-v1018.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ dṛṣṭe 'py adṛṣṭe 'tha kalpitāṃśāṃśikākramāt /
phalayogaḥ sa evādya rūḍhaḥ saṃvidbhuvi sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1082]

mv-k07-v1019.plain_english: Is the settled view that a body in the other world comes from the rice-ball offering and not otherwise, implying that embodied beings have no mutual connection apart from that?
mv-k07-v1019.sanskrit_cite:
dehaḥ piṇḍāt pare loke nānyatheti sthitiḥ kṛtā /
anyonyānanuṣaktatvaṃ jantūnāṃ dehabhṛd iti ? // [AgMsv_1.1083]

mv-k07-v1020.plain_english: And by all those masses of scriptures, stakes of doubt were planted; rooted in the ground of ignorant minds, they grew into fixed conclusions about karmic fruit.
mv-k07-v1020.sanskrit_cite:
tatsarvaśāstrapūgaiś ca śaṅkāśaṅkuḥ praropitāḥ /
ajñacittadharārūḍhaḥ phalaparyantatāṃ gataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1084]

mv-k07-v1021.plain_english: One thinks, 'Today I have someone to offer me rice-balls; through that offering I enjoy my limbs again, and I am whole and well-established.'
mv-k07-v1021.sanskrit_cite:
asti me piṇḍado 'dyāhaṃ piṇḍadānakkramāt tathā /
prapnobh/m(?)yavayavābhogaṃ pūrṇadeho 'smi susthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1085]

mv-k07-v1022.plain_english: Through unseen rites arranged by a son, disciple, oneself, or others, one imagines having a share in heaven, fully enjoying it and firmly settled there.

mv-k07-v1023.plain_english: One thinks, 'I have no one to offer me rice-balls, I myself have done great wrong, there is no savior for me anywhere, and I am falling into the ocean of hell.'
mv-k07-v1023.sanskrit_cite:
nāsti me piṇḍadaḥ kaś cit svayaṃ cāsmy atiduṣkṛtī /
na me trātāsti kutrāpi patāmi narakārṇave // [AgMsv_1.1087]

mv-k07-v1024.plain_english: Thoughts like 'Somehow, sometime, I will have a savior' are expansions of awareness, and they bear fruit in just that form by themselves.
mv-k07-v1024.sanskrit_cite:
bhaviṣyati mama trātā kvāpi kāle kathaṃ cana /
ityādiḥ saṃvidāṃ sphāras tathaiva phalati svayam // [AgMsv_1.1088]

mv-k07-v1025.plain_english: Even if there is no actual person performing the rice-ball rites, one experiences the result exactly as it appears in awareness, fashioned by one's own resolve.
mv-k07-v1025.sanskrit_cite:
tasyās tu piṇḍakartrādir mābhūd atha yathā sphuret /
sa tāvat tatphalaṃ bhuṅkte svasaṃkalpena kalpitam // [AgMsv_1.1089]

mv-k07-v1026.plain_english: This belief, tightly sealed within by the diamond-hard plaster of doubt, is burned away root and all in an instant by the fire of Bhairava alone.
mv-k07-v1026.sanskrit_cite:
śaṅkāvajrapralepāntardṛḍhabaddhāṃ tv imāṃ matim /
bhairavānala evaikaḥ samūlaṃ pluṣyati kṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.1090]

mv-k07-v1027.plain_english: The fire that burns up the whole dream-house of the world, contained in all varied consciousness, is the flashing realization, 'I alone am Śiva.'
mv-k07-v1027.sanskrit_cite:
aśeṣacitracidgarbhasaṃsārasvapnasadmanaḥ /
ploṣakaḥ śiva evāham ityullāsī hutāśanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1091]

mv-k07-v1028.plain_english: Deluded by that, with consciousness variegated by karmic cognitions, one takes what is really a construction of resolve to be the varied world of transmigration.
mv-k07-v1028.sanskrit_cite:
tanmūḍhaḥ karmasaṃvitticitrībhūtacitis tathā /
saṃkalpam eva saṃsāraṃ vicitram abhimanyate // [AgMsv_1.1092]

mv-k07-v1029.plain_english: For that reason, a child who dies without other impressions, but with firm worldly tendencies lying dormant, would be born again as an infant.
mv-k07-v1029.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva mṛto bālo vāsanāntaravarjitaḥ /
śiśur eva bhavet suptadṛḍhasaṃsāravāsanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1093]

mv-k07-v1030.plain_english: In that way, by the sequence of those impressions, one reaches youth again and continues according to those same latent tendencies.
mv-k07-v1030.sanskrit_cite:
tānyau tathā (?) /
yāvadyauvanam abhyeti punas tadvāsanakramāt // [AgMsv_1.1094]

mv-k07-v1031.plain_english: Through cognition shaped by impressions, one takes various transmigrations to be real; and someone, through the impression of inertness, may even become inert while still associated with space and wind.
mv-k07-v1031.sanskrit_cite:
saṃskārasaṃvidā tās tāḥ saṃsṛtīr abhimanyate /
kaścij jaḍatvasaṃskārāj jaḍībhūto 'pi khānilaiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1095]

mv-k07-v1032.plain_english: Joined with earth and water, one may become flower and fruit; eaten and transformed into seed, one may come again into the state of a womb.
mv-k07-v1032.sanskrit_cite:
saha bhūjalayogena yāti puṣpaphalātmatām /
bhakṣito vīryarūpeṇa punar āyāti garbhatām // [AgMsv_1.1096]

mv-k07-v1033.plain_english: Again and again, Śiva, dwelling in his own impressions and tendencies, takes varied worlds of transmigration to be real, all in one and the same place.
mv-k07-v1033.sanskrit_cite:
yāvad punaḥ punaś citrān saṃsārān abhimanyate /
ekatraiva svasaṃskāravāsanāvāsitaḥ śivaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1097]

mv-k07-v1034.plain_english: It experiences heavens, hells, and other enjoyments fashioned by its own freedom, appearing sometimes as earthy, sometimes as watery, and sometimes as mixed.
mv-k07-v1034.sanskrit_cite:
bhuṅkte svarnarakādyāṃs tu bhogān svātantryakalpitān /
kvacid bhūmimayī kvāpi jalātmā kvāpi miśritā // [AgMsv_1.1098]

mv-k07-v1035.plain_english: Thus awareness shines by its own nature as made of worlds; wherever it is held, there, from its own impressions, it experiences pleasure and the like.
mv-k07-v1035.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ bhuvanamayy eṣā saṃvid bhāti svarūpataḥ /
dhriyate yatra tatraiva svasaṃskārāt sukhādikam // [AgMsv_1.1099]

mv-k07-v1036.plain_english: One knows, but is not seen by another in that same way; one knows others differently. In ultimate truth, there is no place and no time at all.
mv-k07-v1036.sanskrit_cite:
vetty anyena na dṛśyas tu sa tv anyān veda cānyathā /
na deśaḥ paramārthena na ca kālo 'sti kaś cana // [AgMsv_1.1100]

mv-k07-v1037.plain_english: In the doctrine of difference, if space is the common place, everything would be in one place; but if difference comes from limiting conditions, even those differently placed conditions depend on further difference.
mv-k07-v1037.sanskrit_cite:
bhedavāde hi gaganadeśāt sarvaikadeśatā /
upādher eva deśād bhiddeśasyāpy upādher bhidā // [AgMsv_1.1101]

mv-k07-v1038.plain_english: Thus, because of mutual dependence, there is no real difference of place; only a difference of intrinsic nature would fit as a true differentiator.
mv-k07-v1038.sanskrit_cite:
ity anyonyasamāśrityā deśabhedo na kaś cana /
svarūpabheda evāto bhedakatve susaṃgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.1102]

mv-k07-v1039.plain_english: But that intrinsic difference does not exist in things whose nature is one light; this has already been established. Those who lack this reflective insight miss it.
mv-k07-v1039.sanskrit_cite:
sa ca nāsti prakāśaikasvarūpeṣv iti sādhitam /
enayaiva parāmarśadṛśā ye parivarjitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1103]

mv-k07-v1040.plain_english: Those deprived of that insight are made doubtful by floods of doubt-producing scriptures and become absorbed in them, taking as real the endless inert beings imagined in their own dreams.

mv-k07-v1041.plain_english: Those without awakening are vainly made to cling to doubt by mere semblances of scripture; yet awareness, though hidden for long, can still awaken.
mv-k07-v1041.sanskrit_cite:
śāstrābhāsair vṛthā śaṅkāṃ grāhyante bodhavarjitāḥ /
yathā prabuddhyante saṃvin nibhṛtāpi ciraṃ sthitā // [AgMsv_1.1105]

mv-k07-v1042.plain_english: Even so, such things mostly bear fruit through constructions of the mind and the like, because of the sovereign freedom that manifests multiplicity.
mv-k07-v1042.sanskrit_cite:
tathāpi phalatīty evaṃ prāyaś cittādikalpitaiḥ /
evam ābhāsanānātvasvātantryaiśvaryaśālinā // [AgMsv_1.1106]

mv-k07-v1043.plain_english: Whatever is fashioned becomes for that person a body and the like; when joined with reversed appearances and tainted by sensations such as cold, it takes that disturbed form.
mv-k07-v1043.sanskrit_cite:
kḷptaṃ yad eva tat tasya yāti tanvādirūpatām /
viparyayābhāsayoge śītādyābhāsadūṣite // [AgMsv_1.1107]

mv-k07-v1044.plain_english: Then, when the channels and so forth are afflicted by contraction, bursting, blows, and the like, the body—like a great bellows-machine with its wheel of winds—goes out of order.

mv-k07-v1045.plain_english: When the vital breath breaks apart, the body appears inert, and one passes into another sphere of experience that arises according to the sequence of earlier latent impressions.
mv-k07-v1045.sanskrit_cite:
prāṇo vighaṭate tena jaḍābhāsaṃ kalevaram /
yasmin yāty adhikāre vā jāte prāg vāsanākramāt // [AgMsv_1.1109]

mv-k07-v1046.plain_english: In that very state one may fashion an experience called the other world, or one may feel like stone, or else one may wake up again.
mv-k07-v1046.sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva kalpayed bhogaṃ paralokābhidhānakam /
pāṣāṇatāṃ vā vetty eṣa punar vā pratibudhyate // [AgMsv_1.1110]

mv-k07-v1047.plain_english: It is called another world because of one's firm conviction, and whatever heaven, liberation, or the like has become settled in the mind for someone here takes shape accordingly.
mv-k07-v1047.sanskrit_cite:
paro 'yaṃ loka iti ca rūḍhyāsya paralokitā /
svargamokṣādi yasyeha yathārūḍhaṃ ca cetasi // [AgMsv_1.1111]

mv-k07-v1048.plain_english: In just that way it shines outwardly for that person, and so even there there is variety: bondage and liberation, happiness and heaven, suffering and an inert state.
mv-k07-v1048.sanskrit_cite:
tathaivāsya bahir bhāti tatas tatrāpi citratā /
bandho mokṣaḥ sukhaṃ svargo duḥkhaṃ jaḍamayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1112]

mv-k07-v1049.plain_english: Consciousness alone, in its own freedom, shines forth in this way as Śiva-nature; and just as a being made of parts has an 'I'-sense only to a limited extent,
mv-k07-v1049.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvid eva svatantretthaṃ śivarūpatā virājate /
bhūyo 'vayavayuktasya yathā tāvaty ahaṃsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.1113]

mv-k07-v1050.plain_english: so too Bhairava's 'I'-sense abides in a form that is the whole universe; just as a child, even in an empty place, perceives a goblin as something that produces real effects.
mv-k07-v1050.sanskrit_cite:
tathā viśvātmake rūpe bhairavasyāpy ahaṃsthitiḥ /
śiśuḥ śūnye 'pi vetālaṃ vetti satyārthakāriṇam // [AgMsv_1.1114]

mv-k08-v1051.plain_english: Thus the variety of meditation, worship, and the like becomes effective in action: an embodied, divided deity, when invoked, can abandon its own enjoyments and act in an instant.
mv-k08-v1051.sanskrit_cite:
dhyeyapūjyādivaicitryam ittham arthakriyākaram /
mūrto bhinnaḥ samāhūto hitvā bhogān nijān kṣaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.1115]

mv-k08-v1052.plain_english: Saying 'O god, he comes' is fitting only within scriptural statements; but all this is truly fitting only as the nature of the formless and so forth.
mv-k08-v1052.sanskrit_cite:
deva etīti vārtaiṣā vacaneṣv eva śobhate /
amūrtādisvarūpatvaṃ sarvam etat tu yujyate // [AgMsv_1.1116]

mv-k08-v1053.plain_english: Indeed the self alone, being of that nature, appears just so through division; for this is the very nature of consciousness, and that alone is what appears.
mv-k08-v1053.sanskrit_cite:
ātmaiva hi tathābhūtas tathā bhāty eva bhedataḥ /
evaṃ svabhāva evaiṣa saṃvido yaḥ sa eva tu // [AgMsv_1.1117]

mv-k08-v1054.plain_english: In scripture the karmic impurity is defined as being seized by division; but in the practice of initiation and related rites, it is not regarded as an impurity.
mv-k08-v1054.sanskrit_cite:
bhedagrastatayā kārmo malaḥ śāstre nirūpyate /
dīkṣādikarmayoge tu na malatvaṃ pratāyate // [AgMsv_1.1118]

mv-k08-v1055.plain_english: For initiation is vowed to burning away the entire world of transmigration made of division; and in reality it is of the nature of that true consciousness.
mv-k08-v1055.sanskrit_cite:
sa hi bhedamayāśeṣasaṃsāradahanavrataḥ /
dīkṣā ca vastutas tādṛksatyasaṃvitsvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.1119]

mv-k08-v1056.plain_english: Thus it is said in the supreme doctrine: one who knows in this way knows in truth; for in the yoga of realization, when the sphere of division is quieted, this is understood.
mv-k08-v1056.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ yo veda tattvenety uktaṃ cānuttare naye /
evaṃ vijñānayoge hi śamite bhedagocare // [AgMsv_1.1120]

mv-k08-v1057.plain_english: The self alone is Śiva, the one reality—so what bondage is there, and what liberation? Yet this is taught for the sake of entry into the great consciousness of initiation.
mv-k08-v1057.sanskrit_cite:
ātmaiva śiva evaikaḥ ko bandhaḥ kā ca muktatā /
etaddīkṣāmahāsaṃvidpraveśāya tu bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_1.1121]

mv-k08-v1058.plain_english: This initiation, whose nature is action, is for the removal of karmic and other impurities, operating within actions that are driven by the fixed force fashioned by nature.

mv-k08-v1059.plain_english: Because his experience is brought about simultaneously through the power of mantra, the determinations belonging to breath, space, limited agency, and time are likewise brought into play.
mv-k08-v1059.sanskrit_cite:
bhogo 'sya yugapadyasmāt kriyate mantraśaktitaḥ /
tathā hi prāṇagā deśakalākālādhvaniścayāḥ // [AgMsv_1.1123]

mv-k08-v1060.plain_english: His births are unfolded from earth all the way up to Śiva, and right there he becomes subject to birth, experience, authority, and dissolution.

mv-k08-v1061.plain_english: Thus, having been arranged and elevated from one level and placed in another, initiation—through the mutual, non-conceptual meeting of a guru established in settled consciousness and a disciple of actionless mind—blocks all the powers of prior karma.
mv-k08-v1061.sanskrit_cite:
vidhāyotkṛṣyate tasmād anyatra ca vidhīyate /

itthaṃ guror niścitasaṃvidātmarūḍheś ca śiṣyasya paraspareṇa /
niṣkarmacetor acitaiva dīkṣā prākkarmaśaktīr akhilā ruṇaddhi // [AgMsv_1.1125]

mv-k08-v1062.plain_english: Even there, the series of rice, sesame, ghee, oblations, and so forth—fashioned according to Śaiva necessity—does not, even at a clear stage, make the expanse of obscurity rootless, because division still continues to operate.
mv-k08-v1062.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpi taṇḍulatilājyacaruprabandha ityādi śaivaniyatipratibhārakḷptam /
tāvaty api sphuṭapade na niśāprapañco nirmūlatām upagato 'pi vibhedavṛtteḥ // [AgMsv_1.1126]

mv-k08-v1063.plain_english: Even within difference, this pure element destroys the merit that would cause future transmigration. For that reason, the entire network of principles is only twofold, divided into pure and other.
mv-k08-v1063.sanskrit_cite:
bhede 'pi kiṃtv eṣa punar bhaviṣyasaṃsārakārisukṛtādivighātahetuḥ /
śuddhas tatas tad ata eva hi tattvajālaṃ śuddhetarasthititayā nikhilaṃ dvidhaiva // [AgMsv_1.1127]

mv-k08-v1064.plain_english: The pure reality shines as filled with the three powers and as paired. From this, ritual action is conceived in many ways, and so an expanse of restriction arises that brings about limited forms of enjoyment.
mv-k08-v1064.sanskrit_cite:
śuddhaṃ triśaktikhacitaṃ nanu yāmalaṃ ca bhāty eva tena bahudhaiṣa kṛtaḥ kriyāyāḥ /
vyāpārakalpanāvaśān niyatiprapañcaḥ svalpetaratvakṛtatādṛśabhogayogaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1128]

mv-k08-v1065.plain_english: Where the assemblage of seals and mandalas is practiced together with mantras and tantras, all practices such as yoga become capable of yielding their fruits.
mv-k08-v1065.sanskrit_cite:
mudrāmaṇḍalasaṃghātaḥ samantratantracarcitaḥ /
yatra yogādikaṃ sarvaṃ phaladānāya kalpate // [AgMsv_1.1129]

mv-k08-v1066.plain_english: Those who are fixed in the narrowed desire to attain liberation regard unlimitedness itself as the fruit to be obtained here.

mv-k08-v1067.plain_english: In what is unlimited and unbroken, there is no room for conceiving sacrifice and similar rites; such is the view of those who have transcended all that. Still, even when the supremely nondual reality is known, some desire for a fruit can remain.
mv-k08-v1067.sanskrit_cite:
na hy anantānav/yacchede kāpi yāgādikalpanā anavacchinnavāñchā // 1.1131 //

tatsarvottīrṇadṛṣṭayaḥ /
tathāpi vidite hy arthe paramādvayasundare // [AgMsv_1.1132]

mv-k08-v1068.plain_english: Because consciousness is free by its very nature, some people still desire fruits. For their sake, the entire teaching is set forth, from earth up to Śiva, so that their aims may be fulfilled.
mv-k08-v1068.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvitsvabhāvasvātantryāt keṣāṃcit phalakāmatā /
tāny evoddiśya tat sarvaṃ pūraṇāya dharāditaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1133]

mv-k08-v1069.plain_english: The teaching on concentrations sets out the whole range up to Śiva in many divisions. Here, unlike in other systems, nothing that appears is unreal; so for those who abide in truth, what could possibly fall into the category of what must be rejected?
mv-k08-v1069.sanskrit_cite:
śivāntaṃ bahudhā bhedair dhāraṇāgrantha ucyate

iha hi nānyanayeṣv iva kiñcana sphuritam asti na yat kila satyataḥ /
tad iha satyapade sthitibhāgināṃ kim iva heyapade nipatiṣyati // [AgMsv_1.1134]

mv-k08-v1070.plain_english: Thus the principle that appears as the culmination of the seventeen sections is determined to be the unsurpassed state of Śiva for those who desire attainment. Everything taught here appears in an opposing form, because this entire expanse stands animated by difference.
mv-k08-v1070.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ saptadaśādhikāracaramaṃ tattvaṃ yad ābhāsate tan nirṇītam anuttaraṃ śivapadaṃ saṃprāptikāmān prati /
etat sarvam ihoditaṃ ca jagadānande vipakṣātmakaṃ bhedaprāṇatayā yato 'tra nikhilo 'py eṣa prapañcaḥ sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.1135]

mv-k08-v1071.plain_english: Thus, in the second section, the great Lord is established as the self of all and is worshiped through gradual knowledge and yoga, and through concentrations.
mv-k08-v1071.sanskrit_cite:
dvitīyaḥ kāṇḍaḥ

evaṃ maheśvaro devo viśvātmatvena saṃsthitaḥ /
kramikajñānayogābhyāṃ dhāraṇābhir upāsyate // [AgMsv_2.1]

mv-k08-v1072.plain_english: In the eighteenth chapter, the sequence of principles is fully expounded as freed from the net of duality, impurity, māyā, and the like.
mv-k08-v1072.sanskrit_cite:
tattvakramaṃ gatadvaitamalamāyādijālakam /
aṣṭādaśe tat paṭale tattvaṃ samyag vibhāvyate // [AgMsv_2.2]

mv-k08-v1073.plain_english: Here, practices such as breath control are described as to be abandoned, because they are not a means to supreme knowledge.
mv-k08-v1073.sanskrit_cite:
prāṇāyāmādikaṃ yatra heyam ity eva varṇyate /
na hi tasya parāṃ vittiṃ prati kācid upāyatā // [AgMsv_2.3]

mv-k08-v1074.plain_english: What is firmly established within consciousness cannot be moved into the apparatus of breath and mind; so how could a method of practice make that happen? If some still strive to refine consciousness through practice, we doubt what they could accomplish, where, from what basis, and how.
mv-k08-v1074.sanskrit_cite:
antaḥ saṃvidi yan nirūḍham abhitas tat prāṇadhīvigrahe saṃcāryeta kathaṃ tatheti ghaṭatām abhyāsayogakramaḥ /
ye tv abhyāsapathena saṃvidam imāṃ saṃskartum abhyudyatās te kiṃ kutra kutaḥ kathaṃ vidadhatām ity atra saṃdihmahe // [AgMsv_2.4]

mv-k08-v1075.plain_english: Practice means doing something over and over again, and even that arises from differences of space and time and from involvement with appearance and otherness; so it takes place on the path of body, mind, breath, and senses.
mv-k08-v1075.sanskrit_cite:
abhyāso hi punaḥ punar arthaḥ so 'pi ca dikkālapratibhedāt /
ābhāsetarayogasamuttho dehamanaḥprāṇākṣapathe syāt // [AgMsv_2.5]

mv-k08-v1076.plain_english: Those who wish to enter the Bhairava form, which is dense with pure light alone, become firmly established simply by resting in knowledge that shines forth once.
mv-k08-v1076.sanskrit_cite:
prakāśaikaghane rūpe bhairavīye vivikṣavaḥ /
sakṛdvibhātavijñānaviśrāntyaiva susaṃsthitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.6]

mv-k08-v1077.plain_english: For that reason, concentration is declared here to be the supreme and universally helpful limb, and concentrations determined through that same door may become of that very nature.
mv-k08-v1077.sanskrit_cite:
atraivātaḥ paraṃ proktam aṅgaṃ sarvopakāri yat /
dhāraṇā api taddvāraniścitāḥ syus tathātmikāḥ // [AgMsv_2.7]

mv-k08-v1078.plain_english: But surely, what confidence can be placed in reasoning that has no firm ground? Or else, why would your own statement not be struck down by the same lack of ground?
mv-k08-v1078.sanskrit_cite:
nanv apratiṣṭhe kas tarke samāśvāsaḥ prakalpyatām /
kiṃ vā na bhavatāṃ tādṛg apratiṣṭhāhataṃ vacaḥ // [AgMsv_2.8]

mv-k08-v1079.plain_english: Likewise, if some insist that scripture alone is the valid means of knowledge, how is certainty to be reached when there is a whole host of scriptures that contradict it?
mv-k08-v1079.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hy āgama evaikaṃ pramāṇam iti niścitaiḥ /
tadviruddhāgamavrāte sati niścīyatāṃ katham // [AgMsv_2.9]

mv-k08-v1080.plain_english: But if acceptance by the great multitude is taken as the reason for validity, that too is ungrounded, because a great multitude opposed to it can just as well exist.
mv-k08-v1080.sanskrit_cite:
mahājanaprasiddhis tu tatra prāmāṇyakāraṇam /
apratiṣṭhā tadviruddhamahājanasusaṃbhavāt // [AgMsv_2.10]

mv-k08-v1081.plain_english: Even perception, in matters like taste and so on, is seen to be overruled, and it becomes subject to an endless regress of later cognitions, does it not?
mv-k08-v1081.sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣam api rucyādau dṛṣṭabādhakasaṃvidam /
uttarottaravijñānānavasthābhājanaṃ nanu // [AgMsv_2.11]

mv-k08-v1082.plain_english: If even self-awareness were overruled in that way, how could this person, skilled in joining differences together, carry on any practical dealings at all?
mv-k08-v1082.sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid api tatraiva bādhiteti kathaṃ kila /
vyavahāram ayaṃ kuryād bhedasaṃdhānapaṇḍitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.12]

mv-k08-v1083.plain_english: But for us there can never be groundlessness at any time or place, because for us the supreme, all-full ocean of Bhairava is present everywhere.
mv-k08-v1083.sanskrit_cite:
asmākaṃ tv apratiṣṭhānaṃ na kadācit kvacid bhavet /
yeṣāṃ sarvatra saṃpūrṇaḥ paro bhairavasāgaraḥ // [AgMsv_2.13]

mv-k08-v1084.plain_english: Especially for those whose awareness has received the supreme nectar by crossing the ocean of reasoning, reasoning itself is not ungrounded.
mv-k08-v1084.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣatas tu tarkasya tān praty evāpratiṣṭhatā /
ye tarkārṇavatārāttaparamāmṛtasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.14]

mv-k08-v1085.plain_english: For all the parts of reasoning that do not touch self-awareness never, anywhere, attain Śiva as their final fruit.
mv-k08-v1085.sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi sarve tarkāṃśā anāmṛṣṭasvasaṃvidaḥ /
sarvatra paryantaphalaṃ na śivaṃ pratipedire // [AgMsv_2.15]

mv-k08-v1086.plain_english: The meaning of all scripture is essentially non-difference; any difference brought forth there is for attaining that non-difference, yet those of deluded intellect take delight in the difference itself.
mv-k08-v1086.sanskrit_cite:
abhedasāraḥ sarvo hi śāstrārthas tatprapattaye /
yas tatrodbhāvito bhedas tatra mūḍhadhiyo ratāḥ // [AgMsv_2.16]

mv-k08-v1087.plain_english: Reasoning is skilled only in cutting down the arguments of views based on difference; but surely, does reasoning have any usefulness even in the realm of non-difference?
mv-k08-v1087.sanskrit_cite:
tarkaś ca bhedavādāṃśayukticchedaikapaṇḍitaḥ /
nanv abhede 'pi tarkasya kā cid asty upayogitā // [AgMsv_2.17]

mv-k08-v1088.plain_english: In the vision of supreme nonduality, even reasoning is not truly fitting; therefore, for that supreme nonduality whose nature is grace to the universe, the text declares the Heart, whose nature is vibration, to be the supreme means.
mv-k08-v1088.sanskrit_cite:
paramādvayadṛṣṭau ca so 'pi naiva na saṃgataḥ /
ata eva parādvaitaṃ yad viśvānugrahātmakam /
tasyopāyaṃ paraṃ brūte hṛdayaṃ spandanātmakam // [AgMsv_2.18]

mv-k08-v1089.plain_english: In the Heart, which is made of awareness, there is a self-reflective awareness, the wonder of full consciousness, which all at once, suddenly and forcibly, dissolves the outward flashing of the universe.
mv-k08-v1089.sanskrit_cite:
hṛdaye bodhamaye yaḥ svavimarśaḥ pūrṇaciccamatkāraḥ /
yugapad drāgiti haṭhato līnīkṛtaviśvataḥsphuraṇaḥ // [AgMsv_2.19]

mv-k08-v1090.plain_english: In the first and last moments of grasping things, that state which is fully filled with surging bliss and made of the bliss of the whole world is called the universal vibration.
mv-k08-v1090.sanskrit_cite:
bhāvagrahādyacaramadaśāyor ullāsinirvṛtisupūrṇaḥ /
jagadānandamayo 'sau sāmānyaspanda ity uktaḥ // [AgMsv_2.20]

mv-k08-v1091.plain_english: The manifest flashing of the Heart, which shines forth as pure being from the abode of emission, leads one into the triad of powers to the very extent that it is recognized.
mv-k08-v1091.sanskrit_cite:
sphuraṇaṃ hṛdayasya yat kila prakaṭam idaṃ visargadhāmnaḥ /
sad iti pratibhāti yāvatā trikaśaktau viśatīha tāvatā // [AgMsv_2.21]

mv-k08-v1092.plain_english: This Heart is defined as the supreme nectar of Bhairava awareness, situated on the trident of the powers of will, knowledge, and action; from the supreme abode it is emitted.
mv-k08-v1092.sanskrit_cite:
tad idaṃ hṛdayaṃ nirucyate paramaṃ bhairavasaṃvidāmṛtam /
iṣidṛkkṛtiśaktiśūlagaṃ parame dhāmni visṛjyate tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.22]

mv-k08-v1093.plain_english: In the supreme, lordly Self this universe flashes forth as consciousness, situated on the trident of the three powers, and then proceeds by the path of emission on the Śāmbhava level.
mv-k08-v1093.sanskrit_cite:
parame bhagavatparātmani sphuritaṃ viśvam idaṃ cidātmakam /
śaktitrayaśūlagaṃ tataḥ śāmbhavabhūmivisargavartmanā // [AgMsv_2.23]

mv-k08-v1094.plain_english: That is then proclaimed as pure being; this full Heart, of the nature of 'I', always shines forth as the very flashing of the union of Śiva and Śakti.
mv-k08-v1094.sanskrit_cite:
tad atho sad iti pragīyate tad idaṃ pūrṇam ihāhamātmakaṃ /
hṛdayaṃ śivaśaktisaṃgamasphuraṇātmaiva sadāvabhāsate // [AgMsv_2.24]

mv-k08-v1095.plain_english: Here, in the Heart, sequences of creation, dissolution, and maintenance shine forth by the hundreds or even by thousands of millions, eternally, gathered through the agencies of Hara, Viṣṇu, and the lotus-born.
mv-k08-v1095.sanskrit_cite:
iha sṛṣṭilayasthitikramāḥ śataśo vāpi sahasrakoṭiśaḥ /
pravibhānti sadātanātmanā haraviṣṇvambujahetusaṃcitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.25]

mv-k08-v1096.plain_english: But for one who is not able to enter immediately through the collection of reasonings stated before, the vibration of the Heart is made manifest by the path of the śākta means.
mv-k08-v1096.sanskrit_cite:
iha tu puroktād yuktikalāpād yaḥ praviśet sadyo nāśaktaḥ /
taṃ prati śāktopāyapathena prakaṭīkriyate hṛdayaspandaḥ // [AgMsv_2.26]

mv-k08-v1097.plain_english: One reaches the path of the Heart by impelling the breath at the tip of the trident, and becomes intent on resting in the moon-digit of consciousness within that.

mv-k08-v1098.plain_english: Then, suddenly, by abandoning that level and casting off those states beginning with absence of bliss, which are situated amid the five elements, one moves beyond them.
mv-k08-v1098.sanskrit_cite:
jhaṭity evātha tadbhūmityāgena projjhya tā daśāḥ /
nirānandādikāḥ pañcabhūtamadhyavyavasthitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.28]

mv-k08-v1099.plain_english: Intent on complete rest, one should abandon the former stage and move to the higher one, because the ground of innate bliss follows upon the peaceful state.
mv-k08-v1099.sanskrit_cite:
tyajet pūrvāṃ parāṃ krāmet samyagviśrāntitatparaḥ /
yato nijānandamayī bhūmiḥ śāntapadānugā // [AgMsv_2.29]

mv-k08-v1100.plain_english: Nirānanda and parānanda, connected with puruṣa and the unborn, arise from the expansion of bliss produced by masses of undivided and divided objects of experience.

mv-k08-v1101.plain_english: A wondrous state of great bliss, of leftward course, shines forth in the great abode of Bhairava, in consciousness that has taken all within itself.
mv-k08-v1101.sanskrit_cite:
mahānandasthitiḥ kāpi vāmācārā samullaset /
bhairavīyamahādhāmni svīkṛtāśeṣasaṃvidi // [AgMsv_2.31]

mv-k08-v1102.plain_english: Great bliss, having become the bliss of consciousness, proceeds again in this triad that has taken in all the right, left, and upper aspects.
mv-k08-v1102.sanskrit_cite:
mahānandaś cidānandībhūya bhūyaḥ pravartate /
asmiṃs tu svīkṛtāśeṣadakṣavāmordhvagatrike // [AgMsv_2.32]

mv-k08-v1103.plain_english: In the triad whose nature is to grasp both duality and nonduality in every way, things may appear as undivided, or divided, or both divided and undivided.
mv-k08-v1103.sanskrit_cite:
trike sarvātmanā dvaitādvaitasaṃgrahaṇātmani /
abhinnā vātha bhinnā vā bhinnābhinnā athāpi vā // [AgMsv_2.33]

mv-k08-v1104.plain_english: Beings, joined with the five states of bliss beginning with innate bliss, arise from the state of intense, overflowing universal bliss.

mv-k08-v1105.plain_english: Innate bliss is founded only on resting in the aspect of the subject, while the state of nirānanda arises from resting only in emptiness.

mv-k08-v1106.plain_english: Supreme bliss also fully arises from resting in the domain of the object, when the object is filled on all sides with the collision of infinite knowables.
mv-k08-v1106.sanskrit_cite:
prameyapadaviśrānteḥ parānando 'py udety alam /
anantameyasaṃghaṭṭapūrṇe meye tu sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.36]

mv-k08-v1107.plain_english: The state called great bliss arises from the means of knowing through the yoking of savoring; it is skilled in devouring the apprehension of all masses of knowers and knowns.
mv-k08-v1107.sanskrit_cite:
pramāṇāc carvaṇāyogān mahānanda iti sthitiḥ /
samastamānameyaughakalanāgrāsakovidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.37]

mv-k08-v1108.plain_english: When one attains a rest that is unconditioned and utterly full, then indeed there is consciousness-bliss, which is not nourished by anything inert.
mv-k08-v1108.sanskrit_cite:
yadā viśrāntim abhyeti nirupādhisunirbharām /
tadā khalu cidānando yo jaḍānupabṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.38]

mv-k08-v1109.plain_english: Where there is no divided state of inert form, where there is no division at all, and which shines forth on every side.
mv-k08-v1109.sanskrit_cite:
na ca yatra sthitiḥ kāpi vibhaktā jaḍarūpiṇī /
yatra ko 'pi vyavacchedo nāsti yad viśvataḥ sphurat // [AgMsv_2.39]

mv-k08-v1110.plain_english: Our teacher declared that very reality—unstruck awareness nourished by supreme nectar—to be the abode of universal bliss.
mv-k08-v1110.sanskrit_cite:
yad anāhṛtasaṃvitti paramāmṛtabṛṃhitam /
tad eva jagadānandadhāmāsmākaṃ gurur jagau // [AgMsv_2.40]

mv-k08-v1111.plain_english: Where contemplation and other practices have no primary applicability, rest should be established there through the yoga of utterance in the heart.
mv-k08-v1111.sanskrit_cite:
yatrāsti bhāvanādīnāṃ na mukhyā kāpi saṃgatiḥ /
tatra viśrāntir ādheyā hṛdayoccārayogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.41]

mv-k08-v1112.plain_english: The complete rest attained there is called supreme nonduality; it comes about through the application of the breath-staff and the equalizing of before and after.
mv-k08-v1112.sanskrit_cite:
yā tatra samyag viśrāntis tat parādvaitam ucyate /
prāṇadaṇḍaprayogena pūrvāparasamīkṛteḥ // [AgMsv_2.42]

mv-k08-v1113.plain_english: By the yogin, elsewhere than in the ordinary person’s division of bondage and liberation, the ground is sprinkled by the mansion of the pendant lotus tetrad.

mv-k08-v1114.plain_english: By the unsurpassed nature that operates through the activity of speech, united with the dissolution and flourishing of the supreme I in the reflective awareness of consciousness.

mv-k08-v1115.plain_english: When the entity is illuminated by the sun—emptied of effort and whose nature is the true twelve phases—it is filled and fully pervaded.
mv-k08-v1115.sanskrit_cite:
udyogavaśariktena saddvādaśakalātmanā /
sūryeṇābhāsite bhāve pūrite paricarcite // [AgMsv_2.45]

mv-k08-v1116.plain_english: Having entered the fire of awakening, the one possessing the sixteen named phases completely releases the phases, which are slowed by the power of devouring that.
mv-k08-v1116.sanskrit_cite:
tadgrāsamantharavaśāḥ ṣoḍaśākhyakalājuṣā /
praviṣṭeṇa vibodhāgnau samyag visṛjatā kalāḥ // [AgMsv_2.46]

mv-k08-v1117.plain_english: By the one who has internalized the infinite principles from ka to kṣa on all sides, whose state remains unchanged after attaining emission, the four life-giving powers are attained.

mv-k08-v1118.plain_english: Joined to the heart where there is no reflection on the essence of the beingness of things, resting upon the eye of the yogin lineage fit for outward emission.

mv-k08-v1119.plain_english: By the state of Rudra-union, that stairway-garland of powers—ending in consciousness, breath, quality, and body—is always indeed established.
mv-k08-v1119.sanskrit_cite:
rudrayāmalabhāvena nityaṃ yā niṣṭhitaiva tām /
citprāṇaguṇadehāntaśaktisopānamālikām // [AgMsv_2.49]

mv-k08-v1120.plain_english: Then, having released through emission moving within the womb of vibration, one embraces the ground of emission, which enjoys the state of the fish-womb.
mv-k08-v1120.sanskrit_cite:
visargena visṛjyātha spandanodaravartinā /
visargabhūmim āśliṣya matsyodaradaśājuṣam // [AgMsv_2.50]

mv-k08-v1121.plain_english: Having ascended the ground of the trident, connected with the three channels, one reaches the supreme phase that is present in all, pervading all, and life-giving to all.
mv-k08-v1121.sanskrit_cite:
sarvasarvagatāṃ sarvajīvanīṃ paramāṃ kalām /
triśūlabhuvam ākramya nāḍītritayasaṃgatām // [AgMsv_2.51]

mv-k08-v1122.plain_english: One reaches the stairway-garland of powers ending in the brow-center, bindu, and nāda—expanding and contracting, and resorting in sequence to unity.

mv-k08-v1123.plain_english: She contracts and expands like the alternating flow of a she-donkey and a mare, again and again full of streams of beings that dissolve and are created.

mv-k08-v1124.plain_english: She makes the great root spike into one emissive abode and rests in the heart of Bhairavī, who nourishes all beings.

mv-k08-v1125.plain_english: This goddess, who has won the supreme name by boldly filling all, is without beginning or end and is inclined toward the whole universe.

mv-k08-v1126.plain_english: Having attained the goddess, the moonlight of the consciousness-moon in the space of heart-awareness and ruler of the triad, what indeed does one not obtain, and even cause others to obtain?
mv-k08-v1126.sanskrit_cite:
hṛdbodhākāśaciccandracandrikāṃ tritayeśikām /
devīṃ prāpya na kiṃ nāma labhate lambhyaty api // [AgMsv_2.56]

mv-k08-v1127.plain_english: Therefore, when the yogi, using means grounded in the contemplative body, wishes to enter the supreme, he first trembles.
mv-k08-v1127.sanskrit_cite:
tad atra bhāvanādehagatopāyaiḥ pare sati /
yadaiṣa pravivikṣuḥ syād yogī tāvad prakampate // [AgMsv_2.57]

mv-k08-v1128.plain_english: He trembles because, for hundreds of past births, he has been certain of identity with the body and has imagined consciousness and body to be one, like water mixed with dust.

mv-k08-v1129.plain_english: He may first enter the perfectly full conscious self, free from the māyā called difference, through the process of pressing forward by his own power.
mv-k08-v1129.sanskrit_cite:
bhedākhyamāyārahite paripūrṇacidātmani /
praviśet prathamaṃ yāvat svabalākramaṇakramāt // [AgMsv_2.59]

mv-k08-v1130.plain_english: For him there may arise a kind of sleep that loosens his immersion in the body, appearing just as trembling, so long as firm establishment in the supreme self has not yet arisen.
mv-k08-v1130.sanskrit_cite:
bhaven nidrāsya sā dehāveśaśaithilyadāyinī /
kamprarūpaiva yāvan no rūḍhir jātā parātmani // [AgMsv_2.60]

mv-k08-v1131.plain_english: This is the unmanifest sign, whose nature is man, power, and Śiva, in which this whole universe is dissolved and which is understood as present within.
mv-k08-v1131.sanskrit_cite:
etad avyaktaliṅgaṃ tannaraśaktiśivātmakam /
yatra viśvam idaṃ līnaṃ yad antaḥsthaṃ ca gamyate // [AgMsv_2.61]

mv-k08-v1132.plain_english: Moreover, this whole aggregate of paths has already been determined as present in the body; by the force of its unfolding, absorption may become clear.
mv-k08-v1132.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cādhvajātam etad dehasthatayaiva pūrvanirṇītam /
tasyonmeṣavaśena sphuṭatāṃ yāyāt samāveśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.62]

mv-k08-v1133.plain_english: When the mind-principle abides in a state of special vibration, consciousness-bliss arises from the fullness of Śakti's radiance, bearing within it the supreme essence of mantra-power.

mv-k08-v1134.plain_english: This sign, consisting of man and power and being both manifest and unmanifest, is said in scripture to blossom with the sap of the fruit of accomplishment.
mv-k08-v1134.sanskrit_cite:
naraśaktimayam idaṃ tadvyaktāvyaktaṃ bhavel liṅgaṃ /
siddhiphalaprasavarasaprasūnam iti kathyate śāstre // [AgMsv_2.64]

mv-k08-v1135.plain_english: But the manifest sign is said to be that which consists only of man; this threefold division is an arrangement of one single vibration.
mv-k08-v1135.sanskrit_cite:
vyaktaliṅgaṃ tad uktaṃ tu yat kevalanarātmakam /
ekasya spandanasyeyaṃ tridhā bhedavyavasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.65]

mv-k08-v1136.plain_english: Those whose hearts lack knowledge of this sign worship an external liṅga in vain; that is mere effort and cannot bring the true fruit.
mv-k08-v1136.sanskrit_cite:
etalliṅgajñānapraviyuktahṛdā vṛthaiva hi bhajante /
bāhyasthaliṅgapūjāṃ prayāsamātraṃ phalāya na hi tat syāt // [AgMsv_2.66]

mv-k08-v1137.plain_english: The manifest sign called the self-sign, resting on the human form, arises when the whole external universe is filled with non-difference from the body.
mv-k08-v1137.sanskrit_cite:
yad vyaktam ātmaliṅgākhyaṃ nararūpasamāśrayi /
dehābhedamaye bāhye viśvasmin bharite sati // [AgMsv_2.67]

mv-k08-v1138.plain_english: For the yogi absorbed on the level of great bliss, the primal sign therefore comes directly face-to-face.
mv-k08-v1138.sanskrit_cite:
samudeti mahānandabhūmau līnasya yoginaḥ /
tenādyaṃ liṅgam abhyeti saṃmukhīnatvam añjasā // [AgMsv_2.68]

mv-k08-v1139.plain_english: One should always abide in this sign, intent on resting in worship, for it is the heart of the yoginīs, the temple of supreme bliss.
mv-k08-v1139.sanskrit_cite:
atra liṅge sadā tiṣṭhet pūjāviśrāntitatparaḥ /
yadyoginīnāṃ hṛdayaṃ paramānandamandiram // [AgMsv_2.69]

mv-k08-v1140.plain_english: There, in the abodes of bliss of the previously taught seed, womb, parts, and emission, the wise gather an indescribable attainment of identity.
mv-k08-v1140.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvoktabījayonyaṃśavisargānandamandirāḥ /
yatra kāmapi tādātmyasampattiṃ cinvate budhāḥ // [AgMsv_2.70]

mv-k08-v1141.plain_english: There, without effort, the whole host of deities abides in the bliss-filled abode, their nature being eternally arisen consciousness.
mv-k08-v1141.sanskrit_cite:
yatra prayāsavirahāt sarvo 'sau devatāgaṇaḥ /
ānandapūrṇe dhāmny āste nityoditacidātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_2.71]

mv-k08-v1142.plain_english: That shining of Lord Bhairava as contraction and expansion appears even though, in truth, contraction and expansion are not present in him.

mv-k08-v1143.plain_english: Sprinkled by that stream of bliss arising from the impact of consummation, this universe casts off its oldness.

mv-k08-v1144.plain_english: There, effortful striving as a task is misplaced, because what is ever risen like the sun does not need to be sought with a lamp.
mv-k08-v1144.sanskrit_cite:
tatra praveśane yatnaḥ kāryatvena prayāsakṛt /
yataḥ sadodito bhānuḥ kiṃ dīpena vicāryate // [AgMsv_2.73]

mv-k08-v1145.plain_english: Whether the yogi is established in his own self on the level of Śiva's conscious vibration, or delights the circle of yoginīs through special streams of external beings,
mv-k08-v1145.sanskrit_cite:
yadi svātmasthito yogī śivacitspandabhūmigaḥ /
yadi vā bāhyabhāvaughaviśeṣayoginīkulanandanaḥ // [AgMsv_2.74]

mv-k08-v1146.plain_english: Even in the absence of an object like a pot, that state consisting of the appearance of universal vibration is the supreme Bhairava seal, with inward focus and outward gaze.
mv-k08-v1146.sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭābhāve 'pi sāmānyaspandābhāsamayīṃ sthitim /
parabhairavamudrāṃ tām antarlakṣabahirdṛśam // [AgMsv_2.77]

mv-k08-v1147.plain_english: Then that supreme Śaiva goddess resorts again to the stream of phenomena, which is fashioned by the play of her freedom and consists of manifold efficacies.
mv-k08-v1147.sanskrit_cite:
yad āśrayati śaivī sā parā devī tataḥ punaḥ /
svātantryahelānirmeye tattadarthakriyāmaye // [AgMsv_2.78]

mv-k08-v1148.plain_english: In that stream of phenomena, joined to the savor of eager, awakening awareness, she touches Śakti—the true ground of particular vibration—and abides there.
mv-k08-v1148.sanskrit_cite:
bhāvaughe sotsukaunmukhyavimarśarasayogataḥ /
viśeṣaspandasadbhūmiṃ śaktiṃ saṃspṛśya vartate // [AgMsv_2.79]

mv-k08-v1149.plain_english: Presided over by this power, one's own mantras, in its manifestation, attain autonomy even in the midst of various accomplishments.
mv-k08-v1149.sanskrit_cite:
etenādhiṣṭhitā dhāmnā svamantrāstatprakāśane /
yānti svātantrayogitvaṃ vicitrāsvapi siddhiṣu // [AgMsv_2.80]

mv-k08-v1150.plain_english: Having become firmly established in a mode beyond rejection and acceptance, he sees everything shining forth, through its connection with all manifestation, as consciousness itself.
mv-k08-v1150.sanskrit_cite:
hānādānatiraskāravṛttau rūḍhim upāgataḥ /
sarvabhāsanayogena bhāsamānaṃ cidātmanā // [AgMsv_2.81]

mv-k08-v1151.plain_english: Seeing the visible from a stance of non-difference, through the wonder of consciousness, he abandons the timid state that comes from the wretched craving for practical results.
mv-k08-v1151.sanskrit_cite:
abhedavṛttitaḥ paśyan dṛśyaṃ citicamatkṛteḥ /
arthakriyārthitādainyakāritāṃ kātarāṃ sthitm // [AgMsv_2.82]

mv-k08-v1152.plain_english: Having abandoned that state, as long as he remains so, he effortlessly enters the Bhairava-like Śāmbhava level, the supreme state.
mv-k08-v1152.sanskrit_cite:
vihāya yāvad āsīta tāvac chāṃbhavabhūmikām /
bhairavīm āviśaty eva parāṃ bhūmim ayatnataḥ // [AgMsv_2.83]

mv-k08-v1153.plain_english: For one whose awareness is entered by this state, everything is seen as pervaded by the nature of light, for it is consciousness that shines.
mv-k08-v1153.sanskrit_cite:
etadāviṣṭasaṃvitti sarvam eva nirīkṣyate /
prakāśarūpatākrāntaṃ caitanyaṃ hi prakāśate // [AgMsv_2.84]

mv-k08-v1154.plain_english: And what is unmanifest does not attain manifestation merely by being connected with something to be manifested; this has already been explained at length.
mv-k08-v1154.sanskrit_cite:
na cāprakāśaṃ prākāśyayogād eti prakāśatām /
iti vistarataḥ pūrvaṃ prakāśitam idaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.85]

mv-k08-v1155.plain_english: All his activities dissolved through union with great audacity, his mind becomes wholly filled by a concentrated mass of his own rays.

mv-k08-v1156.plain_english: Thinking of nothing and having abandoned the state of clearly seen difference, as long as he remains so, the previously described levels come forward.
mv-k08-v1156.sanskrit_cite:
akiṃciccintakaḥ spaṣṭadṛṣṭabhedojjhitasthitiḥ /
yāvad āsīta tāvat tu pūrvoktā eva bhūmayaḥ // [AgMsv_2.87]

mv-k08-v1157.plain_english: Those levels come into presence as the sole causes for burning away the intoxication of worldly existence, and so does the divine aggregate of senses that had been overgrown by the firm sense of difference.
mv-k08-v1157.sanskrit_cite:
sāṃmukhyaṃ yānti saṃsārasadmadāhaikahetavaḥ /
yaś ca divyo 'kṣasaṃghāto bhedarūḍhitirohitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.88]

mv-k08-v1158.plain_english: When that aggregate, whose nature is play that nourishes freedom, remains fruitfully turned inward for even a single moment, then—
mv-k08-v1158.sanskrit_cite:
svātantryapoṣakakrīḍāmātropakaraṇātmakaḥ /
yadā nimīlanāvandhyas tiṣṭhaty ekaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tadā // [AgMsv_2.89]

mv-k08-v1159.plain_english: Then the universe, melted by the great flame of awareness that has arisen through that door, attains the state of resting in the ocean of supreme bliss.

mv-k08-v1160.plain_english: Resting in the drinking of that savor and satisfying the goddesses of awareness, he soon attains freedom from the fear of death and birth.
mv-k08-v1160.sanskrit_cite:
tadrasāpānaviśrāntaḥ saṃviddevīḥ pratarpayan /
acirād eti maraṇajanmatrāsavihīnatām // [AgMsv_2.91]

mv-k08-v1161.plain_english: For awareness, having congealed and taken on the form of its own awareness, body, senses, and objects, returns by the proper method—once that state has dissolved—to its own dense body of consciousness.
mv-k08-v1161.sanskrit_cite:
āśyānabhāvaṃ hi gatā svasaṃviddehendriyajñeyamayatvam āptā /
yuktyā tu sā prāptavilīnabhāvāt saṃvidghanaṃ svaṃ vapur eva yāti // [AgMsv_2.92]

mv-k08-v1162.plain_english: By the very same method through which those whose minds are overpowered by external objects emerge outward, there arises the awareness of Bhairava's bliss.
mv-k08-v1162.sanskrit_cite:
yuktyā yayaiva bāhyārthavivaśīkṛtacetasām /
vyutthitir jāyate saiva bhairavānandasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.93]

mv-k08-v1163.plain_english: By that very method, received through the lineage of the yoginī's mouth, the entry of impurity is shaken off and the state made of consciousness stands firm.
mv-k08-v1163.sanskrit_cite:
tayaiva yoginīvaktrasaṃpradāyakramāptayā /
vidhūtakalmaṣāveśā tiṣṭhate cinmayī sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.94]

mv-k08-v1164.plain_english: When the yogin slightly opens the mouth of awareness, all the inner circles of the senses and channels, resting on that traversal, are activated.
mv-k08-v1164.sanskrit_cite:
vaktram īṣad yadā yogī vikāsayati saṃvidaḥ /
sarvā indriyanāḍyantaścakrākramaṇasaṃśrayāḥ // [AgMsv_2.95]

mv-k08-v1165.plain_english: Then, because of turning toward consciousness, they suddenly move into an expansion consisting in the absence of difference among grasped objects, even though differences like blue and yellow had appeared.
mv-k08-v1165.sanskrit_cite:
tadā vikāsaṃ grāhyārthabhedābhāvamayaṃ haṭhāt /
prayānti cidunmukhatvāt nīlapītādibhedavān // [AgMsv_2.96]

mv-k08-v1166.plain_english: The difference in the relation between grasper and grasped is split at once through attainment of the lineage rooted in the yoginī's mouth.

mv-k08-v1167.plain_english: Immediately, by the experience-giving seal, he is wholly sealed and absorbed in direct Bhairava, the consciousness-form that presides over all.

mv-k08-v1168.plain_english: That yogin, filled with wonder, obtains awareness of his own self and remains in a state that does not depart even amid the arising and passing of various objects.
mv-k08-v1168.sanskrit_cite:
sa yogī vismayāviṣṭo labhate svātmasaṃvidam /
tattaddṛśyodayāpāyayoge 'py anapayatsthiti // [AgMsv_2.99]

mv-k08-v1169.plain_english: Water lying low in a tank does not flow elsewhere, even with effort, because it is incapable of doing more than filling that place alone.
mv-k08-v1169.sanskrit_cite:
taḍāgavartinimnāmbu tannānyatra pravartate /
prayatnenāpi tanmātrapūraṇāya yad akṣamam // [AgMsv_2.100]

mv-k08-v1170.plain_english: But when it is filled with savor by a stream of water flowing through the inner door, then streams filled by that overflow in all directions.
mv-k08-v1170.sanskrit_cite:
yadā tvantaḥdvāravāridhārasaṃpūritaṃ rasāt /
bhaved bhaveyustatpūrṇāḥ pravāhāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ // [AgMsv_2.101]

mv-k08-v1171.plain_english: Thus, by the force of its own surge, consciousness opens forth by itself and, without division, makes the portions of beings shine as non-different from its own self.
mv-k08-v1171.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ svollāsarabhasāc caitanyaṃ pronmiṣatsvayaṃ /
avibhāgena bhāvāṃśān svātmābhedena bhāsayan // [AgMsv_2.102]

mv-k08-v1172.plain_english: If, even for a moment, it does not sink into closure, then through the dissolving of māyā the level of Bhairava shines forth.
mv-k08-v1172.sanskrit_cite:
mīlanāviṣayībhāvaṃ śrayed yadi muhūrtakaṃ /
māyāvigalanād bhūmir bhairavīyā virājate // [AgMsv_2.103]
