mv-k08-v1173.plain_english: For the limitation born of conceptualization may afterward show division; that very division is māyā, the power of the free one that reveals the vision of difference.
mv-k08-v1173.sanskrit_cite:
vaikalpiko 'hyavacchedaḥ paścād yāṃ darśayed bhidām /
saiva māyā svatantrasya bhedadṛṣṭiprakāśinī // [AgMsv_2.104]

mv-k08-v1174.plain_english: For one who rests only in the opening of consciousness, that māyā is rootless and cannot arise; so what is the use of saying more in this method of the unsurpassed self?
mv-k08-v1174.sanskrit_cite:
unmeṣamātrarūḍhasya sā nirmūlā na saṃbhavet /
itthaṃ kiṃ bahunoktena naye 'nuttarātmani // [AgMsv_2.105]

mv-k08-v1175.plain_english: In reality, no limb of yoga can serve as a means, for its own nature is formless, being free from all limitation.
mv-k08-v1175.sanskrit_cite:
vastuto 'sti na kasyāpi yogāṅgasyābhyupāyatā /
svarūpaṃ hyasya nīrūpam avacchedavivarjanāt // [AgMsv_2.106]

mv-k08-v1176.plain_english: Even the means is not a means, because it stops effortful activity; it is free from exhalation and inhalation and from the regulation of body and breath.

mv-k08-v1177.plain_english: Thus this mind carries the self across from the ocean of difference, even when it is sinking while still in the taste of objects.
mv-k08-v1177.sanskrit_cite:
tārayaty evam ātmānaṃ bhedasāgaragocarāt /
nimajjamānam apy etan mano vaiṣayike rase // [AgMsv_2.108]

mv-k08-v1178.plain_english: A gourd without holes does not become soft inside; likewise, those who forcibly restrain the mind's own path, as if holding back a horse, do not make it inwardly receptive.
mv-k08-v1178.sanskrit_cite:
nāntarārdratvam abhyeti niśchidraṃ tumbakaṃ yathā /
svaṃ panthānaṃ hayasyeva manaso ye nirundhate // [AgMsv_2.109]

mv-k08-v1179.plain_english: For those who try to break the mind, it runs off along countless wrong paths; wondering, 'What is this?', the mind mostly keeps longing restlessly, even in pain.
mv-k08-v1179.sanskrit_cite:
teṣāṃ tatkhaṇḍanayogād dhavaty unmārgakoṭibhiḥ /
kiṃsvid etad iti prāyo duḥkhe 'py utkaṇṭhate manaḥ // [AgMsv_2.110]

mv-k08-v1180.plain_english: Through knowledge one can become dispassionate even toward pleasure, discerning 'this is this'; for the teacher has taught this in many ways in his own scripture.
mv-k08-v1180.sanskrit_cite:
sukhād api virajyeta jñānād etad idaṃ [tv iti] /
tathāhi gurur ādikṣad bahudhā svakaśāsane // [AgMsv_2.111]

mv-k08-v1181.plain_english: The activities of the senses fall away through indifference and dispassion alone; but as long as they are forcibly controlled, they keep acting turbulently.
mv-k08-v1181.sanskrit_cite:
anādaraviraktyaiva galantīndriyavṛttayaḥ /
yāvat tu viniyamyante tāvat tāvad vikurvate // [AgMsv_2.112]

mv-k08-v1182.plain_english: Even that so-called withdrawal which is applied to the net of the senses becomes, for one whose bondage is already firmly set, a binding as hard as diamond cement.
mv-k08-v1182.sanskrit_cite:
pratyāhāro 'pi nāmāyaṃ yo 'kṣajāle pravartyate /
bandhasyārūḍhavṛttes tad vajralepena bandhanam // [AgMsv_2.113]

mv-k08-v1183.plain_english: Amid objects, their enjoyment, and the pleasure or pain that arises from them, those whose fear has dissolved, though their minds are immersed, do not truly enter into them and know within the ease of the quieting of mental activity.
mv-k08-v1183.sanskrit_cite:
artheṣu tadbhogavidhau tadutthe \ \ duḥkhe sukhe vā galitābhiśaṅkam /
anāviśanto 'pi nimagnacittā \ \ jānanti vṛttikṣayasaukhyam antaḥ // [AgMsv_2.114]

mv-k08-v1184.plain_english: When the self, the great light of consciousness, is present in the heart, and the senses and objects such as taste are also present and active, the yogi abides very clearly in a fullness whose arising is free of difference; let that reality be accepted.
mv-k08-v1184.sanskrit_cite:
saty evātmani citsvabhāvamahasi svānte tathopakriyāṃ tasmai kurvati tatpracāracature saty akṣavarge 'pi ca /
satsv artheṣu rasādiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yad bhedavandhyodayaṃ yogī tiṣṭhati pūrṇaraśmikhacitas tat tattvam ādīyatām // [AgMsv_2.115]

mv-k08-v1185.plain_english: To say that non-discrimination is supreme bondage is only a common saying; for non-discrimination itself can be the supreme stairway to attaining liberation.
mv-k08-v1185.sanskrit_cite:
aviveka eva param iha saṃsāra iti pravādamātram /
aviveka eva hi paraṃ niḥśreyasalābhasopānam // [AgMsv_2.116]

mv-k08-v1186.plain_english: Abandon deliberate concentrations; where, indeed, would you place concentration? Examine it yourself: in the full it is not fitting, and in the not-full it does not attain true being.
mv-k08-v1186.sanskrit_cite:
tyajāvadhānāni nanu kva nāma dhatse 'vadhānaṃ vicinu svayaṃ tat /
pūrṇe 'vadhānaṃ nahi nāma yuktaṃ nāpūrṇam abhyeti ca satyabhāvam // [AgMsv_2.117]

mv-k08-v1187.plain_english: Wherever union with bliss arises, there one's own nature is full; if the delusion of difference is understood, one may reach peace there. Even in waking and in every state, the yogi can become the lord of the great wheel of consciousness, moving through varied activities while shining with mantra power.
mv-k08-v1187.sanskrit_cite:
yatraivānandayogaḥ kvacana nanu bhavet tatra pūrṇaḥ svabhāvaḥ --- --- te veti tatra praśamapadam iyād yady ayaṃ bhedamohaḥ /
tajjñāne jāgradādāv api nikhilapade cinmahācakranātho yogī jāyeta nānāvyavahṛtapathago 'pyullasan mantravīryaḥ // [AgMsv_2.118]

mv-k08-v1188.plain_english: Just as one who sets out to dig a well feels accomplished only when water is reached, while another is satisfied with water already in hand, so the way of attaining the supreme is varied.
mv-k08-v1188.sanskrit_cite:
yathā hi kūpaṃ pracikīrṣur eva prāpte jale yāti kṛtitvam ekaḥ /
kaścit punar hastagatādi[vāri]mātrād itthaṃ paraprāptividhir vicitraḥ // [AgMsv_2.119]

mv-k08-v1189.plain_english: This is without means; so how, by the usual relation of means and goal, or in any other way, could a person be freed from the bondage of difference?
mv-k08-v1189.sanskrit_cite:
anupāyam idaṃ tasmād upāyopeyayogataḥ /
bhedabandhād vimucyeta kathaṃ vetarathā janaḥ // [AgMsv_2.120]

mv-k08-v1190.plain_english: Even though this reality is without means, this scripture teaches means in many ways, functioning through relational instruction.
mv-k08-v1190.sanskrit_cite:
anupāye 'pi caitasmin kiṃcit sāṃbandhyavṛttitaḥ /
upāyasyopadeśo 'yaṃ śāstre 'tra bahudhā kṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_2.121]

mv-k08-v1191.plain_english: Just as children are clearly led into the real nature of sound through written letters, so the deluded are gradually led by those provisional means.
mv-k08-v1191.sanskrit_cite:
yathā lipyakṣarair bālāḥ satye varṇātmani sphuṭam /
praveśyante tathā mūḍhais tair aupāyikaiḥ kramāt // [AgMsv_2.122]

mv-k08-v1192.plain_english: For that very purpose, even in the nondual supreme reality, this scripture respectfully teaches something appropriate, such as worship and meditation.
mv-k08-v1192.sanskrit_cite:
tadartham eva cādvaite paratattve 'pi sādaram /
pūjādhyānādi śāstre 'sminn ucitaṃ kiṃcid ucyate // [AgMsv_2.123]

mv-k08-v1193.plain_english: Whatever delights the mind, in any state of the senses, can be joined to the abode of true awareness, to the very opening of Brahman.
mv-k08-v1193.sanskrit_cite:
yat kiṃcin manasāhlādi yatra kvāpīndriyasthitau /
yojyate bodhasadbrahmadhāmni brahmabilātmani // [AgMsv_2.124]

mv-k08-v1194.plain_english: Resting on absorption in true being that follows the self, one naturally and without effort comes to function as an instrument in the worship of the wheel of the supreme Kula lord and his powers.
mv-k08-v1194.sanskrit_cite:
ātmānusārisadbhāvasamāveśadaśāśrayāt

tattatparakuleśānaśakticakrārcanākrame /
prayāty evāprayatnena karaṇatvaṃ svabhāvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.125]

mv-k08-v1195.plain_english: Having made the support-ground cleansed by a moment of sprinkling with the essence of wonder, I worship you, O God, together with the Goddess day and night in the temple of the body, using flowers of my own nature taken from the mind and filled with their own fragrance, through the method of the priceless offering-vessel of my own heart overflowing with the nectar of bliss.
mv-k08-v1195.sanskrit_cite:
kṛtvādhāradharāṃ camatkṛtirasaprokṣākṣaṇakṣālitām āttair mānasataḥ svabhāvakusumaiḥ svāmodasaṃdohibhiḥ /
ānandāmṛtanirbharasvahṛdayānarghārghapātrakramāt tvāṃ devyā saha dehadevasadane devārcaye 'harniśam // [AgMsv_2.126]

mv-k08-v1196.plain_english: Thus, wherever one may stand, by the very nature of one's own reflective awareness, there the entry of the three powers shines forth in a threefold way.
mv-k08-v1196.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ yatra kvacit tiṣṭhet svavimarśasvabhāvataḥ /
tatra śaktitrayāveśas tridhā tāvat prakāśate // [AgMsv_2.127]

mv-k08-v1197.plain_english: When that shining appears ninefold, arising from the stated twelve wheels, its repose occurs in a single moment and takes the form of a state numbering one hundred and eight.
mv-k08-v1197.sanskrit_cite:
navadhā bhāsamānasya proktadvādaśacakrataḥ /
viśrāntir ekakṣaṇagā sāṣṭottaraśatasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.128]

mv-k08-v1198.plain_english: That state is clearly discerned as one alone, numbering a hundred; and in this way, whatever speech at all may arise from this yogin belongs to that same state.
mv-k08-v1198.sanskrit_cite:
ekaiva śatasaṃkhyā ca sā sthitiḥ pravibhāvyate /
itthaṃ yat kiṃcanaitasya vacanaṃ yogino bhavet // [AgMsv_2.129]

mv-k08-v1199.plain_english: That very speech becomes mantra practice on the unsurpassed path, constantly and without any need to rely on the presence of inner fuel.
mv-k08-v1199.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva japayogāya jāyate 'nuttare pathi /
antarindhanasadbhāvam anapekṣyaiva nityaśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.130]

mv-k08-v1200.plain_english: If one reflectively understands that all beings enter into that which blazes with hundreds of foremost flames spreading forth from all the streams of the senses, then that very place is where their entry occurs.
mv-k08-v1200.sanskrit_cite:
yo jvalaty akhilākṣaughaprasṛtāgraśikhāśataḥ /
tatraiva sarvabhāvānāṃ praveśaś ced vimṛśyate // [AgMsv_2.131]

mv-k09-v1201.plain_english: Surely, when their gross form is suddenly burned away, things forcibly attain unity with the great blazing light of awareness by their very nature; this is regarded as the supreme offering in the Bhairava tradition.
mv-k09-v1201.sanskrit_cite:
nūnaṃ jhaṭiti saṃpluṣṭasthūlarūpatayā haṭhāt /
yānti bodhamahājvālāprakāśaikyaṃ svarūpataḥ /
sa eṣa paramo homo bhairavīyakrame mataḥ // [AgMsv_2.132]

mv-k09-v1202.plain_english: When entities are properly offered by method into the fire within one's own awareness, they abandon the division of difference and, by their own power, kindle that very fire.
mv-k09-v1202.sanskrit_cite:
nijabodhajaṭharahutabhuji bhāvāḥ samyagsamarpitā yuktyā /
jahati bhedavibhāgaṃ nijaśaktyā taṃ samindhate yasmāt // [AgMsv_2.133]

mv-k09-v1203.plain_english: Whatever sense-object consciousness creates before itself by its own will and by the force of its creative nature becomes fit for meditation on that very object.
mv-k09-v1203.sanskrit_cite:
yad eva svecchayā sṛṣṭisvābhāvyavaśataḥ puraḥ /
nirmimīte 'kṣaviṣayaṃ taddhyānāyāvakalpate // [AgMsv_2.134]

mv-k09-v1204.plain_english: For although the abode of consciousness is formless and yet made of all forms, for those who seek results some particular form is established as the object of meditation.
mv-k09-v1204.sanskrit_cite:
nirākāre hi ciddhāmni viśvākṛtimaye sati /
phalārthināṃ kācid eva dhyeyatvenākṛtiḥ sthitā // [AgMsv_2.135]

mv-k09-v1205.plain_english: Just as, even within a nondual and full reality, someone fetching water eagerly seeks a pot by setting aside other forms, so too a particular form may be chosen.
mv-k09-v1205.sanskrit_cite:
yathā hy abhedasaṃpūrṇe bhāve 'py udakam āharan /
anyākṛtyapahānena ghaṭam arthayate rasāt // [AgMsv_2.136]

mv-k09-v1206.plain_english: In the same way, through the unfolding of the supreme Lord's self-restriction, some particular form gives rise to some particular conception of a result.
mv-k09-v1206.sanskrit_cite:
tathaiva parameśānaniyatipravijṛmbhaṇāt /
kācid evākṛtiḥ kāṃcit sūte phalavikalpanam // [AgMsv_2.137]

mv-k09-v1207.plain_english: But for one whose activity is the fullness of consciousness and who desires no result at all, meditation in the form of the whole universe unfolds at all times.
mv-k09-v1207.sanskrit_cite:
yas tu saṃpūrṇacidvṛttir na phalaṃ nāma vāñchati /
tasya viśvākṛti dhyānaṃ sarvadaiva vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_2.138]

mv-k09-v1208.plain_english: For the Kula yogin reeling from the intoxicant of the surging Bhairava essence, whatever arises, in whatever way it arises, simply arises.
mv-k09-v1208.sanskrit_cite:
kulayogina udriktabhairavīyarasāsavāt /
ghūrṇamānasya yaḥ kaścit ko 'py udeti yathā tathā // [AgMsv_2.139]

mv-k09-v1209.plain_english: The bodily absorption whose nature is delight and melting is, in the unsurpassed teaching, the seal that has taken the whole world as its seal.
mv-k09-v1209.sanskrit_cite:
śarīragaḥ samāveśo modanadrāvaṇātmakaḥ /
sā svīkṛtajaganmudrā mudrā nairuttare mate // [AgMsv_2.140]

mv-k09-v1210.plain_english: This rare method of yoga abides in the heart of someone whose wheel of consciousness becomes clear, quickly, as in the case of one who is in his final birth.
mv-k09-v1210.sanskrit_cite:
eṣa yogavidhiḥ ko 'pi kasyāpi hṛdi vartate /
yasya prasīdec ciccakraṃ drāg apaścimajanmanaḥ // [AgMsv_2.141]

mv-k09-v1211.plain_english: Even while being seen by people and remaining in the condition of bodily bondage, when yoga has matured he attains in an instant an incomparable awareness.
mv-k09-v1211.sanskrit_cite:
lokenālokyamāno 'pi dehabandhavidhau sthitaḥ /
abhyeti yoge rūḍhe na kṣaṇāt kām api saṃvidam // [AgMsv_2.142]

mv-k09-v1212.plain_english: But right here, the intellect of our earlier teachers strongly affirmed the non-presence of the delusions of worldly experience.
mv-k09-v1212.sanskrit_cite:
atraiva tv asmatpūrvācāryāṇāṃ dhiṣaṇā bhṛśam /
abhyamaṃsta bhavābhogavibhramāṇām asaṃnidhim // [AgMsv_2.143]

mv-k09-v1213.plain_english: Enough with the Vedic, Samkhya, dualist, logical, Buddhist, and worldly views, and with Pancaratra, ritual scriptures, Siddhanta, and the rest.

mv-k09-v1214.plain_english: All those various practitioners, cultivating the fitting portions of knowledge and action and established in their own procedures, act according to what is appropriate for them.
mv-k09-v1214.sanskrit_cite:
ucitocitavijñānakriyāṃśaparibhāvakaiḥ /
sarvaiḥ svaprakriyārūḍhais tais tair aucityayogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.145]

mv-k09-v1215.plain_english: Where the very extensive sequence of acts such as sowing, implanting, and digging was carried out by the many branches of the Shambhava teaching.

mv-k09-v1216.plain_english: The unsurpassed fruit of that tree of consciousness-Bhairava is this, beyond practices such as life-stage observances and even ascetic marks like matted hair and ointments.
mv-k09-v1216.sanskrit_cite:
tasya cidbhairavataroḥ phalam etad anuttaram /
āśramasthitacaryādyair jaṭājālāñjanāntakaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.147]

mv-k09-v1217.plain_english: Where no difference is found between what is done and what is not done, for those who rest in that very yoga the pageantry of worldly existence dissolves.
mv-k09-v1217.sanskrit_cite:
kṛtair apy akṛtair vāpi yatra no labhyate bhidā /
tatraiva yoge viśrāntiṃ kurvatāṃ bhavaḍambaraḥ // [AgMsv_2.148]

mv-k09-v1218.plain_english: Like a mass of snow in the great summer, it melts away by itself; for when this juicy nectar of awareness is savored, that is enough.
mv-k09-v1218.sanskrit_cite:
himānīva mahāgrīṣme svayam eva pralīyate /
alaṃ hi carvyamāṇe 'smin sarase saṃvidāsave // [AgMsv_2.149]

mv-k09-v1219.plain_english: Great raptures flow forth, of which there is no number; their manifestations were already set out at length before, but here in Abhinavagupta's treatment only some are definitively stated.
mv-k09-v1219.sanskrit_cite:
nissaranti mahollāsāḥ saṃkhyā yeṣu na vidyate /
teṣāṃ ca prakaṭīkārāḥ kṛtāḥ prāg eva vistarāt /
atrābhinavagupte tu tattve ke 'py eva niścitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.150]

mv-k09-v1220.plain_english: In the rich fragrance of the ketaki flower, the bee alone is the connoisseur, not the fly; likewise, in the worship of the supreme nondual Bhairava, some rare one delights, not one deluded by duality.
mv-k09-v1220.sanskrit_cite:
ketakīkusumasaurabhe bhṛśaṃ \ \ bhṛṅga eva rasiko na makṣikā /
bhairavīyaparamādvayārcane \ \ ko 'pi rajyati na bhedamohitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.151]

mv-k09-v1221.plain_english: For one established here, no purification of any kind would need to be done anywhere; for what in the world, whose very nature is Bhairava, could be impure?
mv-k09-v1221.sanskrit_cite:
nātra rūḍhasya kāryā syāc chuddhiḥ kācana kutracit /
aśuddhaṃ hi jagaty eva bhairavātmani kiṃ bhavet // [AgMsv_2.152]

mv-k09-v1222.plain_english: And even if the mass of beings were impure, by what means could purification be effected? In that way there would be infinite regress and likewise a futile mutual dependence.
mv-k09-v1222.sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhe 'pi ca bhūtaughe kena śuddhiḥ pratāyatām /
anavasthā bhaved itthaṃ vyarthānyonyāśritis tathā // [AgMsv_2.153]

mv-k09-v1223.plain_english: When the impure is concealed, what is called the pure dissolves as well; for that is constituted by its opposite and is not established by its own nature, like blue.
mv-k09-v1223.sanskrit_cite:
aśuddhasya tirodhāne śuddhaṃ nāma pralīyate /
pratiyogikṛtaṃ tad dhi na svabhāvena nīlavat // [AgMsv_2.154]

mv-k09-v1224.plain_english: Therefore there is no insistence at all on either grasping or rejecting sense objects; for one whose nature is the consciousness of supreme Bhairava, enjoyership surges forth by itself.
mv-k09-v1224.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva na kaścid āgraho \ \ viṣayāṇāṃ grahaṇe 'py apohane /
parabhairavasaṃvidātmanaḥ \ \ svayam evocchalitā hi bhoktṛtā // [AgMsv_2.155]

mv-k09-v1225.plain_english: Since everything established here fits together by this path, the whole system is coherent. If one rejects this path, surely no other approach attains any coherence at all.
mv-k09-v1225.sanskrit_cite:
sarvam atra vihitaṃ yato 'munā \ \ vartmanā sakalam eva yujyate /
mārgam evam apahastya kiṃcana \ \ kāpi naiva nanu yāti yuktatām // [AgMsv_2.156]

mv-k09-v1226.plain_english: For example, initiation is that which cuts away impurities; but how can this possibly be explained in the view of those who assert difference?
mv-k09-v1226.sanskrit_cite:
tathāhi dīkṣā nāmeyaṃ yā malānāṃ nikartanī /
sa bhedavādināṃ pakṣe kathaṃ nāmopapadyate // [AgMsv_2.157]

mv-k09-v1227.plain_english: For how can the so-called impurity cover a self whose nature is consciousness? And where is there any act of covering for an all-pervading being?
mv-k09-v1227.sanskrit_cite:
tathāhi yo malo nāma sa kathaṃ citsvabhāvakam /
ātmānam āvṛṇīte kva vibhor āvaraṇakriyā // [AgMsv_2.158]

mv-k09-v1228.plain_english: Light is never covered by darkness, because the very arising of light is an act that destroys darkness.
mv-k09-v1228.sanskrit_cite:
na ca prakāśas tamasā jātu saṃvriyate yataḥ /
prakāśodaya evāyaṃ dhvāntadhvaṃsakriyātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_2.159]

mv-k09-v1229.plain_english: Moreover, covering is said to be an obstruction of something that moves, like rays; so how could that apply to an all-pervading being that has no motion?
mv-k09-v1229.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cāvaraṇam uktaṃ hi raśmyāder gatidharmiṇaḥ /
pratīghātātmakaṃ tat kiṃ vibhor agatidharmiṇaḥ // [AgMsv_2.160]

mv-k09-v1230.plain_english: Or else, covering is merely the concealment of knowability, as when a pot is covered by a cloth; it is not an alteration of its own nature.
mv-k09-v1230.sanskrit_cite:
api vā jñeyatāmātratirodhānaṃ hi saṃvṛteḥ /
paṭādinā ghaṭādeḥ syān na svarūpānyathāsthitiḥ // [AgMsv_2.161]

mv-k09-v1231.plain_english: But selves, because they are of the nature of consciousness, do not admit knowability; so to speak of their being covered is not fitting even in words.
mv-k09-v1231.sanskrit_cite:
na cātmānaś cidātmatvāj jñeyatvam adhiśerate /
tadāvaraṇam eṣāṃ tu śabdeṣv api na śobhate // [AgMsv_2.162]

mv-k09-v1232.plain_english: But surely, one objects, those atomic selves are knowable to the Lord. How so? For what is of the nature of consciousness is not knowable, since that would conceal its conscious nature.
mv-k09-v1232.sanskrit_cite:
nanv īśvarasya te jñeyā aṇavaḥ katham īdṛśam /
cidātmakaṃ hi na jñeyaṃ cidātmatvatirohiteḥ // [AgMsv_2.163]

mv-k09-v1233.plain_english: The expression 'awareness is knowable' seems to recall its own fellow, the statement 'my mother is barren,' since both are self-contradictory.
mv-k09-v1233.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvij jñeyeti śabdo 'yaṃ vandhyā me jananītyadaḥ /
vākyaṃ smarayatīva svaṃ svātmasabrahmacāri yat // [AgMsv_2.164]

mv-k09-v1234.plain_english: Moreover, the Lord's omniscience would be impaired to that extent, because he would not know the covered atomic selves; yet there would be no harm to the selves themselves.
mv-k09-v1234.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃceśvarasya sārvajñyaṃ tāvatā pratihanyate /
āvṛtān vetti nāṇūn yan na tv eṣāṃ kācana kṣatiḥ // [AgMsv_2.165]

mv-k09-v1235.plain_english: But surely, when a blue object is uncovered the knower sees it, and when it is covered there is no seeing; likewise, one might say, an omniscient being covered by impurity would be obstructed.
mv-k09-v1235.sanskrit_cite:
nanv anāvaraṇe nīle jñātur āvaraṇe sati /
na darśanaṃ tathā bādhā na sarvajño malāvṛtaḥ // [AgMsv_2.166]

mv-k09-v1236.plain_english: Not so. In that case, a cloth obstructs the outgoing rays of sight, but there is no possibility of covering the knower himself.
mv-k09-v1236.sanskrit_cite:
maivaṃ tatra hi dṛgraśmīn gacchataḥ pratihanti tat /
paṭādi na tu vijñātur asty āvaraṇasaṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_2.167]

mv-k09-v1237.plain_english: It is clear that a non-pervading impurity cannot be the coverer of what is all-pervading; even in a pot, it would by its own nature make space non-empty only in a limited way.
mv-k09-v1237.sanskrit_cite:
malaś cāvyāpako vyāptur āvāraka iti sphuṭam /
ghaṭe 'pi vyomni saṃdadhyād aśūnyatvaṃ svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_2.168]

mv-k09-v1238.plain_english: And if impurity produces no effect because the self is not subject to modification, how can it be capable of covering? Surely, sir, what then?
mv-k09-v1238.sanskrit_cite:
ātmanaś cādhikāryatvān malaḥ kiṃcitkaro na cet /
katham āvaraṇāyaiṣa śakto nanu ca bhoḥ kimu // [AgMsv_2.169]

mv-k09-v1239.plain_english: Indeed, its covering is said to be merely the existence of impurity; the atomic self is described as covered simply because it has impurity as a second.
mv-k09-v1239.sanskrit_cite:
malasadbhāvamātraṃ hi tasyāvaraṇam ucyate /
malena sadvitīyo 'ṇur āvṛtaḥ paribhāṣyate // [AgMsv_2.170]

mv-k09-v1240.plain_english: Alas, by this reasoning, even for those of the stated nature there would truly be a covering of Shiva, merely from the existence of impurity.
mv-k09-v1240.sanskrit_cite:
hantānena nayenaiṣa śivam uktātmanām api /
sthitam āvaraṇaṃ satyaṃ malasadbhāvamātrataḥ // [AgMsv_2.171]

mv-k09-v1241.plain_english: Moreover, if the self covered by impurity does not even know the impurity, then in that non-awareness of it, is another impurity to be posited?
mv-k09-v1241.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃcāvṛto malenātmā malam eva na vetti kim /
tadasaṃvedane tasya kiṃ malāntaram ucyate // [AgMsv_2.172]

mv-k09-v1242.plain_english: But what of it? Let it know the impurity. Then, without vidya and kala, there would be omniscience; and if the impurity were known, the self could abandon it by various contrived means.
mv-k09-v1242.sanskrit_cite:
nanv ataḥ kiṃ malaṃ vettu tarhi vidyākale vinā /
sarvajñatvaṃ bhavet tac ca malaṃ viditam eva sat // [AgMsv_2.173]

mv-k09-v1243.plain_english: Let the self abandon it by those various contrived means; and if so, what covering would that impurity produce in the self?
mv-k09-v1243.sanskrit_cite:
jahātv ātmābhyupāyais tais tair vicitraiḥ prakalpitaiḥ /
kiṃcāvaraṇam etena yasyātmani bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.174]

mv-k09-v1244.plain_english: How would this self come to be a knower and doer with respect to pots and such things? Surely, one replies, because vidya and kala are held to be the basis of limited knowing and doing.
mv-k09-v1244.sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭādau jñātṛkartṛtve katham asya bhaviṣyataḥ /
nanu vidyākale kiṃcijjñatvakartṛtvapade smṛte // [AgMsv_2.175]

mv-k09-v1245.plain_english: In this way the deluded are deceived, but not the wise: this maya is inert by nature, and kala and the rest are its offspring.
mv-k09-v1245.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ vimūḍhamatayo vañcyante na tu paṇḍitāḥ /
jaḍasvabhāvā māyaiṣā tatsūtiś ca kalādikaḥ // [AgMsv_2.176]

mv-k09-v1246.plain_english: How could what is non-conscious be capable of manifesting consciousness? And if all-pervading consciousness were manifested, how could it be qualified by limitedness and such attributes?
mv-k09-v1246.sanskrit_cite:
acidātmā kathaṃkāraṃ cidabhivyañjanakṣamaḥ /
abhivyaktā ca cidvibhvī kiṃcittvādiviśeṣaṇaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.177]

mv-k09-v1247.plain_english: How could it become qualified? For that is fitting only for things that have parts. But surely, one objects, God, using kala and vidya, could manifest consciousness.
mv-k09-v1247.sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣyatāṃ kathaṃ nāma sāṃśavastūcitaṃ hi tat /
nanu devaḥ kalāvidyākaraṇo vyañjayec citam // [AgMsv_2.178]

mv-k09-v1248.plain_english: Let him manifest it in all ways—alas, there is no incapacity in him. But if there is insistence on an eternal impurity, how will liberation ever come about?
mv-k09-v1248.sanskrit_cite:
vyanaktu sarvato hanta nāsyāśaktir athāgrahaḥ /
male sadātane cāsya kathaṃ muktir bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_2.179]

mv-k09-v1249.plain_english: The claim that impurity has an obstructing power which sometimes stops and sometimes acts is foolish talk.
mv-k09-v1249.sanskrit_cite:
roddhrī śaktir malasyāsti sā ca kvāpi nivartate /
kvāpi pravartate ceti dhig idaṃ mūḍhabhāṣitam // [AgMsv_2.180]

mv-k09-v1250.plain_english: Insentient things cannot deliberate, so how could that selective operation happen? If so, one must admit that God is the cause even in that case.
mv-k09-v1250.sanskrit_cite:
jaḍānāṃ ko 'nusandhiḥ syāt taṃ vinaitat kathaṃ bhavet /
atha tatrāpi devasya hetutābhyupagamyate // [AgMsv_2.181]

mv-k09-v1251.plain_english: For what reason would that God set that power in motion, or for what reason would he make it stop again once it has been set in motion?
mv-k09-v1251.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nimittam asau devas tāṃ śaktiṃ saṃpravartayet /
pravartitāṃ vā kiṃ nāma tāṃ nivartayate punaḥ // [AgMsv_2.182]

mv-k09-v1252.plain_english: If the answer is that God acts from autonomy, then let that plenitude alone be accepted. Why bring in impurity, which is of the nature of darkness, and why suppose any maturation of it at all?
mv-k09-v1252.sanskrit_cite:
svātantryād iti cet pūrṇaṃ tad evāśrīyate na kim /
malasya dhvāntarūpasya na ca pāko 'pi kaścana // [AgMsv_2.183]

mv-k09-v1253.plain_english: For maturation, by involving a connection with another state, would destroy mala's fixed nature. By this reasoning, the idea that a soul is impelled by God's will because of its connection with impurity is refuted.
mv-k09-v1253.sanskrit_cite:
sa hy anyatādānayogād dhanty amuṣya dhruvātmatām /
etena malasaṃbandhād īśvarecchāpracoditaḥ // [AgMsv_2.184]

mv-k09-v1254.plain_english: The claim that the bound soul, caught up in the desire for enjoyment, is favored by creation is struck at the root; that consequence follows from what has been shown.
mv-k09-v1254.sanskrit_cite:
bhogalobhakathāviṣṭaḥ paśuḥ sṛṣṭyānugṛhyate /
iti yad bhaṇyate mūlahataṃ taj, janitaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.185]

mv-k09-v1255.plain_english: They know impurity to be nothing but the mere play of concealing one's own self. For why would the autonomous, all-pervading Lord not manifest anything within himself?
mv-k09-v1255.sanskrit_cite:
svātmapracchādanakrīḍāmātram eva malaṃ viduḥ /
svatantro hi vibhuḥ kiṃcit kiṃ na svātmani bhāsayet // [AgMsv_2.186]

mv-k09-v1256.plain_english: And as for karma, which is also accepted, let that first be examined. For even if the connection with karma remains, how can there be such a state as the great dissolution?
mv-k09-v1256.sanskrit_cite:
yac ca karmāpi nāmeṣṭaṃ tattāvat pravicāryatām /
tathāhi karmasaṃbandhe sthite 'pi katham īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.187]

mv-k09-v1257.plain_english: How can there be a great dissolution, or a great creation? Surely, one may say, karma becomes restrained there by the will of God.
mv-k09-v1257.sanskrit_cite:
mahāpralaya ucyate mahāsṛṣṭiś ca vā katham /
nanv īśvarecchayā tatra karmāyāti niruddhatām // [AgMsv_2.188]

mv-k09-v1258.plain_english: Does the Lord do this through karma's inactivity, or by depending on another karma, or not? In the first alternative, that very possibility becomes an issue.
mv-k09-v1258.sanskrit_cite:
karmaudāsīnyayogena karmāntaram apekṣatām /
īśvaro 'tha navā pūrvapakṣe saṃbhava eva ca // [AgMsv_2.189]

mv-k09-v1259.plain_english: If that is impossible, in what respect could he possess sovereignty? Then all this—creation, dissolution, and the rest—would come about from karma alone.
mv-k09-v1259.sanskrit_cite:
nasaṃbhave sa kutrāṃśe caiśvaryam adhigacchatu /
karmataḥ sarvam evedaṃ syāt sṛṣṭipralayādikam // [AgMsv_2.190]

mv-k09-v1260.plain_english: But if, without depending on karma, he restrains karmas, then let the all-pervading Lord keep them restrained always.
mv-k09-v1260.sanskrit_cite:
atha karmānapekṣo vā karmaṇāṃ rodhanaṃ tataḥ /
sadā niruddhāny eveśaḥ karmāṇi kurutāṃ vibhuḥ // [AgMsv_2.191]

mv-k09-v1261.plain_english: But surely their nature is to produce enjoyment. How could that be an intrinsic nature if it has come to depend on another condition?
mv-k09-v1261.sanskrit_cite:
nanu teṣāṃ svabhāvo 'yaṃ yadbhogaprasavātmatā /
kathaṃ svabhāva eṣa syād yaḥ paropādhitāṃ gataḥ // [AgMsv_2.192]

mv-k09-v1262.plain_english: For the intrinsic nature of things is independent. Therefore, whatever form karmas have when they do not depend on the Lord's direction—that is their own true nature.
mv-k09-v1262.sanskrit_cite:
anapekṣo hi bhāvānāṃ svabhāvaḥ karmaṇāṃ tataḥ /
īśaiṣaṇānapekṣāṇāṃ yadrūpaṃ tatsvakaṃ vapuḥ // [AgMsv_2.193]

mv-k09-v1263.plain_english: And do the karmas dissolved in the great dissolution, or even those that still persist, get awakened by God? What, indeed, is accomplished by those karmas?
mv-k09-v1263.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ ca pralayalīnāni karmāṇi sthitibhāñjy api /
kiṃ prabodhayate devaḥ kiṃ nu dṛ[sṛ]ṣṭair hi taiḥ kṛtam // [AgMsv_2.194]

mv-k09-v1264.plain_english: If it is said to be for the maturation of impurity, that too has been thoroughly dismissed. And this self is all-pervading—what, indeed, can karma do to it?
mv-k09-v1264.sanskrit_cite:
malapākāya cet so 'pi sudūram apasāritaḥ /
kiṃ cātmā vibhur evaiṣa sa kiṃ nāma karoti hi // [AgMsv_2.195]

mv-k09-v1265.plain_english: This examination has already been elaborated at length. In the clay, stick, wheel, and threads, it is the intelligent Lord who stands as the true agent.
mv-k09-v1265.sanskrit_cite:
iti pūrvaṃ vicāraś ca vistareṇa prapañcitaḥ /
mṛddaṇḍacakrasūtreṣu dhīmān karteśvaraḥ sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.196]

mv-k09-v1266.plain_english: In what respect, indeed, does the potter's agency stand, especially in the sprouting and growth of seeds that have not been ploughed or cultivated?
mv-k09-v1266.sanskrit_cite:
kumbhakārasya kartṛtvaṃ kutrāṃśe nv avatiṣṭhatām /
akṛṣṭapacyabījeṣu prarohaprasavādike // [AgMsv_2.197]

mv-k09-v1267.plain_english: Let it be a cause earlier, but not in the crops—what principle is that? This is a bad deed and that a good deed, distinguished by the difference in their fruits.
mv-k09-v1267.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvaṃ karotu hetutvaṃ na sasyeṣv iti ko nayaḥ /
idaṃ duṣkṛtam etac ca sukṛtaṃ phalabhedataḥ // [AgMsv_2.198]

mv-k09-v1268.plain_english: If that division is made, does only his will unfold there? If he is autonomous, why would he adopt a will of his own that causes harm to others?
mv-k09-v1268.sanskrit_cite:
iti yat pravibhaktaṃ kiṃ tatrāsyecchaiva jṛmbhate /
svatantro yady asau kasmāt parapīḍākārīṃ nijām // [AgMsv_2.199]

mv-k09-v1269.plain_english: Why would he, who is always filled with compassion, adopt such a will? But surely, one may say, karma is such by its own nature and therefore gives those fruits.
mv-k09-v1269.sanskrit_cite:
icchāṃ gṛhṇāti yo nityaṃ karuṇārasanirbharaḥ /
nanu svabhāvāttattādṛk karmātaḥ phaladāyakam // [AgMsv_2.200]

mv-k09-v1270.plain_english: Considering that karma might be pacified through expiation and the like, God accordingly promulgates scripture that gives varied instruction.
mv-k09-v1270.sanskrit_cite:
prāyaścittādikaraṇāc chāmyec ceti vicārayan /
devas tathaiva tanute śāstraṃ citropadeśakam // [AgMsv_2.201]

mv-k09-v1271.plain_english: To say that the Śaiva teaching, or that karmas, are such by their own nature—what principle is that? People like us know that a seed has the nature of producing a sprout.
mv-k09-v1271.sanskrit_cite:
śaivaṃ, svabhāva edādṛk karmaṇām iti ko nayaḥ /
bījam aṅkurasaṃsūtisvabhāvam iti mādṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.202]

mv-k09-v1272.plain_english: People like us are able to know such things from the established usage of earlier generations. But the Lord, indeed, never acts without his own will.
mv-k09-v1272.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvavṛddhavyavahṛter vijñātuṃ prabhaviṣṇavaḥ /
īśvaras tu nijecchayā vinā na hi kadācana // [AgMsv_2.203]

mv-k09-v1273.plain_english: Having observed the intricate diversity of karmic fruits, if the Lord alone were the doer of everything, the group of individual selves could in no way be doers. But if they too are not doers, then, aiming at these beings barren of action, the Lord would not be the all-doer.
mv-k09-v1273.sanskrit_cite:
avalokitavān karmaphalavaicitryacāturīm /

tasmād devaḥ sarvakartā yadi syāt kartāraḥ syur nātmavargāḥ kathaṃcid /
no kartāras te 'pi cet karmavandhyān uddiśyainān sarvakartā na devaḥ // [AgMsv_2.204]

mv-k09-v1274.plain_english: Thus, from the standpoint of duality, this so-called karma is not well-reasoned. Here only a brief summary is given, while the fuller elaboration has been shown elsewhere.
mv-k09-v1274.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ca bhedadṛṣṭyedaṃ karma nāma na mu[yu]ktimat /
etāvān atra saṃkṣopo vyāso 'nyatra tu darśitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.205]

mv-k09-v1275.plain_english: The Lord is one, whose very nature is consciousness; therefore he is indeed the all-doer by his own nature. Because of diversity, he is spoken of as connected with karma.
mv-k09-v1275.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvedanātmako deva ekas tasmāt svataḥ khalu /
sarvakartā sa vaicitryāt karmayogīti bhaṇyate // [AgMsv_2.206]

mv-k09-v1276.plain_english: And that so-called Maya, which is established as the cause of the universe, containing within her womb the elements of the tattvas ending with earth—if she is clearly eternal...
mv-k09-v1276.sanskrit_cite:
māyā ca nāma viśvasya yā kāraṇam iti sthitā /
sā dharaṇyantatattvāṃśagarbhā nityā yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_2.207]

mv-k09-v1277.plain_english: Then dissolution would never occur. But surely it occurs through the state of manifestation? We do not recognize manifestation as such, because cognition consists in being an object of grasping.
mv-k09-v1277.sanskrit_cite:
pralayo na kadācit syān nanu sa vyaktibhāvataḥ /
vyaktiṃ nāma na jānīmo vijñānaṃ grāhyatā yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.208]

mv-k09-v1278.plain_english: Its being grasped by the Lord's supreme knowledge is everlasting. If that were absent, how could the Lord be the cause?
mv-k09-v1278.sanskrit_cite:
tadīśvaraparajñānagrāhyatāsti sadātanī /
tasyām avidyamānāyām īśvaraḥ kāraṇaṃ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_2.209]

mv-k09-v1279.plain_english: One might think it will be in the Lord as when someone clearly produces a pot. Not so, because of the distinction between inner and outer instruments.
mv-k09-v1279.sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭaṃ prakurute kumbhaṃ tadvad īśe bhaviṣyati /
maivam antarbahīrūpakaraṇapravibhedataḥ // [AgMsv_2.210]

mv-k09-v1280.plain_english: In the making of a pot, cognition that is clear, unclear, and so forth is fitting; but the Lord possesses a clear, noble, prior cognition.
mv-k09-v1280.sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭāsphuṭādivijñānaṃ yuktaṃ kumbhakṛti sphuṭam /
īśvarasya sphuṭodārapūrvavijñānaśālinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.211]

mv-k09-v1281.plain_english: What part would not be known, even where dependence on manifestation is assumed? In the view of the satkarya theorists, the universe is clearly established even in the cause.
mv-k09-v1281.sanskrit_cite:
ko na jñāto bhaved bhāgo yatrāpi vyaktyapekṣitā /
satkāryavādināṃ deśe kāraṇe 'pi sphuṭaṃ sthitam // [AgMsv_2.212]

mv-k09-v1282.plain_english: Thus, for the universe to be clearly present in Maya would be incongruous, since Siva and the selves are pervasive, together with the tattvas and mutually so.
mv-k09-v1282.sanskrit_cite:
viśvam ityapi māyāyāṃ sphuṭaṃ syād asamañjasam /
vyāpakāś ca śivātmānas tattvaiḥ sākaṃ parasparam // [AgMsv_2.213]

mv-k09-v1283.plain_english: And how indeed could they exist, given the concealment of pervasiveness? The supreme expansion of consciousness is its pervasion, and in division it is spoken of accordingly.
mv-k09-v1283.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ ca nāma vidyantāṃ vyāpakatvatirohiteḥ /
vikāsaḥ paramo vyāptiḥ saṃvido bheda ucyate // [AgMsv_2.214]

mv-k09-v1284.plain_english: The group of coverings born of Maya, as well as the collection of instruments, has already been examined before, and the group of effects has also been discussed.
mv-k09-v1284.sanskrit_cite:
māyīyaṃ kañcukavrātaṃ yathā karaṇasaṃcayaḥ /
vicāritaḥ pūrvam eva kāryavargaś ca carcitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.215]

mv-k09-v1285.plain_english: As long as the universe, devoid of resting on the state of Siva, does not shine forth, this is merely talk of its autonomy; let that be understood.
mv-k09-v1285.sanskrit_cite:
yāvac chivapadādhyāsavandhyaṃ viśvaṃ na visphuret /
tatsvātantryakathāmātram etad ity avadhāryatām // [AgMsv_2.216]

mv-k09-v1286.plain_english: Thus, in the absence of impurity and the like, what initiation could there be, who would be the initiator, and who the recipient? None of this fits.
mv-k09-v1286.sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ malādyabhāve hi kā dīkṣā ko hi dīkṣakaḥ /
dīkṣāpātraṃ ca ko vā syād iti kiṃcin na yujyate // [AgMsv_2.217]

mv-k09-v1287.plain_english: How could the installation of the entire path in the disciple, the path, the fire, the vessel, the mandala, the ladle, the hand, and so on, be possible?
mv-k09-v1287.sanskrit_cite:
śiṣye 'dhvany anale kumbhe maṇḍale srukkarādike /
samastādhvakṛto nyāsaḥ kathaṃ vāpy upapadyatām // [AgMsv_2.218]

mv-k09-v1288.plain_english: Surely they would not all be present in that way. But, one may object, by the power of conception this entire relation of purifier and purified has indeed been declared.
mv-k09-v1288.sanskrit_cite:
nahi tāvanta eva syur nanu saṃkalpanāvaśāt /
śodhyaśodhakabhāvo 'yaṃ sarva evodito nanu // [AgMsv_2.219]

mv-k09-v1289.plain_english: If what is merely imagined could bear fruit, then truly those who have gained riches in the kingdom of fantasy would triumph by attaining the repose of heavenly sovereignty.
mv-k09-v1289.sanskrit_cite:
kalpitaṃ cet phalet satyaṃ manorājyārjitaśriyaḥ /
jayanti nākasāmrājyalābhaviśrāntiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.220]

mv-k09-v1290.plain_english: Do states that follow the path of strong, vivid conception not bear fruit in that way, like the destruction of poison through meditation and the like?
mv-k09-v1290.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nāma balavadrūpasaṃkalpapathavartinaḥ /
phalanti na tathā bhāvā dhyānādiviṣanāśavat // [AgMsv_2.221]

mv-k09-v1291.plain_english: Meditation is precisely firmness of conception; but meditation tainted by doubt does not bear fruit at all, because it grasps two alternatives.
mv-k09-v1291.sanskrit_cite:
saṃkalpadārḍhyam ity eva dhyānaṃ saṃśayarūṣitam /
dhyānaṃ ca na phaled eva svayaṃ pakṣadvayāgrahāt // [AgMsv_2.222]

mv-k09-v1292.plain_english: Look—if its fruit were to arise from the application of conception, why would you desire some external entities that are not made of consciousness?
mv-k09-v1292.sanskrit_cite:
hanta saṃkalpanāyogād yadi jāyeta tatphalam /
kim asaṃvinmayān bhāvān bāhyān kāṃścit abhīpsasi // [AgMsv_2.223]

mv-k09-v1293.plain_english: By conception alone there is consecration pertaining to the pit, fire, guru, and disciple; and that same thing, appearing as the fruit, remains as that consciousness.
mv-k09-v1293.sanskrit_cite:
saṃkalpenaiva saṃskāraḥ kuṇḍāgniguruśiṣyagaḥ /
sa eva ca phalābhāsī tatsaṃvid avaśiṣyate // [AgMsv_2.224]

mv-k09-v1294.plain_english: And the manifestation in such a form of autonomous consciousness should indeed be understood as initiation, by which beings are liberated.
mv-k09-v1294.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaś ca svatantrāyās tathārūpāvabhāsanam /
dīkṣeti kila mantavyaṃ muñcyante jantavo yayā // [AgMsv_2.225]

mv-k09-v1295.plain_english: For that very reason, no sequence or fixed rule has been determined here in the scripture regarding the essential nature, taking, or measure of sesame, ghee, and the like.
mv-k09-v1295.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva tilājyādeḥ svarūpe grahaṇe mitau /
kramo vā niyamo neha kaścic chāstre nirūpitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.226]

mv-k09-v1296.plain_english: But surely, what fixed rule is there in mantras? For the supreme form is declared to partake of all letters; so how could initiation not be the same way?
mv-k09-v1296.sanskrit_cite:
nanu mantreṣu kiṃ nāma niyamaḥ sarvavarṇabhāk /
rūpaṃ paraṃ hi kathitaṃ dīkṣāpi na tathā katham // [AgMsv_2.227]

mv-k09-v1297.plain_english: Thus, the burning of letters as you approve it is indeed beneficial; but for those who have not yet attained firm establishment, a definite rule certainly applies to them.
mv-k09-v1297.sanskrit_cite:
evam evārṇadāhasya yadbhavatsaṃmataṃ hitam /
kiṃ tu tāvati ye rūḍhiṃ na prāptās tān prati dhruvam // [AgMsv_2.228]

mv-k09-v1298.plain_english: This mantric rule has been declared and it serves a real purpose, for those mantras are awakened and move along the path of reflective awareness.
mv-k09-v1298.sanskrit_cite:
māntro 'yaṃ niyamaḥ prokta upayogaṃ ca gacchati /
pratibuddhā hi te mantrā vimarśapathavartinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.229]

mv-k09-v1299.plain_english: Because the light of consciousness is autonomous, the mantras, made of agency, enter that very teacher through the application of identity with it.
mv-k09-v1299.sanskrit_cite:
svatantrasyaiva ciddhāmna svātantryāt kartṛtāmayāḥ /
mantrā viśanty evācāryaṃ taṃ tādātmyaniyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.230]

mv-k09-v1300.plain_english: They make him autonomous, and even instruments attain agency; thus, initiation and whatever other rites are accepted become possible.
mv-k09-v1300.sanskrit_cite:
svatantrīkurvate yānti karaṇāny api kartṛtām /
itthaṃ dīkṣādividhaye ye 'py anye vidhayo matāḥ // [AgMsv_2.231]

mv-k09-v1301.plain_english: What, indeed, is to be done by those who act, and how could there even be prohibition? Both are established right here, for all of that is enjoined here.
mv-k09-v1301.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ nāma kurvatāṃ kṛtyaṃ niṣedhaṃ tv api vā katham /
te 'py atraivopapadyante tat sarvaṃ vihitaṃ tv iha // [AgMsv_2.232]

mv-k09-v1302.plain_english: And all this is prohibited only from that other standpoint; for when its prohibition is clearly shown, what force does it have for one who rests on the nondual path?
mv-k09-v1302.sanskrit_cite:
sarvaṃ caitad amutraiva pratiṣiddhaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam /
pratiṣedhe darśite 'sya kiṃ cādvaitapathāśritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.233]

mv-k09-v1303.plain_english: Even prohibition is enjoined, and that too is prohibited; thus the ocean of one's own awareness surges abundantly within itself.
mv-k09-v1303.sanskrit_cite:
pratiṣedho 'pi vihitaḥ so 'pi ca pratiṣidhyate /
itthaṃ svasaṃvidambhodhiḥ svātmani procchalaty alam // [AgMsv_2.234]

mv-k09-v1304.plain_english: Thus this entire universe is beautiful with the bliss of the world, and in this way it utterly dissolves the opposing element of difference.
mv-k09-v1304.sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ca viśvam evedaṃ jagadānandasundaram /
tadvipakṣaṃ ca bhedāṃśam itthaṃ kṣapayatetarām // [AgMsv_2.235]

mv-k09-v1305.plain_english: From the moon of knowledge risen from the mouth of the Supreme Lord, beautiful rays radiant with the fullness of their own light spread in all directions.

mv-k09-v1306.plain_english: The deadly poison that darkens the moon of all beings, melted by the mere touch of the mass of rays from Shiva's moon, turns into an elixir.

mv-k09-v1307.plain_english: Plunging there unceasingly and reeling from drinking that essence, we become that essence itself and abide pure, freed from the three kinds of suffering.
mv-k09-v1307.sanskrit_cite:
tatrāniśaṃ nimajjantas tadrasāpānaghūrṇitāḥ /
tadrasībhūya tiṣṭhāmaḥ śuddhās tāpatrayojjhitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.238]

mv-k09-v1308.plain_english: The mouth of the Supreme Lord is said to be his power, namely will; having arisen, that will takes on the functioning of the moon of knowledge in the distinct states beginning with Īśvara.
mv-k09-v1308.sanskrit_cite:
parameśamukhaṃ tu śaktir uktā bhavatīcchā nanu sodbhavaṃ gatā /
pratipadyata īśvarādibhinnasthitivijñānaśaśāṅkaśaktivṛttam // [AgMsv_2.239]

mv-k09-v1309.plain_english: The fully spread mass of rays streaming forth on all sides from that moon is indeed the Supreme Lord's own power, declared to consist of action and to be made of the world.
mv-k09-v1309.sanskrit_cite:
śaśinaḥ kila tasya sarvato yaḥ paripūrṇaḥ prasṛto marīcipuñjaḥ /
iyam eva hi sā kriyātmikoktā parameśasya jaganmayī svaśaktiḥ // [AgMsv_2.240]

mv-k09-v1310.plain_english: Thus this, full of the three powers, expands as the supreme Bhairava alone; nothing different from it could exist, and its own expansion is proclaimed as its victory.
mv-k09-v1310.sanskrit_cite:
tad idaṃ trikaśaktinirbharaṃ paramaṃ bhairavam eva jṛmbhate /
na tu tadvyatireki saṃbhavet svavijṛmbhā vijayo 'sya kīrtitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.241]

mv-k09-v1311.plain_english: From that very reality these powers clearly conquer the world; the meaning becomes manifest and fits for us, since such a connection with many expressions belongs to that fullness and accommodates the division of statements.
mv-k09-v1311.sanskrit_cite:
tata eva jagaj jayanty amī sphuṭam arthaḥ prakaṭo 'pi yujyate naḥ /
bahuvācakayoga īdṛśaṃ tat paripūrṇatvam amuṣya vākyabhedam // [AgMsv_2.242]

mv-k09-v1312.plain_english: Thus this single verse clearly explains Bhairava himself, whose nature is consciousness, full of the entire sequence of all beings.
mv-k09-v1312.sanskrit_cite:
ity eka eva śloko 'yaṃ cidātmā bhairavaḥ svayam /
samastabhāvasaṃdarbhanirbharo vyākṛtaḥ sphuṭam // [AgMsv_2.243]

mv-k09-v1313.plain_english: For the destruction of the poison of worldly existence, those whose vision is empowered by Garuda employ poison itself and attain an immortal state.
mv-k09-v1313.sanskrit_cite:
saṃsāragaranāśāya tārkṣyādhiṣṭhitadṛṣṭayaḥ /
viṣam evopayuñjānāḥ prāpnuvanty amṛtīṃ sthitim // [AgMsv_2.244]

mv-k09-v1314.plain_english: Thus it has been shown to this extent: by self-luminous own-awareness everything is established, and apart from that nothing at all is possible.
mv-k09-v1314.sanskrit_cite:
iti darśitam etāvat svaprakāśasvasaṃvidā /
siddhaṃ tadvyatirekeṇa na kiṃcid eva kalpate // [AgMsv_2.245]

mv-k09-v1315.plain_english: Whatever rests in own-awareness is real to that very extent; for if reality depended on another time, it could not be real anywhere.
mv-k09-v1315.sanskrit_cite:
yāvatsvasaṃvidviśrāntaṃ yat tāvat tat sad eva hi /
kālāntaravyapekṣe hi satyatvaṃ syān na kutracit // [AgMsv_2.246]

mv-k09-v1316.plain_english: The connection of awareness with time has been refuted at length; therefore own-awareness functions just as it spreads out space.
mv-k09-v1316.sanskrit_cite:
saṃvidaḥ kālayogaś ca vistareṇa nivāritaḥ /
tat svasaṃvid yathā deśaṃ vitared vartate tathā // [AgMsv_2.247]

mv-k09-v1317.plain_english: Likewise, whatever cannot be placed on the touchstone of awareness is fit only for doubt; even in scripture that is called unreal.
mv-k09-v1317.sanskrit_cite:
tathā saṃvidy akṣamayyāṃ nikaṣāśmani ropitam /
na yat tat saṃśayāyaiva śāstre 'py uktam avastu tat // [AgMsv_2.248]

mv-k09-v1318.plain_english: What does not rise to own-awareness is no different from idle talk; that alone is scripture and that alone is method which unfolds within awareness.
mv-k09-v1318.sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid anupārohi pralāpān na viśiṣyate /
tac cchāstraṃ prakriyā sā ca yat saṃvidi vivartate // [AgMsv_2.249]

mv-k09-v1319.plain_english: All these risings and settings of the whole world arise from the heart, like a dream from deep sleep, and are examined by the scripture of own-awareness.
mv-k09-v1319.sanskrit_cite:
hṛdayāj jagato jātāḥ sarvasyaite kṣayodayāḥ /
svapnasyeva suṣuptākhyāt svasaṃvicchāstracarcitāḥ // [AgMsv_2.250]

mv-k09-v1320.plain_english: The totality of form, light, and attention; withdrawal, maintenance, and creation; closing and opening; and the construction of contraction in beings — all these are its operations.
mv-k09-v1320.sanskrit_cite:
rūpālokamanaskārasāmagrī saṃhṛtiḥ sthitiḥ /
sṛṣṭir nimeṣonmeṣau ca satāṃ saṃkocakalpanam // [AgMsv_2.251]

mv-k09-v1321.plain_english: Such an abiding state, having the form of knower, known, and knowing, is always the spontaneous fashioning of the manifold world by perfectly full own-consciousness.
mv-k09-v1321.sanskrit_cite:
ityādikā mātṛmeyamānarūpā sthitiḥ sadā /
svasaṃvidaḥ supūrṇāyāḥ prapañcaracanā svayam // [AgMsv_2.252]

mv-k09-v1322.plain_english: She indeed is by herself the form of all, of all selves, directions, places, and times; and from her alone arises the determination of what is true and what is false.
mv-k09-v1322.sanskrit_cite:
sarvasarvātmadigdeśakālākārā svayaṃ hi sā /
satyamithyātvanirṇītis tata eva hi jāyate // [AgMsv_2.253]

mv-k09-v1323.plain_english: Teacher Utpaladeva also taught this very thing: even what appears outside as being or nonbeing is, in own-consciousness, my seeing.
mv-k09-v1323.sanskrit_cite:
ācāryotpaladevo 'pi tadetadupadiṣṭavān /
bahiḥ sadasadātmāpi svasaṃvidi madīyadṛk // [AgMsv_2.254]

mv-k09-v1324.plain_english: The regulation of the autonomous, expressed as 'let it see' and called together with the senses, is that very consciousness which, ascending from Shiva down to the worm, rests upon its own awareness.
mv-k09-v1324.sanskrit_cite:
paśyatv iti svatantrasya niyatiḥ sendriyābhidhā /
saiva rūdhā śivād ā ca krimeḥ svāṃ saṃvidaṃ śritā // [AgMsv_2.255]

mv-k09-v1325.plain_english: That very same reality is worldly bondage, and it is Shiva, the supreme lord; one who has attained rest in it is called liberated.
mv-k09-v1325.sanskrit_cite:
tad eva deve saṃsāraḥ sa śivaḥ parameīŭvaraḥ /
tatra viśrāntim āpanno mukta ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_2.256]

mv-k09-v1326.plain_english: By the grace of this, all beings from Brahma down to the immobile live; let this consciousness be understood as always unobscured.
mv-k09-v1326.sanskrit_cite:
etatprasādāj jīvanti brahmādyāḥ sthāvarāntakāḥ /
aviluptā sadā seyaṃ saṃvittir iti gṛhyatām // [AgMsv_2.257]

mv-k09-v1327.plain_english: Even while shining forth, that goddess never establishes a self anywhere as devoid of her; in one place she may establish it, in another fault it, in another do otherwise.
mv-k09-v1327.sanskrit_cite:
vibhānty api hi sā devī na tayā rahitaṃ kvacit /
ātmānaṃ sādhayet kvāpi kvāpi dūṣayate kvacit // [AgMsv_2.258]

mv-k09-v1328.plain_english: She places things otherwise, yet she does not undergo change; even while barren of establishing, faulting, and otherness, she remains the supreme goddess.
mv-k09-v1328.sanskrit_cite:
anyathaiva sthāpayate na ca yāti vikāritām /
sādhandūṣaṇānyatvavandhyāpi parameśvarī // [AgMsv_2.259]

mv-k09-v1329.plain_english: And she shines clearly in that very way, autonomous indeed; she is the glorious great lord, the god who is the teacher even of those who came before.
mv-k09-v1329.sanskrit_cite:
bhāsate ca tathātvena tat svatantrā sphuṭā hi sā /
śrīmān maheśvaro devaḥ pūrveṣām api yo guruḥ // [AgMsv_2.260]

mv-k09-v1330.plain_english: He proclaimed this for the grace of the world: 'Deluded ones, why do you abide in vain in essenceless speech like the cawing of crows? Honoring your own consciousness, all who respect what is instructed even nearby by the goddess-consciousness become liberated while living, in whatever place they are.'
mv-k09-v1330.sanskrit_cite:
sa etad eva provāca lokānugrahahetutaḥ /

mūḍhāḥ kiṃ niḥsāre vāyasaviraṭitakalpe tiṣṭatha vacasi vṛthaivaṃ svāṃ saṃvidam āvarjya /
saṃviddevatayaiva yad ādiṣṭaṃ nikaṭe 'py atha sarva ādriyamāṇās tattaddeśe jīvanmuktā bhavanti // [AgMsv_2.261]

mv-k09-v1331.plain_english: Therefore, in this guiding principle, consciousness alone is called the teacher, because it indeed swallows the universe through creation and dissolution.
mv-k09-v1331.sanskrit_cite:
tad atra nītau saṃvittir evāsau gurur ucyate /
giraty eva yato viśvaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃhṛtiyogataḥ // [AgMsv_2.262]

mv-k09-v1332.plain_english: Therefore, here the primary firm relation is called the supreme one; whatever knowledge is instructed through it is indeed innately accomplished.
mv-k09-v1332.sanskrit_cite:
tad atra mukhyā yā rūḍhiḥ saṃbandhaḥ para ucyate /
enayā yad yad ādiṣṭaṃ jñānaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ tu tat // [AgMsv_2.263]

mv-k09-v1333.plain_english: Where the eternal abiding of our lineage of teachers is established, from there proceeds the division of the transmission beginning with Tryambaka.
mv-k09-v1333.sanskrit_cite:
yatrāsmadguruvargasya sthitā nityāvasthitiḥ /
traiyambakādisaṃtānabhedo yasmāt pravartate // [AgMsv_2.264]

mv-k09-v1334.plain_english: Where it was previously said that identity with ignorance perishes, this world shines forth from the variety grasped by own-consciousness.
mv-k09-v1334.sanskrit_cite:
yatroktaṃ pūrvam ajñānatādātmyaṃ naśyatītyapi /
svasaṃvidas tu vaicitryaṃ gṛhṇatyā bhāty ayaṃ tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.265]

mv-k09-v1335.plain_english: The confluence of scriptures—intermediate, great-divine, divine, and so forth—consists of the rays of the teacher's own true speech, fashioned by his own self.

mv-k09-v1336.plain_english: The primacy of own-consciousness is manifest—whether from the teacher, from scripture, or from oneself; therefore this effort has been made with that as primary.
mv-k09-v1336.sanskrit_cite:
prādhānyaṃ prakaṭaṃ svasaṃvidaḥ /
gurutaḥ kila śāstrataḥ svataḥ /
tad ayaṃ mukhyatayā kṛtaḥ śramaḥ // [AgMsv_2.267]

mv-k09-v1337.plain_english: The teacher depends on the operation of scripture, and that is established in one's own self-consciousness; therefore all this attains accomplishment through self-consciousness and is never obstructed.
mv-k09-v1337.sanskrit_cite:
śāstravṛttiparatantrito guruḥ svātmasaṃvidi ca tatpratiṣṭhitam /
tena sarvam idam ātmasaṃvidā siddhim eti nahi jātv asahyatām // [AgMsv_2.268]

mv-k09-v1338.plain_english: O seekers of liberation, let this scripture be practiced with effort; do not let life be spent in vain, strained over other scriptures.
mv-k09-v1338.sanskrit_cite:
etac chāstraṃ prayatnena carcyatāṃ he mumukṣavaḥ /
mā vṛthaivāyur āyastam anyaśāstreṣu nīyatām // [AgMsv_2.269]

mv-k09-v1339.plain_english: Whatever view of non-difference or view of difference there may be, it comes to fulfillment here alone; therefore let this be carefully examined.
mv-k09-v1339.sanskrit_cite:
abhedadṛṣṭir yā kācid bhedadṛṣṭir athāpi vā /
sātraivāyāti nirvāhaṃ tenaitat pravicāryatām // [AgMsv_2.270]

mv-k09-v1340.plain_english: Just as one is freed from sleep by recognizing the dream state, so one whose heart is awakened by sustained practice of this scripture remains always awake.

mv-k09-v1341.plain_english: Own-consciousness indeed is that scripture, and she is free from dependence; if it is to be stated thus, let its authoritativeness be said to be from itself.
mv-k09-v1341.sanskrit_cite:
svasaṃvid eva tac chāstraṃ sā cāpekṣāvivarjitā /
tathā yady abhidhīyeta svataḥ prāmāṇyam ucyatām // [AgMsv_2.272]

mv-k09-v1342.plain_english: Teaching, what is to be taught, and the teacher—this triad, in that state, is not measured by time and is beautiful with freedom and nonduality.
mv-k09-v1342.sanskrit_cite:
śāsanaṃ śāsitavyaṃ ca śāsakaṃ ceti yat kila /
tattatrākālakalitaṃ svātantryādvaitasundaram // [AgMsv_2.273]

mv-k09-v1343.plain_english: Having internalized that intrinsic, never-departing state, lord Shrikantha proclaimed it in the glorious Kirana scripture.
mv-k09-v1343.sanskrit_cite:
tām avasthitim ātmīyāṃ garbhīkṛtyānapāyinīm /
śrīkaṇṭhanāthaḥ provāca śrīmatkiraṇaśāsane // [AgMsv_2.274]

mv-k09-v1344.plain_english: All this is for the sake of engaging hearers through differentiation; but this difference, arising from difference of meaning, is constructed only by metaphorical usage.
mv-k09-v1344.sanskrit_cite:
sarvam etat pravṛttyarthaṃ śrot\rr ṇāṃ tu vibhedataḥ /
arthabhedāt tu bhedo 'yam upacārāt prakalpate // [AgMsv_2.275]

mv-k09-v1345.plain_english: No difference of fruit should be assumed here in the Lord's teaching; if one were assumed, it would be a false assumption, making this teaching of the Lord appear divided by distinctions of ten, eighteen, eight, and eight.
mv-k09-v1345.sanskrit_cite:
phalabhedo na kalpyo 'tra kalpyaś ced ayathātatham /
daśakāṣṭādaśāṣṭāṣṭabhedabhinnam idaṃ vibhoḥ // [AgMsv_2.276]

mv-k09-v1346.plain_english: This teaching has the single fruit of attaining the state of being Śiva, and it applies to the qualified individual soul who is eager for that attainment, without regard for birth, family, caste, and the like.

mv-k09-v1347.plain_english: As long as this teaching, once set forth, maintains its unity of discourse, the wise know it as one, even though there is variety in the functions of its subsidiary and principal parts.
mv-k09-v1347.sanskrit_cite:
pravṛttam ekavākyatvaṃ yāvad āsādya vartate /
aṅgāṅgivṛttavaicitryāt tāvad ekam idaṃ viduḥ // [AgMsv_2.278]

mv-k09-v1348.plain_english: The Trika scripture, the teacher who is of that nature and nondual here, and the collection of its subsequent textual portions and sections all belong to the same unified framework.
mv-k09-v1348.sanskrit_cite:
trikaśāstraṃ tathābhūto gurur atrādvayātmakaḥ /
tadanantaravākyāṃśapuñjaḥ prakaraṇāni ca // [AgMsv_2.279]

mv-k09-v1349.plain_english: Even when the accounts of differences produced by māyā become clear, the attainment of Śiva remains established as the primary and final fruit.
mv-k09-v1349.sanskrit_cite:
māyīyabhedavṛttāntasphuṭabhāve bhavanti ca /
tathāpi śivasaṃprāptir mukhyam ante phalaṃ sthitam // [AgMsv_2.280]

mv-k09-v1350.plain_english: The qualified person is truly one, the recipient of attaining Śiva-hood; even when the teaching appears only in limited sectional form, that single qualification and attainment remain.
mv-k09-v1350.sanskrit_cite:
adhikārī caika eva śivatāvāptibhājanam /
tathāpi tāvanmātre ca jāte prakaraṇātmani // [AgMsv_2.281]

mv-k10-v1351.plain_english: The fruit may be clear and primary, or it may be the final result; it may belong to the main element or to an auxiliary; and it may appear in its opposite, in another side, or in some other opposing condition.
mv-k10-v1351.sanskrit_cite:
yādṛk phalaṃ sphutaṃ mukhyaṃ paryantaphalam aṅgi vā /
tadaṅgaṃ vā tadvipakṣe parapakṣe paraṃ ca vā // [AgMsv_2.282]

mv-k10-v1352.plain_english: Even one who becomes a vessel for manifesting aspects of various opposites is affected by having a suitable body and by sharing in the proper preparatory conditioning.

mv-k10-v1353.plain_english: Such a sequence of qualification is declared for both teacher and student, just as in the case of someone who undertakes the procedure of the death-destroying elixir.
mv-k10-v1353.sanskrit_cite:
guroḥ śiṣyasya cāpy uktas tādṛśo 'dhikriyākramaḥ /
tathā ca mṛtyuvidhvaṃsirasāyanavidhiṃ śritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.284]

mv-k10-v1354.plain_english: First, for the sake of gaining the proper preparation, one uses decoction, emesis, and purgation; and the alteration brought about by initiation should not occur later during the ritual procedure.
mv-k10-v1354.sanskrit_cite:
pūrvaṃ saṃskāralābhāya kvāthavāntivirecanaiḥ /
dīkṣayā yā ca vikṛtiḥ nottaratra kriyāvidhau // [AgMsv_2.285]

mv-k10-v1355.plain_english: Therefore the restriction of qualification arises from factors such as one's body and knowledge; for this reason Vaishnavas and others, who depend on the discipline of bound souls, are spoken of as limited in that way.

mv-k10-v1356.plain_english: They are not qualified in the Shaiva scripture; Shaivas are not qualified in the left sphere; those are not qualified in the right; and those are not qualified in the Kula doctrine or in the Trika.
mv-k10-v1356.sanskrit_cite:
na śaive 'dhikṛtās tantre na śaivā vāmagocare /
te 'pi no dakṣiṇe te 'pi na syuḥ kulamate trike // [AgMsv_2.287]

mv-k10-v1357.plain_english: It is said in the revered Bhairava Kula that the teacher fit for the rite of the five initiations is one who has transcended the lower streams or who is grounded in the Trika scripture.
mv-k10-v1357.sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ śrībhairavakule pañcadīkṣākriyocitaḥ /
gurur ullaṅghitādhastyasrotā vā trikaśāstragaḥ // [AgMsv_2.288]

mv-k10-v1358.plain_english: Thus there is a single qualification insofar as all rely on the self-principle, yet qualification becomes differentiated because of differences in preparation.
mv-k10-v1358.sanskrit_cite:
ittham ekādhikāritvam ātmatattvasamāśrayāt /
saṃskārāśraya .... bhedād bhinnādhikāritā // [AgMsv_2.289]

mv-k10-v1359.plain_english: Therefore it is said in the Svacchanda Tantra that in every scripture Shiva is the fruit, because all arise from Shiva and all have Shiva's abode as their fruit.
mv-k10-v1359.sanskrit_cite:
svacchandatantre tenoktaṃ sarvaśāstre śivaḥ phalam /
yataḥ śivodbhavāḥ sarve śivadhāmaphalā iti // [AgMsv_2.290]

mv-k10-v1360.plain_english: And there again it is declared, in the discussion of the higher principles: what is not known by the Samkhyas, not by the great yogins, and not, O beloved, by the Pancharatrikas.
mv-k10-v1360.sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva ca punaḥ proktam ūrdhvatattvavivecane /
yan na sāṃkhyair na yogīndrair na priye pāñcarātrikaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.291]

mv-k10-v1361.plain_english: Thus, as many as three hundred and sixty-three disputants are challenged, for they discriminate only within that limited measure.
mv-k10-v1361.sanskrit_cite:
iyādi yāvad ākṣiptaṃ vādināṃ tu śatatrayam /
triṣaṣṭyā cādhikaṃ te hi tāvanmātravivecakāḥ // [AgMsv_2.292]

mv-k10-v1362.plain_english: How could they be knowers whose very nature is knowledge of the unlimited Shiva principle? Now suppose they posit the presence of Shiva even in that mere partial portion.
mv-k10-v1362.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ syur aparicchinnaśivatattvavidātmakāḥ /
atha tatrāṃśamātre 'pi śivasadbhāvam eva te // [AgMsv_2.293]

mv-k10-v1363.plain_english: If they were to superimpose that, it would not be clearly coherent; for in a sentence like 'Devadatta,' the reference is to a complete form in every respect.
mv-k10-v1363.sanskrit_cite:
āropayeyus tat tāvan naiva suspaṣṭasaṃgati /
devadattādivākye hi sarvataḥ pūrṇavigrahe // [AgMsv_2.294]

mv-k10-v1364.plain_english: How could someone who hears only the word 'Devadatta' superimpose upon that limited word the meaning of entire previous sentences?
mv-k10-v1364.sanskrit_cite:
devadattapadaśrotā tāvanmātrapade katham /
samagrapūrvavākyānāṃ samāropaṃ kariṣyati // [AgMsv_2.295]

mv-k10-v1365.plain_english: And how could he understand so much meaning from the sentence? If one says, 'just from that,' then he is not merely a hearer of a word, nor—
mv-k10-v1365.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ cādhigamas tasya tāvato 'rthasya vākyataḥ /
tasmād eveti cet tarhi na padaśrotṛtā na ca // [AgMsv_2.296]

mv-k10-v1366.plain_english: —is that the meaning of only that much. Thus, in the present domain, understanding must come through knowledge of the entire meaning of the Shaiva scripture in its complete form.
mv-k10-v1366.sanskrit_cite:
tāvanmātrasya so 'sty artha itthaṃ prakṛtigocare /
samagraśivaśāstrārthajñaptyā saṃpūrṇarūpayā // [AgMsv_2.297]

mv-k10-v1367.plain_english: If one were to construe Yoga, Samkhya, Arhata, Nyaya, Pancharatra, Veda, and Smriti as complete through the Shiva principle—

mv-k10-v1368.plain_english: Let that be granted to that extent; but the full expansion is not there. It has been examined that knowledge of the Shiva principle must be preceded by the proper preparation.
mv-k10-v1368.sanskrit_cite:
tāvad astu na tu sphāras tāvāṃs tatreti carcitam /
jñaptiś ca śivatattvasya tatsaṃskārapuraḥsarā // [AgMsv_2.299]

mv-k10-v1369.plain_english: Otherwise there would be a transgression for both teacher and student; but if the proper preparation is received, then the meaning of the scripture may indeed be of that kind.
mv-k10-v1369.sanskrit_cite:
anyathā pratyavāyaḥ syād upadeṣṭrupadeśyayoḥ /
tatsaṃskāragrahaś cet syāt kāmaṃ śāstrārtha īdṛśaḥ // [AgMsv_2.300]

mv-k10-v1370.plain_english: But even after receiving higher and higher preparation, he does not cease to be Vaishnava, Samkhya, or Vedic in identity; he still continues to practice accordingly.
mv-k10-v1370.sanskrit_cite:
na tu vaiṣṇavatā tasya sāṃkhyatā śrautatāpi vā /
anyasaṃskāram ūrdhvordhaṃ gṛhītvāpy anutiṣṭhati // [AgMsv_2.301]

mv-k10-v1371.plain_english: Then, if he remains Vaishnava and so on, his transgression is even greater. But surely, in this nondual state, what is this primary conceptual restriction?
mv-k10-v1371.sanskrit_cite:
vaiṣṇavādy eva tarhy asya pratyavāyo mahattaraḥ /
nanv advayapade 'muṣmin keyaṃ mukhyā prakalpanā // [AgMsv_2.302]

mv-k10-v1372.plain_english: What are you saying? You yourself, whose conduct is struck by duality, have resorted to this very supreme duality.
mv-k10-v1372.sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ brūṣe svayam eva tvaṃ bhedopahatavṛttikaḥ /
etad eva paraṃ dvaitaṃ bhavān eva saṃśritaḥ // [AgMsv_2.303]

mv-k10-v1373.plain_english: When you say, 'Being a Vaishnava, why am I not qualified in the Shaiva domain?' you yourself are deluded by duality; and in duality, restriction applies by force.
mv-k10-v1373.sanskrit_cite:
yad ahaṃ vaiṣṇavo bhūṣṇuḥ śaive kiṃ nādhikāravān /
tat svayaṃ bhedamūḍhas tvaṃ bhede ca niyater balāt // [AgMsv_2.304]

mv-k10-v1374.plain_english: Therefore, by those rules, transgression would arise; this has been established. Moreover, a deity is worshiped through identification, and so—
mv-k10-v1374.sanskrit_cite:
tatas taiḥ pratyavāyaḥ syād yoga ity upapāditam /
kiṃ ca tādātmyayogena devatā pūjyate tataḥ // [AgMsv_2.305]

mv-k10-v1375.plain_english: If someone has become identified with Vishnu, how could that person worship Rudra? The Gita says that whoever has faith in a particular deity is, in effect, that very deity.
mv-k10-v1375.sanskrit_cite:
viṣṇutādātmyam āpannaḥ kathaṃ rudraṃ prapūjayet /
gītāsu ca tato gītaṃ yo yac chraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ // [AgMsv_2.306]

mv-k10-v1376.plain_english: Practices of contemplating identity with a deity, along with mantras, give their own results. Therefore, for someone whose self has been shaped by that contemplation and who desires a particular fruit, they bring success.
mv-k10-v1376.sanskrit_cite:
tādātmyabhāvanā yogāḥ phalaṃ mantrāḥ sva }} /
dadyus tadbhāvitātmātaḥ phalakāmasya siddhidaḥ // [AgMsv_2.307]

mv-k10-v1377.plain_english: For someone who desires liberation, even one who seeks liberation through a particular scripture, it is clear that being overcome by dwelling on its faults makes a person capable only within that limited application.
mv-k10-v1377.sanskrit_cite:
mokṣakāmasya tac chāstramokṣalipsor api sphuṭam /
taddoṣabhāvanākrāntaḥ kṣamas tāvati yojane // [AgMsv_2.308]

mv-k10-v1378.plain_english: This indeed is the primary method: whoever is established in any domain and has permanently attained identity with it is authorized there.
mv-k10-v1378.sanskrit_cite:
mukhyas tāvad ayaṃ kalpo yo yatraiva pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
nityaṃ tādātmyam āpannaḥ sa tatrādhikṛtas tv iti // [AgMsv_2.309]

mv-k10-v1379.plain_english: For that very reason it is said that knowledge should be received from him, since he has attained identity through the ordered method of contemplating that.
mv-k10-v1379.sanskrit_cite:
ata eva tato grāhyaṃ jñānam ity abhidhīyate /
sa hi tādātmyam āpannas tadbhāvanavidhikramāt // [AgMsv_2.310]

mv-k10-v1380.plain_english: But when a student is only then receiving the scripture in its proper sequence, how could he at first connect by his own understanding what is coherently taught in it?
mv-k10-v1380.sanskrit_cite:
śiṣyas tadaiva śāstraṃ tu gṛhṇan pūrvāparakramāt /
kathaṃ svabuddhyā saṃdhattāṃ tāvad yat tena saṃhitam // [AgMsv_2.311]

mv-k10-v1381.plain_english: But whoever strives to join the teaching together by himself is directly the supreme lord; what could a teacher do for him? He is called the teacher of others.
mv-k10-v1381.sanskrit_cite:
yas tu saṃdhātum īheta sa sākṣāt parameśvaraḥ /
tasya kiṃ vā guruḥ kuryāt so 'nyeṣāṃ gurur ucyate // [AgMsv_2.312]

mv-k10-v1382.plain_english: For people think that knowledge does not come from anyone other than those who know; therefore one who has attained identity with that is designated a teacher.
mv-k10-v1382.sanskrit_cite:
nānyato vedavidbhyaś cetyata eva hi manvate /
tasmāt tādātmyam āpanno gurur ity abhidhīyate // [AgMsv_2.313]

mv-k10-v1383.plain_english: And he is so only to that extent and in that domain, not otherwise. But surely, does the meaning of Vaishnava scripture, at the time of contemplating Shiva, become affected?
mv-k10-v1383.sanskrit_cite:
sa ca yāvati yatraiva tatra tāvati nānyathā /
nanu vaiṣṇavaśāstrārthas tatkālaṃ śivabhāvanāt // [AgMsv_2.314]

mv-k10-v1384.plain_english: If someone says that such identity destroys teacherhood, the person of full understanding replies that this is mere prattle; for in the dramas of Rama and Ravana, these are not actors' roles in that fixed sense.
mv-k10-v1384.sanskrit_cite:
tādātmyaṃ gurutāṃ hanti pūrṇadhīḥ pralapaty ayam /
rāmarāvaṇanāṭyeṣu nahy etā naṭabhūmikāḥ // [AgMsv_2.315]

mv-k10-v1385.plain_english: Otherness is assumed by changing costume and the like; so too a Vaishnava reflects, 'I am indeed Vishnu' or 'I am his servant.'
mv-k10-v1385.sanskrit_cite:
nepathyādiparāvṛttyā yenānyatvaṃ prapadyate /
vaiṣṇavo viṣṇur evāhaṃ taddāso veti carcayan // [AgMsv_2.316]

mv-k10-v1386.plain_english: If one now says, 'I am not thus,' is that really coherent? For in that case, one of the two awarenesses ends up being false knowledge.
mv-k10-v1386.sanskrit_cite:
idānīṃ na tathāsmīti kim etat susamañjasam /
atra hy ekatamā saṃvin mithyājñānatvam aśnute // [AgMsv_2.317]

mv-k10-v1387.plain_english: By that same outlook a disciple may become fallen, so the main rule is that for each scripture the proper teacher is its own teacher.
mv-k10-v1387.sanskrit_cite:
yayā sa eva patitaḥ śiṣyo vā patito bhavet /
tasmān mukhyo hy ayaṃ kalpaḥ pratiśāstraṃ gurur guruḥ // [AgMsv_2.318]

mv-k10-v1388.plain_english: The independent scriptures say that someone devoted to another scripture, or even absorbed in that other scripture, does not give the fruit of spiritual attainment.
mv-k10-v1388.sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ svatantraśāstreṣu nāsau siddhiphalapradaḥ /
anyaśāstrarato yaḥ syāt tacchāstranirato 'pi vā // [AgMsv_2.319]

mv-k10-v1389.plain_english: Even in ordinary life the same convention holds: Vishnu is served by Bhagavatas, the Sun by Magas, Shambhu by ash-smeared ascetics, the Mothers by their specialists, Brahma by brahmins, the Buddha by Shakyas, and the Arhat by naked ascetics; whoever worships a deity by its own method should perform that deity's rite.
mv-k10-v1389.sanskrit_cite:
loke 'pi yāvad īdṛkṣaḥ pravādo jyotirādike /

viṣṇor bhāgavatā magāś ca savituḥ śāṃbhor jaṭābhasmino māt-ṛṇām atha mātṛmaṇḍalavido viprās tv atha brahmaṇaḥ /
śākyāḥ sattvahitasya buddhavapuṣo nagnās tathaivārhato yo yair deva upāsyate svavidhinā tais tasya kāryā kriyā // [AgMsv_2.320]

mv-k10-v1390.plain_english: Therefore, even if someone with higher knowledge is present in the same place, that does not create different eligibilities.
mv-k10-v1390.sanskrit_cite:
ata evādhikajñānaśālī saṃnihito yadi /
deśe tatra bhaven nānā nādhikārasya bhājanam // [AgMsv_2.321]

mv-k10-v1391.plain_english: But one who is firmly established in this full awakening and in the real teaching sets the disciple's mind toward ever higher ascent.
mv-k10-v1391.sanskrit_cite:
yas tv asmin pūrṇasaṃbodhe rūḍho vāstavaśāsane /
uttarottararūḍhyarthaṃ śiśoḥ karaṇamānasam (?) // [AgMsv_2.322]

mv-k10-v1392.plain_english: For the attainment of fruit, or for a disciple governed only by a partial disposition, that teacher should indeed bestow grace, because of his fullness and his functioning from a higher level.
mv-k10-v1392.sanskrit_cite:
phalasaṃpattaye vāpi bhāvāṃśavaśaśālinaḥ /
anugrahaṃ sa vai kuryāt pūrṇatvād ūrdhvavṛttitaḥ // [AgMsv_2.323]

mv-k10-v1393.plain_english: Someone may object: in nonduality, what could be higher? Nothing. The answer is that those who think this are deluded by difference; for you the lower state is difference, because difference itself is lower.
mv-k10-v1393.sanskrit_cite:
nanv advaye kim ūrdhvaṃ syān na kiṃcid bhedamohitāḥ /
bhavatas tv adharāvasthā bheda evadharo yataḥ // [AgMsv_2.324]

mv-k10-v1394.plain_english: Therefore, any others who follow teachings meant for bound souls—such as Vaishnavas, Buddhists, Vedic ritualists, and Vedanta speakers—are included in that class.
mv-k10-v1394.sanskrit_cite:
tasmād ye kecanānye syuḥ paśuśāsanavartinaḥ /
vaiṣṇavāḥ saugatāḥ śrautās tathā śrutyantavādinaḥ // [AgMsv_2.325]

mv-k10-v1395.plain_english: Such groups are never authorized in the Lord's teaching, as has been stated in the scriptures when determining who is eligible.
mv-k10-v1395.sanskrit_cite:
ityādayo nādhikṛtā jātucit patiśāsane /
uktavān yatra śāstreṣv apy adhikārivivecane // [AgMsv_2.326]

mv-k10-v1396.plain_english: If a deluded Vaishnava were to give initiation to a Shaiva disciple, the disciple should abandon that sinful deceiver and follow the proper course.
mv-k10-v1396.sanskrit_cite:
yo vaiṣṇavo manuṃ dadyāc chaivaṃ mūḍhamatiḥ śiśoḥ /
taṃ pāpaṃ vañcakaṃ tyaktvā śiśur nyāyyaṃ samācaret // [AgMsv_2.327]

mv-k10-v1397.plain_english: Here too it is said that one who gives liberation must possess well-practiced knowledge; and that supreme knowledge is well practiced because there is no falling away from it.
mv-k10-v1397.sanskrit_cite:
ihāpy uktaṃ mokṣadaḥ syāt svabhyastajñānavān iti /
abhyastaṃ ca paraṃ jñānaṃ yato nāsty eva vicyutiḥ // [AgMsv_2.328]

mv-k10-v1398.plain_english: From supreme nondual realization there is indeed no falling away at all, because its functioning is fully pervaded by all knowledge established on the side of the Self.
mv-k10-v1398.sanskrit_cite:
paramādvayavijñānān na khalv apy asti vicyutiḥ /
svātmapakṣasthitāśeṣajñānanirbharavṛttikaḥ // [AgMsv_2.329]

mv-k10-v1399.plain_english: How, or who, or from where could it fall away, or where could it stand otherwise? This meaning of the scripture stands firm just as it is, by the power of śakti.
mv-k10-v1399.sanskrit_cite:
kathaṃ ko vā kuto vāpi cyavatāṃ tiṣṭhatu kva vā /
itthaṃ ya eṣa śāstrārthaḥ sthitaḥ śaktiprabhāvataḥ // [AgMsv_2.330]

mv-k10-v1400.plain_english: Filled within with all principles, letters, and the rest, bearing all names, and whose very nature is Bhairava, he alone abides in his own true form.
mv-k10-v1400.sanskrit_cite:
antaḥkṛtāśeṣatattvavarṇādibharanirbharaḥ /
sarvābhidho bhairavātmā so 'yam eva svarūpabhāk // [AgMsv_2.331]

mv-k10-v1401.plain_english: In this scripture composed by the Supreme Lord under the name Jñānacandra, I have explained this clear yet profound statement, following the method of establishing the authority of our own tradition and also through various relevant contexts. For those whose minds have entered into it, the greatness of its authority, exalted by universal nonduality, shines forth; sincere-hearted people will know this for themselves, so what need is there for praise?
mv-k10-v1401.sanskrit_cite:
śāstre 'smin parameśena jñānacandrākhyayā kṛtaḥ /

tadvyākhyātam idaṃ prasannagahanaṃ vākyaṃ mayā svāgamaprāmāṇyapratipādanakramavaśāt tattatprasaṅgād api /
atrārūḍhadhiyāṃ pramāṇamahimā viśvādvayoddāmito bhātīti svayam eva satyahṛdayā jñāsyanti kiṃ ślāghitaiḥ // [AgMsv_2.332]

mv-k10-v1402.plain_english: Those who inquire properly are truly auspicious, so what effort is needed toward them? And what use is there with those who are lame in climbing the far peak of reflective awareness and whose conduct has turned to stone? As for those people barren of scripture, their vehemence is like the ocean at cosmic dissolution; therefore this agitation only whirls back within oneself.
mv-k10-v1402.sanskrit_cite:
ye samyak pravicāriṇo nanu śivāḥ kas tān prati prodyamaḥ kiṃ tair ye pravimarśadūraśikharārohakrame paṅgavaḥ /
pāṣāṇāyitavṛttayaḥ punar amī ye śāstravandhyā narāḥ saṃrambhaḥ pralayambudher iva tataḥ svātmany ayaṃ ghūrṇate // [AgMsv_2.333]

mv-k10-v1403.plain_english: Grow calm of yourself within the self; quickly abandon your ostentatious display of flaming matted locks, O fire of cosmic dissolution. There is nothing left for you to burn now, because by hundreds of terrible, dense, whirling sparks of your blazing, this universe has been pervaded and swiftly dissolved, becoming of the nature of your own light.
mv-k10-v1403.sanskrit_cite:
saṃśāmya svayam ātmani tyaja javāj jvālājaṭāḍambarān bhoḥ kalpānala dāhyam asti bhavato nādyāpi kiñcid yataḥ /
tvatprollāsavighūrṇanāghanaghuradghorasphuliṅgaśatair viśvaṃ vyāpya vilīnatāṃ gatam idaṃ drāk tvatprakāśātmakam // [AgMsv_2.334]

mv-k10-v1404.plain_english: In the eastern city named Pravarapura, the Kashmirian Abhinavagupta composed this vārttika on the great teaching beginning with the Mālinī.
mv-k10-v1404.sanskrit_cite:
pravarapuranāmadheye pure pūrve kāśmīriko 'bhinavaguptaḥ /
mālinyādimavākye vārttikam etad racayati sma // [AgMsv_2.335]

essence: Divine parents and heart are invoked as the offering's opening.
The guru whose knowledge illuminates all is praised.
The guru is thanked for liberating teachings.
Śambhunātha's grace is invoked.
A superior teacher is saluted; liberation from grasping is declared.

essence: By abiding in the limit of consciousness, the yogin rests beyond temporal division in a mere instant.
Because time is limiting appearance, the yogin who devours it attains the freedom of a sky-mover.
Since manifestation is only the play of one's own rays, restraining them blocks the entire sphere of paths.
Scriptural authority confirms that relishing the devouring of time leads spontaneously to the khecara state.
Through restraint of the rays and tasting the supreme nectar in the unlimited present, one becomes happy.

essence: Whether one underlying thing can remain despite apparent difference is questioned.
Causal difference is contrasted with ultimate difference: can different form still be one?
Whether action can be one agent when nature differs stands challenged.
Fruit production causes no harm, since action is not a separate power for us.
Power is the lord's own power, and the lord is the form of world-self.

essence: the challenge questions prior silence and boastful power
The coherence of such union is questioned.
the dilemma undercuts the resolver's role
Resolver effort is separated from sense dependence.
How object-contact yields knowerhood stands questioned.

essence: Dependence in the self-created realm is not imposed from outside but is manifested by the Lord himself.
The sole defining mark of dependence and autonomy is that the autonomous Lord freely fashions dependence.
Treating the limiter as itself limited threatens to collapse the distinction between limiter and limited.
Because the external object lacks self-luminosity, its apprehension cannot be grounded in it alone.
Knowledge cannot ground manifestation if it is itself unmanifest and not self-luminous.

essence: Because past, future, and present all dissolve in consciousness, time is fully manifested by the lord of consciousness alone.
For consciousness whose nature manifests time, transmigration is the play of being and nonbeing appearing within its own form.
The unfolding of knowerhood is the dynamic abiding in one's own form through affirmations and negations of 'I', 'this', and 'that'.
The varied play of nonbeing belongs to manifestation, but pure knowerhood itself does not contain separate abiding of those distinctions.
Pure isolated knowerhood cannot account for cognition, whereas all worldly knowerhood is constituted by such differentiated cognition.

essence: Bheda-infinity gives way to the ordered reckoning of divisions from water upward.
The fifteenfold lower course is enumerated, and the bound souls knowerhood within it is refused at the supreme level.
The soul-classes are stationed across night, middle, and vidyā-domain stations.
The one self-luminous Śiva-state emerges through the ordered knower-system, then differentiates into numbered Mantreśa groups.
Śakti, knower, and power-holder entail one another, so their separateness is not difference.

essence: The variety of meditation and worship is effective because an embodied, divided deity can be invoked and act immediately.
The coming-and-going account is only scripturally suitable, while the formless nature is what truly fits.
Division is not external to the self but is consciousness manifesting according to its own nature.
Karmic division counts as impurity in bondage but not in the liberating use of initiation and ritual.
Initiation is essentially the true consciousness that destroys division-based transmigration.
mv-k08.essence_source: derived from argmap inferences (machine-proposed; assessor review outstanding)

essence: The supreme offering is the sudden dissolution of gross forms into the blazing light of awareness.
Entities offered into awareness both lose their separateness and intensify the fire of awareness by their own power.
Any sense-object freely manifested by the creative nature of consciousness is fit to serve as an object of meditation.
Within formless, all-form consciousness, a particular form is posited as the meditation object for result-seeking practitioners.
Seeking a particular form within nondual fullness is analogous to choosing a pot to fetch water without denying the fullness of reality.
mv-k09.essence_source: derived from argmap inferences (machine-proposed; assessor review outstanding)

essence: Qualification depends on the specific kind of fruit and the context in which that fruit appears.
Eligibility is shaped by both the practitioner's embodied condition and their received preparation.
The order of qualification for teacher and student follows the same logic of preparatory fitness as other regulated procedures.
Purification must come before initiation so that disruptive change does not interfere with subsequent ritual performance.
Because their conditioning belongs to the paśu level, Vaishnavas and others are not qualified for those rites.
